title: Lilia

reviews.review:
I don't want people to come to this place cause I cant get a reservation last minute and thats really annoying.


Food is solid, service great and consistent, very nice cocktails too.


Just please stop coming here.

Lilia truly captures the essence of Italian cuisine right in the heart of Brooklyn. From the moment we arrived, we were met with warm hospitality and an inviting atmosphere that set the stage for an unforgettable dining experience. The classic Italian cocktails were expertly crafted, perfectly balancing flavors that complemented our meal beautifully. Every dish showcased an extraordinary level of attention to detail, from the delicate textures of the handcrafted pastas to the bold, smoky flavors of the wood-fired seafood. It's clear that the team at Lilia, led by the incredibly talented Chef Missy Robbins, pours passion and expertise into every aspect of the menu. The service was impeccable, with staff who were both knowledgeable and attentive, ensuring that we had everything we needed to enjoy our meal to the fullest. If you're looking for a place that serves authentic, elevated Italian cuisine in a charming and lively setting, Lilia is an absolute must-visit.

Loved the music and ambiance. Felt like the staff was attentive and helpful. Will definitely come back. Recommend 8-10 dishes for 4 people, save room for dessert. Recommended dishes: Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti Saffron Dried Tomato Honey, Grilled Clams, Ricotta Gnocchi with Broccoli Pesto, Focaccia and Green Garlic Butter

Always enjoy coming to Lilia! Have been here several times and they have changed parts of their menu over the years/seasons while also keeping some of the staples like the focaccia with garlic butter, clams, and the mafaldine. The space is really beautiful and cozy, and the service is always great! I've never felt rushed here and the one time we were asked to wrap up since the next reservation was waiter, the server brought us dessert to go on the house which was so nice. I love trying all their different veggie dishes and enjoy the perfectly cooked pastas!
Super tough to get a spot so I was pretty excited when finally getting a res, though it was outside and food quickly got cold. The layers of flavors are enjoyable but I do think it's a bit overpriced
Food is good but do not warrant the high high prices / portions are small and poor value for money. Service is unremarkable -- competent but not additive. Pleasant sitting inside.

About 7 years late I finally made it to Lilia. Misi is close enough to me that I can make the stroll over and try to snag a last minute seat at an odd hour, but for Lilia I was waiting for the random Monday when I'd be compelled to endure a late reservation for the sake of trying their inventive pastas. That Monday was today.

The best bites were the oblong agnolotti with a slight smoky sweetness coming from the saffron (a nice redemption after tasting the disgustingly sweet saffron pasta at Barano) and the simple but well-executed pesto gnocchi. The cacio e Pepe fritters were also a crowd-pleaser.

The mafaldine was probably my least favorite item. The pasta itself was nicely al denté, but I found the sauce quite noticeably salty. I also would skip the artichoke next time - while tasty, the portion of artichoke meat was rather paltry.

The dense olive oil cake is a winner - don't skip dessert here.

underwhelming and overhyped. the bread was good probably best thing from the entire experience it was nice and warm although had way too much pecorino cheese. mafaldini was bland and tasteless skip. the agnoletti was good but not enough to stand up the meal. the steak was mediocre. overall would not return or recommend.

Feb '25. The service here is exceptional. In the last 10 years we've lost really good service but here, your glass of wine won't get below half full without an arm reaching out to refill it. They have a sommelier ready to assist you with any wine decisions you have to make. 

The pastas are all good of course but I wouldn't come here just for the pasta-- it's good in the way most upscale Italian is good. The best bites of the nights were all the apps. 

You MUST get the focaccia. I went to bed dreaming about this bread. And the butter with the focaccia I believe is the same as what's on the mussels. No clue what the hell is in there but it's magic in your mouth -- cannot recommend enough. 

Great spot to order several plates and try a bit of everything!

One of the best meals I've ever had. We had the leek focaccia, artichokes, prawns, mussels, lemon pasta, rigatoni diavola, and sheep's milk cheese agnolotti. I would highly recommend any of the dishes but particularly the focaccia, artichokes, and agnolotti. 

Also, the drinks could have been a bit better. Service was phenomenal once we were seated but took an hour to seat us with a reservation. Still very worth it for the food!
What. An. Experience! Terrific food and lovely service. We got almost everything on the menu we had to try it all. If you can get a reservation RUN don't walk there!

Been wanting to try this place for a while since I've heard great things and finally snagged a reservation for 2 on a monday late evening a couple of hrs after reservations opened for a few weeks out! 

Note that there are a few doors but you can only enter from one side at night and the door is pretty heavy. We waited for a bit for our seats to be ready. I had previously booked seats at the bar but luckily we were able to get a table, which was nice. The tables were nicely spaced out between parties and the place was pretty big. It's a nice spot for a date with great dim light intimate setting. 

For food we tried the mozzarella and garlic bread, the grilled clams, the grilled artichoke, rigatoni diavolo and the Mafaldini. The garlic bread was cruncy but didn't have much garlic flavor as I expected. The mozzarella was creamy and fresh but the combination felt a bit out of place. Nonetheless it was delicious. The pastas were fresh and cooked perfectly al dente. For flavors I loved the tomato sauce with light spice in the rigaotni. The Mafadini was good but it was a bit more tart than I preferred. 

Overall, it was a good experience to try this place! Portion size is on the smaller side

This was on my list for such a long time, and finally - my friend was able to get a reservation for us! Overall the food was delicious - my friend and I got the mozzarella and garlic bread, the grilled clams, the grilled artichoke, and two pastas to share. The garlic bread doesn't have a particularly noticeable garlicky flavor, but the mozzarella was creamy and fresh. The grilled clams were covered in this Calabrian chili paste, which had a nice kick. Initially we were not sure about how to eat the grilled artichoke (surprising this is the first time we ate a complete artichoke haha). But once we figured it out, it was absolutely delicious.

Now in the pastas: they were fresh and cooked perfectly al dente. The rigatoni diavolo had a wonderful sauce. The other pasta was also yummy, but I'm not sure if it was the pasta dish we ordered.  I thought we ordered the Linguini with lamb sausage and tomato pasta too, but instead the dish we got had a nice creamy cacio e pepe flavor. 

Still though, we enjoyed the food. The restaurant ambience had a romantic vibe, and was just a really chill place for more intimate get-togethers. Not sure if it is all worth the difficulty in getting a reservation, but the food is good, and the vibes are lovely!

It look me forever to get a reservation at Lilia, so I was happy to be able to see what all the hype was about.
There were things we loved and things that were just "meh:"

Loved: 
-the Select Spritz (it was perfectly balanced and one of the best spritz I've had)
-Focaccia (truly a flavorful bread)
-Agnolotti (popular for a reason!)

Meh and lacking a hint of flavor: Cacio e Pepe Fritter (not bad just expected more - would benefit from a dipping sauce); Acorn Squash; Gnocchi 

So, did Lilia live up to the hype? In my opinion no, but it is worth trying at least once!

We could never get a reservation here - so we showed up at 5 on a friday and there were plenty of seats at the bar! This ended up working out i think better because the bartenders were very nice and provided great, quick service since we were in a bit of a rush. The cocktails are unique and there was something for everyone. The food was outstanding- anything on the menu is a hit. We got the ravioli and fettuccine - the pastas are fresh and homemade , perfectly cooked and portioned. The reason i give this 4 stars- its waaaaaay over priced. I still think its worth trying if you can get a seat, but I dont think my pockets could handle frequent visits. Prepare to enjoy the food, but spend a pretty penny.

I am livid at how my friend was treated at this restaurant. We bought my friend a $200 gift card for her birthday to try out this restaurant. Before she was able to make a reservation, she was alerted that someone had redeemed her gift card. She had not been to the restaurant.

She sent multiple calls and emails to the restaurant with absolutely no response. She had to go into the restaurant in person to speak to anyone about the issue. At this point, all they could tell her was that "their hands were tied".

I am so upset that our $200 was redeemed by someone unknown and appalled at the lack of customer service she received. Do not waste your money by patroning Lilia. And DEFINITELY never buy a gift card

The service was fantastic, and the staff were incredibly friendly! We did not have a reservation, but we arrived right when they opened at 4 PM and managed to get bar seating.
The food was outstanding--some of the best clams and grilled artichoke I've ever had! The pasta Rigatoni Diavola and Sheep's Milk Cheese Agnolotti was flavorful, but unfortunately, it was served cold, which is why I'm giving this review 4 stars instead of 5. That said, the dessert was absolutely out of this world and the perfect way to end the meal.
Overall, it was a great dining experience

The below is an order for 2 people. I didn't know the portions. I'm a good eater with a steel stomach and I usually finish all my meals but I didn't know Lilia would cap it. I personally can't believe I didn't finish. Here's what I got 
Bagna cauda - yummy, very anchovy less garlicky, came with a medley of happy fresh radishes, celery, fennel, raddicchio, roasted carrots cipolini onions, boiled potatoes and grilled bread drizzled w oil. Very yummy and savory.
Pizette de cacio e Pepe- this is an ABSOLUTE MUST. It's a 2.5" fried ball that when bit into it (note it's steamy hot in there) the inside is filled with a doughy or mashed potato parm cheese mix. This was a very VERY happy morsel. I want more of this next time. 
Leek focaccia w green soft butter - it comes in the shape of a boule. Very tasty bread but if you order this and the crostini and the pizette, it might be too greasy of an order.
Gem salad - tart, refreshing. I used some of the bagna to cut that citrusyness.
Grilled clams- tiny, baked, tart ending. This is a good finger food dish. But I can skip it next time.
Crostini w chicken liver topped w braised green onions?! And capers - this is a thick slice of bread. The crostini is from a 6" elliptical slice of bread. So each crostini is about 3" and you get three of them. This is a very rich rich dish. I used some of the gem salad to easy on the richness. Don't get me wrong I liked it. I love chicken liver pate.
Lamb steak- this was a pice approx 10" x4" grilled and topped with some dressed fennel. This pice was perfectly cooked. I personally like fatty bits which I found. Lamb is gamey and this was cooked and seasoned very well.
Agnolotti about 1"x3", dough is silky soft almost like a wonton noodle. The cheesy filling was very good and this agnolotti had honey on top which I loved. This is a lovely dish. I'd get it again. 
I didn't know what the portion sizes would be but I brought half my lamb steak and half of the boule home. Service is lovely.

took the cake for best italian food i've had in the city without a doubt. the mafaldini and the agnolotti are must-try's and the italian job gelato was to die for. i have genuinely never had a dessert so delicious and unique in my life, lilia's really got me out here looking up where to find fennel pollen just to try recreating this bite of heaven. focaccia was a great starter too, all around amazing meal. 10/10 would most certainly go again
Food and drinks were excellent! Our server recommended the perfect amount of plates to share. Can't wait to go back!

Very high quality elevated Italian fare, on par with the upper echelon of top notch Italian restaurants in the city. But with that being said, the meal wasn't entirely that memorable. Nothing was bad but nothing jumped out that will endure in my memory.

Very popular restaurant so didn't get seated until about 20 minutes after our reservation start time which was a bit of a bummer. The food was delicious & service was on top of it. Would recommend for a special occasion or a date. Not great for any groups larger than 4. Definitely need a reservation! Personally liked the apps better than the pastas itself. So much good Italian in NYC so would go somewhere else next time. A little overhyped in my opinion but still really good!

They served me under cooked chicken!!!!

I was unaware of the hype. Didn't know the level of difficulty getting in the place- my wife made it happen. 
We sat at the bar and service was great. The bartender was knowledgeable and polite. A bit arrogant but not demeaning. 
The leek focaccia with garlic butter was great. The prawns had good flavor but were over cooked.
Always great. Haven't been in a while but they haven't missed a step. I don't normally mention hosts but Izzy was the highlight of this visit...

considering how hard it was to get a res, i had high expectations for this place. to be honest, while i enjoyed my meal, i was underwhelmed. especially when comparing the ambience to other establishments such as torrisi. 

i wasn't a fan of their garlic toast, or any of their toasts such as the one they used for the anchovy dish as it was stale. there was no softness to the bread; it was just hard to bite through. the mozzarella didn't do too much for me either. 

although, the roasted leek foccacia with the green garlic butter was delicious. the bread was so savory and the butter was so smooth and flavorful. 

the cacio e pepe frittelle suprised me as i did not expect to like it as much as i did. it was crunchy on the outside but warm, smooth, and peppery on the inside. 

as for the clams, they were quite unmemorable. i genuinely can't remember their flavor, and i think that's indicative that it could've had more. the clam meat itself was also very small so this was lacking. the grilled scallops were good, but again i've had better. i did like the walnut yogurt sauce it came with. the acorn squash was also unmemorable as it did not even come with a sauce on top, mainly just cheese and brown butter. 

i did really enjoy the pastas at lilia, i thought they were more well rounded than torrisi's (although the tortellini cannot be beat). i really loved the chewiness of the mafaldini and the subtle flavor yet cheesiness from the parmigiano. the agnolotti is their signature dish, and although it was good, it was so good that i'll be thinking about it again. i didn't like the lemon spaghetti--too sour with lack of depth to its flavor. 

the vanilla gelato with olive oil on top was utterly delicious. definitely one of the best gelatos i've ever had. the olive oil cake was alright, i honestly wish it was sweeter, but i liked the blood orange accompaniment.

What's to say that already hasn't been said? Hands down one of the best Italian spots in nyc. The pasta is the reason to come, but any of the items on the menu are remarkable. 
If it's your first time, I highly recommend the sheep's milk pasta. 
The service is impeccable and the vibe is thoughtful, but not loud. 
Prices are what you would expect to pay at a quality restaurant in nyc. 
Absolutely try to get a reservation!

Finally made it to the famous Lilia and what a treat it was. Ordered a bunch of items on the menu and none of them disappoint. Started with the  housemate mozzarella, and the gem salad. Rigatoni Diavola and fettuccini with lamb sausage, grilled chicken thigh and leg and ended the meal with olive oil cake.My favorite dish was the fettuccini and lamb sausage. Mix of flavors in your mouth. They have a big dining room with about 12-15 bar seats. A little loud with the music but overall great experience.

One of my favorite dinners in NY, so glad I finally got to make it here after it's been on my list for so long.

Came here for dinner, the ambiance was very nice, each table had a candle. The food was so good! The focaccia was perfectly crusted and then soft and pillowy inside. The green butter was also interesting. The tortellini was so good and the filling was the highlight of the meal, super creamy. Then topped off with the dessert that was an apple crumble topped with fresh cream -- it had all the elements of a dessert that I like, the warm gooeyness, nice crunch, and a freshness from the cream.

Overall, can't recommend this place enough and will hopefully find my way back!

went to Lilia 15 minutes after it opened to ask for a last minute res, and they were super accommodating!! the server was so kind and friendly. 

Satvi and I went for DATEEE NIGHTTTT. The foccacia was the star of the night, literally chefs kiss. bread melted in my mouth and I wanted moreeee

the pasta was good but tbh nothing to write home about. ognolotti had a saffron taste and was really al dente pasta which I appreciated.

the gnocchi was a flop idk was not a fan

I would go again and try other dishes, loved the service and the restaurant is a VIBE

Fantastic restaurant in Brooklyn with great appetizers, pasta, and lamb chop. We ordered 4 dishes to share and 2 glasses of wine.

- Focaccia with garlic butter: 100/10 (lovedddd the bread and the garlic butter. This might be some of the best bread I've had in a restaurant-- it closely follows the bread I had in the four horsemen!)
- Goat cheese agnolotti: 10/10 (yummy! Loved how creamy and slightly sweet the pasta was.)
- Lamb steak: 100/10 (fantastic lamb steak! Loveddddd the curry-esque sauce that was on top of the lamb. The portion size was also humongous!)
- Olive oil cake: 9/10 (good cake that's not too sweet)
- Wine: 6/10 (wine was subpar) 

The ambiance during dinner was fantastic-- loved the open kitchen concept and loved how dark the whole restaurant was! Perf for date-night. Service was good but the pacing was a bit too slow-- we were in the restaurant for almost 2 hours!

We didn't have reservations which is highly recommended but they were able to seat us in the back half and hour later. Aiden was an amazing sever and made some nice recommendations. Customer service wise, definitely a 5 but food was average. Scallops with sauce and Alonds on top isn't something that stand out, or the garlic bread with mozzarella again wasn't something I'd order again. The pasta however was cooked to perfection. Just enough spice and lamb meat sauce. Again I wouldn't go out of my way to come here but to each their own.

We were able to get a late night reservation at Lilia and were very excited to try it! Because our reservation was on the late side, they ran out of the Angliotti pasta we wanted but offered us the corn tortellini instead. It ended up being our favorite bite of the night. I didn't care for our other pasta but I think that was a personal preference. The cacio e pepe fritters were also very good. The dessert was interesting and unique to try. I like olive oil gelato but something about the spices on top threw me off. I also got a tasty aperol spritz. The inside is much more cozy and warm feeling than the sister restaurant Misi. It was well decorated and not too crowded. If you are able it snag a reservation it's definitely a must try!

The sheep's milk cheese agnolotti brought me back to Lilia for a second time and did not disappoint again. The homemade mozzarella and baked clams were also to die for here. We ordered the pesto gnocchi which I was not impressed with at all but did the job.

Well executed 4 star - Lilia is the sister restaurant of Misi. However, I do prefer the ricotta toast of Misi as the appetizer. We had the mozzarella on toast which was good, but not fall-out-of-my-chair amazing. 

The clams were great and the pasta were oerfectly el-dente. The signature dish that you absolutely cannot go wrong here are the agnolottis. Perfectly rich and creamy, not too heavy or bland, I would definitely order this the next time I come back.

One of our friends was able to snag us last-minute resys this summer while we were on a week-long trip to NYC. Oh, man of man! We were impressed by EVERYTHING here. You HAVE to start with the prawns! Some of the best I have had! The Agnolotti was my favorite pasta here, but everything else we had was heavenly! The service was attentive and friendly. 

I would definitely stop in next time I am here!
Delicious and cozy spot! I will say I had extremely high expectations and I don't know if it met them but still a great spot for some good pasta and sides.

The food was disappointing after all the hype. Spicy rigatoni and mafaldini pastas way too chewy and brought out a little cold. Only the agnolotti would be worth going back for. Service was great however, and setup is really nice for dinner.

Lilia is notoriously hard to get into, so we were thrilled to finally secure a reservation. We started with two mocktails, which were average, but the focaccia with green butter was fantastic--soft bread with perfectly seasoned butter. Unfortunately, the mains were a bit disappointing. The Rigatoni felt underseasoned, and the Sheep's Milk Cheese Agnolotti was too rich and overpowering for my taste, much like a similar dish I'd tried at Misi. Still, the service was excellent, the ambiance beautiful, and I'd return to try other dishes.

I was fortunate enough to snag a reservation here twice--this place is in high demand and usually books up fast.

Here's what I ordered:
 * PROSCIUTTO - Because why not? Always a classic.
 * ROASTED EGGPLANTS - Served with olives, capers, and pine nuts. It was okay, but I'd probably skip this next time.
 * GRILLED CLAMS - Definitely a must-order, these were fantastic!
 * MUSSELS WITH HERB BUTTER - Absolutely delicious!
 * SHEEP'S MILK CHEESE AGNOLOTTI - The true star of the meal. Hands down the best pasta I've had here!
 * RIGATONI DIAVOLA - Cooked perfectly al dente, though I wished for a bit more spice.
 * MALFALDINI - Another favorite!

I highly recommend trying this spot at least once. The pastas are outstanding!

I had high expectations for this restaurant, but unfortunately, it didn't quite meet them. While the pastas were well-prepared, they lacked that memorable, standout quality that would make me eager to return. The staff was attentive, but the service felt somewhat perfunctory, perhaps due to the restaurant's established reputation. We had a reservation for 4 PM, and there was already a line forming upon our arrival, which adds to my uncertainty about the overall hype. In my opinion, it's a place you could skip.

I loved my experience at Lilia. To start, I had the focaccia that came with the green butter. This was a great first impression that excited my stomach for the main course: goat's milk ravioli. Powerful flavor and creamy texture, I get why this dish is so popular. Ended the meal with the Italian job, which was a surprisingly good combination of salty seasoning, olive oil, and honey over vanilla ice cream. Three contrasting dishes made for a fun full experience!

This place is worth the hype . The dishes that stood out were the pastas . 

To start from the beginning I loved their take on a Aperol spritz which had a grapefruit flavor . 

The cacio e Pepe fritelle were cheesy yet light and I would order it again . The scallops were good but I don't know if I would get it again . The grilled clams although small the flavor was amazing . It had a kick to it . 

The lamb was a bit salty but cooked well and the fennel topping was perfect to balance the richness of the meat . 

My favorite dishes were the agnolotti, the caramelized onion ravioli and the mafaldini. The mafaldini was my favorite dish of the whole night . I want to go back to 
 try all their pasta dishes .

been wanting to try this place for awhile and was finally able to get a reservation. decent food overall. start with the housemade mozzarella. it's garlicky and lemony flavors go well together. the sheep's milk cheese agnolotti is a must try pasta dish, which includes saffron, dried tomatoes, sweet honey, and a soft cheese filling.

Just to be clear, this review has no bearing on the food that this establishment serves. That's because I never even got to try it. I'm sure the food is as good as everyone says, but man, what a poorly run business/reservation system.

Anyone that lives in New York know that it is extremely difficult to get a good dinner time reservation at this restaurant. So considering that, I made a reservation for my girlfriend's birthday a month in advance. I was so happy when I was able to get a 7:15pm reservation on the evening before her birthday. We wanted to try Lilia because one of our first dates was at Misi, this restaurant's "sister/brother" restaurant. 

Fast forward to this afternoon, I receive a text stating that my reservation was cancelled due to forecasted rain. There is no percentage chance of rain in Williamsburg this evening, so I have no idea what this is about (See text and forecast below).

No sensible resolution or help offered by the staff of the restaurant. It's such a shame that our evening and her birthday are now likely ruined, but I thought it would be prudent to warn others of this situation. I would absolutely not rely on this restaurant to honor your reservation for a special occasion!
Man. This pasta was shockingly not good. Which is extra sad because we really enjoyed the focaccia. Very disappointed to have wasted $70/person on such untasty pasta.
The service was impressive and the dishes were absolutely amazing. We had the focaccia, mussels, grilled melon, mafaldini and fettuccini.

Came here with a friend who snagged a last minute reservation. It was a Wednesday night and slammed - waited 20+min past our time before we were seated. We split the broccolini, focaccia with herby garlic butter, and of courssseeee each got the agnolotti pasta. Everything was incredible. Broccolini was probably the least exciting item, wouldn't order again - but would absolutely order the other two items! The pasta lives up to the hype, the sauce is this honey, spicy, buttery delicious situation. Dirty martini was delicious as well! 
This place lives up to the hype.

There was a LOT of hype before going and in the end I get it. It's certainly hard to get a reservation and there's a reason for it.

We had somewhat thought out what we wanted ahead of time and were super pumped to try the agnolotti, as this seemed to be quite popular. Unfortunately, this was not available the day we went-womp womp. We ended up starting with the mozzarella toast. I'm usually really into toast like this but this one kind of missed the mark for me. The toast itself was a bit too substantial and I truly did not appreciate the bottarga, as it didn't go well with the cheese (or any cheese?). We also went with the little gem salad. I enjoyed this! Love a salad that uses breadcrumbs like this and the texture I enjoyed. Finally to start were the grilled clams. There's a reason every single person has this in their pictures-it's delicious and a must when you're here. The clams are pre-shucked, which is clutch, and perfectly breaded. Quite easy to eat and a nice portion. 

We chose two pastas: the malfadini and the gnocchi. Malfadini is not a pasta we really ever eat, so it was a nice option. It took me a while to warm up to whether I enjoyed the taste of the peppercorn sauce but in the end found it to be a nice balance of zest and cheese. The latter (the gnocchi) I preferred but it would be difficult to make a pesto dish I didn't enjoy. Particularly enjoyed the addition of the pistachios. I will say I wish that the pasta options had more meat representation, as I don't typically love a meatless pasta by itself. We weren't so inspired by any of the main meat dishes so opted out of this.

The experience itself was quite nice. We were sat outside, which I typically don't love but it was a lovely night. The service was prompt and pleasant and overall was a smooth experience. Definitely worth the effort to get a reservation.

Great place for pasta lovers!
Lilia and Misi are two of the best pasta places in Williamsburg. Highly recommended to try the agnolotti and mafaldini. If you are a cheese lover, try cacio e Pape fritelle.

But never forget to save some space for dessert! The Italian job gelato is the best olive oil gelato I ever have before! It is ever better than a lots of gelato shop!

This place is in my top 10 Italian places! We couldn't get a reservation, but we showed up right before they opened and we were able to walk in and get a table, although we had to leave by a certain time. 
Our waiter was really nice and even though we had limited time, we didn't feel rushed or anything. We got the ramp bread and butter, cesear salad, peppercorn malfadini, and broccoli pesto. Everything was amazing! The pasta was cooked perfectly and was so flavorful. I wasn't a huge fan of the malfadini because it really is only peppercorn flavored. The ramp bread was to die for!! I would go back just to get 10 orders of that bread.

Managed to get a coveted reservation here but was unimpressed. Service was great but the food was nothing special. We had the salad, vodka pasta, spicy clams, and chicken. The chicken was the best dish, tender and flavorful. We sat outside in the sun which probably didn't help the overall experience. Pricey so will not be coming back...
DO NOT GO. Rudest hostess in the world. They do not honor reservations. Seriously, worst experience of my life. Get out of hospitality business.

author.name: Jordan G.
author.location: Upper East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: Wow!  That Italian job gelato was one of my top 10 desserts of all time.  Great service! The place is buzzing so get there when it opens.  If you send them an email a day before, they can usually get you in. Go to their website for the email address.  The owner is a former James Beard winning chef and it shows.  Great menu!

I wish I could give more stars... my experience at Lilia was 12/10. The hostess, Margot, went above and beyond to seat me for my birthday - she made it work and it ended up being one of the best meals I've had in a while. Thank you for making my birthday, Margot, and the rest of the extremely kind and welcoming Lilia team! I cannot wait to come back :).

Service is perfect, food is amazing!
What else can I say!
Good luck getting a reservation 
Best of the best in my opinion 
5 stars is the minimum I can do

Love Lilia Restaurant! What a delicious meal we had! The chicken was amazing and tender and tasty. The dessert, Lemon Ice, was like lemon and vanilla sorbet and was unforgettable! And our waiter was perfect, he didn't hover but seemed to be around when we needed him. Excellent service. He was perfect, coming out the second I dropped my napkin, to give me a new one. 

We ate outside, lucky to have a reservation. 

The salad was good, but kind of strong (lemon?) from the dressing. I like less dressing and often forget to ask. And the Grilled artichoke toppings were a surprise, with what seemed like parmigiano and bread crumbs and a orange butter sauce.  But the thrill of the evening was the chicken. It was the best chicken I have ever had. It was finger licking good!  I wish I could copy the recipe at home. 

We will come back!  My advice: make a reservation! You will be happy you did.

Lilia represents everything NYC dining should be: ambitious, approachable, and slightly unattainable. The effect is potent. Sitting down feels like an accomplishment, but you quickly settle in like a regular at a neighborhood corner. The food is confident and welcoming, inspired without being derivative, imaginative without being self-indulgent. 

Sibling restaurant Misi seems to be more "trendy" than Lilia in recent years. While some of Misi's pastas are more appealing to my palate, Lilia's rustic intimacy generally prevails in my view. In either case, I try to go to both every season to soak up the full breadth of Missy's seasonal pastas.

Recommend some mix of the following: 

* Focaccia - Not a regular focaccia, with a great crunchy crust. Best when ramps are in season, but always superb. 

* Vegetables - Never been unhappy, great for a first course to pair with the focaccia, but don't think you're at Via Carota and try to make these the star of your meal. 

* Rigatoni with diavolo sauce - Rich but subtle heat from the garlic and Calabrian chilies. Really easy to make at home -- get her cookbook!

* Ricotta gnocchi with broccoli pesto - great textural contrast between the pillowy gnocchi and the rather substantial sauce.

* Sheep's milk agnolotti - Lovely nuance in flavors with a subtle layering of sweet and salt, savory and creaminess. But would like more textural contrast. 

* Seasonal pasta - Get this without hesitation. 

* Italian Job - Lots of subtle heterogeneity in textures and tastes, the perfect capstone.

Our waitress was very sweet and the food is ok to good. The other staff members who poured us drinks, served us food, etc were also very nice. HOWEVER, the service inside the restaurant ( the host, other people walking around) were so unfriendly and unhelpful. I asked someone where the bathroom was and they just walked by and completely ignored me. It is a very cold vibe and very unprofessional for a restaurant reservation that is so hard to get. 

The food is fine. Its good but you can find better or comparable italian food in NYC and you don't have to fight to get a reservation. I wasn't very impressed. The lamb was very fatty and chewy which for a restaurant that is so in demand is kind of appalling. Honestly, I don't understand how this place blew up the way it did. It is on the level with italian food you'd find in a mall in middle America.

Managed to get off the waitlist on a Sunday at 4:30 outdoor patio for a party of 2. Was super excited but ultimately disappointed. I don't quite understand the hype. 

TLDR: Decent food but not worth the hype. High quality ingredients but somewhat of a miss on the execution. Get the sheep milk's agnolotti but everything else is forgettable.

Ambiance - the outdoor patio needed fans. There was some umbrella coverage for most tables but some tables are partially exposed (they sat us at one at first but luckily they accommodated my request to move). The indoors was a little too cold - def bring a light sweater even for the summer if you're seated inside.

Food - All the dishes were fine but nothing wowed me and honestly, this is going to be controversial, but I think the pasta at many other places (including Ci Siamo) are much better. Specifically:
- Housemade mozzarella - This was fine but honestly a bit lacking in flavor. It was a bit too bland and definitely needed more salt. I took a few bites and gave the rest to my husband.
- Focaccia - This was much more flavorful, though I wasn't a huge fan of the garlic butter. That also needed more salt and had very little taste to it. I similarly had just a few bites before giving the rest to my husband. 
- Little gem lettuce - The dressing was good but I didn't love the bread crumbs. I usually love bread crumbs in salad but I think these needed to be coated in oil and just a bit bigger. They were super tiny, wouldn't stay on the lettuce, and just falling all over the table. 
- Prawns - These were fine and had good flavor. They claimed the shells were edible but I was skeptical. My husband tried to eat them and decided they weren't charred/fried enough to be edible.
- Sheep's Milk agnolotti - This was the best dish of the night. The pasta was pillowy soft and the sauce had just a touch of sweetness that I really enjoyed. Was not as much a fan of the sun dried tomatoes but my husband liked them.
- Mafaldine pasta - This is usually my favorite pasta but I was sadly disappointed. I thought the pasta was a little undercooked and there was way too much peppercorn. I could only eat a few bites before giving it all to my husband.
- Italian job gelato - The gelato was very good but I didn't love all the toppings and olive oil it came with.

Service: Very friendly and attentive. Our waitress stopped by several times throughout the night after each dish to see how we liked them and frequently refilled our waters.

I feel a little bad giving this place only 4 stars but there are just so many amazing Italian places in the city that it really has to excel to hit the 5. Lilia was good, but probably overhyped so it just didn't wow me the way Misi did and definitely not for the hoopla to get a resy. Also, the shrimp, although delicious, was shell on and almost impossible to peel which really turned me off. 
The Italian job gelato was a true revelation though -- a must try if you do go.

We got a reservation for 4 on an early weekday, and the restaurant was actually still pretty empty, so it felt like there was a good chance you could just walk in. Super beautiful setting, with super high ceilings and great lighting.

We started with the grilled artichoke, which was just ok. Not much meat to the artichoke, and the flavor was overwhelmingly cheesy. Would probably skip!

We then got onto the pastas, and naturally this is where Lilia REALLY shines. We got the agnolotti, the pesto gnocchi, and the rigatoni, and all three were special in their own way. The pesto was unbelievably fresh, and really felt like they had just blitzed it together before serving. It also had a bunch of pistachios, almost a bit too much for my liking, but the rest of the table loved it. The agnolotti was the highlight for me; the filling was magical, so creamy and rich. The rigatoni had a super bouncy texture, and was a bit too al dente for me, but still very very good.

The black bass was super tender, but it somehow imparted an extremely fishy taste to the potatoes that made the potatoes hard to eat. Wouldn't recommend this.

If you were to come, stick to the pastas. Order as many as you can and family style it; they're all super unique and really were some of the best pasta dishes I've had!

Horrible experience here. First, when I walked in, the guy asked me "what I was there for" .... obviously I'm there for a reservation. Once I gave him my name, he laughed? which was strange. I was dressed nicely and just waiting for my table. Then, finally after being taken to our table by another girl, we weren't assigned a server or offered water until 10 mins after being there... it was 93 degrees outside and reportedly the hottest day in NYC to date. Already a horrible start. On top of that, then our waitress, Elle T, provided horrible customer service to us compared to the other patrons (who were 99% white). She asked if we had any questions and my boyfriend asked her if she could point out the vegetarian dishes on the menu if she doesn't mind and she literally rolled her eyes. She went "it's pretty straight forward."..... I'm pretty sure that's a normal question to ask, considering some of these places put chicken broth or stock into their pastas. And even if she doesn't think that's a normal question to ask, it's her job to answer it without being rude. I would potentially give her the benefit of the doubt if she had a long day or dealt with rude people because it was 5:15pm but the dinner service did just open at 5 and unless she's been working since 9 AM I can't imagine a polite question upsetting you. She seemed particularly annoyed by us, not sure what we did.... We were exceptionally polite, just had religious dietary restrictions. After getting the food, she kept asking how it tasted etc and we said it was good, for the Mafaldini my boyfriend was like it's delicious but asked for extra chili flakes on the side and again she rolled her eyes! I swear I've never had such a pretentious waiter. She didn't even make the food and she's this upset. In general, we felt there was disdain towards us while we were eating and made us uncomfortable. 

This review is only a result of Elle T's pretentious and rude service. Every other person who came to our table- whether to clean it, give us water, check on us, give us the food, was kind. I wish we had asked for a different server would've had a much better experience. 

And the last con was that there were so many flies flying around, as said in many other reviews! Gross!

Food was good but unfortunately the overall environment made us uncomfortable and made it hard to enjoy our meal. Service in general was significantly better at Misi (or anywhere else). This place is pretentious and you're better off elsewhere.

Reservations for Lilia are one of the most impossible to get. Ended up walking in on an early Saturday night hoping for a table for 4. By luck, there was a no show, and we were able to get seated after their grace period ended. They told us they would need the table back in an hour and thirty minutes, but that was plenty of time for us. 

We got a bottle of orange wine. We asked for recommendations. I don't remember the exact bottle, but the price was at the lower end of the spectrum of their offerings. However, the wine was crisp and fruity. Everything a new wine drinker would appreciate. 

Started off with the housemade mozzarella toast. It was so smooth and creamy. The mozzrella itself was very mild, but the textural contrast between it and the bread was heavenly. The small bits of bottarga on top provided a little bit of saltiness and the lemon a little bit of acidity. My favorite bite of the night had to be the chicken liver crostini. It was so smooth. The tiniest bit of bitterness from the liver. Freshness from the spring onion, and a bit of sweetness from what I assume the balsamic. The crisp of the crostini. It was amazing. 

Fettuccine was good but not my favorite pasta. Cooked well, but I wasn't wowed by it like I was by the agnolotti. The sauce of the agnolotti was amazing sweet and savory, buttery and silky. The sheep milk was surprisingly not that strong which I preferred. The pocketful pasta was so soft in my mouth. The dried tomato gave a bit of brightness. One of my favorite pasta dishes in NYC to date. 

I would skip the grilled lamb leg steak the next time. While it was cooked to a perfect temperature, it was still somewhat chewy. There were also gristle pieces as well still. A little saltier for my taste too. 

If you can, definitely come in to try Lilia.
Epic epic epic!! The pasta is insanely good ... the vibe is wonderful. Service is magic. Always a great night at Lilia.

What a meal! 

The food, the ambiance, the service - everything everything.

Getting a reservation is a sport here, but once you're confirmed - you're golden!

We arrived on time for our reservation and our table was perfectly set for us! It's a tasting menu with so many options to choose from! 

The food came out as it was readied and it was simply delicious! We definitely were stuffed by the of everything but it was worth every bite! 

Definitely plan ahead and come hungry - it will appease all your hunger pains! 

Hoping to make it back one day!

Sorry to report this place is actually worth the hype! 

I came 20 minutes before opening on Thursday and got seated 10 minutes later without a reservation. (I'd recommend coming early - on a weekday - if you're like me and don't plan your dinners months out.) I sat at the bar which got crammed after a while so if you can get table seating inside or outside. 

I ordered the Focaccia, Grilled Pawns and Sheep's Milk Agnolotti. It was interesting how everything came out slowly and one at a time so I would plan for atleast 2 hours to eat here. Honestly the food was amazing! I wish I had room to try the Italian job but that gave me an excuse to come back. Must try!!

Lilia had been on my list for awhile and I am happy to say it lived up to the hype. Highly recommend calling when reservations come out (as opposed to trying to get one on Resy). I was able to get a reservation for a group of 5 very easily. They were also super accommodating when I added someone to the group.
The food speaks for itself, but some of our favorites were the grilled artichoke, the focaccia, and the agnolotti (probably my favorite pasta I've ever had). And don't skip dessert - the gelato with olive oil (I don't remember the name) is SO good!!

When you have to line up at 3:30pm to get a walk in table at 4pm, it should be off the charts, no? Unfortunately, not. Service was professional, prompt, and friendly, scene is great (Brooklyn industrial chic), and wines by the glass (and bottles) are good and relatively reasonably priced. None of the food was bad, but I wouldn't go back. The agnolotti and mafaldini were way too rich and, while a taste of them might have been good as an appetizer, we didn't enjoy them as main courses. (We love pastas, but didn't even want to finish these.). The focaccia and butter is great, but $17 for bread and butter is just ridiculous. Other starters were also yummy. Maybe we just picked the "wrong" pastas!

Everything we ordered at Lilia was amazing. I seldom find a restaurant where I can't discriminate between what I liked best, but really every dish we ordered was outstanding. We ordered papardelle with lamb ragú, gnocchi with pesto, agnolotti, malfadini, clams and bread. The clams were unique and delicious with a bright flavor to counter the richness of the buttery clam. Bread was served with a green herb butter that was to die for. Every pasta was cooked perfectly al dente with well balanced sauces.

The atmosphere is bright and elegant but in a casual way, and our server was responsive and knowledgeable. Overall, this place is worth the hustle to get a reservation, it's wonderful.

This was one of the best dining experiences we have ever had! We came by in the afternoon and the restaurant was closed to prep late for dinner. The host still chatted with us and even secured a reservation for us at 4pm when they re-opened. When we came back at 4, there was a line wrapped around the building. The hype is REAL! Every dish was delicious and you have to try the Italian Job dessert (olive oil on gelato). The service was quick but each dish was well timed out so we got to enjoy the ambiance. Such an amazing date night!

Lilia was absolutely OUTSTANDING. I had heard of this place for years and frankly hadn't been able to get a reservation anytime I was in New York. So when I finally got to go this week I was super excited, but slightly apprehensive like I always am about super buzzy restaurants since I fear they might be all hype. I am here to tell you Lilia absolutely lived up to the hype and maybe exceeded it? I'm a huge foodie and go to a lot of well-known restaurants but this one might sit somewhere in my all-time top

We got the bagna cauda with vegetables. The sauce was good ,the veggies fresh . I found a fly on my fennel and showed my waiter. He removed the fennel but didn't offer to bring new veggies and didn't send a manager over . We got the Malfaldini which wasn't cooked well. Sauce is just as stated pink peppercorn. The spaghetti with pine nuts was ok. Just like pasta with parm nothing special.  My second time there won't be back

Lilia has been a name I've been hearing since moving back to NY. It's nearly impossible to snag a res, but if you walk-in around 9pm on a Friday night you might get lucky and get the best seat in the house. It's pasta heaven for all pasta lovers, but I did enjoy some more than others. Overall, the textures are magnificently chewy. Although the flavor profiles didn't wow me, I'd actually skip the sphagetti (which was recommended by our server) next time. The fried prawns were probably my fav - juicy, cripsy, and so flavorful. I loved the soft serve - nice way to end a pretty heavy meal. 

Phenomenal service and super fun atmosphere. Would recommend if you can get a spot! Worth trying for sure.

Easy 5 stars. The pasta dishes & gelato we ordered were delicious. Service was fast. Wait staff was polite and helpful. The best part about this place aside from the food is the natural lighting. Huge windows line the restaurant and create a great ambiance. Open kitchen design was very cool as well.

author.name: Brayden C.
author.location: Lower East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: Extremely nice staff. Hard to get reservation. Mozzarella appetizer was way too salty. Lamb sausage fettuccine was great. Good atmosphere. Vanilla gelato with fennel was good but maybe a little salty. Very good but overhyped. Maybe for Brooklyn it's the best Italian but there's better in Manhattan.

晚市从下午4点开始，没抢到订位，直接顶门walk-in碰碰运气，竟然不用坐吧台。接待和服务员的态度友好，氛围热闹惬意，菜量小，出餐速度比较慢

DELICATE SQUASH, Walnut Parsley Pesto, Sage
【斑纹南瓜】
南瓜切成薄片，带皮烤制，同时拥有绵软和硬脆的口感。一入口是极酸的核桃欧芹罗勒酱，咬到南瓜肉的瞬间甜味迸发，立刻中和了浓郁的酸味。油炸鼠尾草真妙啊，无敌酥，干爽不油腻，后调是清新的植物香气。本来很讨厌的核桃，切丁作为点缀，增加了脆脆的咀嚼感。虽然整体在观感上偏油，但却是清爽的前菜

GRILLED SCALLOP, Walnuts, Yoghurt, Marjoram, Anchovy
【烤扇贝】
扇贝肥美饱满，鲜味扑鼻。炭火猛烈，让扇贝的表皮在极短的时间内变得金黄焦脆，内里却保持着鲜嫩多汁的半熟质地。一进嘴就能感受到扇贝肉的甜美。不喜欢这道菜的搭配，温热的酸奶，质地浓稠，弱化了酸度，点缀以核桃碎和墨角兰叶，单独吃充满了酸奶碗的感觉，但是和扇贝的融合度不高

MAFALDINI, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano
【粉胡椒芝士意面】
那不勒斯波浪形边缘意大利面，辛辣和奶香充分展示了这份意面的配料：粗颗粒粉色胡椒、帕玛森干酪碎。面条是干硬的质地，接近干意面的口感，浓稠的酱汁完美地包裹了每根面条。粉红胡椒虽然闻着有强烈的辣味，但是吃起来却比黑胡椒温和许多，和帕玛森干酪碎搭配出了别样的基础味型

Bianchi
【Zibibbo, Nino Barraco 2022 * Sicily】
闻着是饱满浓郁的果香，酒体却不厚重，质地顺滑偏干爽。喝起来差点意思，风味太过单一，缺少层次

I wanted to come to try out this place after coming back from Italy.  While it is certainly quality food that is nicely prepared, it wasn't quite what I was expecting.  The fritters were slightly on the side of being too salty and the clams were just ok.  The pasta was made expertly though, I kept wondering how a pasta so thin was able to keep in all that filling.  The staff was nice enough to put a candle in the dessert since I was coming here with someone for their birthday.  Overall, not what I was expecting, but I still encourage anyone to try it out for themselves.

Walked in and was seated around 4pm on a Friday and had quite possibly one of the best meals of my life. 

The foccasia with green garlic butter was so delicious. Soft crunchy bread, crispy onions, and garlicky butter - I couldn't ask for more. We also got an artichoke heart which was citrusy, soft, lemony and overall delicious. 

My friend and I split two pastas: the Mafaldini and the sheep's milk agnolotti which were mind blowingly delicious. The mafaldini was peppery and salty it was simple but good. The agnolotti is a must order! So sweet and creamy. 

Now for dessert. You absolutely must must must order the Italian Job. Never have I ever had such amazing, high quality vanilla gelato topped with olive oil, sea salt, and a couple other seasonings I can't name. Though, this was the highlight of my dinner and dare I say one of the best desserts I've ever consumed in my existence. Please get this dessert and give olive oil gelato a try when you come here!

Came here on a Sunday in a whim. They open at 4 pm for dinner, start taking reservations 28 days in advance and thought "no way" I would get in. At 3:30 pm the doors were open so I asked the hostess if there was a chance of getting a table for two. She was very accommodating and said she had a table if we were done by 5:45 pm which was fine. 

Despite a few mixed reviews,  most people love Lilia. We had a great experience and you can tell the staff is well trained, courteous, has the customer in mind and they are well staffed. Kudos to the owner. 

Great  ambience, nice vibe, awesome bar and seating, people were willing to sit outside, even though it was a little chilly. The restaurant provides blankets. 

They put a nice spin on the dishes. They find a way to put a unique flavor. They are a little pricey, some dishes are a little on the small size, and I would have liked to see more variety on the menus for entrees. They are know for their pasta dishes.

I had a margarita which was good, although a little on the small side. 

We started with the house made mozzarella on toasted garlic bread. It was very fresh and flavorful, you can taste all the seasoning.

We shared three mains, two were pastas. Loved the spaghetti, pine nuts and lemon reggiano. Also the fettuccine with lamb sausage, lemon passato and pecorino romano cheese. 

We also had the grilled bass, salsa verde over coal roasted Yukon golden potatoes.

Couldn't pass up on desert. Had the lemon ice which was vanilla gelato, candied lemons, and lemon granita. Also had the apple crostata with honey and creme freiche. 

We spoke to several repeat customers who were extremely happy. They also have a small cafe in the back of the restaurant with a separate door.  They have a nice following. I would definitely recommend them.

Favorite restaurant in the city. Hard to get a reservation but totally worth it. We always get the same items: clams, mafaldini , agnolotti, and the grilled lamb. Then we usually get one or two new things to try. This time we got the focaccia. I didn't love it but my sister really did. Also, unfortunately, the last time we went they didn't have the gelato which we love as well.

A delish spot.

Food and drinks are fantastic. Service was also great.

We enjoyed food, drinks and service while here - I will be back. 

(P.S. idk if I'm team Lilia???)

I had an incredible dinner at Lilia. Firstly, the service was fantastic. Our waitress was very helpful with recommendations. 

To start, we had the Cacio e Pepe frittelle, focaccia, and italian broccoli. All three dishes were great, but the Cacio e Pepe frittelle was my favorite. 

For entrees, we shared the mafdini and gnocchi. Both were delicious. For dessert, we shared the Italian Job gelato, which was to die for. 

I really enjoyed my dinner experience at Lilia and I look forward to returning.

Just left Lilia very full. The prosciutto appetizer was fantastic. 

I was taught:  spread the amazing butter on the crunchy on the outside soft in the middle bread, spread the balsamic over that and then top with the prosciutto!  Yum.

The mozzarella appetizer was equally amazing. Little gem salad was good. Nothing special but good and the gnocchi was also good. I hear the pastas are better so next time (and there will be a next time) for sure. 

By the way, shout out to the fantastic bartender Mari. She was great!

Food was terrible, completely bland, no flavor whatsoever. The rigatoni was hard and undercooked, not al dente. The lemon spaghetti was OK, but tasted like something I'd make hungover in college. 
Also, I said it was my husband's 50th birthday and they did nothing about it, generally at ANY resturant they will giive a small dessert at MINIMUM. They said 'oh happy birthday by the way' as we were leaving. Will never return, completely overrated and tasteless.

One of the best Italian restaurants I've ever been to! Everything we ordered blew my mind. Been wanting to try this place for the longest time and finally had the chance to. It did not disappoint! 

We went during the summer and dined outdoors. Perhaps this may have affected the service in comparison to dining indoors. Nothing bad to say but nothing exceptional to mention either. 

Ambiance is nice and simple outdoors. No complaints. The food is where it's at. 

Try the Italian job gelato!

Unfortunately this place was a disappointment despite the raving reviews and how hard it was to get a reservation. To start, we got nasty stares at our table because of how tight the space was even though there was nothing we could particularly do about it--it was the space they gave us and we tried to not disturb anyone. The table next to us kept staring our party down and when we mentioned it to the waiter he just nervously laughed. They sent multiple waiters to our table because one waiter wasn't sufficient to bring our order out. Moving on to the service, the waiter forgot to pour some glasses for us, forgot to put in certain orders of ours and also forgot to bring some of our appetizers out. Then to food--our pasta was severely Al dente. Severely to the point where it was chewy and just plain uncooked. Some of the dishes were way too salty that we just couldn't eat it and some of the dishes were just underwhelming. For the price point and how difficult it was to get a reservation this restaurant was extremely underwhelming. I would not attend this place ever again. 
Ambiance was great though loved to the vibes but I don't go to restaurants for the ambiance particularly I go for the food.

Inside a renovated East Williamsburg car body shop, dough pro Missy Robbins helms the open kitchen at Lilia. All the pastas on her pan-regional Italian menu are handmade and many showcase inventive twists on classic combinations, such as mafaldini with pink peppercorns and parmesan, and an extra aromatic take on Roman-style cacio e pepe fritelle (sweet fried doughnuts with cheese and pepper). Whole fish and juicy steaks come off a massive wood-fired grill and the all-Italian wine list is concise and focused.
Three words : Caccio Pepe balls. Get a reservation or come right when doors open. A spot outside in the sun with wine is quintessential Brooklyn.

If you like peppery pasta, then you may like the mafaldini with peppercorn. I thought it was okay. The sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti on the other hand was delicious! It had saffron on top and the sauce paired well with the cheese. I was very happy with this dish and would come back to have it again. I made a reservation for 4:15pm for 1 and was seated at the bar very close in between people. I would opt for finding a second person to come with next time and aim for non-bar seating.
Best Italian food I've ever had! Sheep's milk agnolotti, beet casunziei and focaccia are definitely a must! Can't wait to come back!

I dedicate this review to the man in front of us who tried to snag a walk-in table and was promptly told to come back at 9:40pm. In my opinion, Lilia is truly worth the hype (just depends on what you like and what you get). The sheep's milk agnoletti is one of the top five pasta dishes I've had in the city. If you love pouches of greatness that come in the form of filled pasta shapes, this is your go-to order. The after taste of honey made me a happy girl. The mafaldine was also spectacular and well worth it. Go for the lemon granita dessert if you want a light palate cleaner (this wouldn't be my first choice dessert, but the soft serve/gelato machine was broken and will continue to be out-of-service for the next few weeks, as of the time of this review). One of my favorite parts of this dining experience was getting to walk past the open kitchen, where a well-oiled machine of chefs are cutting out pasta shapes, stirring sauces, and making magic happen.

I wasn't huge on the fried cacio e pepe balls. Maybe it's just me, but I found it to taste vaguely reminiscent of the Trader Joe's mac and cheese balls...but the latter have a more exciting texture/richer flavor...

We were very lucky to get seating at this very popular Italian restaurant.

Food was AMAZING! There were no dishes that I didn't like or disappointed, this particular pasta "agnolotti" was beyond this world!!

Service was impeccable, we'll definitely be back!
(That's if we get lucky to get seating again. Lol)-
Yes: it's as good as everyone says! Went here for a special occasion and felt a higher level of detail to service versus a lot of other places. Loved the dishes and attention that Lilia provided!

TLDR: If you can get into Lilia do it!
Lilia has been on my New York wish list for 6-7 years. I looked at Resy on a Monday morning and sure enough, there was a 4:15 bar reservation for 2 available. My friend who I was visiting said sure, let's do it! We can be in Brooklyn early. Well we got a spot right across from it and walked in right at 4pm. We luckily got a table instead of bar seating.  Our server was great. Extremely knowledgeable about the menu. I'll go through everything we ate. Cacio e Pepe Fritelle: it was like a cheesy popover that got tossed in the fryer and rolled in pecorino cheese.  It was light and airy considering. Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga: it was my favorite of the three starters we had. The garlicky bread and creamy cheese are great on their own but they are complemented so perfectly by the acidic pop of lemon, the umami of the bottarga, and the most perfectly placed flakes of Maldon salt. It sounds so simple but it isn't. It's so good.  The third starter we had was the Grilled Artichoke, Garlic, Orange, Parmigiano, Breadcrumbs: again this was done perfectly and the meat of the artichoke was flavorful and tender. Obviously you're here for the pasta so we went with the Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano and the Sheep's Milk Cheese Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey.  Where do I even begin?  The mafaldini noodles were perfectly ruffled and cooked so they still had a nice chew. The pink peppercorns have a fruity flavor that was addictive and nice with the creamy cheese.   I was expecting the mafaldini to be the standout but for me it was the agnolotti. The dough was impossibly thin.  The sheep's milk cheese was light and creamy and the punch of the dried tomato and the sweetness of the honey was just delicious.  I would order this again and again. My dinner date gets to go back in a few weeks for another dinner.  I'm so jealous.  I'll be in Missouri dreaming about the pasta and this great meal I had at an impossible to get into restaurant in Brooklyn that most New Yorkers have not been to!

Went to Lilia for my birthday dinner and had an amazing time. The ambiance was great, dimly lit, very classy but cool vibes. I would definitely return for the agnolotti, and would recommend it to others looking for a nice night out! We had the following dishes-

Appetizers: (all so good, would recommend all)
-roasted squash- 8/10, on the oily side but very delicious 
-cabbage- 8/10, some ppl in my group liked this the best
-focaccia- 9/10, can't complain, super soft bread with a delicious green butter, we literally finished all of the butter 

Pastas:
Sheep milk cheese agnolotti- 10/10- MUST ORDER, still dreaming about this, so so good, mildly flavored but the cheese, honey, and pieces of tomatoes work so well together, this was everyone's favorite pasta
Gnocchi pesto- 8/10, very very delicious 
Rigatoni- with red sauce. 5/10, forgettable and would skip this 
Papparadelle with veal bolognese (seasonal): also 5/10 and pretty bland, would skip this 

Dessert- olive oil cake and Apple pastry dessert were also delicious!

I went to Lilia about a month ago with one of my friends. We were staying in Brooklyn and were very curious to try Lilia, given the hype and how difficult it is to make a reservation. 

Unable to make a reservation, we decided to try getting there ahead of time and waiting before the restaurant opened at 3:50. Despite it being extremely cold that day, there was already a line forming as we got there. Luckily for us, we were able to get seats at the bar. 

Since there was only the two of us, we couldn't order everything we wanted to and had to choose wisely. We ended up ordering the Cacio e Pepe Frittelle, mozzarella toast, mafaldini, agnolotti, and for dessert, the chocolate torta and apple crostada.

I would probably skip the mozzarella toast- it was good, but not outstanding and worth the price or stomach room (ha!). The fritelle were delicious, very rich and heavy, a bit too salty for my taste. 

The pastas were the star of the show. They were cooked perfectly and had unique tastes I haven't come across in traditional Italian restaurants. 

The desserts were amazing! The chocolate torta with espresso mousse was so tasty and the crostada was also very delicious. 

Truthfully, I'm not sure I would wait outside in the freezing cold to eat an early dinner here again- but I definitely want to come back and try more of the items on their menu!

I am not sure if it was the infatuation or all the reviews that got me so hyped up for this dinner. Sadly it was very over hyped and not worth the round trip uber ride. The snap peas were my favorite dish and the gelato was my second most memorable delight. All the other dishes didn't give me what I was expecting. I wouldn't recommend the shrimp as they were messy, hard to eat and not too appetizing. The vibe of the place was great but I really wished they weren't trying to be so cool, just order the Aperol.

Very impressed by this restaurant. 

My friend and I took a chance coming here since there are never reservations available. Luckily, they had two seats open for the night in their cafe area. Little bit of a wait, but when it was time to eat, we went all the way in. 

The focaccia was hands down incredible. Warm, flavorful, and perfect texture with every bite. 

Next we tried 3 pasta dishes. The Sheep's Milk Cheese Agnolotti melts in your mouth, by far the best of the dishes for the night. 

Rigatoni Diavola was a classic and the Ziti Genovese was so so good. We wanted to try more, but we were stuffed. 

The service was great with a friendly staff. Would highly recommend. For sure coming back!

It truly pains me to give Lilia a 3 star review because I had been looking forward to going there for years, but here we are. A friend and I were able to get in at the bar for dinner on a Monday night by using priority notify on resy. To say we were excited is an understatement. We arrived for our 6 pm reservation on time and were taken straight to our seats at the bar. We ordered many things to share because there was so much on the menu that we were interested in trying and we were in from out of town so we knew we wouldn't have the opportunity to come back any time soon. We shared the cacio e pepe frittelle, grilled artichoke, delicata squash, ricotta gnocchi, sheep's milk agnolotti, rigatoni diavola and the lemon granita. The only dish that blew me away was the delicata squash which I could have eaten several orders of, but all the the pasta seemed very one note and not very flavorful. I had read some reviews that the restaurant had been overhyped and unfortunately that ended up being the case for me. The pasta was so underwhelming that I wouldn't have taken any of it to go even if I hadn't been staying in a hotel.

I took forever to get to Lilia, and honestly considered if it was worth it given the mixed reviews. It sure seemed like the experience wasn't the same as a few years ago. With that in mind going into it, I think this spot is still worth the hype and does a very imaginative take on its dishes. 

The service and ambiance for me were mixed. The restaurant is beautiful and the service was overwhelmingly kind and accomodating. Our waiter was very helpful with food allergies and attentive throughout the night. They objectively let us overstay at the table chatting. Yet, the crowd here still sways towards folks taking photos of every course and carefully inspecting the dishware. It therefore feels a bit less cozy.

The food was rather well done in my opinion. The absolutely musts: grilled prawns, focaccia, and olive oil cake. I'd come back every week for these shrimp. I can't express how good the sauce was. I read a ton of reviews about this bread and was skeptical - but they hold true. There really is something special about it. The olive oil cake dessert was simply well executed. It was moist and layered with simple but precise flavors.

Yet what should have been the stars of the night, the pastas, weren't anything too crazy in my opinion. I think generally people overestimate how good a bowl of pasta can be. And these WERE good bowls of pasta. Just nothing worth shouting from the rooftops. We tried the spaghetti lemon, agnolotti, and mafaldini. The agnolotti took the cake, it was rich and creamy. Second fave was the spaghetti but it didn't feel like anything special. The infamous mafaldini was sadly too peppery for me. If you like strong pepper, you'll enjoy.

Oh how the mighty have fallen.  This was an easy 5-star restaurant a few years ago, but now it is uneven and mundane.  Missy needs to get back in the kitchen to remind the crew how to cook and season her dishes.

Great pasta and wonderful service! Me and my friend walked in on a Saturday for dinner and arrived at the restaurant little before 4pm, but there were several parties waiting in front of us! Thankfully, we were still able to get a spot at the bar. 

For starters, we ordered the Cacio e pepe frittelle and the Housemade mozzarella toast. They also gave us homemade potato chips to start which was nice! I liked whatever seasoning they added. As for the appetizers, both were good, but having just eaten at Misi, I definitely prefer their ricotta toast over Lilia's mozzarella toast. I felt like the mozzarella toast was a bit bland and the cacio e pepe frittelle were nicely fried but a tad too salty. I like cheese a lot, so I thought these fried balls of cheese were tasty, but I would not recommend these unless you are an avid cheese-lover. 

For mains, we ordered the Sheep's milk agnolotti and the Mafaldini with pink peppercorn. I am in love with the agnolotti (definitely better than Misi's sheep's milk pasta)! This was the highlight of the meal for me! This dish in general is a real standout from other pasta dishes with the addition of honey. I wish they added enough sun-dried tomatoes to eat one with each bite, but nonetheless, this may be my new favorite pasta dish (unfortunate because it is quite the trek to get here from NYC). The mafaldini was also really good, but is basically cacio e pepe with parmesan instead of pecorino and peppercorn instead of black pepper. Still good though. 

For dessert, we ordered the Apple crostata and the Chocolate torta. Both were superb! I am personally more partial to chocolate, so I preferred the chocolate torta, but the apple crostata was almost just as good! Neither was too sweet! I loved the addition of the coffee mousse with the chocolate cake, and the slight crunch the sugar on the crostata pastry added! 

Overall, I would highly recommend Lilia! However, I do think it is a bit overhyped as there are better Italian restaurants in NYC that aren't as hard to get a table at.

We spent a while trying to snag a spot at Lilia, and finally one day there was a spot. Unfortunately this spot was outside, and it was about 95ºF the day that we went. Fair warning that sitting outside it this sort of weather might have had an impact on my perception. We got arancini to share, and it fell a little flat in flavor or originality. Then we got the grilled artichoke, and it was my first time trying artichoke in that way. I thought it was good but honestly don't have a strong recollection. And then we each got our own pasta dish. He got the rigatoni which I enjoyed muchhhh more than mine. I got the sheep's milk agnolotti, which was very light in flavor. If you're looking for that, then this is perfect. I think I wanted something richer to distract me from the pain of sitting in the heat but otherwise it was delicious.
Delightful dining experience. Food delivered on all points. Far surpassed Misi! I think some of the reviews were off

It's now my favorite Italian restaurant in New York. The agnolotti was super delicious. The condition of the pasta was perfect, and the condiment and sauce were also perfect. I loved the combination of saffron and honey.
My second favorite was the dessert - Italian job. But last time I visited, I think they may accidentally put too much salt. Next time I am going to ask for no salt added.
Some dished I really enjoyed was the Grilled lamb leg steak and the grilled bass. They are cooked perfectly.
But I don't like the salad. The dressing was too sour.
And the service was nice as well.

We arrived here without a reservation but still managed to get bar seating in the back of the restaurant by their coffee machine. We had the artichoke appetizer and two pasta dishes, agnolotti and casunzei. the food was all quite good and the service was excellent, down to the details of properly cleaning the table between courses. Although the ambiance in this part of the house was not great, we still enjoyed the meal. Excellent grappa selection.

This place lives up to its reputation of being incredible. The hype is real and it's worth it to even go if it's a late reservation. We thankfully sat inside, especially thankful after hearing that it's a wind tunnel outside. The ambiance is so lovely. I watched TikToks and was told to get the focaccia, sheep's milk pasta, and malfadini pasta. We got those three items, along with the garlic bread with mozzarella, prawns, and lamb ragu pasta. The malfadini wasn't special or anything good, if i were to return i would not order that again. The sheep's milk and lamb ragu were out of this world. THE FOCCACIA WITH THE GREEN BUTTER stole my heart. I'd go back for just that. The prawns were also incredible minus removing the heads yourself. 10/10 would recommend this place.

I visited Lilia for a birthday dinner for my cousin and wow, what an experience! The servers, staff, and sommelier were fantastic. The restaurant was bigger than we all expected, with high ceilings, and a very industrial meets modern Italy vibe. We started with a great bottle of red, and our server offered non-alcoholic beverage options for our friend doing Dry January. I found that to be incredibly thoughtful and considerate in today's climate. Our friend ended up getting the lemonade and said it was delicious! We followed some of The Infatuation's recommendations and they did not disappoint. Our entire party was a group of foodies, so we chose to share everything, but you can easily order your own plates as well. 

For appetizers, we enjoyed the Grilled Clams, Little Gem Salad, Focaccia, and Cacio e Pepe Frittelles. The salad was refreshing, but we all agreed it was a bit biting from the vinegar and while we enjoyed a few bites, we weren't sure if we'd be able to have an entire plate of it. 

For dinner we had the malfadini (different and delicious from the pink peppercorn), Sheep's Milk Cheese Agnolotti (you MUST order this! By far the favorite pasta of the night), Rigatoni Diavola (enjoyable, but I'd have to be in the mood to order it again), and Fettucine with Lamb Sausage (tasty, but very gamey so make sure you like lamb if you're ordering it). 

For dessert we were disappointed to find out the gelato machine was broken, so we'll have to go back to try again. We did have the olive oil cake though and it was light, moist, and flavorful. 

It's no surprise you still can't get in here. Highly recommend for a great meal in Williamsburg!

Honestly SO disappointed. Was so excited to finally go here and left feeling like what was the point. I've gone to so many other places in this area that were far better. My pasta and everyone I was with's pasta was COLD. Pasta was also so bland. The whole restaurant was so cold the whole time we were there. They did not have any of the food we were excited about from their instagram. Was so excited to go there with friends and make it this big night and walked away feeling like I will never recommend it to anyone. Such a waste.

We were so looking forward to trying this place. We got a last minute reservation and jumped at the opportunity but, unfortunately, it did not live up to the hype. We ordered 4 pastas and they were all cold. The bread & cabbage were amazing, but the dishes we were looking forward to the most were a disappointment. :(

It was just OK.... Misi was way better.

It was worth going once but I'm not sure I'll be back. The dishes weren't too special, feels like I can get them anywhere.

We ordered a bunch off the menu.

The focaccia bread was just a fancy garlic bread. It was good because you can never go wrong with garlic bread but I really wanted all the flavor focaccia really brings so that was a little disappointing.

The homemade mozzarella was just mozz on top of bread, nothing fancy about it.

The prosciutto was ok... the parmigiano butter that came with it was tasty.

The little gem lettuce was way too sour from the vinaigrette - nothing special about this dish, can probably skip.

The guanciale was nothing special. Very thin and not packed with much flavors.

Maybe we just managed to pick all the spicier ones but everything had such a kick to it, wasn't too appealing. Tasted like all the same spice and seasoning - the shrimp and the clams. The scallop was very soft and delicate but the yoghurt made it weird.

Rigatoni felt undercooked and it started out great but got way too spicy towards the end of the bowl. Sheeps Milk Cheese was a good balance. The fettuccine wasn't really anything special - you can skip this for sure.

Service was very attentive which we definitely appreciated. We arrived for our 7pm reservation and got seated right away.

Overall, i think a little too hyped. Food was good but not amazing.

probably one of my all time favorite dining experiences in all of NYC. EXCEPTIONAL food and pasta. the lemon ricotta pasta was unbelievable. we still talk about that dish. will be coming back many more times!
Comida maravilhosa, atendimento perfeito. Um dos melhores lugares em que comi. Voltarei com certeza

The reservations here are so difficult to get but I randomly checked the site and saw an 8:30pm reservation for grabs. The food is good and enjoyable but I definitely would not wait a while to eat here. Here's what we got:

- Sheep's Milk Agnolotti: super creamy and rich filling and the pasta was chewy on the outside
- Focaccia with green garlic butter: had a great crunch and the green garlic butter had an herby taste
- Grilled Clams: a bit too tart for me but the clams had a nice chewy texture 
- Sea Bass: great char and the bass was cooked perfectly tender

Overall worth a try if you're able to get a table!

Lilia offers wood-fried seafood and handcrafted pastas in the Williamsburg 'hood.

We were recommended to this eatery by a friend, so we were curious in checking them out for dinner.

The menu is split into cocktail snacks, antipasti, little/big fish entrees, and meat entrees.  We started off with the housemade mozzarella that was served with toasted garlic bread, lemon, and bottarga (this was a good starter), and the foccacia that was served with roasted leeks and green garlic butter (this was a favorite of my dining partner).  We also added the grilled artichoke that was prepared with garlic, oranges, Parm, and breadcrumbs (this was crispy).

For our shareable entrees, we tried the black bass with salsa verde and coal-roasted Yukon gold potatoes (this was an underwhelming dish; the bass was a bit overcooked) and the rigatoni diavola that was prepared with San Marzano tomatoes, chili, oregano, and pecorino (cooked al dente, but we weren't fans of the sauce and how it tasted).

Service was friendly, but more on the absent-minded; we had to repeat some of our requests multiple times.

+bread apps are decent
+absentminded staff
