The restaurant itself is beautiful with the open kitchen concept, and sitting at the bar and watching everything unfold was super fun! 

The standout dishes were definitely the focaccia and the ice cream w/ olive oil and honey. I would come back solely for those two to be honest. I also got the malfaldini and sheep's milk cheese agnolotti which were both cooked to perfection. The lamb leg steak was delicious too, and the portion was quiet bigger than expected! However, other than the focaccia and ice cream, nothing really 'blew me away', but everything was executed to perfection. Recommend coming here for a cute and cozy date night!

I have to be honest, I was expecting a lot more from Lilia based on all the hype it has received and it comes down to the pasta dishes being a failure in my eyes. I dined here on a Wednesday night as a party of two and we ordered the beloved mafaldini and the Ziti Genovese. The mafaldini was very al dente to a point it was not properly boiled and while the ziti was a bit softer texture wise, both pastas were lack luster and had no richness you would anticipate with a pasta dish. Not sure if it was a bad batch and we were unlucky, but I would not come back here to try either of those dishes again. 
Now, onto what I do like and what was the saving grace of this experience: the ambiance, location and aesthetic were very comforting. The BREAD!!! Whatever you do order the Focaccia it is a must and I would definitely come back for this bread and green garlic butter. The grilled clams were also a nice bite in addition to the olive oil cake. 
Service was also pleasant, however the staff forgot to give us out to go bags and we had to go back once we noticed. 
If I was to dine back at Lilia, I would try the sheep's milk agnolotti to give the pasta a second try before I rule it out completely.

Oh my goodness,

This place is truly incredible. 

Came here on a Friday night with my partner for a reservation for 2 at the bar. Got the reservation for same day by stopping by earlier which was a nice surprise :) 

We got 3 pastas to share and it was a good portion size for us. We left feeling full and satisfied! 

The ricotta gnocchi was honestly life changing. It was savory, sweet, perfectly textured and one of the best pastas that I have ever tried! I'm so glad we got that one.

The agnolotti was also amazing! The saffron inside and the flavors were so well balanced it was hard to describe how it tasted. Must try this one! 

The mafaldini was yummy but felt it was slightly lacking in flavor. It tasted like an elevated cacio e Pepe. Tasty but nothing crazy! the texture of the pasta was delicious and fun to eat with the long noodles.

We also got the lemon ice for dessert which was well textured and super sour! I'm not a huge fan of ice but I still enjoyed eating this. 

Overall, an amazing date night dinner spot :)

First this is a very hard place to get a reservation for unless you actually live in the neighborhood 
My wife randomly called & got a real live person & we got a 7:00 pm reservation 
Very excited!'
We got there packed as can be 
Nice atmosphere it was a garage at one time 
We got seated ordered an espresso martini & a Italian lemon drink both delish 
Our Server Eddie very nice walked us thru the menu 
We ordered the focaccia with the green butter 10/10
The mozzarella on toast 10/10
The Shrimp 100/100 the sauce I could have swam in ask for bread to soak it up
Pastas we shared 
Agnolotti  10/10 sheep's milk cheee bit sweet like pillows in your mouth
Gnocchi with pesto & nuts & basil 10/10 great flavor
Malfadini 4/10 the pasta was gooey & not much sauce but the flavor was there 
Then we got the 
Lamb Steak with Fennel
OMG 20/20
The seasoning on point the fennel nice touch 
The portion HUGE!!!
We barley ate this took a lot home 
& ended with Olive Cake 10/10 which was moist & flavorful.
Over all we booked it again for next month & would try other things off the menu 
But the shrimp & Agnolotti will always order
Bill was over $250 but worth it. 
It was truly an experience

Unfortunately this place was not impressive, especially for how difficult it was to get a reservation. Very nice ambiance. When we got seated we bunched our coats next to us in the booth which did take up a lot of room but when the next table was sat they were offered coat check-weird. The service was stuffy- no one smiles, replies when you say thank you, or checks in on you. We started off with little gem salad, tasty nothing exceptional.
The focaccia with green garlic butter was the star, that bread was amazing fluffy with crunchy crust hint of leek on top. The clams were terrible, overcooked and chewy and just tasted like salt would definitely skip. We each ate one and put it to the side. It sat there until our last course without any inquiry from our server and even more odd because they clear and refresh your plate/silverware between each course. The grilled scallops were cooked well but smothered in the yogurt sauce which was somewhat overpowering. Lastly we got the Mafaldini which I had been very excited to try. We did wait a while for it to come out. The pasta was cooked al dente which I enjoyed but it came out lukewarm in a piping hot bowl as if it was sitting under a heat lamp! Honestly I expected so much more from this place with all the hype and have had way better Italian in NY.
Impossible to get in, but when you do it's totally worth the hours refreshing Resy...........
Fantastic spot for that special dinner with family, friends or partners.  Always beautiful during the holidays.

FINALLY got to check this one off the list. Reservations are near-impossible to get; while walk-ins are definitely doable, I snagged a last minute reservation here with the help of Beli and had a great experience. Amazing food and ambiance at a relatively affordable price point. 

Two of us got the grilled clams, sheep's milk agnolotti, and the pink peppercorn mafaldine to share. The sheep's milk agnolotti was incredibly rich and indulgent--pillowy, creamy, melt in your mouth goodness that evoked a visceral response, but also maybe there can be too much of a good thing because we both were starting to get tired of it by the end. On the other hand, I initially found the peppercorns in the mafaldine jarring and obtrusive, but after the meal the unique flavor and the chewy, al-dente texture of the noodle was what stuck out to me most. The grilled clams were also quite good and a very generous serving. I'd say both pastas are a must-try for first-timers, but the only dish I'd reorder on my next visit would be the mafaldine. 

Our meal in total was just under $100, which was less than I expected considering the food quality and ambiance. Shoutout to their beautiful dishware as well!

I really try to love this place, but after my third visit I can't say I'm impressed. The venue is gorgeous, the service is good, but the food is just so average. I wouldn't even put this in my top 10 favorite Italian spots in the city. 

The mussels are the best I've ever had, I will give them that. The pastas just aren't it. The spaghetti with pine nuts is WAY too lemon-y, it's overpowering and unpleasant. The fettuccini with lamb sausage is fine, just nothing special. 

It's a cool spot, the food isn't BAD by any means, but I think I'm going to have to accept that I'll never understand the rave reviews.

5 stars for service
4 stars for ambiance
3.5 stars for food 

We came across this place several times and always found a line. The bf said that it took him a month to make reservations. I understand why it's packed as their food is freshly prepared and it's a different style food. The ambiance was nice but I didn't care for the table setup as the neighbor table was too closely setup where you can hear their conversations. 

Food was mediocre. The clams had nice seasoning but way too overcooked that it was too chewy. The goat cheese pasta flavor was lovely. The other pasta dish was bland in flavor. Started cacio peppe was too salty, properly too much cheese around it. Dessert was lovely, warm apple pie with sour cream on top. Was looking forward to gelato but their machine broke.

The wine connoisseur was patient with us with great recommendations. Service was amazing, constant plate and utensil changing and refill of water.

Finally snagged a pretty prime time reservation in Lilia. Was shocked at how little seating there was inside - really gave perspective on why getting a reservation here was difficult.

Personally, loved the foccacia bread the most. Delicious and the generous serving of butter really upped the flavor. 

Got the grilled scallops, mafaldini, and agnolotti. All were delicious and definitely preferred the mafaldini more, but having both did help in being able to try more flavors. Scallops are just what I would expect from a restaurant of this caliber - well done but not wowed.

Personally would recommend coming for their togo side, where it is a lot easier to get a sandwich and pastries to go and with less hassle.

Amazing Italian food. Came here on a Sunday night with 2 friends. The restaurant itself is very cute and well decorated. The wait staff was attentive and gave great recommendations. For our starters, we had the housemade mozzerella and the clams. The mozzarella, which came on a perfectly crispy but not too crispy garlic bread, was fresh and had delicious topping that rounded out the dish perfectly. I had never had clams directly out of a shell before, but loved these ones! They were tender and perfectly seasoned. I couldn't get enough. For our main, I split the ziti with brisket and the agnolotti with my friend. The ziti came with parmesan on top and at first we were worried they had forgotten the brisket, but found it at the bottom of the dish though there wasn't a ton of it. Nevertheless, the pasta was perfectly al dente and was so scrumptious. The agnolotti was good, but I found the ratio of filling to pasta to be slightly off (though I think this is more feature of agnolotti rather than how the dish was prepared). It was still seasoned very well and was enjoyable. My friend had the squash as her main, of which I had a few bite, and I loved this as well. The walnut parsley pesto was so flavorful and the crunch of the walnut was a great contrast to the softness of the squash. Overall, I loved the food here and would definitely come back!
Hard to get reservations, but worth it. The food is delicious and service was excellent

Really enjoyed my meal here. The food is delicious and well balanced flavors. The focaccia with green garlic butter-- loved that butter. I wanted to take it home. I couldn't get enough of the prawns with fennel pollen. Well balanced flavors. The star of the night was the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti. They mastered that dish. I would come here just for that. The portion is good for one person. We had another pasta which I can't remember what it's called but was delicious as well. Let's not forget the Italian job as dessert. Decadent. Trust me it lived up to the hype. I would recommend coming here. Service was good, nothing special to acknowledge there. They rush you a little which I don't like so that's why I knocked off a star. Worth going to if you can get a reservation.

Service and ambiance were great here but for how difficult it is to get a reservation + price, the stars rounded down from 4 to 3. Food was good but nothing so special that Wow'd me. 

The best dish I had was probably the cacio e Pepe fritelle

Multiple disappointing experiences here... The first time we got baked clams, focaccia with garlic butter, the most famous mafaldini, spaghetti with lemon, and fettucine with lamb sausage. The only thing that didn't disappoint was the focaccia, everything else was extremely salty, also dishes were served in a really small portion? absolutely not worth for the price. the mafaldini is the most trendy / famous dish at lilia, yet it tastes like the chef didn't know the difference between al dente vs. HARD pasta. I decided to give it a 2nd try and come back, this time we got grilled prawns, rigatoni, ricotta gnocchi, and ragu, and since I liked the focaccia last time, we got that again. EVERYTHING tastes like a CHUNK of salt, no other flavors, just salt. It was absolutely bizarre. The rigatoni tastes disgusting, the gnocchi was decent but if you're counting on a vegetarian dish, there's something wrong, and the focaccia that impressed me last time? absolutely horrible, tastes like bread and salt. 

Now onto service, service was just okay - nothing impressive, but nothing terrible either.

Ambiance - it was cute inside, but again, I waited an entire year to get these 2 reservations. Lilia is known to be one of the most popular restaurants in NY... WHY??? Not impressed at all.

Overall, 1/10 recommendation of coming here.

Before they got too famous and it was easier to get a table I managed to snag a few bites on my hand full of visits.

Although the appetizers can be a bit on the bland side everything else makes up for that. On a second to last visit (during covid) I ate outside (pre-tents:) and had the most amazingly tender lamb through my chattering teeth. I've never ate so fast in my life and I wish I could have savored the meal more. Dining out in the cold is a definitely pass:). If that meal wasn't demanding my first born I'd have gladly eaten another.

During my most recent visit I had a bland super raw scallop but luckily we knew the appetizer may be a let down so we bounced back into it with our mains. The sardine appetizer was excellent however if they would later the pound of butter vertically opposed to horizontally you'd get some in every bit and not lobbing it onto your plate (and less oil to let the fish shine:). For mains my partner, who likes simpler pastas, got the mafaldini and expressed in every way possible how divine it was. The Ziti one me over. Although I would have loved more meat it was absolutely positively scrumptious and evenly hot. The ratio was 80%cheese 19% pasta and 1% meat. But again still deliciously flavored.

Overall leave room in your bellies and wallets for their superb vanilla gelato (with oo and fennel).

I really loved Misi so I was very excited to come and try Lilia. 

Let's start with the vibe and energy of this place. It's very simplistic but has a buzz in the dining room. Very sexy, clean and perfect for date night. I also loved that they have a side waiting room that has coffee and drinks while you wait.

The service was awesome. Very on top of making sure our wine was full (we bought a bottle) and checked in on us the perfect amount.

Ok, onto the food:

- Little Gem salad: this was delicious for just a simple salad. It felt like every little leafy green was coasted just enough in their delicious vinaigrette. It was also the perfect start to our meal.

- Sheep's Milk Agnolotti: a must. The first bite was magical, I looked at my date with wide eyes and said drop what your doing and taste this. The perfect balance of savory, sweet, slightly acidic and just enough tang. It was *chefs kiss*

- Lamb: we enjoyed this but we had to ask for more sauce as it was just a tad dry. It was good, but I won't dream about this.

- sparkling Chardonnay ($55): this was super light and refreshing and it went well with all of our food.

If I were to go back, I'd definitely need to dig into some of their other pastas and I'm eyeballing that focaccia.

I'm not sure who wins over Misi/Lilia but I'm super glad I've now been to both. Delicious, bucket list worthy restaurants.

4.7/5

My celebratory meal moving into the city. My first intro to Missy Robbins orchestration of beauty: beautiful space, beautiful plates, beautiful pastas.

Little gem lettuce and house made mozzarella to start and mafaldini and agnolotti to fill our bellies. Personally, the stars of our meal were the mozz & mafaldini. Both extremely fresh but in different ways, simple also in different ways. You have the mozz -- tender, milky, oozing and goozing in the best ways. The taste is amplified by the bottarga, it's heavenly. On the other hand, you have the mafaldini which is like an elevated caccio pepe moment.

Do not skip out on dessert. The Italian Job is everything. Not to mention, we came to celebrate my partner's birthday and got a cute little candle!

Finally had a chance to visit this infamous Italian spot in Brooklyn. The pastas are fresh, the portion size is quiet small though, price is more on the expensive side when compared to the serving size.

We ordered the following:

-Artichoke: crispy and salty in a good way
-Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti with Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey: my fave - sweet and rich in taste.
-Ricotta Gnocchi with Broccoli Pesto, Pecorino, Pistachios: nutty but a bit bland, personally would pass on this item and try something else.
-Fettuccine with Lamb Sausage, Tomato Passato, Lemon, Pecorino: flavor is robust and hits the spot on a cold day.

This is probably the most overrated place I've been to. Firstly, I love misi. The cacio e pepe fritters were glorified Mac n cheese balls that were so over salted we couldn't finish it. The clams were good but over cooked and there's no complaints with the artichoke. For pastas we got the sheep's milk agnolotti and another one I don't remember the name of. Neither left an impression and neither were finished.
It's one of the great restaurant in Williamsburg. The foods are great and the service is excellent.

Service 3/5: a little condescending about food allergies 

Food: all of the snacks it seemed were with bread, very generous with dairy - abnormal amount of cheese, butter, and butter ratio on our "snacks" portion of the menu, would highly recommend getting the focaccia, and the prosciutto/mustard, agnolotti, cappelletti (seasonal)

Drinks: Rosemary spritz if you want a mocktail is good, espresso martini (7/10) 

The hype is almost real. Would we go back yes, if suggested.

My friend and I came here for dinner the other night as I was able to finally secure a reservation. We were seated right away and our waitress was excellent at walking us through the menu and giving suggestions. For drinks, I ordered the non-alcoholic raspberry spritz and my friend ordered a glass of white wine, which she really enjoyed. For dinner, we ordered a number of items starting with the focaccia bread with the green garlic butter, and it was divine.

For our entrees, we ordered a number of items, all to share, including the little gem lettuce, the grilled prawns and the grilled scallops, all of which were excellent. For our pasta dishes, we ordered the spaghetti which was recommended as one of the favorite dishes, and it had so much flavor. We also ordered the ricotta gnocchi and it was so delicious. 

We couldn't leave without trying a dessert or two, and we shared the chocolate cake, which was so light and not dense at all, as well as the apple tart which was absolutely delicious. 

The ambiance is perfect for a date or catching up with a good friend--the restaurant has huge windows that let in a ton of light, but as the night went on, the lights came down and the dining room was illuminated by candlelight. I would absolutely come back here again! Highly recommended.

Really beautiful view and a nice rooftop bar. The drinks were expensive but typical nyc prices. The bartenders were friendly and efficient. I was here for a chaotic singles party, this venue does a lot of events.
As pretentious as they come. No food is worth this attitude. Don't waste your time, energy or money.

More of a 3.5 for me. Slightly disappointed because of all of the overhype and high praise for Lilia, plus how hard it is to get a reservation. I think that Misi is much better then Lilia. 

~ Homemade Mozzarella w/ toasted garlic bread (3/5) ~
Underwhelming dish. This is a pretty bland Mozzarella,  the flavour mostly came from the lemon. The menu says there are Bottarga, probably referring to the shavings on top, but it doesn't really add much flavour except perhaps some saltiness. Not very creamy either. Whilst eating I keep thinking if only I can get my hands on some burrata..... or Misi's fluffy whipped ricotta! The garlic bread... is not really a garlic bread, doesn't taste very garlicky. The toasted sesame on the crust is very good though, brings a lot of flavour to the dish! 

~ Roasted Leek Focaccia w/ green garlic butter (3.5/5) ~
The focaccia is a bit dry, but the green garlic butter compensates for it, giving it a nice kick of garlicky buttery flavour. Texture wise, it's a bit more crumbly and less chewy then a classic focaccia. It's lacking in the roasted leek flavour, you only get it when your bite have the roasted leek on top, and you don't get that every bite, so I wish there are more leek!!

~ Bagna Cauda (1/5) ~
I'm sorry we hated this dish, had it returned. When we ask if we can return it, the server looked unhappy and ask us a bunch of questions as to why we want to return it, why we don't like it. Even had to go to the manager to ask if they allow returns. I have returned dishes that I don't enjoy in the past, and it's the first time I'm treated this way, given this is an upscale establishment. 
Whilst the menu said roasted and raw vegetables, 90% of them are raw and I hate raw cauliflower, broccoli and radishes. Only the red pepper and onion are grilled. The sauce that comes with it, whilst menu say it's consist of garlic and anchovy, it's also very sharp and tangy, not much garlic taste. It tastes weird to us. I guess people who like raw vegetables would probably enjoy this dish, don't mind me this is a personal preference. Plus, I'm not paying $21 for a dish that barely involve "cooking" skills lol 

~ Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti (4/5) ~
Filling is incredibly creamy and smooth, the agnolotti has the right thickness and al dnte. It's paired with a honey sauce that's a bit too sweet for me, I prefer my pasta to be more on the savoury side. Nonetheless it tasted pretty interesting, and I still really enjoyed it.

~ Mafaldini (4.5/5) ~
Ok this is my favourite dish of the night! The Mafaldini is perfectly chewy, slightly on the thicker side but I love it. The sauce with pink peppercorn and parmigiano is very creamy and thick, so it hang nicely on the mafaldini. It's my first time having pink peppercorn, I really love the flavour! It's similar to black peppercorn but not as strong, it's more bright and fruity, providing a different kind of heat that is really pleasant to taste. It also kinda reminds me of Sichuan peppercorn (花椒) but not as spicy and numbing. It is quite heavy though, 1 person couldn't possibly finish this dish, glad we are sharing!

Will I be back? Maybe
It's a nice meal but nothing extraordinary. Whilst the pasta dishes are pretty good, it doesn't give me the strong urge to come back. And the antipasti are a bit disappointing. With this price, I'd expect something more exciting. The server is not very attentive too.

Lilia had been on my list for so long and I was so excited when I snagged a last minute cancellation on Resy. The Foccacia was good - perfectly crispy on the outside and soft and fluffy on the inside. I did feel like the bread to butter ratio was off, so we had to order extra bread on the side to scoop up the rest of the butter. The Clams were pretty good, but I don't think I'd get again. The Malfadini was covered with peppercorn and pretty good the first few bites, but then the peppery flavor was a bit too overpowering for my liking. The absolute showstopper was the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti. Absolutely amazing. I loved how the saffron flavors complemented the creamy cheese filling so well. I'd be back just for that. YUM.

Amazing everything. Favorites were the two pastas: mafaldini and agnolotti. Little gem salad was bright and delightful, balanced by the rich creaminess inside the cacio e pepe fritelles. I think our favorite app was the grilled clams topped with calabrian chilis. But really every dish was delicious. Great cocktails here and the vanilla soft serve gelato with honey, sea salt, olive oil finished the meal perfectly. Service was fine and ambiance was very nice even on a rainy night. New favorite elevated Italian restaurant for date nights!

I'm in love with this restaurant. In my opinion the food is really good, service is great, and I love the chill vibes. Definitely recommend this place 100% . One of the few restaurants in NYC that are worth the hyped.

I was highly disappointed with my entire birthday celebration at Lilia in Brooklyn. I have been trying to get a reservation there forever and when the reservation ON my birthday opened up, I jumped at the chance!  My friend and I arrived 20 minutes before our reservation, and we were informed to sit in the back bar and to order drinks until our table was ready at 8:45pm. At 8:20, a waitress took our drink orders but never returned with them, even after reminding her. Once we're seated at our table, we informed our waiter that we were still waiting on our drinks. 15 minutes later and our drinks have still not arrived at our table, but the people next to us who sat down after us had just been brought their beverages. I understand restaurants are busy, but this was a poor start to the night. Nonetheless, I still had high hopes for the pasta. The food came, and unfortunately, the only delicious thing we agreed on was the squash appetizer. Everything else tasted good, but it was not nearly as good as the accolades or reviews it receives. After we finished our meals, the waiter kindly asked if we were ready for our check. I asked if we could first see a dessert menu, and informed her that it was my birthday. She understood and we had good olive oil cake with a candle. My friend and I both left disappointed, but lucky for me, we still managed to have fun together, despite our negative experience here.

I visited Lilia a few months ago and I'm still dreaming about the Saffron Sheep's Milk Agnolotti. I've been to many of the popular Italian restaurants in the city and this pasta dish definitely stands out as the most flavorful. The agnolotti is filled with a rich cream that pairs perfectly with the saffron and honey drizzle. In addition to the agnolotti, the focaccia bread with green garlic butter is a must!

Lilia is spacious and the interior is bright and airy. I did an early walk-in on a Sunday evening and secured bar seats with no wait. I've also heard that you can make reservations by phone.

I highly recommend checking out Lilia if you're looking for amazing Italian food!

Super yummy dishes here! We went right at opening on a Sunday and were able to be seated right away. Service was attentive and there was a great wine list.

We started with the foccacia and tomato salad. The bread was a bit too oily for me but very moist and pillowy. Salad was a great summer starter, very refreshing. For pastas, we got the pink peppercorn mafaldini and pesto riccota gnocchi. The mafaldini was delicious and unique! The pepper does a great got of cutting the creamy sauce. The gnocchi was also amazing, I loved the addition of pistachios. Dessert was also a star, the raspberry tart was the perfect balance of sweet and tart. 

Ambiance was also really great, nice clean energy to the place. Would definitely come back!

The ultimate question, is Lilia worth the hype? Short answer - almost, yes. Long answer below. And for those who don't want to read, still go. 

Lilia is set in an old car garage and you can still see a lot of that structure in place and in the layout. It lends itself to making Lilia a very casual affair, a friendly neighborhood restaurant that also puts out amazing dishes. And that is part of the charm of Lilia, its welcoming, open and buzzing. None of the stuffiness that comes with a lot of popular and famous Italian spots. 

The food, without questions is very fresh and well made. Some dishes I preferred more than other but everything was quite authentic without the flare. Started off with the Focaccia and it was, chefs kiss, highly recommend it. Especially with their house made green garlic butter. We also had the Artichoke to start and though it was a popular dish, it wasn't really my favorite. Scrapping off bits from artichoke leaves just wasn't filling nor that appetizing with all the flavor coming from the cheese. 

From the pastas, we enjoyed the Ravioli and Spaghetti, and the Mafaldini was okay. All of them were extremely fresh and well made but everyone has their own pasta preferences so I won't say much here. I didn't like the Mafaldini as much due to it being so heavy but the Ravioli with the tomatoes was so good! 

Service is great, friendly and attentive, couldn't ask for more. Drinks are great as well and they have a vast selection of great wines as well. 

Are there better Italian spots? Yes but not many. This is definitely one of the best in the city hands down. At the level Lilia is at, it just comes down to personal preference. The hype is understandable and you should still go, but I wouldn't crown Lilia the best there is.

What a meal! Everything tasted better than the last and I'm still dreaming of the anchovy garlic dipping sauce for the bagna cauda. I want to try everything on the menu but it's going to be hard not to order everything we did last time. We definitely over ordered for two but we felt so lucky to snag a table that we wanted to try just about everything. Everyone was so friendly and making sure we were comfortable and taken care of. I can't wait to come back!

Lilia's hype is probably unmatchable. Is it a great dinner, yes? Was it the best? Read on. 

Without a doubt the place is gorgeous. Had it not been in the dead of summer I would have enjoyed sitting outside. The service impeccable. The drinks, delicious. My only quarrel is with one food item. 

The drink menu has a wide array of options. They have some pretty exclusive beers that's I love. Even a Goose Island. The cocktails were made to perfection. And the wine list is expansive with tons to choose from. 

I guess I have to start with what I got first and was the most disappointing. The famous cacio e pepe bites. I heard people swearing by these. I was so excited to try them. Overly fried and was too dense. It's richness was overwhelming. I did not care for them at all. Then came the fried clams and scallops, Phenomenal! The fettuccini in lamb sausage was awesome. 

In the end, you should make the voyage here and be a judge for yourself. I think it's a great experience, but not sure it's worth the hype. If you want, make sure you're on Resy at 10 am, exactly four weeks prior.

One of the hardest reservations to get in NYC! Needless to say, I was very excited to finally get the chance to dine at Lilia. It lives up to the hype. 

Everything on the menu was fantastic. I went with a group of 4 which I thought was great to be able to try a ton of things. We started off with the green garlic butter with focaccia, artichokes, Cacio e Pepe fritters, grilled clams, and gem salad. The garlic butter with focaccia and grilled clams were my favorites. As for pasta, we got the Malfadini, agnolotti, rigatoni, and corn capletti. The agnolotti is the star here for a reason. Very smooth and creamy. Also loved the capletti and malfadini with peppercorns. The lamb steak is a gem on the menu! It was a huge highlight and so unique with the flavors. 

We had the Italian sundae and olive oil cake which turned out to be a wonderful pairing together! Fantastic wine selection, food, and ambiance. What more can you ask for?

If you can't get a reservation, you can walk in and they'll most likely be able to seat you at the bar.

We sat at the bar and the bartenders were incredibly friendly! They let us taste a few of the wines before we chose - we got a chilled wine along with a Sangiovese. 

Would skip on the grilled clams - they weren't that tasty and cooked a little too much. The agnolotti was so good and the sauce it came with was DELICIOUS. The rigatoni was good but a little too al dente. 

Would definitely recommend this spot if you're in the area!
Fresh pasta and flavorful ingredients. Our waitress was super attentive and gave great recs. Good service and cute restaurant ambiance

I came here on a Friday night for dinner with two friends. I honestly had never heard of this restaurant, but apparently it's extremely popular. We sat outside, which I'm not really a fan of; would love to try this place again indoors. 

We got a bunch of dishes to share: the prawns, Grilled Clams, Mafaldini, Cheese Filled Agnolotti, ravioli, Little Gem Lettuce salad, Whole Artichoke, Olive Oil Cake and the Italian Job Gelato. All of the pastas were superb; perfectly cooked and the sauces they came with were perfectly balanced. The portions were also decent; I feel like most nice Italian restaurants don't provide healthy portions for the price, and I can't say Lilia is drastically different, but you won't leave hungry. For the antipasti, I wasn't a big fan of the artichoke or the grilled clams. There wasn't a ton of flavor there and with the artichoke, it just seemed like I was eating a ton of sauce and cheese. The rest of the antipasti was fantastic, though. I thought the deserts we ordered were just OK; definitely could have skipped them. 

Overall, I think this is a solid restaurant and I would love to come back again.

FINALLY got a reservation here last minute on a Friday! Such a cute spot with indoor and outdoor seating. We started out with 2 great spritz drinks, and focaccia for a starter. The focaccia was INCREDIBLE. Must try.
Pasta: the sheep's milk angolotti is too sweet for a pasta in my opinion. We loved the spaghetti which had pine nuts and a hint of lemon. 
We were pretty full at this point but the lamb leg was the last thing we tried. Super flavorful but a tad too salty. You could tell the meat was fresh though!
@global_grubs
terrible service the waiters are not friendly I will not recommend this place to anyone the first time such a terrible attitude towards visitors

I've been able to dine here twice and genuinely think the pasta is very well done. The ambiance is beautiful and each dish is absolutely picturesque. That being said, I wouldn't line up at 4 to get a seat here... the hype does make it taste better lol but I don't think any dish is particularly expectional, with the exception of the garlic scape foccacia that I do think is one of a kind... A must try if you go

It was alright. The most exciting part of the meal with the focaccia and the olive oil dessert. I did enjoy the sheep's milk pasta! I was not a fan of the malfadini. The flavors just were bland and not doing it for me.

Why people live this place, I personally won't understand. Overall I thought the staff wasn't very accommodating, the food was fine (my pasta was too oily), and overpriced for the portion size.

I was really looking forward to coming here and they ran out of bread at 7pm on a Saturday, which is what I was super excited to try. That just feels like poor planning to me.

Next, the staff wasn't super attentive to us. They also wouldn't let us order appetizers until we had our entrees figured out. I don't understand why that's a big deal if we are hungry and want to order appetizers immediately.

Now, the food was just OK. 

I got the spaghetti and it was overly oily. I also got the clams and they didn't taste very fresh and were just too expensive for what they were. I also didn't like the taste.

The best thing here is the dessert. The strawberry tart and olive oil cake were both scrumptious.

My niece recommended to take a friend of mine visiting NYC to Lilia in Brooklyn. She said you need reservations, books sometimes a month in advance. Chef Lilia cooks the food! Tons of people she said raves about the quality of food. 
She was there with a friend of mine who was visiting. Based on what they said, it's very good. Only small portions for the prices they ask. She did say it tastes very good. Limited parking, as it is located in the local community. Reservations recommended.

I was hoping this place would live up to the hype, but I was disappointed. I waited over a month for a reservation and the food/ambiance was meh. The air condition was barely working and all the servers were drenched in sweat, along with US, the customers.
Wouldn't recommend.

We enjoyed everything, but the sheep's milk agnolotti was the crowd favorite. While the cucumber salad, prawns, and mussels were all yummy, we'd opt to try other items next time. However, we'd order the agnolotti every time it's just that special!

Love the caffe and they have my favorite G&T here but not a huge fan of the hype surrounding the restaurant after trying a bunch of the pastas. The pasta portions are small, they're expensive, and they're hit or miss. We were blown away by the ravioli special with sungold tomatoes, but that was it. Beautiful space, but not worth the effort to get the reservation, or the money.
Food: 3/5  |  Service: 4/5  |  Atmosphere: 5/5

Got a last min reservation so obviously had to do it! Have been wanting to try this spot for while now. we were immediately seated, greeted, and served which was lovely. we started with this cucumber cold dish that was so refreshing and spicy! the second app was the anchovy dip - huge win if you like anchovies - we dipped bread and veggies into this which was delicious. 
 
for mains we got lamb fettuccine and rigatoni. the rigatoni although their most popular dish to me seriously lacked flavor and came pretty dry. it was cooked perfectly al dente but it could have used more sauce and spice to have less of the pasta as the flavor. the lamb fettuccine on the other hand was delicious! the lamb added so much flavor and juiciness to the dish!

the biggest con about eating here is the fact there were flies flying around- super disturbing and gross as they came close to flying into our food. probably would not come back to this place simply because of the flies

The goat cheese ravioli was amazing but it was lukewarm. The cacio e pepe was also really good but was cold. The soft serve with olive oil and sea salt was amazing probably the best thing I had. 
The mozzarella and bread was really really good just wish maybe it was melted a little bit. I also got the clams and they were good.  Overall it was like a 3/5.

The food is highly regarded and it lives up to the hype. The best dish, and one is what seems like it's mentioned every review is the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti. As everyone describes it, it's like a fluffy pillow or delicious cheese and saffron with an amazing butter and honey sauce. Absolutely worth ordering. 

Other great dishes include the grilled clams and grilled shrimp. Both are loaded with spices and flavor. The clams also have a bit of a kick (spicy).

As good as it is, the ambiance isn't great. Try to book inside if possible. We got stuck outside next to the hot subway grate. The tables felt rickety and it just didn't give you the feel of a fine dining establishment.

Overall go for the food, but not if it's with a date your trying to impress.

Since I've moved to New York, Lilia has been on the top of my list of restaurants I wanted to try. I was able to get a reservation at the beginning of the month for a table at the end of the month. 

We were seated outside and it was super nice since the weather was beautiful. The service was great and was very timely. I'm docking my reviews two stars because of the food. 

The only star of the show was the focaccia bread. The bread was SO good and would highly recommend. I would only come back for the bread. I heard the clams were mind blowingly good but I really thought it was alright. The agnolotti was really sweet. I personally don't like my pasta sweet so it was a little off putting. Out of the two pasta dishes I liked the mafaldini more but I don't recommend if you like a saucier pasta. 

Overall, I really wanted to like Lilia as it was highly recommended restaurant. I'm really glad I tried though! Personally, not the place for me.
Amazing pasta and other inventive dishes! Definitely lives up to its hype and worth a trip to Williamsburg.

In a hundred years when the 3rd or 4th generation of the owners of Lilia handle the restaurant the greatness will still be there with those excellent pasta dishes .
We were lucky this time to sit outside in a fun breezy evening (frankly felt better than the inside...:)
We started this time (to focus on 4 pasta dishes) with fantastic scallops ,real fine starter !
The rigatoni ,the ricotta gnocchi and of course the non comparable non imitable sheep milk cheese filled agnolotti , all , as they were so excellent in the first week .
And then the gelato..... we (two) finish all 3 of them .
Fantastic service and again do not hesitate enjoying (until freezy winter coming) the outside sits.

Highly recommended!!!!

Definitely A Destination!!!!

Even though it is hard to get a reservation, I found Lilia reasonably priced and unpretentious, which I appreciate. The wines by the glass and cocktails were excellent, and I love that the plates are designed to be shared. The focaccia is STELLAR and not to be missed, as is the sheep's milk pasta. We enjoyed a few other dishes that were very tasty and great quality, but nothing remarkable. Overall definitely worth a visit and the ambiance is lovely for a date or small group.

So wonderful and accommodating and don't even get me started on the food! I can't say enough how much I loved it.  Don't miss the focaccia or the pasta! The spaghetti , Mafaldini and the Agnolotti were all exactly as the reviewers and menu described.

Really surprised about the reviews that say food is not great. Maybe these people come on an off night (I will admit we did have one bad dinner once where a bunch of dishes seemed just off)

But in general we find the food here to be outstanding. My husband and I are major foodies, traveled all over Europe, tried a lot of Michelin restaurants and this is one of few restaurants in NYC we keep coming back to. 
The menu changes seasonally with some dishes coming and going allowing you to try new dishes. 
Food is simplish but yet so flavorful. There are a lot of non-meat options in case you want to keep it light. 
Service is always great as well. 

Yes it's absurdly difficult to get a resy and drinks are kinda small but food is just so damn tasty. 

Our favorites are
- artichoke
- focaccia
- gem lettuce
- shrimp
- pine nut lemon pasta
- agnolotti

I could eat here everyday!! Everything is SO worth the hype. The service was amazing and each dish was so unique & high quality compared to other restaurants. The sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti and grilled clams are a MUST!

I was able to get a reservation for 4:45 pm on Wednesday about 3 weeks out. It's in a great location though the entrance is confusing because intuition leads you to the side door. They said they needed the table back by 6:30 for another reservation but we never felt rushed at all. Our waitress regularly checked on us and was able to give us great recommendations based on flavors we said we liked and didn't like.

I will say, our table for 2 outside was a little small for how much food we like to order but we made it work! For appetizers we got the
Sungold Tomato Focaccia with Green Garlic Butter, the Grilled Prawns, Grilled Clams, and the Italian Broccoli. Misi has a very similar broccolini dish and I will say it was much better at Misi. The Focaccia with Green Garlic Butter, however, is a MUST if you come here. Two bites in and we were ready to get another order!

For mains, we got the Mafaldini and the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti. Both were great, I'll definitely order the agnolotti again if I come back.

While I agree with the majority of people that say Misi is better, Lilia is still absolutely worth it and the food is delicious!

I was so excited to try this. It has been on my must try list for over two years, and we finally got a reservation. Honestly, I was let down in more ways than one! The food was just ok, nothing out of the ordinary and I made sure to order a lot so I could try out some of their most famous pasta dishes. It was SO unbearably hot inside the restaurant that it was so unenjoyable. I mentioned it to the waiter and he didn't have an answer as to why it was so hot (I was dripping sweat). I am not sure if we came on a day when the ac was broken or what the issue was. I think I would dine here again, to give it another shot but maybe in the winter time.
Lives up to its reputation. Food, service, and ambiance are all wonderful. The legendary sheep's milk agnolotti was a highlight.

Absolutely worth the hype! Get yourself a resy to this place or drop by around 4pm on a weekday for a walk-in. The flavors are insane, I'm still thinking about the fluffy buttery focaccia with green garlic butter  so so yummy. Everything was a 10/10 especially the dessert (for the none dessert people), the Italian Job - vanilla gelato, sea salt, olive oil, and fennel pollen YES fennel pollen....trust me it's bomb

Lilia seems like a hit or miss. The food was soo salty and disappointing (especially considering their prices). The pink peppercorn mafaldini tasted like pure pepper and salt. The red and white radicchio salad was soggy/soaked in balsamic. The service was mediocre and the waitress recommended red wine that was completely off based on our stated preferences. The grilled scallops were okay. If you want your Italian food fix, there are probably better places in NY.

Anyone who says Lilia is overrated must have been there on an off night because I don't believe a word that they say! I had an off the charts dinner at Lilia.

We were expected at Misi for a reservation at 6:15 and we got a message around 5:45 that the restaurant would be closing due to HVAC issues. As Lilia is Misi's sister restaurant, we figured we could reroute our cab on the off chance they may have space (as they are a tough res to get). We arrived around 6pm and let them know our situation which that were already aware of. They took our names and told us they would let us know. At 6:15, they made that call that they expanded the outdoor dining space for overflow of Misi guests. What incredible care and hospitality that is. I don't know if I've ever been taken care of like that. 

We had a wonderful server named Rose, who took such close care of us. They advised us what appetizers to get to keep us happily fed. The cucumber dish and whole artichoke were absolutely outstanding. The artichoke was definitely the standout as it was easy to share and just so flavorful. The focaccia came after and was hot to the touch, fresh out of the oven. I still think about that ramp butter.

We had 2 gin and tonics and WOW! I love a gin and tonic and this was a good one. Now onto the pastas. THE PASTAS! If you zoom into the gnocchi photo, you can see the ridges from how it was handmade. The gnocchi was so incredibly tasty. The agnolotti was insane. I've never tasted anything like it. Just a harmony of flavors. 

The olive oil cake was good. I think I was just incredibly full so I may have felt it was the best thing in the world with a hungry belly. 

Overall, what an absolutely amazing experience. I will 100% be back and recommending it to anyone I know. Hats off to you Lilia. Please give all the praise to your managers and host staff for how incredibly they handled this situation.

Nestled in the heart of Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Lilia brings Italy to New York City through the culinary wizardry of Chef Missy Robbins. In an era where trendy fusion foods and culinary theatrics often steal the show, Lilia stands out with its masterful rendition of classic Italian fare. The beauty of this acclaimed establishment lies in its dedication to authenticity, exceptional service, and a perfectly curated atmosphere.

Lilia's menu is a tribute to traditional Italian flavors, a testament to Chef Robbins' ability to transform simple, high-quality ingredients into dishes that sing with robust and intricate flavors. The shining star of the pasta menu - my absolute favorite - is the Mafaldini, a ruffled noodle bathed in pink peppercorn and Parmigiano Reggiano. The perfectly al dente pasta and the harmonious interplay of creaminess and spice make for a thoroughly satisfying experience.

Equally compelling is the Grilled Clams starter, a dish that pairs the briny sweetness of clams with the smoky flavors imparted by the grill, all lifted by a hint of Calabrian chili. The entrees shine as well, with the Grilled Lamb Leg Steak, featuring Roman spices and fennel pollen, a tender and aromatic delight. Robbins' ability to tease maximum flavor out of each ingredient is nothing short of enchanting, promising an unforgettable dining experience.

The service at Lilia matches the excellence of its food. From the moment you step in, the staff welcomes you with warmth that makes you feel like a valued guest. Their knowledge of the menu is impressive, and their recommendations are on point, ensuring you get the most out of your culinary journey. Each dish is delivered with precision timing, allowing you to enjoy each course without feeling rushed or forgotten.

One can't help but appreciate the team's attention to detail, from refilling water glasses to swift table clearing, demonstrating an ethos of professionalism that enriches the overall dining experience. Whether it's your first visit or your fiftieth, the Lilia team treats you with consistent courtesy and attentiveness, making every visit special.

Lilia's ambiance effortlessly marries sophistication and comfort. Housed in a converted auto-body shop, the space retains its industrial charm while embracing a modern and airy aesthetic. The high ceilings and large windows let in an abundance of natural light during the day, while soft, ambient lighting sets a cozy and intimate tone in the evenings.

The open kitchen adds a dynamic element to the dining experience, allowing guests a glimpse into the bustling world where their exquisite meals are crafted. The constant hum of conversation, clinking glasses, and the aromatic symphony wafting from the kitchen together create an atmosphere that's lively, warm, and welcoming.

While it's tough to find a drawback in the Lilia experience, securing a reservation can be a challenge due to its immense popularity. However, this minor inconvenience is testament to the excellence Lilia consistently delivers, making the wait entirely worth it.

Lilia is a celebration of timeless Italian cuisine, exceptional service, and a captivating ambiance. Chef Robbins' culinary prowess and her team's dedication to providing a superior dining experience contribute to Lilia's well-deserved reputation. This is not just a restaurant; it's a love letter to Italy, a place that evokes the rustic charm of a Roman trattoria in the heart of Brooklyn. For any lover of Italian cuisine or anyone seeking a delightful culinary journey, Lilia is a must-visit gem in New York City's vibrant dining scene.

My favorite restaurant in the neighborhood -- worthy of the hype! Every dish I've had there is delicious, the staff are friendly & helpful, the ambiance gorgeous. If you want a romantic date-night spot for a special occasion, this is it!

Do yourself a favor and order the cucumbers with calabrian chili & coriander. Unique, crispy, delicious!

I've been dying to go to Lilia for a year and was able to snag a table as a walk-in. Overall it was delicious with the mussels as the top dish! The apps and pastas all came out staggering. It would have been nice to have all the pastas together and all the apps together. Also portion sizes are pretty small for the cost.

Took a chance and came here without reservations for an early afternoon dinner with a friend. Despite no reservations, we were given table. Lilia is a beautiful and classy place. Our server was knowledgeable of the menu and made excellent recommendations with the food and drinks. I cannot wait to visit again.

I have been trying to get reservations for Lilia for a while now, and was so excited to eat here! We walked in at 4ish and were able to get bar seating at 5. I had a drink at the cafe portion. It's definitely a nice waiting spot, and the select spritz was great! The actual restaurant was a very rustic and minimalist decor. All the staff were very professional and helpful. They also moved really fast and were very attentive to moving plates and serving food. We had the mozzarella to start which was good but a bit simple. Then the mafaldini, which was also simple but addictive oh good. The texture of the pasta was great, and the peppercorn was a good balance of interesting but classic. I think it could have had an added layer of spice or herb, but found it to be filling and good. Finally, and my favorite, the agnolotti was incredible. You could taste the saffron in every bite and the filling was delicious. It was surprisingly sweet and rich. It was also a beautiful dish. Overall it was a great experience. I would definitely come back and know it would be a delicious meal.

Good food a drinks. But the lack of AC is unacceptable. I found it very difficult to enjoy my food while I suffered on a hot day in dreadfully  high temperatures. It makes no sense to have good food if the environment is unpleasant

Made a reservation, but had to change it last minute due to inclement weather, and the staff was kind enough to give me a birthday reservation! We ordered the focaccia (the best focaccia I've had on the city and I would come back just for this) and the cacio de pepe arancini (also highlight of the night). We got the saffron pasta, which was good, but for us the appetizers were our favorite. Given how hard it is to get a reservation, I wouldn't come frequently, but definitely a one-time thing when you're in the city! Busy indoors, but still a cute date night spot.

Still impressively consistent and delicious. Particularly was impressed with the shrimp, which were big, perfectly cooked and reasonably priced at a moment when others are price-gouging. Has managed to remain cool and unpretentious despite soooo much hype.

Amazing experience! This restaurant has been on my list for so long and it's so hard to get a reservation! My friend and I were randomly in Greenpoint for a Yelp elite event and we were close by so we decided to do a walk in reservation and what a great decision it was! We weren't able to get a reservation right away but once we got in line we were able get bar seating in 30 mins. We went to the caffé and ordered drinks: select spritz and the Lambrusca. We were able to sit inside which was nice ambiance but a little different then what I was expecting. The restaurant requires you to order everything at once which put some pressure on us but since we looked at the menu probably a hundred times before we had a good idea of what to order. Since it was an early dinner we only got two pasta dishes: the agnolotti and mafaldini. We also got one appetizer: the house made mozz. The appetizer was quite tasty and refreshing and the mafaldini was an interesting texture, but the star of the show was definitely 100% the agnolotti. The presentation was out of this world and the flavor was incredible, the small strands of saffron made a huge difference on the profile of the dish and was well appreciated. Would highly recommend and return!

Lived in the neighborhood for a long time and finally decided to check out Lilia since my wife had been following them on social. Overall the experience wasn't terrible thanks to the food. The food was really good but my biggest disappointment was the service itself.  I worked in service all my youth and understand how important it is. Also the importance of a patron being respectful and engaging with the server in order to make the experience better for everyone. 
What we received was far from that. We were treated as if we were bother to her. The bartender put on a fake smile when she spoke to us but disregarded our responses. She was dismissive and rolled her eyes after every request we and the other patrons around us made.  And the whole time was there right in front of us. Had we of been at a table it may not have been so bad but to have someone visibly not happy and radiating bad energy throughout our meal was less than ideal. Especially when they are standing just a few feet away. 
Maybe she had something personal going on or she simply hates her job.  Either way it ruined our experience.

Exceeded my expectations - it's no wonder it's hard to get to reservation. We came early when doors open and there was already a line waiting to put their names down for dinner at the bar. A great sign of a restaurant that's a master at their craft. 

Our waiter was amazing - gave us great recommendations on his favorite items on the menu. Even gave us a free appetizer that the kitchen made extra of (that's good service!) The pastas are definitely the standout, especially the agnolotti! It's decadent so we ordered another pasta with red sauce to balance it out. They have a wood grill in their kitchen and it was recommended to try a few items like the chicken and clams - one of the best chicken dishes I've had. Tender, flavorful, charred in all the right places. 

Lastly, the Italian Job - vanilla gelato with honey, fennel pollen and olive oil. Sounds odd but tastes amazing! I didn't expect to like it as much as I did!

Had a great meal here, the bread was absolutely hands down the best I've ever had. The garlic scape butter was 100/10. The grilled clams were so full of flavor with a little bit of spice & the breadcrumbs were a nice touch. I wish there was a bit more citrus in the artichoke but overall good dish. The mafaldini pasta was just okay, needed more flavor but the noodles were fun. The agnolotti was great, very rich so be prepared but loved the combination of flavors. Definitely don't skip on the gelato, I love olive oil, honey & sea salt sooo much on ice cream. Service was pretty good BUT the kitchen must have been backed up that night because the wait times between the clams& artichokes & pastas was almost an hour combined. We sat outside in their patio which was very vibey & great.

A wonderful spot in Williamsburg. The ambience of the restaurant was super cozy. Service was very friendly and efficient. Fresh homemade pasta is the best! Each dish was beautifully plated and perfectly seasoned. Everything was delicious! I really enjoyed my unique dessert as well. Creative and tasty dishes!

Lilia is by far my favorite restaurant on earth.  I've now gone to Lilia close to two dozen times and have had almost every item on the menu.  In terms of service, it cannot be beat and the restaurants vibe is awesome, industrial, but upscale.

For food, I always recommend first timers go with:
1. Focaccia with green garlic butter
2. Cacio e Pepe Frittelle
3. Grilled Clams
4. Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti (best pasta I've had in the US)
5. Fettuccine with Lamb Sausage
6. Italian Job, best dessert

Definitely get yourself to Lilia!

Lilia is a Place that you need to experience... a very good original Italian Restaurant. The pasta is exceptional. We order a few entree and shared them. All are very delicious.

In the end, what else, I always enjoy a good Italian Espresso! 

The service is excellent and very good help when I need to us for explanation or recommendation. Definitely a recommended place.

MAKE RESERVATION!!! very popular place.

the service
truly incredible. you can tell they are trying to get a star. water never wasn't being refilled. table always clean. napkin folded when i came back from the restroom. truly delightful. my server - was also just amazing. i hope he gets promoted. 

clams
very tasty but definitely plated wrong. i dont take myself as a food critic, but i definitely enjoy a lot of variety of it. this dish was almost confusing to me. personally, if the pre gutted clam was placed after the chili and breadcrumbs rather than before... the flavor of the oyster would still be prevalent rather then being completely disguised by the toppings. when i then preceded to wipe off the toppings and eat the clams and following with the concoction... it was so much more magical!

lamb ragu fettuccine 
im not sure if im impressed or not. and i truly say that as a compliment. it was widely familiar to a canned ragu i had as a child but enhanced. the spices come through so with delight. it felt like a special dedication to mothers at home feeding their child. 

agnolotti 
honestly not what i was expecting. this being the most ordered dish at the restaurant was intriguing so obviously i had to see what all the hype was about. I wasn't totally let down. the creaminess of that goat milk cheese was heavenly and matched with the honey was a wonderful combination. incredibly fresh feeling on this hot summer day. i do almost wish it had something else to it. it was pretty one note and as amazing that combination is, it might've been better off as an appetizer. 

olive oil gelato
i took a risk here ordering this. was slightly scared of the nature of gelato and olive together. but that savory and sweet mix was SO good! i devoured that large glass so fast. 

overall great experience! would attend again to try more of the menu. i think the potential for this place is beyond.

Easy enough to get a weeknight walk-in, sat outside during golden hour for an incredible meal. Inside was bright and open, very beautiful. Flawless execution on service and food. All staff is friendly, smiling and excellent at their respective positions. Truly, not a single beat in the choreography of service was missed. Drinks filled immediately, meals came out perfectly timed. The grilled clams are an excellent opener. Great texture and flavor. Perhaps the clam should sit on top of the garnish to get more flavor and then enjoy the crumbs etc as desired off the bottom of the shell? The Agnolotti is as good as everyone says. I found it best paired with a savory or spicy pasta and a bit sweet on its own. The olive oil gelato was a must have, even if you're very full.

Personally thought Lilia was much better than Misi, after going to both within 24 hours. We had a good experience even though we had a patio seat and had to abruptly leave because there was a downpour in the middle of our meal. 

The food was delicious! I would recommend the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti and focaccia - both were memorably great and lived up to the hype. The sugar snap peas were also presented beautifully and were a perfect fresh veggie appetizer. The malfaldini was good but not as special as the other dishes. 

I also ordered a Select Spritz and it was perfect for a summer day, like an Aperol spritz but less sweet and more refreshing. 

I would recommend trying for an indoor seat - inside seemed nice and airy. For mild rain, the umbrellas on their patio have pretty good coverage, but in our case the heavy downpour made it impossible to continuing sitting outdoors - unfortunately if this happens, they're unable to reseat people indoors since they're fully booked.

Reservations here are hard to get! I managed to get a table for 4 on a Tuesday at 5:30PM - and this was still two weeks in advance and after weeks of searching. Though after tasting the food, very understandable why everyone wants to eat here. 

I started with the grilled clams and focaccia. The grilled clams were very tasty had a perfect zesty spicy pairing. The focaccia was buttery and I liked it better than the one at Ci Siamo. 

The Gnocchi, Agnolotti and fettucine were all delicious! It was hard to choose a favorite pasta - they were all great in their own ways. 

Lamb here was very generous with the portion. Meat was tender and fell right off the bone. 

Olive oil ice cream was okay - I'm personally not a fan of olive oil but my friends I were with really enjoyed it. It reminded me a lot of salt water taffy

Restaurant has great service and the inside has a rustic feel. Lots of windows and natural lighting - I will be back!

Solid food and pastas! Loved the vibe. I got lucky with an early walk in but I'm not sure it's worth the level of rave I was personally hearing about.

Skip the arancini, the mozzarella they coated it with was super salty.

Broccoli pesto and agnolotti were very good (8/10)

Clams were pretty good too (7/10)

Another famous Italian spot in NYC. Fyi the reservation was open 30 days ahead at 10am. The indoor was nice and had lots of earthy tones. There was lots of natural light. We got several dishes:
- Grilled clams: don't be fooled by the pictures. The portion was like a size of 2 hands. The clams were absolutely smoky and yummy. I would totally come back for this dish.
- Grilled artichoke: i was originally not planning to order this but every table got this dish and it didn't disappoint me at all. The sauce was somewhat similar to the clam dish, the somehow the combination just worked so well. However, you was instructed to use hand to eat this so it was look a bit messy.
- Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti: this is the famous dish that was associated with Lilia. It was creamy but also sweet. I enjoyed it, but wouldn't finish the whole portion. You may want to have this with some other dishes that had either tomato sauce or citrus flavor to balance it out.
- Lamb Fettuccine: this dish was delicious even for someone who didn't like tomato sauce. The texture of the pasta was nice and the dish was a good counterpart with the agnolotti.
- Olive oil gelato: it was sweet, more than what I liked, but the sea salt helped a bit. 

Overall, I think the food here was delicious and worth a visit. I took a star off due to the dessert and the difficulty to get in. But I would come back and try other dishes.

Must I start off by saying the $30 agnolotti was spectacular is worth the hype so deff do order it.  Linguini with a strong kick of garlic, crunchy bread crumbs and cooked to perfection, delicious. The olive oil cake was amazing, tasted more like a pound cake right up my alley and the olive oil ice cream was interesting, you definitely have a strong taste of olive oil but the ice cream was delightful. We did have some issue with service due to slow service but they quickly caught on and became quiet attentive. We sat outside and they gave us blankets for a windy night. Loved the ambiance!

Good pasta & good vibes, not too far from the Bedford subway stop (~10min walk) if you are coming from manhattan. Especially with the summer, they have lots of outdoor and patio space which is nice for an evening meal! Make sure to get a reservation or else you will have to wait a very long time or get turned away. The issue is partly because Lilia reservations have no cancellation fees and no one cancels last minute, so there's almost no chance of scoring these at the last moment on Resy. Wouldn't say the food was the absolute best but it is decent and solid.

I just have to say LOL to all the 4 star reviews made by people who admit the food here is great. This place is one of a kind, and any true New Yorker knows that if you can get a res at Lilia, you're lucky and in for a treat! 

Lilia is by far one of the best restaurants I've ever been to. The effort and work put into every meal is obvious. 

I now live in LA, and look to Missy's cookbook for inspiration as I cannot find a single restaurant on the west coast that compares to Missy's food. It's simple, no fuss, direct - but drenched in Italian culture and relentless effort. 

Do yourself a favor - when you're in New York go to Lilia.
There was a lot of hype revolved around the restaurant, and there is a lot more better and easily accessible italian food around
This place is a gem. Yes it is hyped but rightfully so! Cannot go wrong with any of their pastas. They have indoor and outdoor seating and go at open for a chance to walk in!
Difficult to get a reservation but so worth it. The service was as good as it gets, the food was so so good and a great vibe all together.

It's very difficult to get a reservation, so we just walked ip there at 3:40pm (20 minutes before they open) and got in line to get on the waiting list for that day. If you are in the front of the line you can get a table inside.
Totally worth it though.
The food was amazing.
YOU HAVE TO TRY THE FOCACCIA! It was soooo good.
The desert Italian Job is also to die for!
We also had the grilled scallops, the Mafaldini and Agnolotti. 
For two people you easily leave $120 without drinks.
A restaurant that is actually worth the hype! I've been here a few times and it has consistently blown me away. One of the best restaurants in brooklyn

Someone recommended this restaurant to us highly a few weeks before our recent visit to NYC, and it was quite an endeavor to reserve a table at this restaurant. New reservations are released 30 days ahead at midnight ET every day, so we set an alarm clock for a couple of minutes before the release time and started refreshing the restaurant's reservation page at Resy. Most of the reservations were gone immediately after the clock hit 12:00 am. We did manage to get a reservation in our 2nd attempt the next day.
 
We arrived at the restaurant at the time of our reservation and were greeted warmly. The dishes are all exquisitely prepared. The Focaccia with Green Garlic Butter was baked perfectly and very flavorful. We ordered Red & White Radicchio and Grilled Artichoke for our appetizers. The Taste of the Red & White Radicchio was well balanced and very pleasing. I ate only a quarter of the artichoke heart, which was good but nothing special, because the rest of the dish was too cheesy for me, although one of my companions loved it. The best were the pasta dishes, Sheep Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti and Lamb Sausage Fettuccine. I had only a small quantity of the pasta due to my concern about my lactose intolerance, but the sheep milk cheese and Pecorino caused me no problems, indicating their quality (i.e., well fermented). The complex flavor profiles of the pasta dishes stand out even compared to the best pasta dishes that I had at high-end restaurants in Italy. The only main dish we ordered was Black Bass with Salsa Verde, which was good but did not stand out. The drinks served at this restaurant were also superb. 

Overall, I very much enjoyed my experience.

This is officially my favorite Italian restaurant and one of the best restaurants I've been to overall in New York. My roommate and I got here at 3:40pm, right before it opened at 4pm. There was already a line, which doubled in size by the time the doors opened. We were told to come back by 5:15pm, which was an hour wait - not too bad for a walk-in on a Saturday evening. Getting a reservation here is very hard, so walk-in is a better way to go, anyway.

To start, we ordered the focaccia with green garlic butter. This bread was crazy good - a perfect balance between crunchy and soft, and with the butter, it melted in my mouth. For the mains, we ordered three pastas: the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti, the mafaldini, and the rigatoni. All were 10/10 for me. The sheep's milk pasta was like nothing I've had before. The saffron was present in every bite, and the cheese was light and delicious. My roommate and I agreed that the mafaldini was a twist on a classic cacio e pepe with the pink peppercorn adding a wonderful, almost sweet kick to the thick and fun pasta. We also enjoyed the spicy kick and warm red sauce in the rigatoni. The textures and flavors of each pasta were spot on, managing to be memorable without being obnoxious. If I wasn't already impressed, along came dessert. We got the Italian Job gelato, which is a gelato with olive oil. The olive oil works so well with the creamy gelato - the dessert's savory notes complimented its subtle sweetness well. Overall, I would highly recommend this spot to anybody who wants to experience high quality, unique Italian food in a beautiful setting. I enjoyed every bit of my meal and will definitely be returning.

Finally got to try this highly touted restaurant.  The staff were lovely.  The wine list had something for everyone.  Our group of four worked through most of the menu.   Everything was interesting.   The most overrated dish was the cacio e pepe balls- essentially high concept mozzarella sticks.  Favorite dishes:  grilled artichoke, grilled prawns, mafaldini.  Most surprising dish- spaghetti with pine nuts and lemon.  Tried both meats- the lamb was very good and the chicken was good.  

Fun experience, nice place, good to very good food.

Pro Tip: when it's rainy in the city, find yourself a friend with a car and make your way to BK for the day.

When my good friend Michael asked me to go to the Brooklyn Museum, it was a for sure yes on my side. 

Little did I know the afternoon would lead us to waiting on the 10 person line at 4:30pm before they opened up. Thankfully, we were seated quickly upon doors opening and at the bar.

We ordered a lot and this place is $$$ but worth it.

I tried my first ever gin martini, definitely go for the gin infused with lemon  We also splurged on the bottle of red Barbaresco which was 

My only complaint was not being informed that our 2 hours were coming up and missing the chance to have some gelato. Kinda took away from the experience after we spent $300 plus and were told to take ice cream to go.

We ran out and forgot the lamb dish we didn't get a chance to eat and had asked to pack up but don't worry, be back.. if the gelato is anything like their sister restaurant, it'll be worth it.

Extremely disappointing yesterday.
I always rave about Lilia especially to out of town guests.

My cousin is in town from California and I have been dying to take her to Lilia. 3 of us arrive early on a MONDAY without a reservation, put on the waitlist at 4:56pm. We make it very clear that we will gladly sit outdoors, no problem. 

At 4:56pm there are roughly 6-7 empty tables outdoors that can fit 3 guests. Likely, awaiting 5 and 5:30 reservations, no problem. 

An hour goes by, 5:56pm:  3 empty outdoor tables now that have not been touched, not been sat. 

6:30pm: 2 empty outdoor tables now that have not been touched, not been sat. 

At this point we are frustrated. We could have eaten and left at this point and SAT AT TWO EMPTY TABLES THAT WERE UNTOUCHED FOR 2 HOURS RIGHT IN FRONT OF OUR EYES. We give it until 6:55pm and and are done.  How pretentious and bold of a restaurant - never experienced anything like this.

what a meal. lived up to the hype. in addition to the grilled artichoke app, and grilled prawns, which were both DIVINE, we ordered the agnolotti, rigatoni diavola, and fettucine with lamb sausage. each one was quite simply PERFECT. this meal rocked our world. what a relief!

Sold out of everything by 8pm. Had to wait over 30 minutes for the reservation table we had booked for. Came for the famous dishes however they did not have any of the foods we wanted. The food we ordered was 1/10. Would not return here.

Amazing food, amazing service, amazing atmosphere. The food is spectacular, and the waiter did a great job explaining all the dishes, and how we should order without any pressure. Loved this restaurant, hoping to go back if i can get another reservation.

I really recommend the mussels btw, they were incredible.

Lilia has been on my radar for a couple of years now. One of my brothers alerted me of its existence and after some research I discovered how much of a hype was surrounding this place. I had my initial doubts about how good  Lilia was, mainly due to its location and my skepticism of Italian restaurants in general - however, I know Missy Robbins has an excellent reputation so I made it my intention to secure a table and try Lilia for myself. 

What really motivated me to try Lilia was my good experience at Robbins' other restaurant Misi a couple of months ago. Like Misi, getting a table here was work; reservations open online at 10am one month out, though I heard these are leftovers after phone reservations open. I figured I would try my luck online and snagged a 9pm reservation on a Monday night.

Lilia's aesthetics are somewhat minimal; the space is a repurposed auto body shop and they did a really nice job upgrading it. There are a lot of clean lines throughout the restaurant, with touches of color throughout the space. In addition to the indoor seating, they have two spaces for outdoor seating; when you book a table it will specify where you will be given time slots for indoor or outdoor. 

Like Misi, Lilia specializes in Italian food, but unlike the former there is a larger variety of dishes outside of pasta. The menu is separated by dish size - starting with small apps and making your way up to large plates. I was with my brother and we thought it would be best to share everything. Before ordering, however, we were told that two of our selections (an app and their signature pasta) were sold out. I'll be honest I was a little disappointed - I understand things periodically run out in restaurants, but for the amount of hype around this place and the work it takes to get a table here, there shouldn't be things that are out - let alone one of their most popular dishes. 

Anyway, we decided to order a mix of small plates and pastas: Italian broccoli, mozzarella, clams, prawns, ricotta gnocchi, and linguini. Everything was really good - the broccoli was tossed in parmesan cheese which provided great flavor. I was living my best life with the mozz which sat on top of a warm piece of bread. The clams and prawns were also good; I'm not a fan of peel-your-own shrimp and I probably ate some shell, but the sauce they were tossed in was really good and kinda made up for it. 

The pastas were good; the ricotta gnocchi had really good flavor and were pillowy soft. The linguini was good too, and I much appreciated the whole bulbs of garlic. One thing that puzzled me though was that the dishes weren't warm enough. Like, they were warm, but it was almost like they were sitting out for a few minutes too long and lost some of their heat. We finished with dessert - I got vanilla gelato and had the options to mix and match toppings (fun!). The gelato was tasty, albeit nothing too out of the ordinary (my brother's dessert was more unique).

Service was good, our waiter was friendly enough and all the food came out at a good pace. Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Lilia and had a good meal. My only gripe with this place, like Misi, is that I don't feel my experience  equated to the hype surrounding the restaurant and the work it took to secure a table. Despite this, the food has piqued my interest, and I would return for another meal if given the opportunity.

This review is about the dining experience as opposed to the food.  (But to comment on the food, it was mostly very good.  Although i would not order the white asparagus or the pasta with lamb sausage again - both were bland.)  It is difficult to get a reservation at this restaurant so we had to settle for a 5:15pm reservation.  At no time were we informed of any time limit so naturally assumed we could take our time.  We ordered drinks and soon after ordered the meal.  And then ordered a nice bottle of wine.  Our last course was chicken - it was quite good.  With food in my mouth, the waitress informed us we'd have to move to a different place for the dessert.  That alone was shocking but maybe because we are polite people - or maybe because we had enough to drink - we obliged.  We were escorted to some room for coffee or something that had two open and uncomfortable looking bar stools.
