Well, there were three of us - so i guess they expected one of us to stand while having dessert.  I immediately asked for the manager.  Her body language screamed "what do you want, I'm busy?"  I described the situation but the reality is, she's probably the one that instructed the waitress to do that to us.  And she was not about to apologize for her actions.  She ended up taking $90 off of our $650 bill for three.  I was able to speak with the general manager a few days later.  She profusely apologized, said there was a clear lack of communication on the part of the restaurant, agreed that we should have never been treated like that and said she would welcome us back to "make things right."  And she said I'd receive a gift card.  I did.  It was for $25.

It's one thing to have an avocado on toast for some quick nourishment.  It's another thing to have a dining experience.  Once it's ruined, it can't be undone.  But a restaurant can show they want to do the right thing.  This restaurant did not.

Was super excited to try Lilia after seeing so much about it on social media, and it did not disappoint. It can be a little tough to get a reservation, but they get released at 10 AM daily for a few weeks in advance, so it isn't too bad as long as you plan ahead. 

We got an outdoor table, but the vibes inside seem really nice as well - airy and relaxed, but still pretty upscale feeling. We started with the focaccia with ramp butter, and ordered the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti and fettuccine with lamb sausage. Everything was really great. The focaccia was served warm and the bread was perfectly crusty. The butter also had a nice herby flavor from the ramp. The fettuccine was perfectly Al dente and had the perfect kick of spice. The sheep's milk agnolotti was definitely the star of the show, and is one of the most unique pastas I've ever had. The cheese was super light and pillowy. It's pretty sweet, but the saffron and sun dried tomatoes added great depth of flavor. 

One thing I will say is the server recommended we order 5-7 dishes for two, but honestly three was plenty. Everything is pretty rich and heavy, and ordering that many definitely would have felt like too much. Overall, very solid and will be back to try other things on the menu as well!

RESERVATION
My birthday was fast approaching. I tried so hard to check multiple days to reserve a family dinner on Resy. I signed up for notifications of cancellations and tried calling during business hours, but it kept going to voicemail. What did work was calling earlier in the day prior to opening business hours (not after 4pm). On the day of my birthday, I called around 11am-12pm and they answered! I somehow managed to snag a table for 7:30pm (what I thought was ideal time) on the same day! I literally screamed a little cause everything I hoped for came true. 

ORDERING
When my family and I got there, we were immediately seated - was told in advance that the table was available until 9:15pm (slightly less than 2hrs), which we were totally okay with. We were seated and went straight to ordering our food. We were just going to order a few entrees and was suggested to order an appetizer since the wait for food might take some time. So, I agreed and ordered an appetizer to start. 

DINING
- Artichoke
I honestly had no idea of what it looked like or tasted like. I originally ordered it because it sounded good and was expecting smaller artichoke heart pieces. But what I discovered was a cooked whole artichoke. It was advised that we took each piece off and ate it. The outer pieces were nice and tasty, but the more we dug in, it was getting very hard to chew - almost inedible. We ate whatever we could. Probably wouldn't have ordered had I known what to expect. 
- Rigatoni
This was probably the most common pasta dish here. It's just tomato sauce. A tad bit spicy due to the chilies. Maybe I'm extra sensitive but maybe a tad salty for me as well. 
- Gnocchi
I've had gnocchis before, so no surprise here. I don't love pesto, but I enjoy the light pesto taste and loved the addition of pistachios in it for added crunch. 
- Mafaldini
I really enjoyed the wavy texture of the pasta in my mouth. The grated cheese was amazing. Overall, it's very unique and something that I've never tried. 
- Agnolotti
If I had to rate everything we ate, this would be the top & most recommended (5/5). I loved that it was so unique - something I would never find elsewhere. The cheese was very rich. The ravioli type pasta was very soft texture-wise. 

OVERALL IMPRESSION
I guess I had quite high expectations hearing good reviews online and from some fellow peers. I'm glad to have tried it. It was good, but it honestly didn't fully meet my high expectations. Was a bit disappointed with the wait for the food (almost close to an hour for the appetizer - then the food soon followed). The hardness of the artichoke was a bit disappointing. But to counteract that, the service was very good. They were literally on top of the water refills. The manager came by to ask about how we enjoyed our food and they even provided a complimentary soft serve ice cream with candles due to the fact that I had noted that the occasion was for my birthday.

It's absolutely worth going at least once, I will say some people in our group didn't love the pasta. We did have to wait awhile in between courses and ended up being there for almost 3 hours. But the FOOD. The food is amazing, the bread and ramp butter, the fish, the agnolotti, THE GELATO. All amazing.

One of the best focaccias I have ever had, one of the best lemon pastas I have ever had. Not to mention the service and ambiance were top notch. Lilia is one of the best Italian restaurants in all of NYC.
Overrated restaurant. I was so looking forward to eating at LilLis unfortunately,  The food was just not good. The deserts however were great. And the service was great as well.

Yummy pasta and appetizers. It is a pain to get a reservation, but thankfully we got in through a walk-in. Service was okay. It kinda felt like the staff didn't want us there. Food was worth it though.

Service. Anyone would expect much more, but by far much more at that price level from an establishment that rates itself anywhere close to what the William Vale wants to be.... They are so far from their goal!!!
How many different ways can you combine egg and flour and soak it in butter? Lilia, located above a G train subway grate in a far away neighborhood in Brooklyn begs us to consider one more.

This place is 100% worth the hype. It's pricey so definitely a place I'd go to splurge or for a celebration. The restaurant itself is super cute. It's airy, bright, and despite being a fancier restaurant it has a good energy. The people and staff here aren't uptight, which I really did appreciate. 

The food truly is phenomenal - each dish had a lot of texture and flavor to it. My friend and I got the focaccia, mussels (which I think are leaving the menu soon), and the sheep's milk pasta. All were delicious. Days later, I'm still thinking about that pasta so I couldn't recommend it enough. It was so soft and creamy without it being heavy, which is super hard to find for cheese filled pastas. For drinks, I got the spritz which was a classic. Can't go wrong there. You do have to order all at once, and my recommendation would be to order more conservatively than they suggest. The dishes are quite filling (and more filling than they look). This is also a place I wish that I went with a bigger group, so I could try more things (4 people feels like the right amount). Lastly, the service here was absolutely phenomenal. Our waitress was so kind, accommodating, and genuinely did her best to make sure we were comfortable and happy with our food. I genuinely haven't had a waitress be this kind and thoughtful. I wish I remembered her name!

Actually, Lilia is a really good place for spending time with friends or family because of cozy  ambiance
It was so tasty, I ordered lamb steak, it was incredible 
Moreover, service was great! Writers were very friendly and our dishes were ready to rapidly :)

This was one of my favorite meals among all of my 10+ NY trips over time. Every dish was delicious, however our sommelier was the damper to our experience where he barely explained the wine and looked incredibly impatient when we asked him more questions. He also didn't come back to refill our glasses. Despite the negative experience with our somm, I'd give him the benefit of the doubt and assume he had a bad day and come back here any time.

So.. was the food good? absolutely! Was it worth the hassle of getting a seat here? prob not. Everything was good at Lilia but you'll find comparable dishes all across the NYC at easier to book restos. The more unique standouts were the garlic/anchovy dip and the lemon spaghetti. Would I go back if someone offered? Yes. Would I spend weeks waiting for resy notify myself? No.

Food: 9/10
Value: 7/10
Service: 8/10
Vibe: 7/10
Great food and a very good restaurant. I leave it for others to decide whether the hype is justified. I haven't been in awhile because it's complicated.

Limited specials 
Need more choices food was unique and delicious 
Service was very helpful

Missy Robbins is one of the outstanding chefs by far. Nothing  we ever uhad tasted mediocre only the wow factor. Start with the grilled clams and the scallops and move onto the pasta, any pasta. We had the lamb sausage fettuccine with a tomatoes Passato and from there we had the sea bass.
The service was very good, the old garage turned into a vibrant high ceiling establishment that uses wood to fire up the dishes is outstanding.
We had desert, drinks and coffee as well and the bill was just over $300 for 3 which was fair.
Love it when I am blown away!!!!
The Other restaurant she has is Misi and that too is not to be missed.

I've been trying to come here for some time now. My friend who lives nearby figured out that if you come early enough, you can make a reservation for the night albeit maybe an hour later. We came at 5pm and secured a 6:15 pm bar table for two!

The interior was massive and very spacious. It made me appreciate Lilia more for not packing the space as it could given its popularity.

They give you complimentary potato chips, which I liked but would've preferred them to be less greasy and more crispy.

We split the focaccia bread which was amazing. I would come back for this. It was warm and appropriately salty! 

The artichokes were delicious as well but a little messy to eat. It was topped with top notch parmesan. 

We split the agnolotti, which was good but i think I prefer it to be filled with meat than purely cheese. The malfadini was amazing. 

We also ordered the chicken but even before the pastas came out, we were full so we canceled it without any issues. We were so full that my friend couldn't even finish her second Milano sour which is a delicious cocktail for a pricey 19 dollars.

Overall, I think worth it to come again, but not so unique or spectacular to be months booked in advance on resy.

We managed to walk into Lilia at 7:30 pm on a Tuesday night after trying to snag a walk in spot at 4 pm on a Thursday (to no avail). So week day may be the move?

For the two of us- we ordered
- Foccacia with Ramp Butter: (5/5): AMAZING. I've never had foccacia in a ball or quite like this. So crispy on the outside with a fluffy tender inside. ALSO the garlic parmesan topping on top. SO SO GOOD. It didn't even need the ramp butter it was so good on its own. If you're a butter gal tho they give plenty
- Mozzarella on Sourdough: (2.5/5): this was exactly as you'd expect but the balance felt all wrong. Super thick slabs of mozzarella but not enough bread and the bread also wasn't crispy? Just kind of soggy? It was definitely not the quality I'd expecf
- Sheep Cheese Agnolotti (5/5): I can definitely see why this is Lilia's namesake! Super smooth and creamy sheep cheese enrobed in perfectly al dente pasta. The honey sauce and saffron was not too sweet and was SO SO SO good with the pasta. I was lapping leftovers up with my fork LOL
- Ricotta Gnocchi (3/5): honestly really bland and uninspiring. The frozen sweet potato gnocchi from Trader Joe's is better than this. The pesto was oily and the gnocchi itself had no flavor. We didn't end up finishing this dish because it just wasn't very good.

Lilia was an interesting experience because the dishes I loved- sheep cheese agnolotti and foccacia- I really loved- whereas the other two were extremely uninspiring. Would recommend but maybe come solo and just get those two dishes? Food portion was fine- we didn't leave hungry. Service was pretty pushy which was a little annoying

The bass is supposed to be an entree.  The fish was 1/4 of a pound
with potato -  the same color as the fish intending to make the
potato increase the size of this miniscule fish for $32.  There was
some disgusting green cream on top of the fish.  If I could give this
restaurant a 0 i would.  We also ordered a pasta that tasted like
a bucket of salt was thrown on it. On top of this the pasta was
cold.  The food was so bad that we asked for a check and ran out.

I intend to contact AMEX and be credited for this horrendous food.
Shame on you Lilia!

Ok this place is off the chain. The spaghetti? Unbelievable. Fettuccine? Exquisite. We ordered Chicken, Lamb and Fish for protein. All was fantastic but the bass was otherworldly. Oh and the fresh bread and spread?! If it would have been an entree thats all I would have ordered. Then at the end of this fantastic meal they bring out ice cream with salt and olive oil on it. Brother! Cart me out on a gurney and call 911. The servers must have thought I was a food critic because it was impeccable. If you get anywhere close to Brooklyn, you know, within 500 miles you better stop by this place.

Struggling to get a res and tired of refreshing on Resy? Call them in the day time! It appears they keep a bunch of tables off of Resy for some reason. 

Cacio e Pepe Frittelle - 7/10 - In theory, a fried ball of dough with some cheesy sauce inside would be mouth watering good, but it was only alright.  The insides were a bit cloying and flavor-wise nothing to write home about.

Little Gem Lettuce, Italian Vinaigrette, Pecorino, Breadcrumbs - 8.5/10 - The breadcrumbs and dressing were lovely, and the pecorino strips were generous. A gem of a salad.

Mussels, Herb Butter, Sea Salt - 10/10 - WOW. The green sauce on these mussels was divine. Highly recommend!!

Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano - 10/10 - A MUST TRY!!  There may be few ingredients but they pack a flavorful punch, and the consistency of the pasta is perfectly al dente. Can't wait to come back for more!!

Mortadella Filled Tortellini with ramps and mint. Green tortellini that was served with mint leaves and a sauce that resembled congealed oil. It was alright but we wish we had ordered the agnolotti instead!

The gelato was soft serve, not the rich creamy deliciousness I was hoping for and expecting. I would skip next time.

Overall, 4.5/5 stars.

Awesome dining experience at Lilia! 

I got extremely lucky with a last-minute cancelation (my win!) and was able to make my way to Lilia. We ordered the Red and White Radicchio as the starter and then Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Ricotta Gnocchi, and Lamb Sausage Fettucine as our mains. Nothing disappointed!

I see what the hype was, and I will be back!

I had an excellent meal at Lilia in April 2021 and told lots of friends that the reservations gymnastics were worth it, but a recent experience has filled me with doubt. 
My husband and I had a 9:30pm reservation on a chilly Monday evening in March. We arrived on time and were directed, stomachs rumbling, to wait in the cafe. By the time we were seated and ordered food, they were out of focaccia. We also had to wait in suspense while the waiter checked to make sure there was still agnolotti before he could put in the rest of our order. We learned we would get the last order; while he was gone we decided we would walk out and get pizza slices if we struck out on the agnolotti. 
The first bite of food (homemade mozzarella) did not hit our table until ~45 minutes past our reservation time. Then the other courses came out in such rapid succession that despite inhaling the food it was hard to keep up and enjoy the food at the right temperature. 
The food itself was good -- high quality ingredients allowed to mostly speak for themselves -- but lacked the perfect balance I tasted on the first visit. For example, the broccoli the first time had some heat and the acid of the lemon tied everything together. This time, it was drowned in cheese and I didn't get any heat or acid. At least the agnolotti was as good as I remembered. 
I think it comes down to hospitality. We planned what was supposed to be a fun dinner a month in advance, jumping through some hoops to secure a reservation, only to feel like an afterthought. Like why did I spend money to be hangry and then rushed through my meal? I don't think I will be back on my own dime even though I live nearby.

In a city known for pasta, Lilia has managed to get a cult following even with how hard it is to get a reservation. We were able to snag bar seating on a weekday night, but the place was still packed and we had to wait for our seats. The staff was super nice in terms of the service, so it wasn't the worst overall. 

For the food, we ended up getting the squash appetizer and the saffron agnolotti. In terms of the squash, we felt it a bit heavy on the oil side, but the pesto it came with was to die for. The sauce for the agnolotti was heavenly, and the tomatoes combined with the creamy sheeps milk provided a nice balance of flavor and texture. Both of us thought, however, the presentation could be a bit nicer for the pasta considering how popular it was. Overall, Lilia definitely may be a bit overhyped, but I'm more than glad I tried it!

The agnolotti is as good as reviews say -- surprisingly subtle flavor, nuanced and very creamy. They've upped the price on this ($30).

The rigatoni and malfadini were disappointing. Salty and overpowered by single flavors, chilis and pepper. Neither tasted particularly distinct.

Clams were flavorful, but very rubbery.

Some of the newer starters seem to be brighter, which help balance out the cheese on many of the dishes.

Order however many appetizers and entrees you would normally order. Pastas were rich and portioned large enough to serve as entrees if this is what you would normally eat as a main.

We were mainly turned off by how aggressively our waitress tried to upsell, making us feel bad for *only* wanting to order 2 pastas and 2 starters for 2 people. This would have been plenty (for us) given the butter, oil, and cheese, and very early dinner time. We were pressured to order at least another dish, which we fully packed to go, and didn't get to try the dessert we'd been looking forward to. The waitress refused to take our order initially, saying it wouldn't be enough food. This has never happened to me before at any restaurant. Instead of enjoying our chosen meal, we picked several alternate dishes and were distracted by the bad taste of the initial service interaction.

I feel like they are treating the seating as a one time visit, in which they attempt to get you to try everything on the menu, with the expectation (maybe accurately, given the reservation situation) that you won't be able to return. Doesn't make for a pleasant dinner experience though. We also saw the table next to us taking a large to-go portion.

Paid $$$ for agnolotti and bad vibes. Better to spend your time and money elsewhere.

Managed to get reservations for outdoor seating and was so so close to getting indoor when a party sounded like they were a no show. Kudos to the hostess for trying to get us in though  

Everything tasted amazing though. I would definitely come back again for the pastas. Malfaldini and the clams were my favorite! Perfectly cooked and al dente with every noodle well seasoned. Inside felt very warm and romantic. Outside was cold especially without the sun, and we just focused on finishing the pasta before it got cold. Make sure to request for indoor if you go!

Solid Italian spot in Williamsburg with hard to snag reservations in a vibey lofty space.

Food
Gem Salad - Crunchy, fresh, and acidic with a great aged hard cheese. Loved the crunchy breadcrumbs and would recommend for sharing between two people.

Mussels - I have to say, the sauce was a bit too bright green for my liking? It was giving grasshopper vibes and definitely visually was not what I was expecting to come out. However, the taste was great. Buttery, plump, and came right out of the shell. Also great for sharing between 2 people.

Mafaldini - An aesthetic take on cacio e pepe by using pink peppercorns. Really good, perfect al dente and textured pasta. The pepper was a bit on the heavy side, though. Not even in a spicy way, but more that I wanted to taste more of the milky cheese taste in the dish instead of it being overpowered by pepper. 

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti - Tender and delicious! Definitely a fave and I think one of their most popular pastas. You'll want to bring the lactaid for this one because it is very rich. 

Italian Job - Some of the best gelato I have ever had. This one was a vanilla gelato base with olive oil, honey, and crunchy fenugreek/pollen. The olive oil was extremely rich and flavorful and the perfect contrast to the sweet. The honey solidifies and also provides some crunch. A must order!!

I would say for two people, this was the right amount of food including sharing a dessert!


Service
- Everyone on staff was very kind and attentive, but I think the restaurant was just extremely busy. Our table was 20 minutes behind our reservation because the couple before us was eating slowly. My waiter also forgot about a drink I ordered.

Ambiance
We went at night, and it's got the dim lighting and romantic vibe with candles. High and lofty ceilings. The seats are pretty close together though, so be prepared to be able to hear conversations next to you. There's also a cafe/wine bar in the back that has more casual vibes, but I don't think you can order food there during dinner service. It's more a place to wait while you are waiting for your table to open up. 

Would definitely recommend -- great date night spot. Make sure to get a reservation!

I saw a reservation at Lilia and jumped to take it. I have previously been to Misi and Fini but had yet to try Lilia. If you go you must get the focaccia. I was hesitant to get it, as it is on menus of so many NYC Italian restaurants. But this focaccia was different. It was warm and fluffy but so crunchy at the same time. The spring onion butter complimented it perfectly.

We tried the Radicchio salad as well, which I would skip next time, good but nothing special.  Our mains were the black bass and agnolotti. The bass was good but again, nothing out of the ordinary. I love the agnolotti. It was salty and sweet and savory and melted in your mouth. I thought Lilia was great, but for the bread/pasta. We ended with the gelato dessert finished with olive oil and salt. I loved the herbaceous, peppery olive oil paired with the cold, sweet gelato. In all, for me, the vegetable and pasta forward menu at Misi was preferable.
Excellent food, service and ambiance. Absolutely a must if in NYC, try almost everything on the menu its worth it!

This is a cute little restaurant in Brooklyn! The food was great and came out very quickly. Definitely very hard to get a reservation but is totally worth it. The restaurant was not overcrowded or tight for space which was incredible and unlike other very popular restaurants. I would definitely go back here!

I don't normally like to leave bad reviews but our experience at Lilia yesterday really left a bad taste.

At the outset, our server apologized about the building being cold and drafty and offered us complimentary hot lemon water. We didn't mind that at all as we were looking forward to the food and went on to order 5 dishes for 2 people based on their suggestion. 

The leek focaccia with garlic butter was very tasty and that got us excited for the anti pasti and main courses but what followed was a complete letdown:
The grilled prawns had a spicy Cajun flavor that seemed at odds with the bread we just had. The mafaldini was dry, salty and very undercooked (not al dente). It was like chewing on rubber. The rigatoni sauce was bland and felt like tomato purée with no seasoning. The agnolotti looked heavy but was surprisingly light and flavorful. The sheep's milk cheese inside was delicious and unexpected. We couldn't finish a single pasta we ordered in spite of having walked in with a large appetite primarily because the first few dishes were so disappointing.

I understand that all restaurants have good and bad days so I wouldn't have bothered writing this review but that night my husband also complained of a really bad stomach ache which I can't help but attribute to the food we ate - the prawns I believe, since I barely ate those.

P.S. great service though.

The kitchen staff is obviously very technically skilled, however the 3 pasta dishes we ordered (agnolotti, mafaldini, and rigatoni) were completely lacking in flavor. At this price point, I expect the food to taste good.

What in the world -- this place has all the good reviews of the world but it's not good ya'll. It's bland - I have been all over Italy and had food that was stunning .. this ain't it. What the hell was it that I ate . Bland pasta with a bland sauce -bland pasta with bland cheese .. child please -- that's not good. Even the wine wasn't so great. I have travelled alll over Italy. I know good Italian food and that ain't it

First off, love the ambiance!! It's perfect for a date night or catch up with a friend you haven't seen in a long time. The service was also great, our waitress was super helpful in recommending which dishes to try. We also had a lovely red wine recommended to us that we both really loved!

On to the food, so we started with the roasted squash. That was so unique, great crispy texture and the pesto on top really brought it all together. We shared the rigatoni, mafaldini, and agnolotti pastas. We really loved the rigatoni, it had a bit of a kick to it which was nice. The mafaldini was okay, too pepper-y for our tastes and just dry. And the agnolotti was probably my favorite pasta, it was so good!! 

We also shared the sea bass and you shouldn't skip it. It was perfectly cooked and just incredible.

I really wish that I could give 5 stars, but how do you run out of the agnolotti? Everything we ate was truly amazing. We ordered the focaccia, mussels, grilled artichokes, cacio e pepe balls, malfadini, spaghetti limon and the leg of lamb steak. Everything was really good. All I would change in the agnolotti instead of the spaghetti limon.

Amazing service and food! We were fortunate to snag a last minute resy with our cousins. Everything we ordered was great - we ordered 2 apps, 5 pastas and 2 desserts to share amongst 4 people. Our favorites were the Whole Artichoke and Roasted Squash appetizer. For pastas, we loved the Broccoli Pesto Gnocchi, Sheep's Milk Agnolotti, Rigatoni Diavola, and of course the Pink Peppercorn Mafaldini. The Olive Oil Cake was good like L'Artusi, but the Apple Crisp was out of this world - famous perfect amount of sweetness and the crust was delicious.

The. Best. Food. 
Literally compares to the food I've eaten in Italy. 
Definitely more on the special occasion ranking since it's hard to get a table and on the pricy side, but SO worth it, hands down my favorite restaurant in Brooklyn. The atmosphere is quiet and romantic, great for a date. And the service is great, they offer wine tasting prior to ordering a glass and are great with clearing the table and resetting utensils before the next course. If you go, MUST order the malfaldini, clams, and get TWO of the garlic bread (before they sell out for the night)!!!

If you have some extra extra money to spend it's worth coming to once. The service is really top tier in our experience.  They course the meals, you take your time, it's a really a lovely time and you will spend a minimum of two hours here (depending on how much you order).  Everything is typically made to share.  There flavors are very unique.  I would absolutely PASS on the Agnolotti.  I think you have to be a cheese enthusiast to really like the flavor of sheep's milk cheese.  That was a no for us.  I couldn't eat it. The Malfidini was good, def a unique flavor you wouldn't typically get for pasta. Grilled prawns  a YES, Mussels a YES.  We ordered the olive oil cake for dessert, SO GOOD.  And we ordered a dessert I can't remember the name of but it was a gelato with bee pollen.  The bee pollen is a distinct flavor so I'll leave it up to your discretion to try!

If I could give 3.5 stars, I would. Mostly because of how ridiculously difficult it is to get a reservation. The hype this place has isn't worth the quality of food, hot take. But to have reservations fill up a month in advance, that creates high expectations for what you'll experience. For me, it felt very average.

Service: 5/5
Great service, very attentive. My friend who was meeting me was running late. They didn't make me feel rushed, allowed me to sit at the table before she arrived. All in all, couldn't ask for more when it came to the service.

Atmosphere: 3/5
It's unfortunate that resys are so hard to book, how are you supposed to predict the weather a month out? If you book for outside seating and it ends up raining, they'll cancel your resy and rebook you. Which unfortunately happened to me. I wish the outside seating was a little more accommodating for different weather situations. 

Food: 4/5

Cacio e Pepe Frittelle: 5/5
Chefs kiss. Delicious. Get them. Of course it's delicious, what fried gooey cheesy thing isn't?

Little Gem Salad: 4/5
It was an enjoyable salad. Not one I'd think about and desperately need again. Wasn't bad, wasn't anything out of the ordinary.

Italian Broccoli: 5/5
May have enjoyed this the most out of everything. Which is funny, because I don't remember the last time I had a meal with pasta, and preferred the broccoli.

Mafaldini: 3/5
The pink peppercorn was an interesting addition! But that was it, otherwise it was a bit dry and didn't have many other flavors to compliment the peppercorn.

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti: 3/5
I was most excited about this one and most let down. It looked like it would have more flavor than it actually did. The filling didn't feel as lush as it looked.

Olive Oil Cake: 4/5
The fresh cream and figs took the cake on this, literally. The cake was good, but wouldn't have been as satisfying on its own. Together it was quite delicious. They added a little candle since a birthday was mentioned, cute touch.

Would I return? No. Am I glad I tried it? Maybe. I've had much cheaper Italian meals in the city that I'd rank higher than Lilia.

A while back my friend and I dined here for a memorable Italian meal. The vibe of the this place is bright and beautiful. Reservations can be tricky to get but not downright impossible. The decor is industrial but charming w small touches like candles and flowers which makes the dining experience quite lovely. I especially love the open kitchen concept so you can see the chefs creating your food. 

We started off with bread which was mind blowing. The butter that came with it was amazing, appropriately salty and the perfect accompaniment. We ordered the artichoke as well - this dish was my favorite because it was a whole artichoke chock full of parmesan cheese and butter. We worked diligently to remove the petals and enjoy this creation. I love a dish that's interactive and this was exactly that. 

The star of the show was the sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti, of course. Beautifully made ravioli, tossed in a sweet honey saffron sauce. The tang and saltiness of the cheese paired w the sweetness of the honey and aroma of saffron - a marriage made in heaven. If you are dining here DO NOT miss out on this dish. A lot of other Italian restaurants continue to crop up around the city but Lilia will always be a cult favorite and rightfully so! A part me of me does wish that every dish had a flavor profile that would mean to wow. While the food is undoubtedly great, I don't necessarily think everything on the menu is memorable for life like the agnolotti. I would like to see more variations of those sort on the menu. That being said, this place is still very well worth the trip.

An abominable restaurant in which you can freeze to death while they prepare lukewarm spaghetti. The artichoke monstrosity of an appetizer tasted like they used Kraft shredded cheese and took a piss on it. Wouldn't recommend this place to my worst enemy. Caveat emptor.

Awesome spot that is really good, might be a tad overhyped but still really good. Best thing I ate was the ricotta lemon toast app. Man that was so delicious. The Instagram famous pasta was good and is also worth getting. The other stuff was just good. Overall great ambience and vibe.

mAN it's hard to get a reservation here bUT if you're down to eat dinner at 4:45 PM, it's possible!

We went on a Thursday night and first off, the neighborhood and restaurant 
are both lovely. The ambiance is quiet and the staff was super friendly too!

In terms of food, it was all delicious but there were some absolute knock-outs! The leek focaccia was sO flOOfy and warm and mM yummy with the leek butter. The sheep's milk agnolotti was another truly delicious dish and had such an airy filling (in the best possible way). The pasta was so soft and the subtly sweet honey sauce was oH so yummy. We also got the lamb fettuccini with tomato sauce which was a bit more generic but nonetheless enjoyable. 

Overall, an amazing experience and I definitely want to go back to try more dishes!

We were finally able to snag a last minute reservation the other night (s/o to Resy notifications) and had a lovely time at Lilia. The ambiance is quaint but polished, and the staff was very knowledgeable when it came to reccos. To start, we shared the Cacio E Pepe arancini, baked clams, and little gem salad. The arancini was decadent and delicious and we loved the dressing on the little gem salad, but thought that the clams could've had more flavor. 

Pasta wise, we opted for the Lemon Spaghetti, Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, & Spicy Lamb Fettuccine. The lemon spaghetti was my favorite of the trio, by far. It had such a lovely mix of fresh flavors, and somehow felt light. The agnolotti is worth getting a side of to share - it's a relatively smaller dish, but very rich. We thought that the fettuccine was the most underwhelming - it really wasn't flavorful and the noodles seemed over cooked. 

Overall, we had a great meal but I'm not sure if it's worth all the hype.

Managed to snag a lunch reservation and went with my roommate. The food was solid but a little mediocre for how hyped this place is. I personally prefer Misi, their sister restaurant.
-Mafaldine: 6/10 Good but nothing special.
-Scallops: MUST ORDER. they were my favorite dish. a little pricey for what you're getting but the yogurt and flavor in this dish is amazing
-Cacio e pepe fritelle: 5/10 a little too much carb going on. would pass on this

My best friend had glowing reviews about Lilia and recommended it (amongst a few other spots in Brooklyn) while I was looking for a place to celebrate my boyfriend's birthday! It was close to the Williamsburg Hotel (where we had tickets to an event) and the menu looked incredible so it was the obvious choice. Known for their wood-fired seafood and hand crafted pasta, the restaurant offers an upscale aesthetics with a casual vibe. 

I was a little worried when I couldn't land a reservation on Resy and when no one answered the phone after calling a couple of times. Post googles and reading an article on the Infatuation titled "Where To Go When You Can't Get Into Lilia" I figured I should just put in a reservation elsewhere.     But day later Lilia called back and had an opening for the time and date I wanted. (Phew!!) 

The first thing you notice about Lilia when you walk in is the ambiance. It's romantically dimly lit and the soundtrack -- a mix of the buzz of people talking and the bustle in the kitchen, which you can peek into, created a space that felt welcoming and lived in. Nothing stuffy or uptight. The staff was extremely attentive and provided great recommendations on how to navigate the courses.

We started with the leek focaccia with green garlic butter (honestly, I could have eaten this all night!). The butter was rich and flavorful and the brea, flaky and warm. Next a palette cleanser with the little gem lettuce salad to prepare us for the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti with honey and the Rigatoni Diavola. The sheep's milk pasta definitely had great flavor but it may have been a bit too sweet for me. (In full transparency, I'm not the biggest sweet and savory fan) The rigatoni sauce was good but the pasta was a little undercooked. 
We ended with the grilled lamb steak which was cooked very well but maybe a little too much pepper. 

This place wins when it comes to ambiance, service, the focaccia and salad but the pasta and steak were just okay for what I heard about it.
SO DELISH! Everything was so tasty and the ambiance is perfect for a date night. The food was so fresh and the staff was very friendly!

Man oh man. With a cool staff and romantic ambience, Lilia was a fun little treat. 

1. Broccoli - the broccoli was salty and lemony but also a biiitttt cold? Personally wish we got something else but my friend rly enjoyed it
2. Agnolotti - yep, the infamous agnolotti. So delicious, creamy, perfect, etc. Need this in my life everyday
3. Spaghetti - lemony and nutty, the spaghetti was affirmed to be one of the favs by our waiter. Again, I personally wish we got something else
4. Italian job gelato - this had allllll the great and amazing flavors in one cup. I thought the gelato was too sweet (even with the oil and salt and herbs to help counteract). But! Still worth it
5. Olive oil cake - just a no :/ 

Overall- although some dishes didn't wow me, I felt like the atmosphere, the staff, and both the Agnolotti + gelato made Lilia worth the trip. I'd like to go again to try some of their seafood dishes.

Despite the hours devoted to checking resy to try to get in, I was pleasantly surprised that they were able to get me and my husband a table just by sending a simple email and letting them know that this was the only place I really wanted to eat during my trip. I definitely did not hold back when ordering (although they suggest 2-3 dishes per person, I don't think that's really the case, cuz ya girl can eat and I was STUFFED).

Prawns - very delicious and incredibly messy, but the warm/wet towel made this PA girl feel extra fancy.

Focaccia with green garlic butter - this was oddly my favorite dish of the night. So simple, but so good. I'm really bummed I can't eat this everyday.

Radicchio salad - Ordered this after seeing Katie Lee rave about it on instagram. The hazelnuts added an extra special touch however I had some trouble finishing it due to how much acidity was in the vinegar.

Fettuccini with spicy lamb sausage - really delicious pasta. Pretty simple and feel like I could make this at home (sounds liek a toxic trait, but I really think I could). Although this is delicious, this can likely be skipped and copycatted pretty easily in your own kitchen.

Mafalla - despite my husband calling this a "stupid noodle" I really liked it and the cream sauce was not too heavy. The pasta was al dente and had great flavor.

Roasted chicken - this was really yummy but very difficult to eat. It was hard to get the meat off the bone, but the flavor was incredible. The potatoes were a little undercooked though and we ended up only eating a few bites of those and leaving the rest. 

Olive oil cake - this cake was so simple, yet so decadent. Really unique flavor and paired perfectly with a decaf cappuccino. 

Worth the hype :)
So good and highly recommend! Food and service is amazing. We had a 4:15pm reservation on a Saturday and the restaurant was lively, but not too packed.
So expensive and really bad. I was incredibly disappointed. Took my partner here for a birthday dinner and it was flavorless. Very dissatisfied. Never recommending it.

The sheep milk cheese pasta was delicious melt in your mouth. The other pasta I didn't think it was worth it. However their seafood dishes are delicious. The scallops are yummy. The clams are delicious they got the seafood dishes right. The olive cake is too strong or too much of olive oil. The other desserts are delicious.

The famed sheep's milk-filled agnolotti from Lilia caught my eye from a Tiktok, and I knew I had to try it. From previous reviews and resy, it looked to be difficult to secure a reservation. My friend and I came early evening on a Tuesday and were able to be seated at the bar. I would recommend coming early on a weekday if you don't have a reservation!
The restaurant sits itself in a former auto body garage with tall ceilings and dark wood accents. It's pretty dim inside with candles lit -- perfect for a romantic vibe. 

We started off with the Housemade Mozzarella Garlic Bread with Lemon and Bottarga. As the carb-lovers we are, we loved this appetizer. Small amounts of bottarga adorned the cheese, which was a really nice balance of salty and savory flavors with the slight tart sweetness of lemon. 

The Sheep's Milk Agnolotti did not disappoint! Soft pasta combined with the sweet notes of saffron and sun dried tomatoes really put together this dish. Would love to try more dishes next time.

Oh man, such a disappointing dinner and experience.  Just not at all what it was when I went years ago, despite being a lot of the same dishes.  Overall, I just felt like there were flat flavors, as well as off ones in one case, and the service fell a little flat too.

First of all, since people talk a lot about how difficult it is to get in, I will describe how we did.  My buddy put our name in for two at about 630 on a January Wednesday.  They told us 715 at the bar.  We returned at that time, and were seated promptly.  Didn't even try to get reservations because it seems impossible.

We started with the mozzarella.  I'm not a huge fan of this in general, but setting that aside, I thought the portioning was weird and the seasoning.  Specifically, I would have liked about twice as much bread--which was delicious--and half as much salt.

The bagna cauda was a home run dish.  Fun and delicious.

I said to my friend, "we have to get the grilled clams, clams are always good."  I was proven wrong.  Heavy bread crumbs and heavy vinegar hot sauce.  Overpowered clams.

"Grilled" artichoke was mushy, like steamed into oblivion, and also overpowered with bread crumbs and cheese.

Agnolotti was pretty good, with one weird taste.  It was rich, but not too much butter, and the seasoning was quite nice.  Loved the dried tomatoes on it.  But it just tasted a little off, like a soapy dishwater taste.  Probably a fine dish and that it just hit me wrong.

Lamb steak seemed cooked all right, but was nearly flavorless.  Adding some salt help a little, but in the end, enjoyed the garnish more than the meat.

Negroni was good, as was a glass of barolo, but the latter was $28, so it needed to be.

Aggressive hospitality.  Kind of in your face with descriptions of the food--robotic recitations when delivering dishes--and answers to questions, like, "only the barolo is served at cellar temperature" like how dare you expect the other $20 reds to taste right.  On the other hand, they paced our dishes very nicely and didn't rush us at all.

I like the atmosphere there, but on the other hand, a little drafty by the door where they put us.

Prices overall aren't terrible, especially because servings are generous.

So not all bad, and tough to decide if this is a 2 or 3 star review, but ultimately, "could have been better" better describes my experience.

As we all know, getting a reservation here can be quite difficult- however, I was very excited when I was able to score one a few weeks out. When the day arrived I was very excited to visit and I my expectations were exceeded. Places like Lilia (hard to get in) can be a hit or miss for me but this one was everything you've heard about and more. 

From the moment my party and I walked in, the staff was gracious and gave us a warm welcome on a cold NYC evening. As we were directed to our table, I was already thinking about ordering some of the popular items I had read about. The server gave us some recommendations on the best shareable dishes since we wanted to order dishes we could share. 


We ordered the Milano Sour and the G&T to get started. For the cocktail snacks, we ordered the Cacio e Pepe Frittelle and the Housemade Mozzarella. Both were delicious, however, the Cacio e Pepe was my favorite of the two. I loved that it was a bit crunchy on the outside and tender on the inside. For the little fish section we ordered the Cured Sardines which was prepared with Capers, Dill on Fettunta. Out of all the little fish dishes this one in particular was the one I was looking forward to and it was really good! 

We skipped the big fish and went straight into the Primi. We knew we were going to order the Mafaldini (so many people recommended it) however, we were undecided between the Fettuccini with lamb and the Sheeps milk cheese filled Agnolotti. The server said the we could order both, since the portions were small and we decided to go with her suggestion. I really can't remember the last time I had 3 different pastas at a restaurant but I am so glad we did. All 3 were obviously unique in their own way but somehow complemented each other nicely. My favorite of all 3 was the Sheeps milk plate. It was just *chef's kiss*. Words just can't describe how delicious it was. 

I am so looking forward to booking another reservation in the near future and trying out some of their other dishes. I highly recommend Lilia if you are looking for an amazing dining experience; just make sure to book that reservation well in advance and you'll be good to go.

I went around 4PM on a Monday. The service was fresh and quick. Super chill vibe. The Focaccia with Green Garlic Butter blew my mind. The Agnolotti is a must. I would probably try the Mafaldine over the Fettuccine next visit. Sadly we didn't have room for dessert, but plan to try some sweets from the Lilia Caffé another day!

We were finally able to get a reservation at Lilia this weekend and were so excited to try it after hearing rave reviews on it. We arrived a bit early hoping our table would be ready earlier, but it turned out our table wouldn't be ready until around 10 minutes after our reservation - they suggested we go to the bar around the corner to wait.

To start, we got the housemade mozzarella and the cacio e pepe fritelle. The mozzarella came with a delicious garlic bread, but I wish it came with 2 pieces of the bread given the amount of cheese we got! I liked the salt mixture on top as well, though my partner felt it was a bit too much salt. The cacio e pepe fritelle were much larger than we expected and quite good, but a little peppery for my taste.

We then got the Agnolotti and Mafaldi for our main dishes. The agnolotti was DEFINITELY the star of the show. It had such a light and fluffy texture and the saffron sauce had a very subtle sweetness that really complimented the rest of the flavors. I'm not typically a fan of sundried tomato, but it went very well with the agnolotti. I really enjoyed the texture of the mafaldini, but this dish also had a bit more cracked pepper than I was expecting so it wasn't my favorite. 

To end the meal, we got the Italian Job gelato which was a creamy vanilla topped with olive oil, honey, sea salt and fennel powder. It was absolutely divine.

Because we finished our starters (those fritelle were larger than expected!), we couldn't finish our pasta and got the rest to go. When they packaged it up, they put both pastas in the same box as opposed to separating them - I would have preferred they ask before assuming we would want to meld the flavors together! 

Overall it was a great experience, but I would rather return to their sister restaurant Misi.

Lilia comes up in almost "must try restaurants" list in NYC, and you can imagine how hard it is to get a reservation here as a result. I managed to snag a prime time weekday dinner reservation for my boyfriend's birthday here after refreshing the page right at 10am! 

Shoutout to the hostess because we were about 20 mins late because of bad weather and slow trains-- she held the table for us and gave us our full 2 hour time slot!

The service was very good-- timely and not overly attentive. I asked the waiter to order a surprise dessert for the end and he handled it perfectly! 

We opted to get cocktails for drinks-- we got the Select Spritz and Rome with a View. Rome with a view was quite good (4/5); i thought Select Spritz tasted a bit chemical-y but still pleasant. 

For food we got: 
Focaccia - 5/5: I've never had round focaccia before! I will be making it my life's mission to recreate the texture of this focaccia. It was crispy on the outside and super soft and bouncy on the inside. The leek butter was flavorless in my opinion, but the parmesan seasoning on the bread itself was delicious! 

Italian Broccoli - 3/5: the Italian Broccoli is steamed and topped with loads of parmesan and lemon. The flavor profile of this dish is great, but I do wish the broccoli was charred to some extent- the overall texture of this dish was just soft, I wish it had some crunch in it. 

Malfadini - 4/5: the pink peppercorn flavor that lingers in the folds of the malfadini pasta is incredible! I liked both the texture and flavor of this dish a lot. 

Agnolotti - 3.5/5: i'll start by saying the first bite of this pasta is really really good. The sheeps milk cheese is creamy and the pasta is soft. After that though, I was looking for some sort of bite or acidity to balance out the richness of the cheese. Definitely a good one to split for sure! 

Olive oil cake - 4/5: we would've enjoyed this more if we weren't super full! I liked how this cake wasn't overly sweet. Very heavy on the whipped cream! 

Overall: Lilia was good! However, considering the hype and how difficult a reservation is to get, I left wanting more from them. No dish left me in awe, and no flavor seemed extremely original. I enjoyed my time here, but not sure I would go through the effort of getting a reservation again.

Average at best. I can't understand the hype around this place. The rigatoni tomato sauce you could easily make at home. Same with the mafaldini. Trader Joe's frozen Cacio e Pepe but less spicy. The Agnolotti is sweet and is okay. Do not fall into the hype there are so many better Italian restaurants. So many. The staff was extremely nice and attentive so giving this 3 stars for the staff

I wrote this review a few years ago but never posted it:

Came to this spot about a month or two ago with my wife on a day out. Realistically it's somewhat pricey compared to the absolute average of all restaurants and the portions are a bit smaller than what you might expect, but the quality, freshness and taste ABSOLUTELY make up for it. 

We started with the focaccia as an appetizer. It comes with a super tasty green butter that we couldn't get enough of. The gnocchi was refreshing and light (triple recommended on a hot summer day). The clams were well seasoned and cooked to perfection. We topped it off with an ice cream as well!

I missed fresh Italian cuisine so much and was so happy to know that Lilia lives up to the hype. We started with the foccacia, which leans too salty but is still great with the pesto ? butter and has a garlicky punch. The agnolotti was a star; love how the tomato is so sweet and the creaminess. My favorite was actually the fettucini because of the pasta texture; since it's fresh, it snaps differently than pasta at other restaurants. Earns 5 stars due to freshness of pasta, I liked the creativity; I'd just say although dessert was also good, a bit more work can go into making it great (olive oil cake is good but can use a little more detail, same goes for the gelato but overall fine)
Good attentive service, and a nice, elegant ambiance, perfect for a date night or anniversary.

Our distinguished server was Max.  He was well-informed, knew exactly how to describe the flavors and textures of the meals and made on point recommendations without imposing his opinion.  The entire staff was always aware of what was needed at the table and their timing was impeccable.
The pasta was perfectly cooked and there were flavor combinations that I thought would not work on paper, but the gastronomic gods had different ideas of this full moon evening.

3.5 stars, rounding up to a 4 because the ambiance in the restaurant is lovely. However, I was not impressed with the food given how hard it is to get a reservation here! Everything we got here was good but not much better than the average Italian restaurant in NY, I don't really understand the hype. I think the temperature of the dishes might have been off as the pasta we got was a bit cold/lukewarm. I will not be going through all the trouble of getting a reservation to eat here again!
I think this place used to be better. At least I had a better dinner experience here vs brunch.

Food: 3.5/5
For dinner, we ordered the rigatoni, the fettuccini and the agnolotti. Everything was uniquely prepared. The rigatoni was fresh and al dente but not remarkable. We thought the fettuccini was on the salty side. The agnolotti was  probably the most memorable dish and had a creamy umami flavor.

Overall, we were a bit underwhelmed considering we had high expectations after experiencing Misi.

Service: 4/5
The service was great. Our waiter was very attentive and took care of us all night.

Ambiance: 4/5
Lilia is much more laid back compared to Misi. Lots of wood decor and a bit more rustic. Casual yet romantic.

I am going to call this experience the "Theater of Food". 

I have been looking forward to eating at Lilia, so much so that i brought my mom, dad, and 91 year old grand who came straight from Italy. 

We made very clear to our server that because of allergies and different wants we will be ordering separately, without sharing. 

Right off the bat, the server lets us know that the chef is "particular about how the food gets out."

This is when the ridiculousness starts. So bad we actually started laughing.

My grandma and my mom have to watch me and my dad eat two salads for 20 minutes. They were so vinegary that we probably got first degree burns. 

Then, my dad and I have to watch them eat prawns, their main course, for 20 minutes. 
At this point we remind the server that there is no point in holding the pastas back because those are our mains, and we would like to all eat at the same time. Nothing. 

After 20 minutes, my dad gets his pasta, and they still bring 4 sharing plates, even after we reminded them again that we won't share. 

Here, we all watch my dad eat his pasta and wait for another 15 minutes until my pasta comes. At this point, all my family has the pleasure of watching me eat my main while they are all done. 

They didn't say sorry or acknowledge that we all watched each other eat individually. 
The pasta was actually not even that good, or at least not worth the experience. 

Unless you love watching each other eat like at a food theater, I suggest you pay visit to the hundreds of better Italian restaurants in NYC and Brooklyn. 

Food: 5/10
Service: 2/10

The food we had wasn't amazing it was just decent.  The focaccia was the only item that was actually really good.  The mafaldini, the sheeps milk agnolotti, and the drinks weren't great. The service, however, was amazing. Our waitress was extremely sweet and attentive. One of the best parts of the restaurant is that at certain seats you can see the chefs cooking.... On point in vibes but the food is forgettable.
Seriously average bordering inedible pasta for a place that has an insane waiting list. Really has no place being on any New York restaurant wish list. Extremely disappointing

Okay so this is one of those NY spots that are impossible to get a reservation at and luckily my roommate had Amex get one for us. We arrived at Lilia and the waiter was pressuring us to order and when we said we wanted three pastas he suggested getting something grilled instead, which was fine but throughout dinner he continued to overstep which took away from the experience. We started with the appetizers which were AMAZING, both the cacio e pepe fritelle and focaccia with sage butter were so unique and tasted spectacular. Then we got our three pastas:
Mafaldini- loved the texture of the pasta but the actual taste was underwhelming and didn't taste like much.
Ricotta gnocchi- we love gnocchi and pesto but again the taste wasn't really there and the texture of the gnocchi was harder and not chewy, kind of like cheese
Sheep's milk filled agnolotti- the most unique of the three, the cheese inside was super soft and melts into your mouth, the honey taste on the outside made it sweet yet savory with the cheese. This would be my favorite of the three but wasn't to die for. 

And for the desserts we got the olive oil ice cream which the waiter comped bc he wanted us to try it with the apple dessert, which we liked much more. Overall I'd say it's worth trying but not if you have to go through a lot for a reservation.

i was sooo excited to come here but was honestly unimpressed. the place itself is stunning but the food & service is mid. 

first of all, our server told us that we should order a total of 8-10 dishes. EXCUSE ME? we disregarded her ill advice and thank god bc the portions weren't minuscule so i don't know why she said that. then, she made us try to order more dishes when we didn't want to and asked my friend if he "needed help translating the wine menu" when he said no to drinks - major yikes. 

i'd come back for the leek focaccia alone but everything else is way too hyped. the lemon spaghetti was a close winner but tasted like it was missing something! i'm undecided on the dessert - the olive oil was throwing me off at first but it was kinda good by the end! 

+ leek focaccia & garlic butter: 5/5 
+ lemon spaghetti: 4.5/5
+ italian job: 4/5
+ grilled prawns: 3.5/5
+ ricotta gnocchi: 3/5
+ sheep's cheese agnolotti: 2/5

would i come back again? sure - i'd love to try another pasta. will i fight to get a resy? nope

author.name: Judy C.
author.location: Central City, Salt Lake City, UT

reviews.review: Knowing how hard it is to snag a dinner reservation I decided to come by for lunch instead. We showed up for Cafe Lilia around noon on a Wednesday. After walking in and not being greeted by the 4 workers present I asked if they could seat a party of two. The worker behind the counter said, "You can sit outside." It had been overcast and drizzling all morning so I said, "But it's raining..." as all of the seats and tables outside were clearly drenched and it was a cold November morning. She had repeated in an exasperated tone, "You can sit outside." No further communication or explanation for anything. Their website says they begin serving lunch at 11 but the workers seemed annoyed that anyone had shown up at all as they were busy relaxing. We ended up leaving and going to another spot a few minutes away. I suppose the spot's exclusivity leads to their employees superiority complex as well. They should just close entirely until dinner if they're going to treat people this way.

Ambiance was amazing! Very cozy & comfortable environment with top notch service. 

The host was very accommodating and did her best to get us exactly what we needed on short notice. Our table wasn't quite ready yet so we had some cocktails at the bar. 

Everything we had was flavorful & timed perfectly. It was difficult to choose what to order, just based off of Yelp pics & the servers recommendations. We would definitely return again!

An unforgettable birthday dinner! Leek focaccia with the most unbelievable green garlic butter, a massive grilled and stuffed artichoke, sublime agnolotti with saffron, dried tomatoes and honey, pappardelle with porcini mushrooms and chestnuts which first appeared on the menu that day, a simple but delicious and light spaghetti with lemon and pine nuts and delicato squash with walnut pesto.  The entire meal, without exception, exceeded my unrealistic expectations.  The atmosphere is relaxed and comfortable and the staff is friendly, attentive and well-versed on the menu.  Worth the wait for a reservation and am planning my return visit!

I used to love this place. 

They do not have a user friendly system for making a reservation and if you are to make a reservation, it will have to be too far in advance. 

They used to reserve their bar seating for first come first serve which I believe is required by NYC law. They have now moved to reserving half of their bar and have an arbitrary rule that they can't take a party of 3 or larger at the bar. 

Hence, one star. 

Will not be coming back here as I've come here twice, was the first in the line with my group when they open, and could not get seated.

I've been dreaming about coming back to Lilia since dining here 3 years ago. The restaurant gods were finally on my side when I was able to snag reservations recently! Service is always top notch and next level - Tobias was very knowledgeable, great sense of humor, super attentive and gave us the best suggestions. We ended up ordering their off menu dry aged rib eye, focaccia, lemon spaghetti with pine nuts, a seasonal pappardelle porcini, Italian broccoli, and the Italian job for dessert. 

From start to finish our meal was phenomenal. The flavor profile of every dish was so prominent and was the perfect balance of salt, fat and acid. I just couldn't get enough. I have dreamt about their Lemon Spaghetti dish for as long as I can remember, and it remains, til this day, my favorite dish at Lilia. The focaccia is to die for. My husband wanted us to get another order after we devoured the first lol I'll be adding this dish to my future dreams as well! The steak was a big boy - 32oz to be exact! It was cooked perfectly medium rare with garlic, butter and rosemary and served with a side of roasted smashed potatoes. We paired this with some greens, and went with the Italian broccoli, based on Tobias' suggestions and I'm so glad we listened! For dessert, we ended our night with the Italian Job to share and O M G -  hands down!!! THE BEST ice cream I've ever had. So good.. I didn't want to share the dessert at all lol 

All in all, thanks to Lilia my heart is happy and my belly is full. I will be dreaming about this meal until I'm able to get another reservation in the future!
Nothing special food wise. Very standard mozzarella , little gem salad. Artichoke was delicious but you can find better pasta at many other nyc restaurants.

Service is 100%. Amazing attention to detail. Only thing I could fault was my focaccia was a bit underproved. But the butter  AGNOLOTTI DELISH. My favorite part of the whole meal was the Italian Job dessert.
Delicious Breakfast and perfect coffee in the morning. Delicious dishes at night. Michelin star service and you can tell. Bright white and fresh with dim lights and a vibe.

I managed to snag a coveted reservation at this Italian restaurant and came here for an early dinner. The place is spacious, while the interior decor is lovely, with exposed brick. There is an elegant, yet casual, as well as inviting vibe. 

For the appetizer, we decided to try the Housemade Mozzarella on toasted garlic bread, lemon and bottarga. This looked impressive, but was just okay. The bread didn't taste that garlicky, but I enjoyed the mozzarella, which was a pillowy, creamy delight with just the right amount of saltiness. 

We chose 3 different pastas, even though I think 2 would have been enough. These are the ones we selected (in order of preference): Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Fettuccine with Lamb Sausage, and finally, Malfadini. 

The Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti came with a sauce made out of saffron, dried tomato, and honey. The Agnolotti was cooked perfectly al dente, with plenty of soft, mild tasting Sheeps Milk Cheese filling. The ingredients of the sauce mingled together very well, and was a delicate balance of sweet and savory, with pronounced honey flavor, making for truly mouthwatering bites.

Fettuccine with spicy lamb sausage, tomato passato, lemon, as well as sharp and yummy  Pecorino cheese. I was worried that the dish would be too spicy for me, but that wasn't the case. The fettuccine was cooked to a nice consistency and chewiness. The lamb sausage was tender, hearty and wonderfully well seasoned, while the tomato sauce was tasted bright and warm with a variety of spices. 

The last pasta dish that was served was the Malfadini with pink peppercorn and Parmigiani. This was a nice pinkish color, as well as incredibly, irresistibly cheesy. It was also quite oily. 

There were only 2 options for dessert. I ordered the olive oil cake with homemade whipped cream and cherries. Though it looked simple, the cake was delightfully moist, rich with a subtle olive oil flavor. The whipped cream was velvety smooth and had just the right amount of sweetness. 

Service was great. Our waiter was friendly and knew the menu well. Prices were on the higher side, so it is best to share a few menu items. Instead of having all pasta, I would've liked to try the Grilled Lamb Leg Steak and Black Bass. However, I am not in a rush to return.
Sadly we did not enjoy our meal here tonight. Every single dish was way over salted. We have all eaten at lilia a few times in the past and enjoyed it but this time was a huge miss.

Is this a great spot for pasta? Yes, but for how long I had to wait for reservation I'm not sure it's worth it. I would say the angolotti is definitely worth getting but I wasn't blown away by anything else.

Less impressed last night , my second time here. Gave us a nice small table in corner for 6  though larger would have been better. Way less impressed this time with the menu. Waiter was very sweet and drinks were pretty good. Food not so great honestly . Little gem salad was just blah nothing to rave about. My bass was good but once again nothing to rave about . It was just bass with too much pesto on it and some potatoes under it. I have had much better. My husband actually didn't like his pasta at all. We make better at home .as for dessert nothing much to choose from so we went with the olive oil cake . I have had this many times before and it's always light and airy. This cake was dense and heavy, not how olive oil cake supposed to be. I honestly think this restaurant is way hyped up more than should be.. just being honest

Does anyone else have dreams about this place or is it just me? Really, just me? Okay, cool.

Loves:
+ For an app we got the housemade mozz which was good, but the cacio e pepe frittelle is what I would go with next visit.
+ The pasta is SO good. We tried the mafladini and pesto gnocchi first, and for last we had the sheep's milk agnolotti which is truly the standout. I get an appetite every time I see a photo of it... my gawd.
+ Lovely staff. Our server really did us a solid but putting the agnolotti last in our order.
+ Space is beautiful. There are big windows too which bring in so much natural light.

Okay, now to get in!!! Unless you're mighty speedy you won't get a reservation through Resy and that's okay. My advice is to show up at 5pm on a weekday and you might be able to do a walk-in OR they will put you for a time two hours or so later which is splendid. Best for solo diners or pairs. 

Honestly, I'll be coming back here again soon and I cannot wait. Thank you for the amazing time, Lilia x3

This was our first time at Lilia, given the challenge to get a reservation. What is done exceptionally well is the service. The servers are very attentive and the waitress was extremely knowledgeable. Fresh plates for every course and they do a great job to make for a great experience.

We were told the food is the be shared and coursed out, for two people, we were recommended 7 items (which in retrospect seemed like a lot). We ended up ordering the focaccia bread, cacio frillettes, lettuce gem salad, raddichio salad, and theee pastas (gnocchi, mafaldini, and Rigatoni). The concern with coursing the meals what that the time between each meal was very long. Our entire dinner experience was almost 2 hours 15 minutes and the delay between courses means you get full a lot earlier that the back courses can't really be eaten. We packed everything to go. 

For the appetizer, the bread was well cooked and the green butter has a distinct flavor to it. The fritette seemed a bit dry from the Parmesan on top. 

Both salads were perfect on dressing. The pastas were discussed above that I wish the sauces had a bit more flavor. 

The to go gelato, though, was perfect consistent and flavor. We got the chocolate which had hints of salt and was clearly fresh. 

It was definitely worth going for the experience but would need some convincing to return! 

The texture of the pasta was fantastic and it was evident that each were fresh pastas. But it felt lacking in flavor, we expected a pop in each dish but felt

Finally got to try Lilia! Overall, I thought it was good but for the most part, nothing really blew me away. 

We started off with the radicchio and house made mozzarella. I thought the radicchio was a bit too sour for my liking but was still decent and the hazelnuts balanced the dish well. The house made mozzarella was also decent but nothing super special. The clams were next. They had a nice flavor and I enjoyed the breadcrumbs - they added a nice texture to the dish. 

Next we got the fettuccini with lamb and the sheep's milk cheese agnolotti. The fettuccini was pretty tasty and the noodles were very thin and were a nice compliment to the agnolotti since it was more savory and hearty. The agnolotti was definitely my favorite dish out of the appetizers and pastas. I liked the balance of savory and sweet since it had honey on it. It got a bit too sweet by the end but overall really enjoyed this dish! 

For dessert we got the olive oil cake and the Italian job gelato. The olive oil cake was decent but a bit too dry - I enjoyed that the whipped cream wasn't really sweet and helped keep the dessert light. The Italian job gelato was probably my favorite dish of the night!! I was surprised with how well the olive oil went with the gelato - it was a bit savory and sweet and just blended so well together. Very unique and delicious!!

I also just want to say that the service was really great as well! Our waiter warned us that some things might run out and went to check and got us the last sheep's milk agnolotti, which I was super grateful for because I was the most excited for that dish. He gave us some good recommendations as well.

The agnolotti was banging as the internet says. A must-get. My next tip is don't go with a gluten-free, dairy-free friend! This place is about CARBS and DAIRY! 

Here's my wanna-be food critic quick review: 
Grilled Artichoke - tasty but not unique
Roasted Delicata Squash - my date loved this, unique textured dish
Scallops - to die for, and I don't even like scallops
Bass was good, lamb was overcooked (to me) but date loved it - questioning his taste! 

Can't wait to go back and be a gluttonous pasta slob plus the scallops, sardines and mozzarella.

I waited 3 months for a reservation. 3 MONTHS. And when I finally reached my date I was so excited. I was greeted by someone who made it seem like I was ruining their day by simply announcing myself. "Hi my name is Drei, I have a reservation for 8" 
I basically got an eye roll in return. Was told to wait but felt in the way because there wasn't really a waiting area. We were finally told to wait outside in the cold. After 15 minutes they finally seat us. You would think after waiting 3 months we could have a table promptly at 8 and not be told to wait in the cold. We finally get seated BY THE BATHROOM. I was very upset about that. I'm my opinion there shouldn't be any tables near the batbroom door in a restaurant like this. I mentioned to the waitor who also seemed like I was in his way that we wouldn't mind waiting a bit longer for a table that wasn't by the bathroom. Even bar would have been fine. He said that wasn't an option. So we had our meal staring at 3 tables and the bar that stayed empty the entire duration of our stay. It was very unpleasant and frustrating. We were tucked away where there was no life in the restaurant. Meanwhile the other side seemed more ambient and lively. Finally oiur food comes and the pasta was so oversalted that as hungry as I was, I could not finish it. 2 people with very healthy appetites left food on the table which is so unlike us. If you like highly over salted food and being treated like you're a nuisance from the moment you step in, this is the place for you. I can't believe i waited this long for such poor service.

The agnolotti is absolutely driving this rating, as it is an unforgettable pasta; perfect sauce coating and it feels like little pillows filled with cheese. I'll come back just to order this. Id skip on the broccoli pesto gnocchi because I didn't think the flavors were all that special... I'd even say it's a miss of a pasta. We also got the pink peppercorn mafaldini, which is a solid option if you're looking for a second pasta as it is a very crisp, unique flavor; but also, nothing that blew me away. The house made mozzarella appetizer is loaded on salt and oil as a warning; yummy, but how can those flavors not be haha. And the olive oil gelato was a beautiful ending! So all in all, 5 stars and would come back again for the agnolotti and gelato :)

This review is solely for the olive oil ice cream. I have never had olive oil ice cream in my life, and I was hesitant to try. However, I heard great things about it, so of course, I had to try it. I was so pleasantly surprised by the flavors of the ice cream, and how much I enjoyed it. I definitely think this ice cream is worth the try at least once! I definitely do want to come back and try Lilia.

SERIOUSLY so good. Can't decide which is better-- Misi or Lilia?

Bests:
-Roasted delicata squash, walnut pesto, sage
-grilled artichoke, garlic, orange, parmesan, breadcrumbs
-all the pastas...yummm

Really good:
-grilled clams, calabrian chili, breadcrumbs
-Grilled lamb leg steak

Tldr; it was worth the 4-hour wait. GET THE SPAGHETTI. 

I wanted to eat here during my stay in Brooklyn, so I tried to get reservations online as soon as they were released -- nothing. So I signed up for the wait list; every time I got a notification that a time slot opened up, I went straight to the website but was too late. 

So we showed up at 5 PM, in-person on a Sunday, and asked to be added to the wait list. At 9 PM, we were finally seated and very excited! This restaurant is walking distance to plenty of shopping over in Wythe & 6th. (Madewell, Everlane, MUJI, and much more)

Because we waited so long, we were already full from another dinner, boba, and cocktails. Even though, we weren't hungry, the food was still delicious!

We only ordered one small dish as a starter, and it was excellent. Grilled prawns w/fennel pollen and lemon. The shells were crispy enough to eat whole, and the fennel pollen was so tasty! 

Pastas in order of favoriteness: 
1) Spaghetti w/pine nuts, lemon, parmigiano reg
2) Sheeps milk agnolotti w/saffron, dried tomato, honey 
3) Gorgonzola ravioli w/anchovy, garlic 
4) Fettuccine w/lamb sausage tomato passato, lemon, pecorino 

All four us LOVED the spaghetti. It's a must-order. 

I really liked the sheeps milk agnolotti, but it was too rich for others at the table. And no one was really wowed by the fettuccine, so I'd skip that dish next time. Service was great, I definitely want to eat here again.
Very delicious and unique pasta dishes. Great ambience and service. Honestly overhyped though. The appetizer - fried caccio e Pepe was not good.

Staff is great.  Well run.  Bones are great.  Beautiful space.  But man oh man.  The food.  Talk about over complicating it.  This place is the perfect example of just over complicating food.  And it's Italian.  How can you go wrong with Italian?  Well they did.  A plus for effort but in the end just ask yourself am I making good tasting food?  This place falls flat on its face.  I really wanted to love it here but alas it's just foo foo.  Very limited menu which I don't mind.  But go back to making good tasting food.  And don't worry about what other people say.

WOW. The food was pretty underwhelming. After trying for years to get a reservation, we finally managed a Saturday night table for 2. The atmosphere and staff were great. My drink, Rome with a view, was delicious, my husband's gin and tonic had great presentation. 

We ordered:
Delicata squash appetizer was delicious though a little rich
Artichoke heart appetizer was fine, not much flavor other than cheese
Scallop dish was not balanced, way too much yogurt sauce for 2 scallops
Agnolotti was delicious 
Gnocchi was dry, as if not cooked through, and the pesto was flavorless we had to send it back. The room temperature Trader Joe's gnocchi I had at our child's school pot luck was better.

We did not bother to stay for dessert.

Perhaps we missed the window where Lilia was the new must go to restaurant.
Incredible Italian spot in Williamsburg. I'll be dreaming of the leek focaccia with green garlic butter and sheep's milk filled agnolotti with saffron for years to come.
One of my favorite spots in Williamsburg! Very hard to get a reservation, but worth the effort.

Food was great but wouldn't recommend due to overall experience. After making a reservation a month in advance the restaurant canceled on us DAY OF, with no help other than an option to reschedule over a month later. After we arrived we waited 45 minutes for our appetizer (mozzarella toast) to arrive. It was delicious, but toast with fresh mozzarella doesn't take that long. It took another 40 minutes for our entrees to arrive and it was all ordered at the same time. Again, amazing pasta but wouldn't come again or recommend to others. Overrated for the experience as a whole considering the day of cancel and 2.5 hour dinner when it could have been much quicker

TLDR: The Agnolotti is a MUST order! 

Lilia is a quaint space with minimalist finishes and impeccable service. The restaurant was Michelin quality.

We started with the mozzarella which was served on a delightful sesame sourdough. The freshness and quality of ingredients really shined. 

I was hesitant about the pink peppercorn flavor but it felt like a very elevated cacio e pepe and the cook on the pasta was perfect. The gnocchi was a bit underwhelming but the sauce was fresh and vibrant. 

The star of the show was the Agnolotti. The combination the lightness of the sheeps milk and the savory sauce/sundried tomatoes was impeccable. We could not get enough of it.
