The olive oil gelato sounded odd but was beautifully creamy and fresh. A great way to round out the meal.

This restaurant was awesome.  I originally had a 4:15 reservation, when they texted that morning to confirm I asked if they had anything later and they moved me to 6.  We got there at 5:15 and we were seated by around 5:30. Both the host and manager were awesome and accommodating, especially since it was just me and my 5 yr old son.  We had the Cacio Fritelle, Little Gem Salad, Rigatoni, Agnolotti, my son had vanilla Gelato with Sprinkles while I had the Italian Job.  The food was awesome, no complaints with that or the service.  The main reason I am writing this review is because of the Rigatoni.  My 5 yr old son loves Rigatoni. when I saw it had some spice, I asked the waitress and she told me they couldn't make it more mild but that it was a popular kids option.  I will tell you that it was even spicy for me, and I am 46.  I would avoid the Rigatoni for kids completely unless they love spicy food.  The waitress offered to switch it out or bring cheese, so I have no complaints about the restaurant or staff being accommodating.  The whole purpose of this is just to warn parents of this dish who are bringing kids.  Even though the pasta was too spicy, both my 5 yr old and I loved the restaurant and would go back in a heartbeat.

getting reservations here was quite easy. took me about a month but the food was definitely worth the wait. everything was flavorful and tasted super authentic! i would definitely come back in the future. the staff was friendly and informative on what they had to offer!

The three of us had a reservation for 8:15 PM. We ended up getting to Lilia a few minutes early and had to wait about 20-30 minutes. This place was packed!

To start the dinner off, we all shared the following appetizers: broccoli, mussels, and fritelle. The mussels were really good. I would eat here again simply for those mussels. 

For entrees, the three of us ordered a total of four pasta dishes, including spaghetti, agnolotti, gnocchi, and mafaldine. I really enjoyed the agnolotti filled with cheese and the gnocchi. The main knock on this place is the small portions. Overall, the food is great, and Lilia is worth visiting.

It isn't very often that restaurants live up to their hype but Lilia absolutely does! It is super hard to get a resy so def check well in advance and take that 4pm if it's all that's available. We had a 4pm resy and we're worried we wouldn't be hungry enough to eat everything but they do a great job of spacing out the dishes. I think the absolute must haves are the focaccia, spaghetti and agnolotti. The only dish that I didn't love was the ravioli with Gorgonzola but that might be a personal preference since the cheese was a bit strong for my taste.

To start, the focaccia and cacio e pepe fritelle were delicious. Clams had nice flavor but overcooked and chewy. The pastas weren't memorable, places in the area like Le Fanfare do it better. Chocolate gelato came with a generous amount of toppings and was equally delicious. Olive oil cake was good too. Service was slow but attentive. Silverware and plates were changed after every course. Not totally worth the hype but glad we experienced it!

UPDATE TO MY PREVIOUS REVIEW...

It's been over a month and the trash and sludge situation has not changed. It is beyond repulsive. Missy and her partners have seen my previous posts, but apparently do not care. As i am sure thier parent Grove House does not care either.

It was really hard to get a reservation but finally got it. I must say I am glad we did!! Everything was spot on. A must try out of all dishes we got was the pesto gnocchi and focaccia with garlic butter. I didn't take a picture of the desert but we got the Italian job which is basically gelato, olive oil, honey, salt. I don't how but it worked and it was delicious. You just have to try it. Service was excellent, not sure why they are not a Michelin restaurant... but it was better than the some of the Michelin restaurants I have been to

The place is airy and modern and industrial. Typical Brooklyn. The menu was all in all well put together and simple but balanced. I had one from every part of the menu and the top dishes were obviously pasta then the appetizers then the meat. I would have given 5 stars but the lamb was average at best. It wasn't cooked properly so some parts were rare while other parts medium well. I was most impressed how the dishes weren't overseasoned like most of the other top Italian restaurants seem to do these days. Wine list left a lot to be desired but their corkage policy is excellent so I brought my own wine and was fine.

Just moved from Santa Barbara where food was my go to for any bad day and was worried about the amount of fast food vs good restaurants in ny. I'm impressed at level of taste the dishes here provide. Well done chef ‍

One of the best Italian restaurants I've been to! Each one of their pasta dishes tastes so unique and different and has an abundance of flavor. My personal favorite was the pink peppercorn one and the saffron one with the sheep's milk!! So creamy and you can seriously taste the freshness. I personally would skip on the pesto gnocchi next time. The corn seasonal pasta was good too but a little too sweet for my liking. 

Taking off a star since it was super hard to get a reservation (my friend and I called more than 90 times collectively) and ultimately got a reservation online but only for 5pm. Also they have strict rules where you have to order everything at once and can't anything later after you order, which was a bummer.

Wow. Totally worth the hype, totally understand why it's so hard to get a reservation here, totally understand why people from all over the city travel to the most random part of Williamsburg for it. Absolutely amazing pastas, and one of those meals that I walked away thinking about. I was told to try the Italian job dessert but didn't realize it's an off-menu favorite, so stuck with what was listed and still was not disappointed! Everything was amazing. The drinks were delicious as well (an aperol spritz and limoncello to go with dinner? sure). The agnolotti by itself was totally worth any frustration there might be with getting a reservation. And yes, it's very aware of how popular and good it is so they do not accommodate changes and moves very often but if you can find a decent normal-ish dinner time, don't hesitate to try and rearrange your schedule to make it work.

And again, Lilia didn't disappoint.
Great restaurant, best Italian food, amazing service!

Extremely disappointing food for how many positive reviews there are and recommendations I received to try this place

Got the cacio e Pepe frittelle, little gem salad, sheep milk agnolotti, and malfadini. Out of those, agnolotti was the best because of the strong garlic flavor. 

-Cacio e Pepe tasted overly salty and bland, textures were all wrong - would definitely pass and try out the focaccia. 
-Little gem salad was extremely salty and vinegary. Wanted something to cut the taste of the greasy and heavy feeling of pasta but this did not do the trick. 
-malfadini very mediocre. Heavy on the peppercorn which overtakes this dish. 

Several other pasta places in NY that you would be better off trying. It might be worth trying once if you want to say you tried Lilia for the sake of saying that..otherwise pass because it's truly not worth the trouble of trying to get a reservation here.

Easyyy 5/5! We were lucky to snag a reservation on resy (10am 30 days in advance) since we have been looking forward to dining at Lilia since moving to nyc a year ago! We got the clams and focaccia which were both incredible. All the pastas were great, the mafaldini and agnolotti were the best. Olive oil cake was our favorite of the desserts. Also very reasonably priced for a fine dining experience. Highly recommend and would definitely return!
The pasta never misses but if I had to recommend one thing it's the house made garlic bread with mozz and lemon. Phenomenal

I managed to snag an extremely last minute reservation for my birthday, and Lilia was the perfect place to celebrate. Our table was at 4:45pm and the restaurant was already in full swing when we got there. If you don't have a reservation, just get there as early as possible - the bar was still pretty empty and they had plenty of tables outside.

We started with their housemade mozzarella and grilled summer beans. The mozzarella was really decadent, and served on thick slices of bread with a little chili. The summer beans were very fresh, and tasted great with capers and mint.

The real stars of the meal, however, were the pastas. My favorite was the sheep's milk agnolotti - they were so pillowy soft and had a really strong saffron flavor. The mafaldini, their other signature pasta, had an excellent texture, and the simple butter, cheese, and pink peppercorn really let the pasta shine. We also tried their black bass, which was flakey in the best way possible and came with some of the best potatoes I've ever had.

They surprised me with a cup of their vanilla gelato topped with sprinkles for my birthday, and it was the perfect way to end the meal. The gelato tasted like incredibly fresh milk, and I couldn't stop eating it.

Thank you Lilia for an amazing meal!

We came to Lilia while visiting family in New York and loved it! We ordered everything to share with the table including the Cherry Tomato Focaccia, Little Gem Lettuce, Grilled Scallops, Grilled Clams, Rigatoni Diavola, Mafaldini Peppercorn, Spaghetti and Bass. Everything was wonderful, but the focaccia, scallops, and spaghetti were some of the favorites of our table. Overall, we enjoyed the experience. Great service, great drinks, great food, and great overall atmosphere. Highly recommend for anyone looking for great Italian food in the Brooklyn area.

Had an awesome time here! Our server, Rose, was so great she made the experience she gave such good recs and everything was amazing! We had the spaghetti on her advice and wowza I think it was the best dish we had. Everything was amazing and I can't wait to come back.

The food was amazing however, there was a table next to us that was so loud - we couldn't hear each other. The hostess knew it was bad and was going to have the manager ask the table to bring their voices down... but these people were friends of the owners. It was inconsiderate for all the tables around and produced a bad yelp review.

The food is definitely delicious but what stood out even more is the outstanding service. I had a 5pm reservation with my friend and she was running late but the hostess was still able to seat me while I waited for her. There were also a lot of empty tables indoors and outside at that time so I wonder if walking in would have been easier than trying to snag a hard to get reservation. When my friend arrived, she wasn't feeling well and the manager Samantha had the foresight to offer us a different table in the dining room instead of being seated next to a loud large group which we thought was so caring!

Onto the food -
Appetizers: Grilled clams, focaccia with green garlic butter and cacio e pepe frittelle. All were sooo delicious but my favorite was the focaccia. It was so crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside and unlike any other focaccia I've ever had. The garlic butter is green from blending in spinach and other vegetables that don't impact the taste but make a stunning color. The cacio e pepe frittelle were also very unique and also crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, almost like a hush puppy. I also appreciated the large portion of clams and perfect balance of flavors with the Calabrian chili. 

Entrees: sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti and a seasonal sweet corn cappelletti. Both were delicious and had perfectly balanced flavors. I usually prefer pasta with some meat but I was surprised with how much I enjoyed these vegetarian pastas. 

Dessert: blueberry tart and vanilla gelato with olive oil. I was skeptical about the gelato paired with olive oil but it was my favorite of the two. The olive oil was very high quality and flavorful and was a nice savory balance to the smooth gelato. 

Overall, we had a great dining experience here. If I had to chose, I'd say the standouts were the appetizers although the pastas were also delicious and freshly made. The service also felt personalized - will definitely be back!

Diverse and unique selection of pasta. The seasonal pasta entree, the Ziti, was out of this world. Four stars for the outdoor dining placement however. Did not want to be smelling the unappetizing subway odor all night.
Love this place so much! The pasta is great and I highly recommend trying it out. You can hardly get a reservation though.
Next to Boston or Italy this place has the best pasta! Super flavorful and fresh! Get the olive oil icecrem

- make that resey
- fills up around 6, after a 4pm opening
- cacio is good
  it's dense but not very heavy
  u likely never had anything like it
  all u need is one, but they serve 3
- great service
- scallops were just alright
- clams were just alright
  scallops and calms were both skippable
- fettuccini is great
- agnolotti was great
  fettecini and agnolotti were a great combination
- olive oil cake and tres ice cream were a fantastic complement to each other
- drinks were well made
- environment is bright and sunny

We had a rough experience with the service (normally the service is so good), but the manager Mary did a PHENOMENAL job making everything right. For us it's key that when a restaurant makes a mistake they own it and have an empathetic and reasonable conversation and Mary did that expertly. We really appreciated that, and the food was excellent as always!

I visited Lilia with my girlfriend and we received amazing service from the beginning to the end! Our time at Lilia was unforgettable. What we loved most about the menu was that it was simple and it felt like there were no bad options. We opted for a family-style approach to do our best and try everything. (I highly recommend family style). Our server Sophia was second to none! She had phenomenal food recommendations and amazing wine pairing suggestions. 

My girlfriend and I went in with an open mind and let Sophia guide us through the menu. From first cocktails to well-portioned antipasti, top-notch wining pairings, as much pasta as we could bare to eat, and an amazing soft serve dessert, nothing was a miss! Felt like everything we order was battling for first place. 

If I had to pick 1 stand-out item about Lilia, it would have to be the service and food knowledge that was demonstrated by the manager and staff alike. I know this will sound like hyperbole, but going to Lilia was a highlight of our trip to New York. At Lilia, they have the perfect marriage of amazing food AND award-winning service. Having a waitress who really knew the menu AND never missed a beat while being friendly, is hard to find. A huge shoutout of gratitude to Alicia and the restaurant you run. Lilia will forever be on my New York must-eat list and I cant wait to go back! Thank you for making our trip so memorable!

It isn't everyday that she agrees to go to Brooklyn much less to, drum roll, Williamsburg, there I said it, with its gentrified modern buildings that host some sort of little humans you barely see on the island, praise the lord.
The little gems came and went as forgettable, vinagre too much, flavor too little, same happened with the anchovy bruschetta that hosted some type of rolled cheese, was it butter?, killing the fish, again, this time in my mouth. 
Sadness was the spaghetti that even if al dente, not sure, were surrounded by an accidental sauce that gave them a campy runny texture. 
To the rescue came the agnolotti, with panache, an interesting filling and dried tomatoes on top, but yet , it alone couldn't Schwarzenegger the meal out of its suburban ditch. 
This was my second time at Lilia and I advertised it as Italian pasta coming to Brooklyn's rescue.  But maybe my memory tricked me, we were right out of COVID culinary lockdown, back then even plated dog food would be rewarded with our puppy eyes. Shalom.

Overall, my wife and I had a very disappointing experience at Lilia. Our food took absolutely forever to come out and when it finally did, it was cold. It got to the point where all excitement to eat at this restaurant wore off and we were simply waiting around (hungry) instead of enjoying ourselves. It was almost laughable. I would have sent the food back, but after waiting (there's that word again!) for so long that was simply not in the cards.

To make matters worse, I was drinking a tequila on the rocks when a member of the wait staff poured water in my tequila cup. While our server remediated the issue after noticing it shortly after (I didn't even bother saying anything at this point), it was not something you come to expect from a place with this reputation.

The outdoor seating (towards the back) was also nothing to write home about. Needless to say, I won't be back here. Plenty of other spots in Manhattan / Brooklyn to check out that are easier to get into and have better food.

Lilia in Williamsburg is the amazing sister restaurant to Misi serving hand-crafted pasta. For the pasta course we ordered the sheeps milk agnolotti with honey and saffron, lamb sausage fettuccine, and the mafaldini with pink peppercorn. We loved the incredible range of these pasta dishes from the rich lamb ragu sauce to the sweet and creamy agnolotti. It made it difficult to pick a favorite. For appetizers we ordered the little gem salad and the fragrant roasted leek focaccia served with green garlic butter. We were initially intimidated by the size of the focaccia but quickly proceeded to finish the entire loaf after tasting how perfect the bread was. We also enjoyed the grilled scallops served with yogurt sauce and topped with walnuts. For desert we ordered the vanilla and "Italian job" gelati, with the Italian job being a clear favorite with its unexpected mixture of flavors. The base of the dessert was vanilla gelati topped with honey, olive oil, sea salt, and a dusting of fennel pollen. This was an incredible meal overall made more pleasant by the cozy yurts the restaraunt offers as their outdoor dining option. A must-try place for all pasta lovers.

Expected nothing but the best from Lilia, Snd they of course delivered. I haven't been since around when it opened, but frequent their sister restaurant often, and was excited to be back. They saw and accommodated a note requesting quiet seating since my guest was deaf (this almost never happens, especially wo saying a word. They so so Apprechaite that). Our server was incredibly knowledgeable and friendly. Everything was insanely delicious. BUT the artichoke was the star!! I love when a place prepares their veggies as if they are as important as the pasta and nests. Can't wait to go back for it!

4 stars for the food, 2 stars for the service.

Listen, I can sympathize with many facets of the plight of the hospitality industry. I know there's a workforce shortage. I know there are supply chain issues. I know pandemic has driven a lot of places out of business. I know some customers are always going to be entitled jerks. Hell, I even wrote a book to help out local businesses.

But what I can't excuse is being lied to multiple times. I showed up an hour before my reservation in the off-chance they could move our reservation up. It was a no-go, which is understandable. The lady at the host stand told me to come back at my reservation time and my table would be ready. To be honest, I also popped in so they would know I was in the area since restaurants usually prioritize parties who are already present.

A quick beer later, and we returned at 8:45. This time, a young guy told us they were just cleaning our table. 20 minutes later, I went back in to ask, and it was the lady again. She said several tables just finished and they'd be ready for us within a few minutes. 15 minutes later, and we were finally called in. So if your math skills are up to snuff, we were seated 35 minutes after our reservation time. What's even the point?

We were already cutting it close with trying to catch the end of a show nearby, but that 35 minute delay meant we missed it entirely, which sucked. Not ideal timing on my part, but with Lilia, you take whatever reservations you can get.

Didn't help that we witnessed (who I can only assume was) the manager go out of her way to have tables set up outside for friends of hers, after they had already started putting furniture away.

The pasta, however, is spectacular. Unfortunately, they were out of the sheep's milk agnolotti, which we had our eyes on. Ended up getting the seasonal sweet corn cappelletti and the mafaldini with pink peppercorns. Portion sizes were kind of all over the place, and our waiter told us 5-6 dishes for 2 people is common (which would've been overkill). I love corn, so the cappelletti was great. Never had mafaldini before, but it's toothy and looooong. I've cooked with pink peppercorns before, and you can really taste the difference vs. black or green. Very distinct flavors.

We also got the grilled head-on prawns to start. Our server told us that the entire thing was edible, heads/shells and all. My friend had previously had this preparation at Lilia and started doing the same thing on the grill. The key is to get it hot enough so the exoskeleton gets crunchy enough. Unfortunately, the kitchen didn't seem to get the prawns hot enough because the shells were most definitely NOT edible. Great flavors though (with a little kick), and definitely appreciated the wet towels afterwards.

All the people we dealt with once we sat down were amazing, and I will in no way fault them for the restaurant management's faults.

At the end of the day, I'm glad we got to experience Lilia. It was on my pandemic bucket list, but could never time it right with reservations (and wasn't going to pay $250 a head for their AmEx bubble dining). All the pieces for a perfect meal were there, but they need to work out a lot of their issues.

Maybe I'll give Misi a try.

My wife and I came here for our anniversary and absolutely loved it. We had the Little Gem Salad, Grilled Clams, Grilled Scallops, Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Fettuccine, Lamb Sausage, Ricotta Gnocchi and the Italian Job. It's impossible to pick a favorite, but the Clams and Pasta dishes were especially great.

The service was excellent, they helped up pick a great bottle of wine and were knowledgeable and attentive. The vibe was right and they didn't rush us at all, despite being there for hours - there really wasn't anything else we could have asked for.

I was really happy to come to Lilia to celebrate a milestone: the food fit the occasion. While we enjoyed everything we ate, the roasted leek focaccia, green garlic butter alone is reason to come to Lilia. The service was wonderful. However, I really wish the outdoor seating was congruent with the rest of the experience to put it politely.

First visit to Lilia, and I'm already dreaming about when I can go back again. My friend scored a 4:45 reservation mid-week for the patio. It was surprisingly breezy and comfortable during the heat wave, with plenty of shade from nearby umbrellas. We were a group of three who love to eat, so we decided to go family style with our ordering so we could try as much as possible. My one friend has fined her often (lucky!) so we followed some of her recommendations. Do NOT miss out on the homemade mozzarella on garlic bread with lemon. We ended up getting two, which was an excellent choice. The Italian Broccoli with parmigiano, chili oil and lemon was bright and tasty with a nice little kick. For pastas, we went with the mafaldini, agnolotti, and a corn filled cappelletti...you must get that last one...the sweetness of the corn and the pairing of the sauce were absolutely divine. Finished out our meal with the Italian Job (vanilla gelato + olive oil...the pairing I didn't know I needed in my life) and the olive oil cake. Our server was incredibly attentive and let us take our time to savor every morsel. I definitely want to try some of their wines next time, and was very happy with their Aperol Spritz!

Oh no, it turns out Lilia can and does make mistakes. This was the case yesterday, as my radicchio salad was terrible...wilted and flavorless. We had one bite each and sent it back. This was not the same salad I get every single time. The lamb steak was also so unenjoyable. The cut was tough and somehow the temperature was cold, though the meat was also overcooked past medium rare, as requested and normally cooked. Soooo disappointing, as I enjoyed this dish so much last time. We should've sent it back, but we were over it. Lastly, the Italian Job was unavailable, as the machine was broken...Um, what???? (Literally, the main reason my friend and I decided to retry Lilia together since our combined birthday meal last year.) So upsetting that my third dining experience here was the worst so far...

Very rude poor quality hostess tonight 
I usually come in and hope to get a table and usually score a table - say 7/10 tries 
Tonight the dear hostess decided to be rude when I came in to ask if there's any chance a table is available for tonight or bar 
Her low level response was oh yeah sure I can put you in for some time in September - I was confused is she serious or mocking ? Yeah it's hot out tonight but you should be more patient 
Online reservations are never available so don't understand why she had to be this rude oh well hopefully we don't see her next time we try to come in for dinner

I've lived in Williamsburg for 7 years, going out everywhere we can, anytime we can, to support all our local restaurants, and have only been to Lilia once, right when it opened, around 2016. And it wasn't a great experience. The service was a little rigid, they were behind on our reservation keeping us waiting, and our swordfish entrée arrived partially raw. When we complained, they actually argued, insisting that's how their swordfish was meant to be served (it's not, swordfish is notorious for worms, it should never be raw).

Fast-forward a few years, and while no Michelin stars have ever been accrued to Missy Robbin's' mini Williamsburg empire, Lilia has become one of the hardest reservations to get in the neighborhood. However, this time I found Lilia to be a much-transformed, quite wonderful experience, both in terms of the food and service.

While I prefer Misi's more modern, open layout with a view of the waterfront, Lilia, in a converted auto body shop, has its charms. It's actually *very* Williamsburg circa 2016, with a wood beamed ceiling, relaxed open kitchen, and giant factory windows that look out onto Union Ave. They still have no place for you to wait when they are inevitably (this time only a minute!) behind on your reservation, forcing you to stand outside on the street. Lilia has a more intimate, narrow feel, the only downside being occasional bottlenecks at the two main bathrooms in back, and loud-voiced banker types in button downs right on top of you DISCUSSING THE MARKET and HAMPTONS TIME SHARES.

While the prices are bizarrely not displayed on their website, they are in no way outrageous. It was simply too hot for us to go in hard on any of their meatier dishes, but what we did sample was splendiferous. I do not recommend you leave Lilia without trying their housemade mozzarella, with lemon, on garlic bread or their mortadella filled tortelli, as these were two of the best things I've tasted in quite some time. But ALL their pastas were delicious, all their small vegetable plates were great, and the scallops were phenomenal.

Our server was both friendly and exceedingly informed. When I switched over from cocktails to a glass of wine halfway through the meal, I simply described what I was in the mood for, and a glass of exactly my mood appeared in front me a minute or so later. A very easy five stars to Lilia.

They do have lunch here, just in their café part, and it's a bit of a neighborhood secret. But their sandwiches and pastries are divine, you can grab an iced coffee, and sit anywhere you like outside.

Keep those Resy Notifys on, and you'll get lucky eventually.

This place has a special place in my heart. I've always wanted to eat here and it really lived up to the expectations. 

I love how sharable the plates are. Intimate enough for a 1 on 1 or with a small group. 

We tried a little of everything - total of 3 appetizers and 1 entree to share, dessert and a bottle of wine. Was the perfect amount of food for us two. 

We really enjoyed the orange wine. The service was outstanding. Every person that interacted with us was so kind and friendly.
Overrated. Pastas were cold, nothing special about the flavors. We got the agnolotti and the malfadini, and started with the cacio e pepe fritelle.

Ahhhhh, Lilia then.   Five stars do not seem nearly enough.   This place is so integral  to our story, it is the kind of place to take someone special in your life to create unforgettable memories.   There is something about it that borders on the mystical.   And I'm not talking about the universal acclaim that it draws; more so I am talking about what it means to each person who eats here as they create their own experience.   When you dine at Lilia, savor it.   Not just the food, ALL of it.

The atmosphere is super friendly.   There is seating both inside and al fresco (most of the year).   You wouldn't think that a restaurant located in a former garage could create such a casually elegant environment (is that a thing?) but it does.   From the bar seats, you can even watch the food being prepared.

The food here is beyond compare.   To fully enjoy the meal you are going to want to luxuriate over each bite from the hors d'ouvres to dessert.  Speaking of the former, we never pass on the focaccia; it changes season to season.  Do not miss the butter!   This time we opted for the scallops as well for an appetizer.   They were huge and prepared absolutely perfectly.   Although there are other main courses, the pasta here is the headliner, all handmade.   There are so many choices to try, but we always seem to gravitate to at least one entree of the angolotti with sheepmilk cheese, honey and saffron.   Pure bliss.    On this occasion we also got the fettuccine with lamb and tomatoes.   The zingy nature of the dish was a nice contrast to the angolotti.   One thing we like to do as couple to maximize the experience is to order two different pastas and switch halfway through.   Why try one when you can try two???   The desserts are fabulous as well.   Don't sleep on the olive oil cake.   It doesn't sound fancy, but it will knock your socks off.

All in all, Lilia gets my absolute highest recommendation; I truly cannot say enough wonderful things to do it justice.   Truly a special dining experience.   Definitely make sure to make reservations because it does tend to fill up.   If you do not have reservations, I recommend trying to get there as early as possible perhaps even for bar seating.

Everything was outstanding. The aperol spritz was my favorite of the summer and the food was all delectable. Here's what we had: 

The little gem salad - great basic. Refreshing way to start the meal
Grilled artichoke - every time I order a grilled artichoke I forget how awkward it is to eat it. But this one was definitely worth the messiness. So delicious and full of garlic and parmesan and breadcrumbs. Yum.

Sheep's milk filled agnolotti - so light and melted in your mouth.
Spaghetti with pine nuts and lemon - also great. Very simple so we almost didn't order but I'm glad we did.
Linguine with three types of garlic - garlic lover's dream. I'm hungry just thinking about it. 

Olive oil gelato (I think this was called the Italian job?) - really recommend this for dessert! I've never tasted gelato this good. The olive oil and sea salt and bee pollen add so much.

Place is a scene out of a basic b*tch insta feed. The garlic bread and the pasta that everyone gets are the only reason to come to the place. Our waiter was definitely a sex offender but I guess that is ok in Brooklyn. Save your time and money and go for some real Italian.

A culinary experience. 

We enjoyed everything ordered which included: 
Sugar Snap Peas, Lardo, Black Pepper -Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs -Black Bass, Salsa Verde, Coal Roasted Yukon Gold Potatoes -Rigatoni Diavola, San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano, Pecorino -Olive Oil Cake :-) I don't recall the name of the suggested bottle of white wine- it was superb. 

Everything was perfectly flavored and delicious. We sat at the bar- the staff was super friendly and attentive. The bartender was top notch- our glasses were never empty and she was impressively knowledgeable about the menu. A perfect date night.

Seriously blown away by the food at this place.  Had the clams, focaccia, radicchio salad, gnocchi with broccoli pesto, and the Italian job with olive oil cake for dessert.  Each course was better and better with the Italian job vanilla gelato literally as the icing on the cake.  Phenomenal.  Everything so well executed and balanced.  I hope to go back if I am in the area 

Service was excellent as well

SO good. We had multiple pastas dishes and they were all incredible. As good as I've had in the city. The baked clams were delicious as well. The service was top notch - extremely knowledgeable about the menu and very helpful with all the questions we had. Yes, it's very hard to get a table here but it's worth the effort!

I absolutely loved my meal here. I had a worrisome feeling before going because they cancelled my reservation the evening before due to "weather" when it did not rain, but despite an odd first encounter they were able to accommodate us the next evening and I felt very taken care of. I loved the rigatoni and the cacio e pepe balls. I'll definitely be back!

Our meal at Lilia was perfection! From the service to the food, it was 10/10.

My husband, young son and I dined at Lilia together and we were very pleased with the quality and preparation of the meal. We enjoyed several appetizers (all awesome-- Italian broccoli, prosciutto di parma with incredible BUTTER, and sardines) and then we topped it off with the absolutely delicious and tender lamb steak. The wine list is also thoughtfully curated. 

Last but not least, the service was impeccable and friendly. Everyone attended to our needs and they were so accommodating with our son, who needed a high chair.

Thank you so much for the warm welcome & delicious experience!

Snagged a reservation at a normal hour thanks to Resy alerts and fast fingers and had high hopes due to the hype machine surrounding this place. Then I combed through recent Yelp reviews and lowered my expectations slightly in order to not get disappointed. Boy, were we still greatly disappointed. Maybe this restaurant was amazing years ago, but it definitely did not wow us at all and it's NOT worth the craziness of trying to get a reservation.

I will say, our server was fantastic and we had great service. Even when we sent back the clams (more below), we still received great service afterwards. Five stars on that. But, the food (and the wait for the food in between 'courses') dropped this review down to a 3, 3.5 if I'm feeling generous. Writing my review on the food below based on the order we received everything, and with wait times in between (it took forever).

Asparagus: This time it was green asparagus because white asparagus is no longer in season. It comes with a bagna cauda (anchovy-based sauce) to dip in, along with some sourdough bread. Again, this was exceedingly oily. I expected the sauce to be oily and that was fine, but the asparagus itself had too much (and don't even get me started about the bread), that it ended up feeling not crisp but just...oil on oil.

(~10 min wait)

Focaccia: This was delicious, but extremely oily. Seriously, my fingers were soaked by the end and so was my napkin. Focaccia is an oilier bread generally, but this was a bit on the extreme side. The best part was definitely the green butter.

(~15 min wait)

Clams: They were out of the sardines which was what we had really wanted, fine, so we decided on the clams. Big mistake. I had read previous reviews which said they were overcooked and so we were warned, but we still hoped it wouldn't be the case for us. Unfortunately, it was like eating a wad of rubber bands. We rarely send a dish back but we couldn't justify wanting to eat this or spending money on it, so we did. Definitely skip this.

(~20 min wait)

Tortelli: This was our favorite pasta dish because unlike the agnolotti, it actually arrived hot. The peas and pea tendrils were fresh and the mortadella filling was tasty. I would recommend this.

Agnolotti: The famous sheep's milk ricotta agnolotti was tasty, but arrived barely warm. Couldn't help but think the honey, garlic and saffron sauce would be delicious on some not-overcooked clams (yes, we were still a bit upset). We overall liked this dish but would have preferred it to be not cold. Not sure if that was supposed to be the case, or if it was sitting around for ages.

(TLDR - not worth coming here unless they can step up their game. I'm guessing because they're so popular due to the hype, they don't bother/care to execute things properly, which is a damn shame because the dishes could have been top notch if they had. Instead, neither of us plan to recommend this place to any of our friends. What a shame.)

Lilia was so good the first time I had to come back a second. 

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti: Probably Lilia's most popular dish. It's a very uniquely flavored and creamy pasta. Definitely a must order. 

Malfadini: A lovely twist on cacio e pepe with a long, curly edged noodle, pink peppercorn, and parmigiano. The pink peppercorn adds an interesting texture and flavor, and the cheese is not overpowering or too salty. 

Grilled Scallops: Loved this! It was pretty expensive given that the dish only comes with 2 pieces of scallop, but I would order it again and again. 

Grilled Clams: Good but I like the scallops better

Cacio e Pepe Fritelle: These are very heavy, so I would skip this to save room for more pasta 

Rigatoni Diavola: Perfectly al dente noodles, an excellent version of a classic red sauce pasta

Italian Job: a nice treat to round off the night. olive oil + gelato is a beautiful combo

The ceilings are tall and the pasta is lovely.

I managed to get a reservation the day of outdoors I'm guessing because of bad weather but I didn't care because I've waited too long to get one so rain be damned!!!
Since my friend and I figured we'd probably not come back because of reservation difficulties, we decided on eating through most of the menu. 3 apps (Fritelle, garlic scape focaccia, grilled clams), 4 pastas (Linguine w/Calabrian Chile, Ricotta Gnocchi w broccoli pesto, Sheeps milk agnolotti and Mortadella tortellini with peas and mint) and the Lamb leg steak. 
There wasn't a bad dish however we both agreed the tortellini, even though we are not fans of mint, was our favorite. Our server, Tobias was a sweetheart even bringing my friend 81 blanket when he saw she was cold.
Hoping I can return to taste the other dishes at some point.

Hostess needs an attitude adjustment. Asking to sit outside, while there are empty tables and individuals sitting at those tables is not a reason to dismiss a potential customer. Yes it was raining but why have large umbrellas if you can't sit outside in light rain? *blonde hostess with the bad eyeliner*

In short, I don't think Lilia is worth the hype. While it is certainly not bad food, I'm fact some of it was rather good, I don't think the fevered pitch surrounding it, in the month long reservation times and frenzy to get a table, is justified. The portion sizes of the mains (agnolotti, gnocchi, and mafaldini) were a bit too small and rather bland to be satisfied on those alone. Of the three appetizers ordered, of which I believe the whipped and salted butter for the prosciutto and bread was the best part of the meal, none were particularly sumptuous, though the mozzarella was seasoned quite well. Had this been a more inexpensive meal I would have been far more pleased, but given this is my second time dining here, and the prices are on par with some of the city's most lauded Italian, I would recommend trying it to suit your pallet, but all the while keeping in mind Via Carota is only a short train ride away

We had a reservation for over a month to Lilia and we were so excited. Our reservation was at 9pm on a Monday night, but we did not get seated until 9:35pm. It took a while for our waitress to take our order, so we ordered as soon as she came by. They were out of the sheeps milk cheese pasta which was unfortunate so We ordered 3 other pasta dishes. However, our food did not come out until 11:30pm... 2.5 hours after our reservation time!! No apology, no free appetizer or dessert, nothing! I was so appalled by the lack of service and disregard. We then receive our food, and as we are famished, we eat quickly - but 7 minutes later, our waitress comes and asks if we want our food wrapped up. Again, total disregard for timing and just trying to get us out. And honestly, the pasta was very average, nothing out of the ordinary. It was a very disappointing experience, we were really looking forward to this dinner but unfortunately have recommended everyone against going to Lilia.

If you're looking for delicious food & amazing service, look no further.... Lilia is known to be hard to score a reservation but for good reason and it's well worth the wait & struggle of refreshing Resy every day at 10am for a chance to dine here! From the aperol spritz to the pastas, you can't go wrong. Every single dish was packed with flavor and kept getting better. Here's what I ordered:

Aperol spritz (summer, duh!)
Italian Broccoli - delish, spicy & cheesy 
Grilled clams - the tomato paste used with the breadcrumbs was delish. A notable mention of the night! 
Grilled scallop - highlight of the meal! 
Rigatoni - good texture 
Fettucine w/ lamb ragu - bouncy noodles
Grilled lamb - 2nd highlight of the meal *chefs kiss* the breadcrumb & sear on this was to perfection 
Italian Job (Soft serve with olive oil) - this was $12 (pricey I know) but I would do it again! So good.

My boyfriend and I shared everything and we were extremely full; it came out to $260 in total after tips and tax (we had 3 drinks). Def worth the visit for an occasion! We had dinner here for over 2 hours and never felt rushed and received top notch service.

If you're lucky enough to grab a reservation here, just know you will have the best meal ever. This was honestly the top experience I have had. Be warned, I hopped on Resy right at 10am when reservations drop and they were all gone within 2 minutes so you have to be quick. We sample so many of the dishes here you really can't go wrong. Each dish we kept saying "wow this is amazing" I recommend Lilia to everybody.
Always enjoy Lilia. Great for an early dinner during the summer. Enjoyed the malfidini pasta and broccolini with a friend. Also enjoyed the artichoke dish as well. Friendly service as well.
Everything is very nice. Schrimps and cocktails also are very tastful. Service is very perfect

Amazing amazing dinner. One for the books. Went with 5 colleagues. We ordered family style so tried a lot of things on the menu. The cacio e Pepe frittele were so good as were the agnolotti and spaghetti. Everything was amazing. We also got the 30 day aged ribeye. Best steak of my life. Service was excellent as well. They served us in 4-5 courses (including dessert) and it was really well organized.

Outstanding meal at this hard to get into restaurant. I now know why.

Started off with the ramp focaccia for a starter followed by escarole (my 2 guests) and the little gem salad (myself). The breadcrumbs had a garlicky flavor and the salad was excellent. Shared the grilled clams (very good) and chicken liver crostini. For pasta, we chose 2 dishes that we split--mafaldini (very unique shaped pasta) and the spaghetti with pine nuts and parmigiano reggiano. Finished off the meal with "The Italian Job" (vanilla gelato with olive oil).

Very good food, outstanding and non rushed service (our meal lasted more than 2 hours) and very reasonably priced for all the delicious food we ate.

We loved Lilia. Food was amazing. Focaccia is a must. All of the pastas were fresh with great flavors. The only thing that put a damper on the potential 5/5 experience was the atmosphere (in trying to maximize their space, seating felt really tight, a bit unsafe during a pandemic).
It was good, but not as good as Misi (their sister restaurant). Service was impeccable, but a little underwhelmed by the pasta.

As one of the hardest reservations to get in the city, I was very excited to finally be going here. While it was very solid, I would say it underwhelmed slightly especially on the pasta front. Love the atmosphere and the neighborhood. As dumb as it feels to say this, the aperol spritz was one of the best things I've had to drink in a long time. For appetizers, I'd recommend the mozzarella but can probably pass on the cacio e pepe frittele which are a bit too dense  and rich for an app. Would definitely recommend you get a few things from the wood oven, we had grilled clams and Italian broccoli both of which were very good.

Unfortunately the pastas were just not as world changing as I'd hoped. The two we got (agnolotti and fettuccini) were both luke warm when served. Agnolotti had a lot of flavor but eating a whole plate of that flavor became a bit too much, and the fettuccini had the opposite problem in that it didn't have much flavor at all. 

Would still go, but probably lower your expectations a couple notches.

Service was very good.

This was my second time at Lilia and the charm has worn off a little - might be because I sat outdoors and was not dressed for the breeze. 

Food: 
Broccoli 
- wasn't anything special and the combination of cheese and sauce was ok 

White Asparagus 
- the asparagus had a good crunch to it and came with a warmed anchovy dip as well as perfectly toasted bread. 

Clams and mussels 
Personally felt like the mussels were a bit too brine-y for me but the rest of the party loved the mussels! While the kick of chilli was subtle, the clams were doused with garlic and breadcrumbs and was devoured quick by the table. 

Focaccia + ramp butter 
A must order!!! Focaccia came halved and dusted with cheese. A delectable scoop of ramp butter is enough to spread extra upon each bite. 

Black bass  
Considered it was under the "big fish" subsection, it wasn't really big per se. Despite the portion, the bass was tender and paired well with the coal roasted potatoes. 

Agnolotti 
The Lilia staple. It's hard to complain about this dish. The agnolotti might have converted me to a goat cheese fan. The hints of honey and subdried tomatoes make this pasta on the sweeter side, which was a good segway for dessert. 

Crostada 
A galette cousin(?). Encrusted with sugar, the strawberries are snug in this pastry and satisfies any sweet tooth's cravings. 

Olive oil cake 
If you are looking for something on the lighter end to round up the meal. I would opt for the olive oil cake! Not too dense and isn't super rich. 


Seating/Ambience: I sat outdoors right by the entrance and could constantly feel people waiting for a table hovering in the vicinity peering at what I've ordered. It was slightly awkward, but honestly I would have done the same if the roles were reversed! 

I would definitely recommend scoring an indoor reservation as you might have a view of the lovely interior stacked with crockery and the chefs in the kitchen prepping the dishes. 

Overall: 
Great for its service and lovely vibes. The portions at Lilia aren't huge and I would say be prepped to order a bit of everything to share.

Good restaurant with refreshingly unique food. Definitely worth a try if you can get a reservation, though I wouldn't rave about it.

PRICE: Not too expensive (~$50/pax for food).
PORTION: 1 app +1 pasta per person was filling.

FOOD:
* Roasted Ramp Focaccia ($15): Garlic bread dropped an upgraded model?!? Deliciously fresh bread and tasty butter. Perfect balance between light and heavy. Green like Shrek.  5/5

* Mussels ($17): Pretty good. Even more green. 4/5

* Fettuccine + Lamb Sausage ($26): Decent but nothing crazy. Deceptively filling (bowl is deep). 4/5

* Italian Job Gelato ($12): Sweet&salty soft serve. Similar to the Soy Sauce Caramel Soft Serve at Cote. Friends recommended it. 4/5

SERVICE: AMAZINGLY attentive servers. Dropped my napkin and was given a new one before I even got back up.  5/5

Lilia 
- [ ] Asked zero time how our food was, white asparagus left much to be desired, it was chewier than it was supposed to be. The anchovy sauce it was paired with tasted lack luster.
- [ ] The prawns weren't great. The quality of the prawn meat was almost there, but the flavor was so blah that I can't give this dish more than a 5/10
- [ ] Our server was just bad. 
- [ ] This is our second outing to lilia, both times there was something off. Service is we always lost. 
- [ ] Here for 20 minutes before our food order was taken. This place is just trash. There's a reason you can't get above 4.4 stars.

This review is only for the take-out soft serve. While it's the MOST EXPENSIVE soft-serve gelato EVER at $10-12/small cup (def a one time a year thing for me due to $$$$), it is quite excellent. Flavors are refined and delicious.

Cons: There's no casual seating in/outside to enjoy the gelato, as all cafe tables and seating are reserved for dine-in only. There are also no trash bins for customers to throw away the cups/spoons.

For a hyped up place I was super pleased that the food here was actually solid and NOT overpriced. My husband and I came here on a Friday evening & the crowd is what as I'd expect -- young & vibrant if not probably wanna be influencers. Crowd aside we had decent cocktails, albeit inconsistent in alcohol content in between rounds, delicious focaccia bread that everyone raves about ( a must try), cacio e Pepe balls (too salty for my liking), scallops which were great quality & fettuccini which was just freshly made. For dessert I opted in for the Italian Job, which was also scrumptious. The staff was attentive & fun (shout out to Milo), wiping our tables at each course & doling our new plates at the right time.

I didn't pay for my meal, and I didn't make the reservation. So I should've loved Lilia. I didn't.

The Grilled Clams, Rigatoni Diavola, Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, and Fettuccine with Lamb Sausage were all tasty in their own way. The pastas were appropriately al dente. The flavors were as light and airy as the restaurant itself. But they weren't memorable. Any high-end Italian restaurant would do just as well, and if you're lucky, you'll get more bang for your buck. The portions were tiny at $25+ per entree. I had to get two pastas just to feel full. Luckily, as I said, I didn't pay for my meal.

Dessert was equally disappointing. My Olive Oil Cake was drier than sandpaper. The Chocolate Gelato was basic and forgettable. My pastry chef friend remarked with disgust that they clearly didn't have a pastry chef, and it showed in the quality. Honestly, the best part of my meal was my two glasses of Lambrusco. But we know Lilia doesn't make wine.

The ambience is industrial and airy, but the acoustics are too echoey, amplifying all the noise to near cacophonic levels. The clientele, well--let's just say Lilia seems to attract the kind of stuck-up white people who consider Italian their favorite "ethnic" cuisine. I had the misfortune of running into two such women before I'd even finished checking in. Ugh, pray you aren't seated near these people.

Lawdy, the things people will believe with enough hype. Lilia is fine, but it's not worth the hassle of trying to secure a reservation. In a city saturated with Italian restaurants, you will find better for less trouble.

Absolutely amazing. I made reservations at the wrong restaurant thinking it was Lilia....even tho they were booked, they found a way to squeeze us in. Every dish & cocktail was a hit. I absolutely recommend eating her. Make sure you book the correct reservation

I had wanted to come here for so long so when I was lucky enough to happen upon a reservation I was so excited. Overall it was a great experience everything was very yummy but I don't get the insane hype. My pasta tasted very fresh but it was just a very average ragu. My sisters ravioli was very interesting and sweet which is not what I was expecting. At the end of the day your paying a pretty penny for interesting flavored pasta and the experience. I'd come back again if someone invited me but never again for fun.

Good ingredients and careful preparation make the one-month wait for an inconveniently-timed reservation (4;15pm on a Monday) worth it. Service was very good, as my water was refilled quickly and silverware was replaced promptly. I still don't know why restaurants put silverware right on the table though. It's not clean. At least wrap it up in a napkin before doing that. Anyway, on to the food. 

Much has been written about the house-made mozzarella on garlic bread (with bottarga) and sheep's milk agnolotti (with saffron). Those dishes were quite good, as expected. But the tortelli filled with mortadella and garnished with diced ramps was my favorite. I had intended to eat only half of it and take the remainder home but I couldn't help myself from eating the whole portion. Weirdly enough, the flavor reminded me of seolleongtang; a Korean dish which is a rich and hearty ox bone soup. The black bass was perfectly cooked and the tang from the salsa verde complemented it nicely. 

Overall, a very nice meal worthy of a special occasion. All of this - no alcohol, no dessert for me - cost about $145 including tax and tip. Not unreasonable, considering the quality. Having been open for more than six years now, the fact that seats are still hard to come by says something.

5 star service. 4 star food. 5 star Gelato. We were seated outside and it was a bit cold so they brought us blankets. My party was a little delayed but they seated me while I was waiting and were patient as we finished (probably over the 1.5 hour time limit). I want to reiterate how great our experience was thanks to the service! 

We ordered the mafaldini, agnolotti , fettuccini, gnocchi, baked clams and focaccia.

Everyone agreed the agnolotti was the star of the show. Do not come here and not get it. The focaccia was really good too, but she mentioned they often sell out by 7 pm. It looked different than other focaccia I have had, but the ramp butter and roasted ramps was so unique and the crunch if the bread was great. The Gelato was some of the best I've ever had it was so soft and creamy. My sister got the Italian job which had fennel, sea salt, and olive oil and it was our favorite of the four we got. 

I was disappointed by the mafaldini. The taste was fine, but the pepper made the texture a bit Sandy and I would probably pass on ordering this next time (although it was the one I was most excited for). My cocktail was great (I can't remember the name but it had mezcal and egg white). It was the perfect balance between bitter, Smokey, and sweet. 

All in all, it was a great experience and I would love to come back again and eat inside!

This place is always fully booked but my friend and I got really lucky and managed to snag a spot with just one week's notice. We were in the area the week prior for brunch and decided to take our chances and walk into the restaurant to ask the hostess about reservations. She was able to squeeze us in for the following weekend! 

We ordered the roasted leek focaccia, grilled clams, grilled scallops, sheep's milk filled agnolotti, fettuccine with lamb sausage, and the olive oil cake for dessert. Everything was amazing!! The clams and scallops were grilled to perfection, the pastas were fresh, and the sauces were flavorful.

I also loved the vibe here and the staff were all extremely friendly. Highly recommend!

Our favorites were the agnolotti and the Italian job ice cream for dessert. We also tried the garlic linguine, chicken crostini and the homemade mozzarella and while they were all very good, they were not things that we would order again.
One of my favorite restaurants in NY. Delicious food and amazing service.  The only negative thing is that it's impossible to get a ressie!

Everything about Lilia was amazing. The atmosphere, decor, service, and food were all spectacular. We had the Grilled Artichoke to start, then the Sheep's Milk Filled Agnolotti, and the Italian Job for dessert. I HIGHLY recommend those plates because the flavor combinations are surprising but delicious. I already can't wait to go back for the pasta and the gelato with olive oil.

Lilia, being one of those hyped NY restaurants, had been on my hit-list for a very long time. After ~several~ failed attempts to make a reservation, I was able to get a spot for a Saturday evening. Usually reservations are only available like a month out, since this place has such high demand, so plan accordingly if you want to try it. The restaurant itself is very cute, spacious, and bright. It had a nice lively ambiance with a predominantly younger crowd. We had a very kind and attentive waitress who took our order right away and was helpful with recommending what wine to order. We shared: 

Housemade Mozzarella: very good appetizer. Super fresh and mild mozzarella that was enhanced by the flavor of lemon zest and paired really nicely with the toasted garlic bread. Really nice, and subtle umami undertones from the bottarga. Would recommend. 

Little Gem: your traditional little gem salad. Very fresh and crispy lettuce, good italian dressing, and nice amounts of pecorino and crunchy breadcrumbs. Not super filling and pricey so you can probably skip. 

Mafaldini: Nice shape and texture but a bit underwhelming in flavor. I mostly only tasted very mild hints of parmesan and a little bit of the pink peppercorn. Definitely a very aesthetic dish and cooked nicely al dente so worth ordering if you want to try it. The pasta is clearly high quality and very fresh! 

Ricotta Gnocchi: usually I am not a fan of pesto but this one was very nicely flavored and not too overpowering in the dish. It was not oily at all (which is one of my pet peeves) and it was enhanced by generous bits of pistachio that gave it a little bit of sweetness/nuttiness. Could have used a little bit more sauce since the gnocchi was a bit dry but I was a big fan of the subtle ricotta flavor in the gnocchi!

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti: This was my favorite dish and what I would argue is definitely worth the hype surrounding this place. Order this if you come here, you will not regret it! Very creamy sheep's milk cheese inside these satisfyingly shaped pasta pillows. The sun-dried tomatoes give it a bit of sweet acidity that balances the cheese well and the very subtle honey flavor/texture goes makes you feel like this dish dissolves in your mouth. The saffron gave it a nice color and flavor too. A highlight!

The Italian Job: finally, dessert! This was a work of art. The combination of vanilla gelato, honey, and olive oil is truly divine and you will not know until you try it. It had fennel pollen which gave it a unique herb flavor as well as bits of sea salt (even my friend who is not a fan of sweet/salty desserts loved this.) The gelato has a consistency closer to soft serve but it is still amazing. 

Overall, I had a pretty good experience here. It is very pricey and some dishes probably do not live up to the hype -- you can get great italian food anywhere in the city so it might not be really worth it to go out of your way if you have easier options. However, if you are able to get a reservation or are a dedicated foodie and want to experience this place, you will find very exceptional, attentive service (5/5 stars in that regard), a nice ambiance, and some pretty good/aesthetic dishes!

Considering that the location used to be an old auto body shop, this restaurant runs like a well oiled machine with impeccable service and an impressive open kitchen. My boyfriend and I had a reservation for Friday night prime time dinner and every seat was filled. I highly recommend having a reservation to come here and live the dining experience that is Lilia. 

We had the grilled clams, cacio e pepe fritelle, whole artichoke, cured sardines, rigatoni diavola, sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti, and olive oil cake. Everything came out perfectly timed as we finished the previous dish with attention to detail and presentation. The food was of high quality, full of flavor and freshness and most importantly, absolutely delicious. My favorites were the grilled clams, cured sardines, and the sheeps milk cheese pasta. The olive oil cake was also delicious with the perfect balance of moisture, sweetness, and cream. 

Overall Lilia fits well amongst the high ranks of Italian restaurants in NYC. It was easy to commute to via train and they even have another sister restaurant in Brooklyn. I highly recommend this place and cannot wait to come back again.
Lilias pastas are unbeatable. And that olive oil ice cream is unlike any other ice cream you'll ever eat. Eating here is always such a magical experience. The dishes are so well thought out.

I went to celebrate my birthday. It was the best decision of local walking distance restaurants.  The ambiance, food is AMAZING,service, staff and bartender was top notch.
I will be going back again.

Yes, getting in is annoying and feels impossible. But it's worth it. Every pasta is perfect. You can tell so much effort has gone into every dish. The desserts deserve insane acclaim. If you can't get in, at least try Lilia Cafe. You'll see what I mean!

4.5 because although the food is awesome and honestly a pretty great price point for nyc, i think it's way too hard to get into

came to lilia ~4 years ago and sat at the bar after waiting 3 hours. was so good i had to come again. came this time with a group of 3 and seated at a table, really nice service, cocktails are nothing too special though (go for wine!)

leek focaccia - delish, butter could have more onion flavor but the bread alone is spectacular
artichoke - it was better 4 years ago imo, but still really delicious.
pesto ricotta gnocchi - nice, fluffy, great pesto, wonderful texture
lamb parpadelle - great, solid red sauce pasta. super balanced
agnolotti - fire!!! sweet + salty, creamy
chocolate/hazelnut gelato - honestly insane???? salty??? crunchy???? bitter from the coffee?? a bit rich but so good
olive oil cake - very good, but i make a better one now after i had this 4 years ago and went home and obsessively baked this into existence

with 3 cocktails + the food + the tip = $230

not cheap by any means, but not bad at all for 3 people, drinks, and NYC. overall: just great, tasty food in a nice dining room

If you're lucky enough to get an reservation here, please come hungry so you can order so many things. Lilia was so delicious with simple fresh ingredients. We ordered rhe mozzarella with lemon on toasted bread, agnolotti, mortadella tortelli, lamb sausage with fettuccine, and vanilla gelato.

The pastas are super fresh and made daily in house. Every pasta was like a flavor bomb and our minds were blown from all the different flavors. Our favorite was the crunchy bread with fresh warm mozzarella. The agnolotti was finished with honey... and I was shocked on how the flavor just mesh so well with the creamy sheep's milk ricotta.. I think I'm still dreaming and drooling!!! The mortadella tortelli was sooooo good. The lamb sausage ragu was coated all over the fettuccine and I wanted to lick the bowl!!! Our gelato was smoothly and creamy, we get to choose which toppings we wanted. We were a little greedy and chose all toppings!! 

We love the simplicity of Lilia and how they approach their dishes with great ingredients! We loved the service, our waiters were super attentive, friendly, and amazing!! Next, we need to try Misi!!

where do i begin
last night we ate at my favorite restaurant in ny.   lilia in williamsburg brooklyn.   the food was outstanding, the service  was impeccable and kudos to the person who runs this place.  whoever it  is should give classes on how a restaurant should be run.  first the  food
for apps we had
Italian Broccoli, Parmigiano, Chili Oil, Lemon Mussels, Herb Butter, Sea Salt
Delicata Squash, Walnut Parsley Pesto, Sage,   tried this for the first time and loooved it
Mussels, Herb Butter, Sea Salt
for the main courses we had
Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano    my second most favorite dish
Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey.  my favorite.  we had 2 dishes and i don't care where you eat, nothing will be better
Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Pecorino, Pistachios
Grilled Lamb Leg Steak, Roman Spices, Celery Heart, Pecorino
Grilled Chicken Thigh & Leg, Fingerling Potatoes, Grilled Lemon, Garlic
for desert
3 italian  jobs(soft serve vanilla gelato, honey, olive oil, sea salt, fennel  pollen)  the best desert money can buy.  i promise you
this place  is run like a well oiled machine.  everything was perfect and i even  found a parking spot right out front.  in saturday night traffic, it  took me 45 minutes to get to williamsburg from roslyn heights.
tough to get a reservation but well worth the effo

My friend and I had been so excited to finally snag a reservation and get to go here for dinner. We were seated promptly and our server was wonderful. The sommelier was very helpful with his wine suggestions and we order a great bottle of wine. We ordered the artichoke, agnolotti, gnocchi and bass. I am a vegetarian so I personally ate some of everything  but the fish. I really enjoyed the pastas, they were both flavorful and very fresh. They were also light and you definitely can eat more than one dish or share a few between people and not be over stuffed. The artichoke was unique and tasty as well. My friend did not enjoy her bass much unfortunately. Our biggest issue was that all of our food was served at room temperature at best. The pasta was not even the slightest bit warm. We also thought the food was a bit overpriced for what we got, maybe if the food was warmer we would've enjoyed it more.

I have been waiting so long to try Lilia ever since we went to Misi.

service - 5/5, our waitress was very friendly and attentive.

food - 4/5, we ordered cacio e pepe frittelle (5/5), roasted leek focaccia (10/5, the best focaccia I have ever had in my life), grilled clams (1/5, you can skip this, clams were extremely chewy and dry, not much flavors), grilled prawns (2/5, I can tell that these were frozen and texture was very mushy), sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti (10/5, it's a must! so delicious, it actually reminded me of home made ravioli we had in Capri), and Rigatoni Diavola (1/5, not sure why this dish is famous, very blend and lacking flavors). 

drinks - 2/5, we ordered a bottle of Rarefratte Vespaiolo as our waitress recommended and it paired really well with all of our dishes. loved it! but we did not like their cocktails.. (you can skip ordering bianco bianco - tasted very watered down, vesper - really average)

ambience - 4/5

I would definitely come back for roasted leek focaccia and sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti! enjoy!

In short, if you can get a res, totally worth going. I wouldn't spend weeks trying to get a reservation here, but one was given to me so I happily obliged. Skip the scallops, the mafaldine was probably the most unique (slightly too salty) but different, rigatoni was solid, but my favorite dish was surprisingly the little gem (crisp and flavorful). Overall the food was 8.5/10 but the reason I'm writing this is because the service. Our waitress (didn't get her name) was beyond sweet, which was unexpected at a slightly more pretentious spot. She was amazing, and the rest of the service genuinely blew me away. They didn't rush you through your meal and would come and clean up your plates but always check to see if there was a bite or two left and would only take what was totally finished. Service 11/10. Vibes 10/10, fun and bustling yet still felt quaint.

Visited on Thursday afternoon. We couldn't get the reservation for a long time. I saw an available spot randomly. They do take walk ins. If you want to go as a walkin, i would recommend to go on a weekday at 4-5pm, before they open. They get packed really fast.

Lilia is a very nice Italian restaurant. Interior isnt too much. Open kitchen and bar. Many wine and liquor selections. 

Food:

Grilled clamps: various flavors with breadcrumps on top. I highly recommend this. No clam fishy smell. Very well grilled. One of my favorite seafood I had in NYC.

Malfadini: very sharp, richy flavor with parmasean sauce. Noodle was pretty chewy but easy to consume. Absolutely fabulous taste.

Grilled bass: very well cooked. No smell. Uniformly cooked. Very soft. All the flavors work together to create perfect taste. Give this one a try. I loved it!

Overall, very recommended. I would like to come back to try more dishes.

A solid 4 star restaurant!. We went early in the evening without a reservation. Before we sat down the hostess told us they had a table for two but would need the table by 6:30 because they had reservations for the seats after us. We didn't mind, but as we sat down the server again reminded us that they needed the seat at around 6:30. Okay I get it. Although the service was good, at the end they had multiple tables open without any patrons. A little more than half filled restaurant around 630. I asked the server if she still needed the table because we just ordered our desserts and she said it was okay. It left me confused and a little turn off, like they didn't want my business from the beginning and are seeking whose next. 

On to the food:
Very good pasta, very good desserts. We had the the cheese fritter appetizer which was interesting and good, the clams - while the flavors was there, the clams came out dry. The scallops was cooked perfectly but to me I didn't like the pairing of the crème, but my husband didn't mind it. The Sheep milk and the peppery pasta very good .  Also the sea bass was good but too salty for my taste bud. If my husband said the dish is a little salty, it probably is because he loves His salt. All the dishes complimented the red wine the server recommended. I'm sorry I don't remember the exact names of the dishes and only the descriptions. We order the Italian job and the open face apple pie for dessert, which was divine and ended the night on a good note. Overall a delicious place to try if you're in the neighborhood. Would I go back? Probably not, there's just too many places in NYC for me to cover all it. Would I recommend it. Yes

I went to Lilia recently, to celebrate the life of someone very dear to me. The restaurant welcomed us like family and helped recreate a very special evening there. Everything was divine, from the sommelier's wine selection, to the delectable dishes, and surprise desserts. A huge thank you to the staff, for their compassion, attentiveness, and service. We couldn't have asked for a better night in Brooklyn, remembering the one we love. Thank you for taking such good care of us Lilia!

Lilia is amazing! The food is outstanding, atmosphere is wonderful, and the staff is great. Steven went so far out of his way to make sure we had a great time and felt comfortable. Highly recommend! Thank you Steven

After learning reservations are extremely hard to get, I knew I had to come! I had no luck with their online system, so I decided to call one day and luckily they picked up and I was able to make a reservation!

Malfadini - their specialty! The pasta is long and noodle like, and texture of the pasta was perfectly al denté. We ate the Liang Pi noodles from Xi'an Famous Foods a few hours prior to this, so it felt like we were eating Italian Liang Pi lol. It's not too saucy, the flavor is light. Very unique!

Roasted Leek Focaccia with green garlic butter - this will be the best focaccia with garlic butter experience you'll ever have! Trust. The bread is perfectly warm and so fresh, and the butter is so spreadable and every bite is delectable. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. Literally every table in our row ordered this!

I really love the vibe of this place. Buzzy and lively yet the diners weren't sitting on top of each other. Cozy, dim lighting with the tea candles illuminating the table.

I was here for one thing and one thing only - the spaghetti with pine nuts, lemon, and parmigiano reggiano. I remember having it some time in 2019, and it was just as good as I remembered. So damn good. The spaghetti itself was cooked perfectly, and the silky sauce coated each strand. 

And because I shouldn't leave the place having eaten just the spaghetti, my friend and I tried the little gem salad and the scallops. Salad was a nice prelude. Scallops were delicious. It came with a nutty yogurt sauce. They were good separately - but together a bit much. But still enjoyable. Topped everything off with a clean Gruner Veltliner from Alto Adige. 

Will be camping on Resy at 9:59 am so I can score another res. So worth it!

An enjoyable meal from start to finish, but it's hard to understand why Lilia is as highly esteemed as it is. It's clear that the dishes are prepared with care using fresh, high quality ingredients, however, I have been here four times and have never walked away feeling mind-blown by any one item. 

Starters: The little gem salad is light and refreshing, would recommend ordering. The focaccia and garlic bread starters have the potential to be stellar, but the focaccia is on the dry side (rather than fluffy), and the cold mozzarella on the warm garlic bread just doesn't do it for me. 

Pastas: The chewy textures of the Mafaldini and Rigatoni make the pasta itself delightful, but their sauces are lacking flavor. The Mafaldini, which is one of Lilia's most popular dishes, is essentially just coated in butter and pepper. The Agnolotti, also a fan-favorite, is delicate and pleasant, but is nothing memorable. The one dish I explicitly disliked was the gnocchi, which has a dense and spongy, unappealing texture. 

Dessert: the soft serves are tasty, but nothing special. The Apple Crostata we had was divine- would highly recommend. 

Service: poor? weird? We were told upon checking in for our 5:15pm reservation that we'd need to give the table back by 7:15pm. Understandable. When we ordered, we told the server we would want dessert at the end, and asked him to do whatever he needed to do in terms of pacing the courses to allow for us to have dessert and be done with the table by 7:15pm. He told us he couldn't make any promises, but could get us our dessert in to-go boxes if there wasn't time. Not understandable? If there isn't time to guarantee a customer can order 3 courses in two hours, don't place a two hour time limit on a table. Not to mention, soft serve in a to-go box? Then, the server disappeared for 25 minutes towards the end of the meal, and left us feeling considerably rushed when finally returned (after we asked 3 different individuals to send our server over if they could).

I love Lilia! The spicy rigatoni and green garlic focaccia were my favorite. I have been here multiple times and always gotten a reservation. There are so many great options for vegetarians. The service is great too.

Loved the rigatoni and cacio e pepe frittelle. The lamb steak was huge and delicious. The sheep's milk pasta was good but very milky. Our waitress was amazing. The restaurant as cold, recommend that you layer up. Great experience overall.

I love the focaccia that's made here every season.
I'd say the any protein, meat/fish is done very well.
However the appetizers are a hit or miss. ESP the zucchini was disappointing.

Service was pretty good . Could be better, almost felt like they were trying to get rid of us. Any how it's was a good evening

To die for !!
1. Roasted Leek Focaccia, Green Garlic Butter
2. Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey
3. Italian job
Clams, shrimps, scallops, broccoli and on and on and on are all must trys.
Have to come back and try it all. 
No wonder its that hard to get a reservation. Service is great, atmo is vibing, located on the quieter side of williamsburg. Hands down the top 3 italian yummyz in nyc. Bravo !!

I've come here a couple times and each time it has been awesome. You can try calling in the day of to get a reservation for those that last-minute cancel or to get squeezed in for early dinner. Haven't been here for brunch yet. The food is fantastic, and I don't typically like Italian food. The wait time is a bit much. The waitstaff are pretty busy, but each dish is well-cooked and tastes good so the wait is worth it. The wine glasses are nice and the prices are reasonable. The atmosphere is low-key and dark. It's a great date place. They don't do anything special for birthdays.

Nothing to say except that the hype is warranted. It's a pain in the ass to get a reservation over a month out, but damn if that isn't some of the best pasta I've ever had. Also, don't sleep on that squash starter. Melted in my mouth
This place deserves all the hype. The food is simple and delicious.  The cocktails are well crafted. We had excellent recommendations from the sommelier. Dessert and coffee were delicious as well.
bomb ass meal, i  didn't like the cacio e pepe balls - room temp and weird texture, but the bib salad and mushroom pasta omg breakfast lunch and dinner please

Lilia is an upscale Italian restaurant that is notoriously difficult to make a reservation for. 
Tip: go on Opentable and look for open spots the day of and be prepared to go spontaneously.

I highly recommend their Roasted leek focaccia bread, Sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti, and Bianco Bianco cocktail.

I would skip the gnocchi. We did not like it.

Excellent dinner here on a Friday night. Fully packed restaurant, dim lighting, very pleasant ambiance--slightly upscale but still casual with absolutely no stuffiness. I made a reservation for Lilia a month before (which is kind of nuts if you think about it) and they go FAST. If you're set on a particular date, you will have to do the same on Resy.

Our server was very attentive and another waitstaff member cleaned and cleared our table between each course which I appreciated. I usually only get that kind of service when I order prix fixe, so it was a nice surprise. My friend and I ordered the cacio e pépé fritelle, little gem lettuce (I'd pass on this, it was far too acidic), scallops (small portion but delicious and oddly filling), sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti with sundried tomatoes (absolutely must order), lamb fettuccine (was not a fan--I'd pass on this), and olive oil cake. For my next visit I would definitely reorder the agnolotti and olive oil cake, and potentially order the cacio e pépé starter or the scallops as well. I wish I tried the mortadella filled tortelli but that'll happen during my next visit!
