Overall, I had a wonderful time. But I cannot seem to fully comprehend why people rave over this restaurant in the way they do. It's solid, you can't really go wrong, per se, but it's not like every dish was jaw droppingly delicious (though mostly soo very solid). If you specifically want pasta dishes I'd stay in Manhattan and go to L'Artusi first. That said, I'm curious to see how their other pasta dishes fair.

The food is excellent and the wait staff is attentive. Although the restaurant itself is attractive with its large windows and high ceilings, there is a serious heating issue with the building. My husband and I were shivering through our meal, and there was no acknowledgement of or apology for this problem by the staff, even though diners and staff were all wearing winter coats, scarves, and hats for indoor dining! In addition, it was one of the coldest days of the year - 17 degrees outside- and even though we arrived on time for our reservation, we were required to wait out in the cold for about 15 minutes before being invited inside and escorted to our table. Overall, I would recommend going to Lilia during spring or fall to avoid discomfort, or if you decide to go in winter, expect to wear hats, coats, and gloves during your meal. I think for a restaurant if this caliber, this is unacceptable, and they should do better. At the very least, they should acknowledge that they have heating issue and give diners a heads up so that they are prepared and dress appropriately.

Lilia finally we meet. Honestly I think it's overrated. Hear me out. If you live in BK and NYC, love italian food and are able to score a reservation, please, by all means go to Lilia but lower your expectations just a little is all I'm saying.  The gem salad is a bit too tart, my tastebuds couldn't deal, please bring that down a notch (I HOPE with all my heart that they read the middle of the road reviews and learn a thing or two on being better), that's the remedy to complacency. Anyways the pasta I had, the Malfadini, seemed a little undercooked, nah that aint al dente, I been to Italy a few times so I know :).  Also didn't clean my plate on that one. I was in the mood for more flavor but then was torn because why go to Lilia and not get pasta. Next time (yeah I'm willing to give it one more chance but that's itttt) I'll go for the fish or steak and call it a night, I might try one of the very few red sauce pastas on the menu.
BUT wait a second that dessert I had, now THAT hit the spot that was good and almost redeemed the whole evening for me. It was the olive oil cake with cream and that orange compote next to it elevated it to a whole new level. Secret weapon if you ask me.

After living 4 years in NYC, I was finally was able to get to try Lilia and wanted to see what the hype is. I would say, it was really good but not great. I am glad I've tried it though! They also have a sister restaurant called Misi located in Brooklyn as well. 

What I ordered:
- Cacio e Pepe Frittelle 
- Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga
- Grilled Artichoke, Garlic, Orange, Parmigiano, Breadcrumbs (this was okay, it was too much cheese) 
- Grilled Prawns, Fennel Pollen, Lemon
- Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Pecorino, Pistachios
- Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey (must get)
- Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano (must get)

What an amazing dining experience and a must try if you're looking for great service food and atmosphere. An amazing menu selection with wine cocktails or anything you desire. The experience was memorable and great for a date night. 

The staff was exceptional our server Mikel was probably one of the greatest in any restaurant I have been too making great recommendations, tending to every question and also ensuring that each course was to our liking. 

Now onto the food we began with the grilled clams, leek focaccia and also the grilled prawns. All three were spectacular to say the least. 

The grilled clams were a delight in ever bite. The Calabrian chilis were not overpowering yet complemented with the breadcrumb topping which gave the dish some depth in texture and flavor profile. A good portion and serving for the price definitely worth a try 

The grilled leek Focaccia bread with herb butter was phenomenal very decadent and soft. The grilled leek and cheese baked into every bite is perfectly complimented with the herb butter which alone could be a star. The butter is also a nice green hue which gives this dish a great contrast in color bringing what would be just bread to life. 

The grilled prawns were perfect k seasoned which is difficult to execute however the flavor profile throughout each prawn was phenomenal. This portion size was good for the price as well would definitely recommend this dish. 

Main course 
My date had the sea bass which is paired with smashed fingerling potatoes which was a perfect portion. The salsa verde was a great compliment to the perfectly cooked sea bass. 

I had the chicken with fingerling potatoes which was cooked to perfection. The chicken fell off the bone and was seasoned so well that you could taste the flavor profile through every piece. 

Overall this was an amazing experience that my tastebuds thanked me for. Definitely will be returning to taste the pasta soon.

Lilia is always a fabulous meal. By far my favorite restaurant in New York, I recommend anyone visiting NYC or looking for a recommendation to check it out. The service is outstanding, I'm actually always really stoned when I visit so I can fully have my meal peak- and the staff never make me feel guilty - even when we order a second agnolotti with dessert. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu, I seriously could eat here every single night.

Sadly, this supersedes my 4 previously positive visits and reviews.

The exactly same-sized group of all white women added their names to the waitlist right after us - and when we arrived 2 hours later to check on our reservation, they were already seated and enjoying drinks and food.

We put our name down on a not at all busy winter night, and were told we 'might' be 'accepted' 2.5 hours later. We checked in 2 hours later - and we were snidely asked to please put on a mask before continuing to converse with the staff. 

33% of the interior seating was vacated, and more than 60% of the exterior dining domes were empty. Despite this, the (4) hostesses snootily informed us - without looking directly at us once - that they were fully booked and there were no remaining seats for the evening. All this without a single glance directly at us.

In this day and age, you get a text once adding your name to the waitlist, and are provided with an estimated wait time. At Lilia, it seems a spot in their restaurant all comes down to your race. The exactly same-sized group of all white women added their names to the waitlist right after us - and when we arrived 2 hours later to check on our reservation, they were already seated and enjoying drinks and food.

Each of the hostesses had a dismissive and arrogant demeanor. The frail black male hostess had such a sarcastic, rude comportment, we thought he might have been mistaking our group for someone who had antagonized him previously.

After being crudely denied a spot for the night, a manager ran down the block after our group to try to persuade us to try again next time, and asked us to please not take any comments personally, or report them.

There is no quality of food that can overlook such a distasteful interpersonal situation. I've taken down my previous reviews of this restaurant, as no culinary experience can ever excuse such conceited and racist behavior. 

Incredible food is everywhere in this neighborhood. Go literally anywhere else.

I was hesitant to come, fearing it might be over-hyped.

However, I enjoyed a beautiful meal at a very reasonable price.

So glad our waitress made us order the cacio e pepe fritelle. Well, she didn't make us, but she did warn us that they sell out of those. Grateful for that tip. So delicious! I also loved the combination of everything that they do with the little gem salad. The breadcrumbs and all. But really, the pink peppercorn on that mafaldini is unlike no other. I was still thinking about it for days. Weeks. We also agreed we hadn't had the pleasure of tasting fettuccine as good as here- it had the perfect bounce to it and it is just indescribable. Try it. Cannot wait to come back to try the gnocchi and lots more.

This is a busy business restaurant. You have to diligent to score a reservation.  The service and food is pretty outstanding. The pastas are the highlight. Despite being simply sauced they're full of flavor. By far the favorite of my meal was the soft serve ice cream The Itlaian Job The mixture of flavors, olive oil and salt, may sound strange but it works. This alone will warrant another visit

Consensus rating out of 5 stars is between 3-4 (poll of six people)

As with most places, there were some standout dishes and some average dishes. 

Stand outs were the :

mozzarella toast - good dressing
gem salad - tart, crisp, and fresh
grilled clams - tasted like it had meet in it
malfadini pasta - never had this anywhere else
Ribeye steak - as good as a steakhouse

Average dishes:

squash - over cooked 
Cacio Pepe balls - not peppery enough, kind of stodgy filling
agnolotti - a little bland 
rigatoni - standard dish, didn't stand out
scallops - ok
cardoons - didn't taste the anchovy vinaigrette

Pretentious , cold and unwelcoming. Would have at least expected a good meal out of it. The vegetables were over salted and over dressed with grated cheese and breadcrumbs. The pasta was spartan and the lamb was fatty and uninspiring. Small pours and a pedestrian wine list. Don't believe the reviews.

Former auto shop turned into restaurant.. very cool. To be honest the food was ok. We ordered a couple apps and 3 pasta dishes Cacio e Pepe Frittelle, Rigatoni Diavola and Pappardelle. I have to say it was really rich and heavy.! I was a bit disappointed from the meal. It was a lot of white sauced pasta and wish our waitress would have maybe advised us differently when we asked her for her recommendation.

Been wanted to come to this place for a while.  Getting in is difficult. Finally made it   The place is super nice.  The service is exceptional.  We had the Focaccia bread.  Grilled clams and radicchio salad.  All delicious.  An nice bottle of wine.  That was a bit pricey.  The main dishes were all good.  The pasta was super fresh and real good  tried a couple of different gelatos.  When I left I thought it was a five star meal and place.  However. On the drive home I was dying of thirst.  I like salt on my dishes.  However they might have gone overboard.  All in all. It was a pleasant experience.  I recommend trying this place if you can get in.  But as with most hyped up places.  It falls a bit short

One of the best places I've been to for pasta in NY.  Although we sat outside due to the packed seating inside, they gave us blankets to wrap ourselves around.  The ramp butter for the focaccia was delicious and green!  The grilled clams were also very good.  The malfaldini (my first time trying it) is to die for.  Make sure to order the Italian Job for dessert - this is soft serve topped with olive oil, fennel and sea salt, absolutely a must try and scrumptious!  This is one place in NY that I will remember for a lifetime as being one of my favorite places for Italian food, namely pasta!  Would return because the food is delicious!

We ate here last night. The first thing they did is ask for proof of vaccines and photo ID! The mayor of NYC is an jerk. This is not the restaurants job! I'm vaccinated so I could care less, but making non vaccinated people second class citizens is bull$hit and illegal. Enough of my rant, on to the food.
Everything was delicious. Portions are kinda small especially for the prices charged. Atmosphere was okay, a bit noisy and was cold. The artichoke was very good and the heart was tender. I only wish they served some bread to dip into the sauce in the bottom of the bowl. Next we had Cacio e Pepe Frittelle, very interesting, crunchy outside shell with a soft inside. They are good but difficult to describe. Next, Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs, l loved them, a nice spicy taste. Salad was good and the pastas were cooked perfectly!  My favorite was the spaghetti, the mushroom pasta was a close second. We also had the Black Bass it was great but a very small portion. Dessert was also great.
It was an a very different unique meal. Aside from the costs and portions you will love the food,

Fantastic food and wine, and absolutely exceptional service. When we first got here for our 9:15pm reservation, things got off a bit on the wrong foot. We had to wait about 30 minutes or so for a table even with a reservation due to the inside crowd. Once we were able to get seated however, our waiter and another staff member came by with an appetizer and a couple glasses of wine on the house, both of which were absolutely delicious! This kind of service and care for customers is what sets the best restaurants apart, and we didn't even have to say anything. 

Waiting longer for the inside seating is absolutely worth it, as it has very warm inviting vibes. You can see inside the kitchen and watch the chefs depending on your seat too, which I always love. I do want to come try the outdoor tents one day too, which are separate from the other outdoor tables. They look pretty cozy and seem classier than typical outdoor spaces.

Onto the main courses - both pastas we tried were mouthwateringly good. The sheep's milk cheese agnolotti was the hit for me. It was so creamy and soft. I would have liked even more sundried tomato on top because it provided such a great balance against the sweetness of the honey inside, but it was a fantastic dish regardless. The mafaldini was great as well, and is honestly such an under-utilized pasta. It holds sauce perfectly in the little bumps and ridges, and has a great texture.

Overall I was blown away by both the food and service here, and would highly recommend this place for a fancy dinner or an occasion.

This place is WOW. First the service is impeccable. I had a 430pm reservation and NYC traffic is awful on a Friday afternoon that we showed up at 450 and they still took us!! Told us we had until 7pm (which is plenty of time). 

The food is delicious! They put Parmesan cheese on everything so if you don't like parm cheese then this place would not be fore you. Absolutely loved the malfidini!

Considering how hard it is to get a reservation here, our hopes were pretty high for Lilia -- and for the most part were met. The space is industrial yet feels warm, and though we ate indoors the igloos for outdoor seating are really cute and inviting looking. Our waitress had the kind of confidence that makes you feel you're in good hands -- her recommendation for wine was one of our favorite reds we've ever had (even if we shuddered a bit at the $21 price tag we saw after the fact...). 

While the pasta here is certainly great, we found the seafood small plates and desserts surprisingly more memorable. The spicy baked clams and herb butter mussels are bracingly flavorful, and the house made soft serve gelato sundaes with really inventive toppings (on my vanilla, amaretti mini cookies, lemony walnuts, sprinkles and giant chocolate shavings) a super interesting mix of sweet and savory. 

Overall a really pleasant experience (with maybe a tad too steep a price tag).

First visit was great, came back for my gf's birthday and it was night and day. Reservation for 8:30pm and seated us 20min later. Almost ran out of the Agnolotti pasta that my gf came for specifically (we come in from NJ). How do you almost run out of staple menu items at 830? We apparently got the last focaccia bread even though i wanted to order two of them. I paid $31+ for the lamb steak, ate a third of it and was looking forward to take it home. Well surprise surprise turns out the take home was not mine. I know for sure because I had one large piece and didn't have a bone in my entree nor would I ask to have it wrapped to go. Not a good COVID-19 move.

One of the best Italian restaurants in the five boroughs! The pastas and vegetables are incredible here, but the 5-star service really makes the place stand out as compared to comparable restaurants. It's true to form with Missy Robbins' "keep it simple" mantra, which translates to a welcoming and excellent, yet unpretentious, establishment. 

Here's a rundown of our favorite dishes, and I recommend you order multiple things to split with your party: 

- Start with the focaccia and green garlic butter. Surprisingly, the flavor is more packed in the focaccia whereas the garlic flavor is more subdued, making for a great combination and starter for your meal
- For drinks, you can't go wrong with a spritz or negroni
- Zucchini with lemon, capers, and mit. The slow roasted zucchini really absorbs all of the flavor of the other ingredients, so you get a really fresh, light, and summery vegetable 
- Grilled artichokes. Loved the garlic, breadcrumbs, and parmesan on it, but this is a whole grilled artichoke, so just know that going in since for some people, it can be a lot of work to get a little bit of artichoke. It's worth the hassle, but not something I get every time 
- Rigatoni. Just a tiny bit of kick with the chiles, but the pasta is the best version of al dente pasta I've had - just so perfect
- Mafaldini. Ok so I'm not the biggest traditional cacio e pepe fan, but this really blew me away. I like pink peppercorn because I think it contributes to a milder, fruiter flavor, and the cheese is amazing. I can still only eat about half of the dish before the flavors get a bit overbearing for me personally 
- Corzetti. My FAVORITE item on the menu. I wasn't sure what to expect but man, I've never had anything like this dish!!! It's an airy pasta with a light sauce, and the pine nuts and marjoram add a dimension of flavor that, in my mind, is unparalleled 
- Gnocchi. Light and fluffy and although I anticipated the broccoli pesto to be overpowering, it tasted like traditional pesto with a slight kick at the end of a bite
- Italian job is a MUST. Be sure to finish your meal with this soft serve gelato with honey, olive oil, sea salt, and fennel pollen is a chaotic yet heavenly dessert. 

Lilia is one of my favorites, and I hope you enjoy it as much as I do!

Lilia! Omg I've been waiting soooo long to try Lilia but reservations were always impossible. Literally like 5 years later I finally got to go, and even though we just sat at the bar, it was still very pleasant, and easy to snag at 5:30pm. Drinks were great (and mine was super pretty!!) and the pace of food was ok (pasta took a little longer after apps but it was fine I forgave them lol). Ordered a fresh mozzarella toast which was huge and delightful, as were the roasted zucchini, for apps. For pastas, of course I ordered my long awaited plate of mafaldini and a daily special which was a (unknowingly Spicy) sausage Fettuccine I think--both were delicious and the mafaldini texture was a highlight for me. It was slightlyyy heavier than I expected with the cheese, but overall everything was very pleasant. 10/10 would go back!! Ambiance was so cute and the aesthetic was chefs kiss. The great part of the bar was the view of the open kitchen.

I booked a yurt dinner experience for myself and a friend. The yurt was pleasantly quiet and secluded from the bustling restaurant. First antipasti course was like mezze, lots of small plate, mostly vegetables. The caramelized fennel with balsamic was possibly the best dish of the evening. I ordered the bianco bianco and my friend had the lilia version of a whiskey sour. She said her drink was a little sweet. Mine was fresh and light, but not very flavorful. Zuchinni with ricotta salata was a slightly odd combination, but the zuchinni was juicy and well cooked. Radicchio salad needed a sweeter balsamic to tone down the bitterness of the leaves. Next was the pasta course. I was a little disappointed that we didn't get the honey saffron pasta dish. We received the maldafini, corzetti, and gnocchi with pesto. The peppery maldafini was the best of the trio. The gnocchi were just ok, the pesto was not my favorite. Corzetti was mostly butter and pine nuts, so it was tasty but uninspired. Next was steak, potatoes and a spicy rigatoni. The potatoes were awesome and crispy. The steak portion was massive and totally made the price of the yurt worthwhile. I had put in the reservation notes that I am a pescatarian, so I was a bit let down that the accommodation they made was a fourth pasta rather than a fish option. Dessert was essentially a doughnut shaped choux sandwich with a light lemon cream. It was a perfect end to a super filling meal. Anything richer or heavier i would not have been able to enjoy at that point in the meal. I was so full, and both my friend and I each brought home a ton of leftovers. Overall, a great experience!

Went to Lilia for a birthday dinner and it did not disappoint. The staff was incredibly attentive and helpful. Everything we ordered was SO good. We started with the cherry tomato focaccia and green garlic butter. This is honestly one of the best dishes I've had. Like ever. We also ordered the mafaldini and the sheeps milk agnolotti. The mafaldini was heavier than I expected, but so savory and delicious. The sheeps milk agnolotti was quite sweet, and definitely one of the more unique pasta dishes I've had. We finished with the Italian job. Think Gelato with really great olive oil/Italian spices. It's weird, but good!! Overall 10/10.
A truly perfect meal. Everything we ordered was excellent and made me want to return immediately. We ordered focaccia, 4 pastas, and 2 gelatos. Can't go wrong!

I really wanted to love Lilia, especially after all the trouble I went through to get a reservation, but it just did not meet expectations. Don't get me wrong; the pasta was fresh and nothing was bad, but based on the continued outrage over how Lilia remains starless, I expected really beautifully nuanced or bold flavors. I didn't get either. 

If I considered service in my rating, it would be 2 stars. The staff made me feel like a cover, not a person. 

Pass on the soft-serve. It's better than what you get out of a truck, but not by much.

Five stars for the service. Attentive, engaging, thoughtful, observant. As to the food, two stars. Overall, 2 stars with a sprinkling of stardust...2 1//2 tops. I was expecting nuance,  finesse and surprise. The presentation was well executed but the taste underwhelming. My thoughts the next day on the meal and the restaurant: overrated, overhyped , overpriced, oversalted, overbooked, over...

Solid food but a tad overhyped.  Having said that, I didn't try the pasta which I 100% would go back and try. I had the cacio Pepe fritelle which was ok, just lacked any flavor or anything special. The Bass with salsa verde was delish and very flavorful. Service was solid all around and def is worth a try.

The best pasta I've ever had. We ordered the Sheep's Milk Agnolotti, Mafaldini, and Ricotta Gnocchi. All of the dishes were cooked to perfection. If I had to pick a favorite, it would be the Agnolotti since I've never had anything like it before. I'd recommend going with a few friends so you could try various dishes.

Attentive service until the place fills up then you never see your waiter. The food was ok but definitely not worth the hype or waiting forever to get a table. I loved the touch of the sommelier coming to our table and discussing which wine we would like best. Other than that, this place didn't feel special and very overpriced. It was my birthday too :(

My go-to for Italian in the city! Just so good, Missy Robbins just kills it every time. 

Here's what we go:
Seasonal Focaccia - this is a must and best thing to start the meal off with. That garlic herb butter is to die for. I could literally eat it with a spoon! 
Mafaldini - almost like a cacio e pepe but with pink peppercorn, such a unique flavor and I love the shape and bite of this pasta
Sheep's Milk Agnolotti - a crowd favorite and definitely a must! Perfect balance of richness from the cream and saffron and the tart of the tomato. This is a must! 
Corzetti - the sage butter sauce on this pasta is amazing! 
Corn filled cappelletti - I got this one for the first time this time and I was pleasantly surprised! It's definitely on the sweeter side but I love corn and it paired so well with the sauce. 
Olive Oil Cake - love love love this cake! It's so moist and flavorful and the fresh whipped cream and fruit is amazing. This was the perfect end to our meal!  

Overall you genuinely can not go wrong with anything here. Be sure to make a reservation either by calling or on Resy 1 month out. It is 100% worth waking up early to book this place, you won't regret it!

I am a fan of Misi and Chef Robbins.  The starters were ok. The Cacio di Pepe fritters were tasty and adequately peppery. The foccacia was fair, but a bit dry. The mozzarella was good, not great as it was a bit bland. The zucchini looked like a plate of dill pickles and had a soft unrememorable flavor.  The pastas were good, but not great. I have always enjoyed the pastas at Misi, but the pastas at Lilia did not deliver the same pizazz. The angolotti were ok, delivered warm and not hot as they seemed to have been sitting for a while. The corn filled were tasty, but their sauce lacking. The Maladini as a pasta had a great texture, but the parmesan sauce was very light except the heavy laden presence of black pepper. If you have ever had the gelato at Misi, it is rich, but cooling. The gelato at Lilia was again good, but not great. The gelato was delivered a little bit melted down and there seemed to be more interest in the toppings rather than the gelato. I will say the Spritz were delicious and the wine well chosen. The waiter was very nice and knowledgeable.  I would prefer going back to Misi.

I have to first speak on the service I experienced at Lilia - I see some reviews saying otherwise but honestly it was similar to a fine dining experience which was nice given the price point. Everyone was super attentive and pleasant. Really elevated things. 

Didn't love the appetizers but the pastas and desserts were amazing. Servings are small but they let you know this. Usually pretty packed - reservations advised unless you get there super early. I'll be back eventually!

We somehow and luckily got a table without a reservation at night on Labor Day. Everything we had was amazing. We started with the cacio e pepe fritelle, grilled scallops and the artichoke with Lambrusco. Absolutely delicious we were savoring each bite. Then, for our meals we had the Maldafini and the Ravioli. Then, for desert the Italian Job, which was such a unique savory desert with an amaro.

Friends rec this place and brought us here. First of all the Diet Coke wasn't great and served in the smallest glass given to mankind. If I'm going to pay hefty for a Diet Coke, then give me my damn Diet Coke in a glass larger than 2oz please. 

Starters- tasty- but not worth the price tag. Yogurt in a dish for dipping, We didn't finish it. Hummus delicious. Salad- not enough for more than 1? Strange. Each priced $17-$23. Pita bread excellent. 

I ordered shrimp as main.. 6 pieces in a dish like a sardine box. Not even jumbo shrimp. Dish As big as my palm... for real? Not again. 

French fries were seasoned perfectly, served in a small cereal like bowl? Interesting how they are family style but really small servings. Lamb $72 was good but had more goop than lamp.. not sure what it was. Trying to pick out the lamb.. challenging. 

Server knocked over my Diet Coke and broke the glass, it spilled all over my new leather Louis v bag, down my legs- and shattered the glass everywhere. Nothing but a sorry from the helper.  That was bizarre and ruined my dinner for sure. In a situation like that the manager needs to accommodate and make a point of apologizing, offer a round of drinks or dessert at the very least?

Food overall was tasty- not sure it was worth the $450 tab that's for sure.

I'm not a food critic, so I'll be blunt. This place is not that good. 

The portions and prices are fine, but the food is aggressively flavorful. It almost feels as though the chef is trying too hard to be creative with the menu. 

Also, everything is VERY salty. 

Overall, it was a fine experience (the service is good) but I do not understand the hype around this place other than its trendiness and aesthetic.

Just ate dinner here tonight. Not sure what all the hype is about. Most of the food was overly salted, including the celebrated focaccia which is now cherry tomato vs. garlic bread. The agnolotti (the most raved about pasta on the menu) was a strange combination of flavors that didn't quite mesh and nothing else stood out. We ordered the prawns & scallops appetizers, sea bass entree and Italian job dessert in addition to the focaccia and agnolotti. Service was spotty and our server literally fawned over the people right next to us while we were sort of ignored. I promise my partner and I are polite to a fault, didn't complain (until Yelp) and tip well - so I'm not sure why this happened. If this is the best pasta in NYC, then we should hang our heads in shame given how many Italians live here. Won't be going back.

Sister restaurant to Misi, the menu is similar and the food is just as good. They're famous for their agnolotti pasta but we had the Cappelletti with sweet corn this time around and it was delicious. The little gem salad, artichokes and Italian broccoli are all wonderful small plates as well. Top 5 Negroni if you're into that on a hot day.

We tried the restaurant because we heard great reviews of it and obviously the place is infamously hard to get a space. On the day we visited, our starters were good but our main courses - horrible. We ordered three pastas. The first one had to be sent back because it wasn't properly cooked - some of it was inedible. We sent back the pasta but it was returned not much better. Can't say much about the other two dishes. Not good in general and I am a big foodie. I eat most days. I'm not sure if we had a new cook. Needless to say, very very disappointed and I would not go back again.

Where do I start!! We visited this place a month ago and it took me almost a month to get over the food hangover.  This place is definitely WORTH THE HYPE!!

1) Ambience - check (we dined outdoor in the Yurt)
2) Service - check 
3) Drinks -  check 
4) Food -  check check check (incredible.. if I were to be critical, I would say the dessert could've been better)

The place might seem pricey, but the entire experience makes up for it.  Highly recommend seating outdoor (if possible).  Statutory note: There is a long wait to get the reservation.

We had customized menu (which is there speciality).  More then me explaining the food, I will let the picture do the talking.

Overall, HIGHLY recommended, 5 stars to the place.

Restaurant's gotten progressively worse over the last 5 years, from a service perspective, and there is no doubt repeat local customers are not their targeted demographic.  As a business model, it is about maximizing the revenue per sqft and so be it if your waiting customers are told
the wrong wait times and are left standing around even when they could be relaxing in their abode across the street until your table is ready for them.

The new outdoor dining yurts are something, many points for creativity.

Salad is very creative and fresh.  The appetizer and the pasta dishes were underwhelming, and progressively have been the past couple of years -- the things you do for friends!

Olive oil cake is good and I would recommend trying.

The morning coffee and pastries are actually substantially a better experience end-to-end, and their new covid breakfast menu expansion is actually quite nice.

So, dinner 1 star, breakfast and coffee experience 4.5 stars

Evenings geared towards tourist and out-of-towners and mornings more mixed.

Let me start by saying I have been to Lilia before and had a much better experience. This time, we opted to do the Yurt experience for a birthday celebration and were a bit disappointed. We went in expecting Lilia's top menu items, which was not what we were served. When I didn't see some of the pastas I was looking forward to the most I asked if I could swap out a pasta for a different one that was not on our pre-fixe menu and was told no but I could add it a la carte. I said yes sure since it was a birthday celebration and but we never received the pasta, it was not added to the bill but this was a bit disappointing. It also took us 45 minutes to get our first course, while the yurt across from us got 2 courses in that time. We did feel a bit neglected as well as we waited a while between drinks. Overall for the price of the yurt experience, this is not something I would recommend, I would say just visit Lilia normally.

Agree that the food is delicious but the service was less than ideal for a restaurant at this price point. I'm also a server at a restaurant and the hosts didn't have great communication with one another and the server seemed like they would rather have been anywhere else.

Did walk in on a Wednesday around 5 PM and were seated immediately. 

I tried a myriad of cocktails and all seemed either weak or too sweet for me. Ended up sticking with the red wine.

We ordered a number of items, focusing on the vegetarian dishes.

-focaccia: this was good! The butter was bit strong on the salt but the focaccia itself was phenomenal 

-cacio e pepe balls: this was not my favorite. It was incredibly salty 

- little gem salad: this was really refreshing after the salt bomb 

-mafaldini: my favorite of the pastas, this was great with light parm sauce

-agnolotti: 2nd fav; the saffron was actually not my favorite on this pasta (I'm Indian and not used to having my saffron on savory food) but the pasta was perfectly cooked and the Sheep's milk was light and delicious 

-corzetti: this was okay; it kind of felt like ravioli without the filling 

-gnocchi: did not like this dish at all. The flavors of the sauce were off and the gnocchi itself was not cooked well. Would recommend skipping this dish. 

-the Italian job: my favorite dish of the night: dessert! Was delicious with ice cream and olive oil, and seasonings. Would highly recommend 

Overall, wasn't too impressed. They forgot half our dishes mid way through dinner so we had to wait an hour for the second half of our meal. Didn't end up leaving until 3 hours after we got there. 

Not what I expected based on the price of dinner.

Restaurant hype can really kill an experience but in this case it only enhanced mine. A friend who lives in the neighborhood advised me to physically go to the restaurant to inquire about a reservation, which absolutely worked, belying the fact that Resy is not an accurate picture of the world. My friend and I tried the focaccia, broccoli, agnolotti, and mafaldini. The focaccia was sublime and demands to be slathered in the visually striking green garlic butter it's served with. The broccoli was showered in parm and thus awesome. Both pastas were excellent but the pepperiness and al dente nature of the mafaldini was truly spectacular. The Italian job dessert was memorable, but I'm not sure I'm entirely sold on this particular sweet and savory pairing. Our server was excellent and I'd return in a heart beat.

First time here so I can only speak to this one experience. The service was amazing, everyone so was attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. The only thing that negatively impacted our experience was that the food was incredibly salty. We got the mussels, clams, focaccia, and rib eye steak, and every dish we ordered came a little too salty for us. We couldn't finish the steak because of this. If it wasn't for the over salting, the food would have been amazing!

My first time at Lilia and the food did not disappoint! Service was great, food came out decently fast. 

If there are any tips I can give you is book and early reservation! I would give this place 5 stars however they were sold out of half the menu (all the top dishes like the mozzarella bread, tomato focaccia, and the famous sheep's milk agnolotti )

I would highly recommend the following when they are sold out of those top dishes ^

Appetizer: 
1. Prosciutto, Parmesana butter, and Dijon mustard seeds, spread on fresh bread  

Main dish: 
2. Corn stuffed in homemade pasta with white cream that was so decedent I took a nap on the pasta pillows and went to heaven ‍ perfect summertime dish! 

3. Olive oil cake was 8/10, dry, not as much whipped cream on the side for the entire slice. 

4/5 total. If you are able to go,  don't pass up the opportunity!

Managed to find an earlier dinner reservation for two and came with a friend for a little midweek treat. Like prior visits, I left wowed by the meal and happier. 

For drinks, we split a bottle of a light orange wine and each got an Aperol Spritz. Wine was pretty good with nothing to complain about but the spritz is so light, refreshing, and tasty. Definitely recommend. 

For cocktail snacks and antipasti, we ordered the focaccia (cherry tomato) with the green garlic butter, the grilled artichoke and the Italian broccoli. I like that the topping varies for the focaccia which is baked amazingly and the green garlic butter is so dank (good). The vegetables were simple but great flavor with the use of cheese and bread crumbs. 

For the pastas, we ordered the sheep's milk cheese filled Agnolotti, mafaldini, and a new seasonal variety corn filled cappelletti. Agnolotti and mafaldini are classics and must gets I think while the corn cappelletti was great to try but I think I'll stick to first two mentioned or new pastas the next time. It did have a great burst of sweet corn flavor. 

For dessert, we ordered the classic Italian job and the new/seasonal dessert crostata. I liked the crostata as a new flavor/dessert option, but the Italian job is so good it's hard to beat if you could only choose one dessert.

Looking forward to whenever the next visit is and to try more antipasti and a new lemon sorbet dessert.

Decided to stop by on a random Monday and the line was out the door!! We didn't have a reservation but was seated immediately because there was room at the bar. No complaints- the bartender was super nice and knowledgeable on drinks! 
The food was absolutely amazing. I'm in love with the mozzarella with garlic on toast. The mozzarella cheese was super fresh and every bite was delightful. 
The clams were juicy and full of flavor. Highly recommend as well. 
I also got the sheep milk cheese filled agnolotti and mafaldini pastas. Both were very yummy but if I had to choose, I'd go with the agnolotti. The agnolotti was more creamy due to the cheese on the inside but yet light in flavor, while the mafaldini was slightly on the heavier side but somehow managed to have a fresh zesty taste? (Mind blown) 

Either way, you really can't go wrong with any of those! 

Ambiance: 5/5
Service: 5/5 
Good: 5/5 

I highly recommend! 

Also, tip: make a reservation!

This place is really hard to get reservations for. If you happen to be able or want a 5pm dinner reservation sometimes day of around 1pm a few 5/530 reservations open up on Resy. 
I had really high expectations of this place especially given how quickly their reservations go. The menu is on the smaller side but everything is simple and done really well. 
Highly recommend ordering grilled clams, Arancini, prosciutto, sheep's milk pasta. 
I also tried the rigatoni but wasn't crazy about it. Also not crazy about their dessert. The olive oil cake was pretty dry. The whipped cream served with it is delicious though and tastes really fresh. Also tried a vanilla ice cream dessert with olive oil on top it's relatively good. 
The drink menu and beer selection is also very good. Service is very attentive but all times I've come it always starts to fall off mid meal.

If you ever find yourself on a stroll in Williamsburg and craving Italian, look no further.

Was here to celebrate a birthday. We did not make reservations ahead of time but got here around opening time so they had a table. 

We ordered several apps, pasta and dessert. I dont even know where to begin. Everything was amazing. They're obviously all over the 'gram for their mafaldini, and I can see why. 

What really surprised me was the dessert. We got the olive oil cake, strawberry crostata, and vanilla bean parfait (italian job). Omg. That crostata was TO DIE FOR. The vanilla parfait was also fantastic (it comes with a healthy layer of olive oil so if youre not into that then dont get it but...treat yo self).

A delicious classic restaurant in Williamsburg. Everything is delicious, although I do want to come back to try more of their meat and fish dishes as well as their panini breakfast/lunch sandwiches.

We started with the little gem salad and focaccia - we loved both. Absolutely order the focaccia here if you can before its sold out for the night. For entrees we got the mafaldini, agnolotti and this flat pasta I can't remember the name of. All were delicious, but our favorite was the agnolotti. I do wish some of Missy's pastas were a little more varied. I know they offer the rigatoni with red sauce, but its a bit average for me. The buttery/simple pastas are all delicious individually, but when you're having only that it does get a little one note (our fault for ordering this way!). Regardless, well worth the difficult to get reservation and we will be back!

Follow me on Instagram @eatenbysteph

Lilia is absolutely worth the hype, id like to start off with that.
Chef Missy Robins is a pasta genius and the food is just remarkable. I have yet to eat something here that i'm not blown away by.
I went for my 3rd time yesterday for my birthday with my boyfriend. We ordered a LOT, because it's just...how we do things haha. We got the mozzarella (10/10) the cacio e pepe frittelle (10/10) and then some other small dishes which i'll add in the photos. EVERY item i've tried on the menu is a 10/10 here and i would 100% order everything again, over and over and over.

In order to get a seat at this exclusive restaurant you MUST make your reservation exactly 30 days in advance, and slots open up at 10am. It is competitive and if you don't get on as early as opening time it is likely you'll have to wait a whole other day to make your reservation. With that being said, it's worth the wait, it's worth the 30 day in advance reservation, it's worth being cracked out on caffeine staring at your phone waiting for 10am to get that perfect time and table. trust me.

The pasta is the star here. While everything on the menu is beyond delicious and mouth watering chef robins handmade pasta's are the star of the show. I don't have enough words to describe how absolutely incredible the pasta here is but it is just OUT of this world. The Corzetti alle erbe was by far one of the most delicious pasta dishes i've ever had. The pasta is rolled incredibly thin and cut in circles, i was blown away by this dish and wish I could eat it every night. The agnolotti is another favorite of mine, the honey adds a touch of sweetness that is unmatched. My boyfriend and i ordered 5 different pasta dishes on top of all the appetizers (we LOVE pasta) Our eyes are definitely bigger than our stomachs but that's no issue for us because we love us some leftovers.

Now for the reason why I can't give this wonderful restaurant 5 stars and i'm hoping to be able to update it to 5 stars on my next visit in the future. The service here isn't always great. I understand that the restaurant is on the smaller side and that reservations are hard to get, but because they're hard to get, you want to feel good when you're there. I got to Lilia around 5:05 for a 5pm reservation (being late is a huge fear of mine but hey, it is what it is) I was told as soon as I walked in that they would need the table by 6:45 so if we weren't done with dinner they would have to take our dessert order to go and we'd need to leave. I have worked in the restaurant industry so I get it, and I get that reservations are made and sometimes you have to do what you have to do, so I said okay no problem...however hearing that you're given a limited time the second you walk into a place isn't really how you want your dinner to start off (especially your birthday dinner)
Because I have anxiety I was worried the whole time we weren't going to finish in time (which we didn't) so while we were still eating our pasta I asked for the check in advance and told my waitress that we'd pay ahead of time this way it would be easier and quicker for them, and I ordered my dessert to go this way once 6:45 came around we would be ready to get up. 

It was slightly aggravating that i even had to do that, but I tried to not let it bother me. I asked a waiter who came over to pack up our Three  leftover pasta dishes to go (one which had hardly been touched because we were so full) while waiting for our check and 'to go' dessert. 

We got the dessert and our check and left....3 minutes down the block we realized our waiter never brought us our doggy bag with our leftovers! 

My boyfriend ran back into the restaurant and was given the doggy bag, and once we got back to my house (which is over an hour away) it turned out to not be our food. 

There is just about nothing more upsetting and disappointing than getting home with food that's not yours...not only can we not eat it obviously, but when you spend almost $300 at a restaurant, don't finish your food and are looking forward to finishing it later or the next day it's a huge letdown. It's food that was paid for and it feels terrible and like a waste.

The only thing Lilia needs to work on is better service,  and to 10000% check who's order they are giving to which customer, because when you're paying for a meal and taking home leftovers...it's food you've paid for that now you're not getting.
Order as many things as you can.  Then add one more thing. Then get 2 desserts. Ya welcome.

We originally got a reservation during COVID and we finally rescheduled after Lilia opened back up. Reservations are insanely hard to get you have to do a month in advance. On the day of our reservation, NYC was pouring rain and we were supposed to sit outside with no covering. Staffs texted us saying they will call us to reschedule if weather conditions is not great but we never got a call. We tried calling them multiple times and the phone never went through until we literally called within 5 min after they open. It was quite annoying for the rescheduling process and once we got there we tried to get as much as we can get since we don't know when we can get another reservation. The pastas were definitively very unique but my friend and I both thought the garlic cream and bread was the most tasty and worth. The food is great but would not be the first choice to come back given how difficult it was to get reservations. 

PRO TIP: 
1. They do reservations a month in advance and Resy opens up at 10am everyday so make sure to stay on top of it if you are really determined to get a reservation

Went to Lilia for the second time last night for dinner as sort of a second chance. The first time I went to Lilia with my partner was toward the end of fall on a cold night pre-pandemic. We sat outside because it was the only table we could get and we were dying to try the pasta! While the food tasted good, it was cold almost immediately upon arrival. I remember ordering the mafaldini which I enjoyed the taste of but it seemed like the dining experience wasn't conducive to eating in the cold. I tolerate the cold better but my partner was uncomfortable throughout the meal and wished we had gotten a table inside, though I remember they offered us blankets. 

I say all that to preface this review because we were kind of hoping that Lilia would be redeemed with our second visit. We called in the late afternoon on a Sunday to see what the wait time would be like if we walked in around 7 compared to a later dinner around 8:30-9. The hostess gave me the wait time for the current time (it was around 5:15 and I was told we could be seated for 6) but implied she wouldn't be able to give me an estimated wait time for later unless I walked in. With a sigh I said okay, thanks, and asked my partner if he would be willing to chance it again knowing that we would likely wait for a table. Lilia doesn't take reservations for tables for 2 so it's only possible to walk in and hope for the best knowing you will wait. He agreed and we arrived around 8 knowing we would likely have to put our names down and go elsewhere for the mean time. As expected when we arrived we were told we could sit at the bar in 15-20 minutes. We asked how long it would be to wait for a table and were told the first table would be available at 9:15 (an hour and fifteen minutes later). We were already hungry so we stuck with the bar seats and walked down the block to the Exley for a drink (which by the way is a lovely queer bar with a tasty margarita!). We got the notification for the table about 20-25 minutes later and headed back. Given the bar seats this time and outdoor seating in the cold last time, it really seemed like Lilia is just trying to maximize profits and doesn't really care about the customer having a nice time--the next customer will be right behind you willing to wait longer and pay more and they know it. But I digress..

For drinks we started with the bianco bianco which my partner and I both enjoyed and found nice and refreshing. For appetizers we ordered the grilled clams and prosciutto with parmigian butter and bread. The clams had a nice little spice from the Calabrian chili and I covered my entire piece of bread in the parmigian butter! For our entrees we ordered the gnocchi and sheep's milk agnolotti. Both were delicious and I particularly enjoyed the agnolotti; it was slightly sweet, filling, and perfectly cooked! The service at the bar was well paced and friendly, no complaints whatsoever about that. I will say that while the food was absolutely delicious I didn't feel like I was getting the best bang for my buck. The dishes at Lilia are small for the price so we left almost thinking about stopping at the Italian street fair down the block after for a sausage and pepper hero.. ultimately we decided against it but when you're paying a hefty price you'd hope to leave feeling full and satisfied!

Unfortunately I think this second visit will be the last. While I very much enjoy the food at Lilia, the value and experience leaves more to be desired.

We went on a Sunday evening without a reservation. We just wanted to try and see if we could get a table by walking in. We waited 1.5 hours so we just walked around the area. 

We got in total of five items. One isn't pictured: Italian Job 

1. Corzetti Alle Erbe (9.5/10) I absolutely loved this dish. We were shocked by this dish because it was the one we didn't know what to get and asked the server for recommendation. The pine nuts added a nice crunch to the pasta. I highly recommend this although it is a little bit too buttery. 

2. Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti (8/10) this was the most highly rated item but I felt like it was okay. I think I just don't really like sheep milk cheese and I had high expectations for this. 

3. Roasted Garlic Scale Focaccia (10/10) I loved this. This is the one thing I will order 100% without a doubt. It was so fluffy with the garlic and the green garlic butter was amazing with the bread even though the bread was amazing by itself. GET THIS ONE!! 

4. Grilled Clams (6.5/10) this was also another highly rated item but it didn't meet out expectations. We expected more flavor as the waiter said it's spicy, but it was kind of bland with just the sauce on it. The sauce kind of overwhelmed the clam itself

5. Italian Job (7/10) we knew we wanted this as dessert as it was highly reviewed. It was way too sweet for us. The olive oil was nice as it was a savory sweet dessert but there was too much and I can still taste the olive oil flavor. 

Overall, I'm glad we got to try this place and try some of their delicious food. We sat at the bar as we walked in and they had seating there in 1.5 hours. The waiter was really nice and the staff all took care of us.
This place is legit. Go here. Get the broccoli and the clams. You won't regret it. Seriously get the broccoli and the clams. Also the lamb.
Can never not get the Agnolotti! Attentive service always. Really enjoyed the Italian Job dessert as well, lovely textures and balance of flavors.

Delicious pasta and great vibes. We got a 9 pm reservation, but the party before us was 40 mins late so we had to wait since they let them stay over. -1 star for that.

By the time we sat down, they were out of the scallops and had only 1 of the agnolotti, so try to nab an early reservation if you can.

Once we did get our food, the mood drastically improved.  It was light, airy, but somehow still super flavorful. Agnolotti, ravioli and gnocchi were most haves. Rigatoni and mafaldi were very good but kind of plain. We got the mozzarella bread to start which was also great. Great wine selection.

Finished with the Italian job which was very interesting but worth trying. We were in a deep food coma by the end. Would absolutely come back if we had an earlier time slot.

Delicious meal. Amazing experience. We went for the pre fixe yurt experience and ended up being seated at the bar thanks to weather (heat and thunder storms). The entire evening couldn't have been better from the meal, to the wine pairings, to the atmosphere. A delightful night from start to finish and I would recommend a visit to anyone!

Lilia Caffe: 
My sister and I came here for the caffe side of Lilia one afternoon and we ordered two sandwiches and two desserts to share! 

Espresso Cream Bomboloni- 2.5/5, I was not a fan... Maybe I have the wrong impression of what it was supposed to be but it was very dry and bland tasting to me. I didn't taste much of espresso and the insides had plenty of cream but still felt dry. It wasn't sweet (IMO) at all. It was also extremely heavy :(

Sea Salt Chocolate Chip Cookie- 3.5/5 this cookie looked promising!! It was beautiful and it was big but the inside had a very crumbly corn muffin like texture to it. It wasn't bad but it was just not what I was expecting in a cookie! It was still very delicious

Prosciutto, Parmigiano Butter, Balsamic Mustard 5/5!!! This sandwich was phenomenal! The bread was a bit hard but there was a good amount of prosciutto! The little mustards gave the sandwich a nice popping effect!! 

Prosciutto Cotto, Squaquerello Cheese, House Focaccia 5/5 !!! This was SO good, the focaccia was nice and fluffy and the prosciutto cotto really resembled a beautiful ham. The cheese and arugula really help elevate the sandwich and balance all the flavors!!

Lilia- 

Red and White Radicchio, Pine Nuts, Red Onion, Balsamic 3/5- I wish they cut up this salad a little more instead of leaving all these giant pieces of radicchio! I wasn't a huge fan of the balsamic, it felt like it was VERY strong and just overpowered the entire dish! My mouth felt very tart and sour afterwards 

Grilled zucchini with garlic scrape, mint and capers- this dish was TINYYYYYYY. There was probably like 1/4 a zucchini here!!! It was still super delicious but again, so small... the mint, garlic scrape and capers added a nice fresh and salty taste to the zucchini but probably could do without this dish!

Roasted Garlic Scape Focaccia, Green Garlic Butter 5/5- LISTEN TO EVERYONE's REVIEWS!! This was THE BOMB DOT COM. The focaccia had beautiful roasted garlic inside the bread. It was super light and fluffy. And I understand that's a lot of butter but just do it. Just eat it.  ITS GOOD. 

Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs 3/5- I had such high hopes for these clams! They look a lot bigger than they actually are. These clams are really small little necks (I think). I felt like this dish was good but not great. It wasn't spicy and it didn't have that little kick, I couldn't really taste much of the grilled clams. The breadcrumbs were actually the things that overpowered this entire dish! I wouldn't recommend this, I would try the mussels next time! Or the shrimp if you're between those two! 

Grilled Prawns, Fennel Pollen, Lemon 4/5 - I'm not a crazy big fan of fennel pollen but it worked very well with these shrimps! They're perfectly cooked and are head on. Don't discard the heads without sucking on the juices first!!! It's nice and briny from the shrimp and has a good chunk of the fennel pollen seasoning!

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey 5/5- everyone's favorite pasta dish!! I don't like sheep's milk but this was super delicious! Each piece was like a pocket of happiness. The buttery saffron sauce absolutely made this dish! They also do not skimp on the saffron!!!

Corzetti Alle Erbe, Pine Nuts, Marjoram, Parmigiano Reggiano 5/5 - this was just phenomenal. They're just round flat pastas with sauce on top! GET THIS PASTA!!!

Mortadella Filled Tortelli, Fennel Fronds, Fennel Pollen 4.5/5 this pasta dish was really good but lacked a little bit in comparison to the first two!! I'd recommend eating this one first? Or separate from the other two !!

Black Bass, Salsa Verde, Coal Roasted Yukon Gold Potatoes 4.5/5 - perfectly cooked piece of black bass with a very light sauce on top. The potatoes were a bit lemony. It was delicious but might recommend another pasta since that's what they're known for !!

Italian Job - 5/5- smooth and rich gelato with fresh olive oil and I think fennel pollen and flakey salt. It didn't sound like it would be good to me but once you have a taste of the sweet creamy gelato and the savory olive oil with flakey salt, you'll change your mind! 

Olive Oil Cake with whipped cream and blood orange?- 5/5 I'm not typically a fan of olive oil cakes but this one was not overpowering! It was also very moist

Look at my profile-I'm a guy who knows and loves food; this is the best and most pleasurable dinner I have had in NYC. We were blessed enough to sit at the bar (which is usually the best place to sit at any restaurant) and our tall/hot bartender/server recommended a delicious wine to us; not too fruit forward, but still full of flavor. We kicked off the meal with the mozzarella and also the clams. Good god almighty these are good dishes to start with. The mozz: so light, so fluffy, a delicate flavor of lemon to accompany it. For my entree I had the agnolotti which is stuffed with sheeps milk cheese (I called them 'cheese blunts') the flavors were just out of control. Absolutely unreal. The sauce they were in? FUHGEDABOUTIT. The dessert: get the Italian Job ice cream. I can't even describe how great everything was about my experience here. Put your name in and wait however long you have to. There's like 25 bars within a 10 minute walk. Have a few cold ones there and wait until you can eat here. Seriously it is the best food I have had in the city. How was the service, you ask? I dropped my knife on the floor because I'm a klutz, and within 30 seconds I had a brand new knife by my side. For food this good the prices are very affordable. Also there was a big car crash right outside as we were eating! What a night

Honestly I don't even know where to start! We got out of the cab in front of Lilia to down pouring rain. We (6 of us) had to run from the cab into the restaurant because of how bad it was even for a 20 second run. We got there at 8:15 for an 8:15 reservation. Upon getting in there the hostess told us we have to wait outside!!!! We all looked at her like she was insane because it was torrential downpours outside so we just tried to stand out of the way indoors so we wouldnt get wet outside and we received more attitude from the hostess telling us that it was a service entrance we were standing by.. We stood in the back by the coffee bar to get out of the way and we waited a couple minutes for our table to be ready. When we finally got to our seats we ordered a bottle of wine as we looked through the menu. All of a sudden there was a flood coming from the kitchen! Half of the staff was sweeping or mopping a mass amount of water out the side door. They didnt seem phased by this as maybe some of them have experienced this before. The water was about and inch above the floor and was right under our table which was next to the door they were sweeping water out of. My friend and his pregnant wifes feet got wet and his shoes (which were white) were ruined and one of the people sweeping (not his fault) actually splashed my shirt with water. At no point did any staff ask if we would like to move seats or apologize for the water. My friend whos shoes got ruined is an ex chef and has worked in the hospitality industry so he asked as a courtesy if we could be moved until the water situation was figured out, maybe get an appetizer and a bottle of wine while we waited. Our waitress who was very nice said that was fine so we waited it out by the coffee bar again until they got it situated. When we finally sat down to eat the food was very good.. but it also was some of the slowest service i've ever received. We had our dinner served family style but they pretty much brought out the food dish by dish, making our dinner last over 3.5 hours long. If something is on the drink menu, dont look forward to getting it. The first bottle of wine we got they ran of immediately upon us ordering it, and several beers i tried ordering and scotches a friend tried ordering were unavailable that were on the menu. Also one of the two meats (lamb leg steak) was sold out so just very limited availability for a saturday at 8 pm... When the bill finally came 3.5 hours later we saw that we were charged for everything not even comped a simple appetizer like the caccio pepe balls or the bottle of wine that we had while waiting for the water to subside. The bill was over $600 which we were obviously prepared to pay but still is very expensive given the lackluster service. Like i said, the food was very good but the hospitality factor and the restaurant experience was next to horrible. I couldnt honestly recommend with a clear conscience after this experience. APPROACH WITH CAUTION.

Beautiful restaurant. Great service. Good wine. 
Food: 
- roasted garlic scape focaccia -- SO GOOD. Maybe my favorite thing from the meal lol 

- red and white radicchio -- really delicious, but it's a salad. 

- grilled artichoke -- didn't love this and would skip next time. only order this if you LOVE artichoke?? Idk I thought it was just OK.

- grilled clams -- really good! Not super memorable or special though. Would go for the scallops or prawns instead next time. 

Rigatoni Diavola -- big disappointment! Super bland and boring. I think this is one of the signature dishes though. This is where I confess that I don't really like Italian food that much. Maybe you really need to have an appreciation and a taste for subtle Italian flavors and fresh pasta to really like this dish. But for me it really didn't do much at all. Felt overrated and I would definitely skip this dish next time. 

Sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti -- now this was GOOD. Flavors were so light, but still kind of rich and really interesting. The pasta felt like little pillows. The honey was divine. I would definitely recommend this one. 

I wish I could actually give this place 3.5 stars for the food. Some dishes were really good but overall I felt kind of meh about the food considering all the hype around this restaurant. Maybe this is for real Italian food lovers who can appreciate all the subtleties of the flavors and the skill that goes into making fresh pasta. The freshness and quality of the pasta, bread, veggies and seafood were impressive, but the overall composition of the dishes didn't live up to my expectations. With that said, I would definitely go again and give more of their seafood, meat, and different pastas a chance.

I die for their sheep milk filled agnolotti. Honestly my favorite dish in nyc. I've had only great experiences with this restaurant. HOWEVER my only complaint when coming in today for dinner is that the place was SOOOOOOOO INSANELY HOT. I mean uncomfortably hot. We were blushed in the face just sitting down! We thought at 5pm on a humid June night, that inside seating was a good choice. Little did we know that the inside was probably worse than the outside. Even though the food was incredible, we were so distracted by the temperature of the inside, we had to cut our dinner short and not place our additional orders. Please, please, please figure this out because we love the restaurant but when it is as hot as a sauna, it takes away from the overall experience.

It is so worth the wait to get a reservation here...we waited 5 years!  Don;t believe the poor reviews.  The food was out of this world good, staff super polite, friendly and knowledgeable .  They didn't rush us even though they were packed.  Gave us plenty of time between courses so we could chat and digest.  I cannot say enough great things about this place.  They treated us like rockstars!

We've been wanting to eat here for years and were so excited to score a reservation during our last visit. The foccacia and salad were perfect starters and we shared a few pasta dishes. The malfadini and the corzetti were our favorites. We also ordered the rigatoni which was decent. Great service and nice ambiance.

To say I love Italian food is an understatement so I was extremely excited to try this restaurant after reading so many rave reviews. Unfortunately, the dining experience was a bit disappointing considering the hype. We had the prosciutto (which was pretty good), the roasted garlic scape focaccia (which was amazing), and the house made mozzarella (which was okay) to start. Each of the entrees  either came out cold or cooled down extremely quickly (although that could be in part because we were seated outside for an evening reservation).  With each entree we found ourselves constantly making suggestions of what could have been done to make it slightly better. The rigatoni Diavola was my personal favorite of the dishes we tried flavor-wise but the pasta itself was a bit too al dente (you could see the uncooked pasta in certain sections of the noodle when cut). The mafaldini was the crowd favorite although this dish congealed quickly. The sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti was hit or miss because some didn't like the combination of the sweetness of the honey with the dish but the pasta itself was cooked perfectly. We also split the grilled lamb leg steak and were disappointed with the cut of meat. Overall, we would definitely try this restaurant again with reservations inside because we think the ambiance would help. Also, the drinks were good and the service was great! Our waiter switched before the end of our dining experience and both serves were fantastic and informative.

These pictures are from two separate visits, but it's easy to want to order everything on the menu! Overall, very tasty - they have a number of vegetarian pastas (yay!), the focaccia is amazing, and the cacio e pepe fritelle are unique and delicious! The wine selection is also great.

I think I set my expectations way too high for Lilia. The service and staff were amazing, so 5 stars there. However, the food was disappointing. I'm a huge pasta lover and fan, but every dish that my boyfriend and I ordered lacked something in taste or was too rich. We ordered the burrata on toast, scallops, and broccolini to start. Those were okay, but nothing to rave about. The pastas we ordered were so rich that I couldn't even finish it. Bite after bite, it just tasted worse. I can't even explain it. I just know I really enjoyed Misi more than Lilia. Maybe will try again at a later point, if I can snag a reservation again.

One of my favorite restaurants in BK and NYC for that matter. Amazing pastas. Definitely one of the best all around. Simple and delicious. Really nice indoor and outdoor set ups. Super friendly owners.

author.name: Jon S.
author.location: Huntingdon Valley, Lower Moreland Township, PA

reviews.review: Thank you for the $18 bowl of pasta with butter and cracked pepper (insert eye roll). So overhyped because it's just a shape no one sees often. Our waitress was really nice but the kitchen refused to accommodate my friend with celiac. Online they are famed for making GF options available but 2 salads grilled asparagus was not a meal. The mussels were over cooked and the kitchen just seemed too bothered to accommodate us. BIG PASS.

I've been here twice with my husband and we did not understand what the hype was all about. We had two memorable dishes: Mafaldini with pink peppercorn and the cacio e pepe fritelle. Both were the saltiest dishes we had ever had. I remember we had to ask the waiter to refill our glasses of water three times within 45 minutes. We even tried Misi with the same experience. Both scratching our heads, we figured it wasn't worth the third attempt.

Lilia is worth the hype. Came with a group of 4 people and we got 2 snacks, 2 starters, 5 pastas, and a few deserts to share. The waitress was lovely and food came out promptly.

As a snack, we got the homemade mozzarella (4/5) and Cacio e Pepe fritelle (5/5). We then moved on to our starters which were the artichoke (5/5) and Italian brocoli (5/5). We then moved onto our 5 plates of pasta, 4 of which were vegetarian (all at the same time, to share). I had the Agnolotti (5/5!!!), corzetti (5/5), gnocchi (4/5), and Mafaldini (3/5). The only thing I would not recommend was the Mafaldini, simply because it was a bit bland/basic.

We got both of the deserts on their menu and a couple of gelatos, you can't go wrong.

I've worked in the Industry for over 15 years. I completely and totally understand not wanting to change dishes in order to remain the integrity of the dish. But when someone comes in with a celiac, but is ready to order the entire menu that is gluten free, and the kitchen refuses to make any adjustments, I am baffled. We went from trying to order 12+ dishes to only 4. The chef would not even serve the house made mozzarella without the bread so I could at least enjoy that. The artichoke can not be made without topping it with breadcrumbs. None of the entrees (not even mentioning the pastas) can be made in any way to be enjoyed. None of the appetizers, Including the e mussels can be made gluten free. Literally nothing. I was only able to basically have salad and a vegetable. For a restaurant so highly rated, you'd think they would recognize a table ready to drop a lot of money to enjoy their food and support them after a rough year. It was just so completely sad. To top it off my friend who did get to try the mussels and the famed pasta, was not overly impressed. I get accommodating allergies can be difficult, but this was so poorly handled by the kitchen. The waitress really tried her best, and I felt bad to put her through the trouble. But truly heartbreaking to have experienced a restaurant I've looked forward to going to for years, the way we did. 

I felt guilty even writing this review because I know the pandemic has been rough for restaurants, but as I know the art is hospitality well... this was just so so bad. 

If you have a gluten allergy, do not waste your time. Also... If you have a shellfish allergy, I would also not waste your time. They cook every dish on the grill so your steak, appetizers, etc are all cooked where they also do the mussels. Cross contamination apparently is completely unavoidable there. They make no effort to accommodate. So so so so disappointed

Lilia is a family favorite and for good reason! The service, the ambience, the aesthetic, and most importantly the pasta and all sorts of carbs, are impeccable. Huge fan of everything Missy Robbins does lol. Make your reservation by calling at opening time exactly a month ahead of the date you want to eat here. 

This is everything we got: 
- Roasted garlic scape focaccia, green garlic butter - just so good ugh so soft and flavorful I wish we ordered like 5 lol 
- Italian broccoli, parmigiano, Calabrian chili, Sicilian olive oil 
- Sheep's milk cheese agnolotti, saffron, dried tomato, honey - arguably the best pasta I've had in my life, like little pillows of heaven. It's this good EVERY time, never disappoints 
- Mafaldini, pink peppercorn, parmigiano - I love the texture of this pasta 
- Corzetti with herb butter, pine nuts, marjoram, parmigiano reggiano - simple and light, super yummy
- Ricotta Gnocchi, broccoli pesto, pecorino, pistachios - it's just perfect 
- For dessert, the Italian job! - soft serve vanilla gelato, honey, olive oil, sea salt, fennel pollen - unique and delicious 
- I also really liked this wine lol so I'm just including this here

This eatery is the bomb. Brilliant chef. Each dish was better than the last. Attentive service. Cooking like you have never tasted. I thought I was in Italy. They use superior Monini EVOO on all dishes and you can taste the difference. I urge people to go there.

This morning Helga and I had breakfast at Lilia Caffé. We trekked to Union Avenue from the City and it was worth every step. I ordered a fritelli Sangiuseppi, a slice of olive oil cake and an iced latte. Tables were laid out with all the precautions and we had the large umbrella unfurled to ward off the hot sun bearing down. We sat there while I ate the viennoiseries with joy. Before we left I bought a strawberry crostata. Service was friendly and kind. A clean restroom is inside the main restaurant. Cash is not accepted here. We plan to return so that I can try the other tempting offerings. 

Highly recommended.
What can I say waited a long time to get a reservation. Everything was great! the food was yummy and service was friendly and attentive. Just order everything on the menu!
Please hire new baristas for your coffee shop. The service has gotten worse and worse. I've been here twice this past week and I'm tired of the rude and slow service.

Lilia is a gem. Reservations since covid have been surprisingly more achievable, so if you have the chance to go now definitely try to. The servers are all incredible and super knowledgeable and passionate about what they're serving. My favorites are the focaccia and green butter (get it don't question this pick) the shrimp, and genuinely every pasta you get will blow your mind. I didn't leave room for dessert this time but will be back for more :) 

P.s gets a little chilly if you're outside with covid restrictions and there are no heat lamps so wear a jacket. Awesome thing is they will bring you a blanket upon request

Food was okay. Appetizer the focaccia bread was way too salty. The hand made Diablo pasta was way too spicy. And the pasta with the honey was way too sugary. If you took a bite of all 3, they amounted to 1 decent tasting dish.

Review is for Yurt style dining where you pay $125 per person plus tax and tip and you'll get an assortment of prefix items to taste. 

The anti-pasta comes with 8 dishes. Sounds like a lot but it's not. It's like Korean bonchon, only it's not free. What we didn't enjoy was the fact that they essentially gave us celery, onions and fennel and considered each one a dish just because they drizzled balsamic reduction on it. First course was very disappointing. 

Next up was pasta. 3 plates of pasta prepared in different ways. They were good but nothing about each one was spectacular. 

The steak on the other hand was delicious. A 35 oz ribeye cooked and seasoned to perfection. Probably one of the best steaks I've had in a long time. This was the saving grace. 

The dessert was a large Italian Beignet eith lemon cream. It's basically a giant cream puff.

So... based on all the hype, the difficulty in finding a reservation, we expected this to be an unbelievable meal. It was anything but. It fell short in many areas. We won't have to worry and out finding reservations again. Unless the a la carte is that much better, it's not worth the hype.

After stalking Resy reservations for months, I finally snagged a Friday early evening reservation for my birthday! FYI for anyone booking - they release reservations 30 days in advance at around 10am on the Resy app. 

Looking at the menu and all the dishes going by, I wanted to try everything! Using fellow Yelp reviews, we narrowed it down to the focaccia bread, blowfish tails, the sheep's milk agnolotti, the mafaldini pasta and the Italian Job sundae. 

The focaccia bread was covered with leeks and baked to perfection! I would recommend everyone who goes to try it! I was a little nervous to try the blowfish tails but given how unique of a dish it was, I figured I had to try. I was blown away by the flavor and how well they seasoned the fish. Each tail was fairly large and perfectly cooked/tender. I would definitely recommend this dish for anyone who is a little adventurous! Of the two pasta dishes we ordered, the sheep's milk agnolotti was our favorite and the flavor was to die for. We scooped up every last bit of the sauce! The mafaldini was also good and allowed you to really taste their homemade pasta, but was not very exciting. 

For dessert we went with Lilia's famous Italian Job sundae. I would never have thought that olive oil on gelato would taste so good, but the flavors melded perfectly. The sundae was absolutely phenomenal and I would go back to Lilia just to have it again. 

The hostess and our waiter were also so accommodating. We were originally seated at a table by the door which kept opening as staff and customers went in and out. It was a pretty cold day and the hostess must have seen me shivering and offered to move our table to one away from the door. I really appreciated it! 

While I don't think Lilia's food was the most amazing food I've ever had, the atmosphere, customer service and overall quality of the food deserves 5 stars. I will definitely be back to get another Italian Job at the very least!

Today started out exciting for me. 
I headed over to Lilias cafe to try an
Espresso and pastry, As I walked in
I was mugged by a Baristas assistant 
And Bossed right out the door. I was
Told I had to order thru the window,I was actually shook up. They told me we can't come in to order. Lol, I reminded them the Ban was lifted. Especially New Yorkers who have been vaccinated. Anyway, it went from the girl unable to work the credit card machine. I offered cash  it was like they frowned upon the
offer of cash. They said we don't take cash. I guess to be in the trendy circles in NYC You can't accept cash. 
Being it's an espresso store, I was just flummoxed on their business practices and miserable staff!! Ciao

I've been dying to come to this restaurant for a long time. We were fortunate to snag reservations one Monday night for the yurt ~experience~. They have erected a number of private heated tents outside their restaurant during COVID which make for a very unique setting. The one downside of the yurts is you are required to do their pre fixe menu which is about $160 per person including gratuity/taxes (but not drinks!).
