It would have been nice if we could have ordered a la carte instead. 

That said, the experience was really special and I enjoyed the many, many dishes we tried. The beginning of the meal starts with a number of different vegetables paired with a cheesy fondue. We especially enjoyed the blanched asparagus and the onions. Next, they brought three different pastas which were all delicious. And if that wasn't enough we were then brought an entire steak which was perfectly cooked and a huge portion. We ended up bringing most of it home because we were so full! Finally they ended with a cream pastry dessert. I was very pleased with the quality and the quantity of the food. We also ordered wine to accompany our meal that was quite nice. 

The service was also excellent and they were attentive to our needs. I also appreciated that they are very careful to adhere with COVID protocols. 

Overall, this was a very special experience. I'm not sure I would do the pre fixe menu again, but I was very satisfied and would recommend for a date or a small group of friends.

Waiter was super nice but our food came out cold. Got one of the pasta dishes and the pepper was WAY overpowering, and pasta was not fully cooked. Nice atmosphere and good location but overall probably wouldn't come back
Amazing!! Couldn't have asked for a better meal from the bread to the pastas, you can't go wrong with anything on this menu. Will definitely be coming back!

My friend had been trying to get a reservation for us to try Lilia together (he had already been) and it was well worth the wait. Comfortable but hip atmosphere, soaring ceilings and an open kitchen. They take covid protection very seriously, which makes eating indoors totally comfortable. We shared two appetizers, both fantastic - grilled clams and dressed asparagus. The lamb steak with fennel and pecorino and the pink peppercorn mafaldini pasta were to die for. I will be back!

We had to make reservation for this a few weeks in advance and we were so pumped for it. And it was worth the hype! We came in on a Sunday evening and were seated immediately. They require patrons to wear masks when the waiters/waitresses come to the table. We started with the focaccia with green butter. We weren't expecting much but OH MY. You absolutely must get this bread. It is absolutely heavenly! So warm. And the green garlic butter is divine. We also both ordered the sheep's milk agnolotti. It was a melt on your mouth deliciousness that my mouth is still watering over! The sauce it comes with is divine. We had a great experience here. All the pastas looked fabulous. I don't think you can go wrong!

This place is an absolute favorite of mine. You have to usually book a month in advance but it is well worth it. We tried the ribeye special and it was so yummy paired with delicious Parmesan potatoes.

I highly recommend the homemade focaccia with the green goddess butter and the Mafaldini. Both are classics well worth getting. Always ask for the meat special as well it's always incredible!

disappointed isn't quite the word I would use but disgusted rather. I am not talking about the subpar food (4th or 5th visit so I know you can do better). What i am talking about is the service. our waiter was extremely dismissive, rude and a liar. It was a late Saturday night resy. We came to have a good time and were met with hostility and disgust. Shame on Lilia and shame on your staff for mistreating us. It was one of the most humiliating embarrassments I have experienced dining in NYC pandemic or not. If you did not want our business, you should have asked us to leave. However, what you did was provide incredibly sparse and inconsistence service. we waited 15 minutes for our table and finally after sitting down another 45 minutes for beverages only to find out our friend wasn't being served. rather than be upfront, your waiter tried to be coy and play dumb. "we dont have espresso martinis" "we don't have frangellico" YOU ARE AN ITALIAN RESY. THIS WAS BEYOND INSULTING. not only that but we could see people in plain sight drinking espresso martinis. I cannot stress enough how abhorrent our experience was.

First, the food at Lilia is great. However my friends and I were shocked how pushy they were to have us finish the food and just leave. 
When we made our reservation, the restaurant did it tell us they only expected us to be there for 2 hours. When they suggest us to order a big steak for 3 girls which needs 25-30 mins to prepare, they didn't tell us they want us to finish everything and leave within 2 hrs. Neither did the waitress say anything when we ordered a bottle of wine. 

However since the first course, the waitress started pushing like crazy saying: "Are you still working on this? I will have to get this going." "I need to get the seafood on the table." "We have our next reservation coming. "And the end our dinner, she still asked us to order dessert, but "that will have to be packed and go!"

After we complained to the manager, the manager was very kind. She apologized and took the pasta off the invoice. To be honest, we don't mind if the restaurant told us ahead, they only wanted us be there for 2 hours. At least my friend and I can change our plan ahead or just order less food/wine. 
I do think besides the good food, good service is very important for a nice restaurant. Not sure this was just an issue with our waitress or the restaurant in general.

This review is on for the pre fixe dinner at the yurt. 
We got the pre fixe at the yurt which was unsatisfying. There was no signature dishes on the pre fixe menu. Food overall too heavy and the set consisted mostly carbs and meat. One of the person didn't feel well after.  I would not recommend the pre fixe. Definitely not great food and not worth the price

It's been a a long process to get a reservation here. I almost lost hope until I randomly checked Resy one night and saw they had an opening for an early evening time on a Tuesday. For covid precautions - staff wearing masks, tables spread out, temperature checks, contact tracing form must be filled out, and masks must be worn while speaking to staff. 

I loved the ambiance of this restaurant. It was low key but trendy and minimalist. They had a great selection of wine along with cocktails. I started off with the Bianco bianco, which was a refreshing white wine combined with lemon, honey and sage. Perfect drink for a spring/summer day. 

The menu has several vegetarian options! For our appetizer we got the roasted leek focaccia. Let's just say this was the best bread I've ever eaten!!! Wow. This is a MUST!!! We were mind blown with the green garlic butter. It just melts in your mouth. The bread itself was so soft and warm. We really did question ordering another one but we wanted to save room for the rest of the meal. We also ordered the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti.  I'm not a huge fan of stuffed pasta but this may have converted me. I was worried the cheese was going to be too heavy and chunky, but it was the complete opposite. The saffron and honey paired so well together in this dish. Each bite was so smooth in flavor and texture. For my main entree of course I had to get the mafaldini. This dish reminded of a twist on the traditional cacio e pepe. The sauce was perfect and not too much in quantity in comparison to the pasta. I've never had pink peppercorn in a pasta but it had a distinct taste and a "zing" element to it. To end it all, we ordered the Italian job for our dessert. This was a gelato topped with olive oil (!!!), honey, fennel seeds and some sea salt. The concept of olive oil topped on gelato was brand new to me, and I think I will always want this combination from now on. Make sure to give this a mix so you get all of the flavors in every bite. 

Our food came out promptly, and the staff were attentive and frequently check on us. This is easily one of my favorite restaurants, and I already can't wait to go back.

The most annoying part of making this rez a month in advance was paying 644 (including taxes and tips) for 4 people upfront.  I've lived in NYC for 16 years and this is a first. 

2 weeks into the rez my friend canceled so I had requested for 3 people instead of 4. They said no problem. For 2 weeks straight and after 3 phone calls, I received the promise that I will get the refund of 162. Every time I call, the lady (Sarah I believe)  kept insisting it will take 3-5 days. It has been exactly 19 days since I've asked for the refund (3 separate times) 

When we dined a week ago, I told the host they owe us for the one person who cancelled. The host said it is in the system and the refund will be processed within 3-5 days. A week after that, still no credit. It has been almost 4 weeks of calling back and forth, leaving messages and speaking in person with empty promises. 

Today I called again and she still insists it will take 3-5 days and will speak to the manager. 

They had zero problems charging us immediately but why is this refund taking so long ? 

Was the food good? It's overhyped honestly. I live in soho and have been to every top rated Italian restaurant in the city. On top of that, you can't even pick and choose what you want on the menu. I was not in the mood for steak but that was all that was offered.  The cheese fondue was cute, other than that very basic food. If I wasn't so annoyed with the refund I would have had a nice time. It's been almost a whole month of chasing them around for the credit!!!!

Tomorrow I am going to issue a dispute with Amex and demand my refund. 

PS. If the restaurant had a problem with me changing from 4 to 3 people fine! I would have invited another friend!!! The fact that they allowed the change and still charged me for the extra person is very immoral business practice.

WOW - and this isnt a WOW it's so fun to be outdoors, "everyone gets a free pass because it's Covid WOW".  This is a genunine, eating in a "yurt" WOW.  This is in the Top10 dining experiences I have had in my life.  I wasn't expecting this to happen on a balmy Wednsday night - but it did.

Service - perfect, genuine, real.  
Food - Amazing, took shots, risks, all amazing.

I describe the "price fixe" menu this way.
First Course - am I eating with Dan Barber, give me more vegatables cooked perfectly!  YES! YES! YES!  Was this the best radiccho salad I ever had - YES.  Was it the best cippolina I ever had - YES.  Did I dip my bread into cheese - YES!  Did i dip my potato in cheese - YES!  Do they have an amzing beer collection - YES!

Pastas - here's where shit really get's thrown down.  The pasta with pink peppercorns and a PINK IPA - YES!
Beet pasta than was more like a "soupdumpling" filled with borscht - I love it!  Then sprinkle a few poppyseeds to put things over the top.
The 3rd pasta was a simple disc with a deconstructed pesto - simply amazing.  I could have stopped right now and been really happy.
Some of the best pasta I ever had in my life.

I dont eat much red meat anymore.  My GF doesnt eat it ever - until last week where she really enjoyed eating a perfectly cooked steak.  I mean perfect.
She had some sea bass as well.  But she kept going back for the steak.  So now my NYC Steakhouse portion has been covered.  btw - when i'm talking perfect I'm talking better than any steak i have had in 10 years,

Oh then please bring me a chocolate cake - a whole cake for us to devour!
And YES - I will have some of the finest Italian Mead to wash down my cake and espresso.

Like I said - I've been to some of the best.  Lillia is on the list.  And so much fun to sit alone with 4 people dining together outdoors without having to look at all of the other clowns doing the same thing.  Very Special.  Very Special.  Pat yourselves on the back - you are doing everything right!

Lilia's pastas are a trip. Please go here and have pasta!

The pasta and cocktails here are simple standouts. Try any of the antipasti. The filled pastas and seasonal antipasti are delicious.

I recently tried the four course menu in the outdoor yurts, which was a delightful experience with many antipasti dishes, 3 pastas, the ribeye with braised beans, and a chocolate torta.

Also, be sure to check out Lilia Caffé next door for a drink, coffee, sandwich, rosemary shortbread, pastry, gelato or snack.

Also check out Misi!!! Different, vegetable-forward experience with the same standard for amazing pasta.

My fiancé and I have been trying to come here for a few months but it was always impossible to get a reservation so finally for his 30th birthday I decided to really get concentrated on it. I booked a table and we ordered the foccacia, scallops, clams, two pastas, lamb and sea bass. Out of all these dishes the pastas were good and so was the foccacia and scallops. Honestly I have eaten at ammazacaffe without reservations plenty of times and the pastas were just as good. Their duck was much better than the lamb here. Also this place makes you awkwardly put on a mask every time anyone approaches the table. This was honestly the worst especially since all the waiters are vaccinated. My fiancé had to put on a mask while they were bringing out a dessert for him and I couldn't even record him. Bottom line, I'm glad I have experienced this place but I probably won't come back unless it's a no reservation type place as the interior is plain Jane and food not that spectacular.

Service amazing!
Food impeccable.
Covid stuff as good as you can get.
The first thing We had was leek focaccia and it literally made me question what I was doing with my life!

Of Chef Missy Robbins' two Brooklyn restaurants, most people seem to prefer Lilia to Misi, but for me the opposite is true. However, Lilia has two things Misi doesn't: the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti, and the Italian Job, and both are worth going back for.

The other dish I liked at Lilia was the artichoke, but otherwise I felt that all of Misi's appetizers and pastas were superior. Also, I've found Lilia much harder to get into, and despite having a reservation, we still had to wait more than 15min for our table at Lilia. Regardless, I'll be back for that gelato one day.

I'd been wanting to try Lilia for at least a year now so I had high expectations coming in but they were definitely met! The space is pretty large with a warehouse vibe and great natural lighting.. Our favorite dishes were easily the focaccia and the olive oil topped vanilla gelato. That was the best focaccia I've ever had and we even ordered a second because it was just so good! The agnolotti and olive oil cake were also amazing. I wasn't as impressed and probably wouldn't reorder the other pasta dishes or the grilled clams but they were worth trying. I don't think I'll be back next week since it's sort of a trek but I'm so happy I finally got to eat here!

The agnolotti is divine. I definitely understand why it's a must try. I love the olive oil gelato too! The olive oil cake was a little dry and a bit too dense. Overall, a great restaurant for date night.

To make it clear the food at Lilia is top tier. That being said, they SKIMP on diner experience. My Fiancé and I celebrated my 29th birthday here. We were very excited to finally be able to dine indoors. The restaurant took extra covid concerns, which I did not mind, BUT when dining indoor I expect some basic human amenities. We were beyond cold inside, honestly unbearable at times. So much so that when I voiced my concern, the waitress  handed me a blanket and hand warmers... FOR INDOOR DINING?! 
We both ate with our coats on and we we're not the only ones. This is unacceptable for the price we paid. Very disappointed with my experience here.

I was happy to try this place given the reviews and was excited for the pasta but I unfortunately was a bit disappointed. The yurt was nice despite being a bit cold.  I liked  some of the food but the portions were too small for family style and we didn't get to try most of the food I wanted to order due to the preset menu. 

We mentioned one party member was mostly vegetarian and another didn't eat pork or red meat but somehow we got a ton of pork appetizers that mostly went uneaten.  The vegetable appetizers were great but there wasn't a lot to go around. I loved the pastas but was surprised at the small portions and had to order more to satisfy us.  Two members of our party got the fish which they liked and the rest of us shared a massive steak which was ok but not what I would order.  The dessert wasn't special- chocolate cake with powdered sugar.  

It was nice to eat out and I understand Covid makes it challenging for restaurants but it was pretty pricey for a meal I didn't particularly enjoy.  I hope to return when I can order what I prefer to eat one day.

Do not go here. I wish I would've made my Valentine's reservation at literally ANY OTHER place. They are not prepared for indoor dining. Saturday the 13th was a particularly cold night outside. However, there is absolutely no heat inside, so people dining were forced to endure the brutal cold. We were sat there FREEZING the entire time while staff walked around in winter coats, hats, gloves. They were unapologetic for this. Sure, they provided blankets... Keep in mind, we are dressed for a romantic evening - these blankets did little to combat the temperatures.

They have this rule that you need to put your mask on whenever a staffer approaches.... so constantly you are forced to stop what you are doing and put that back on. They will not come up to you until you have it on. We were unable to enjoy our *average at best* dinner because of the cold and the constant back and forth with masks. In hindsight, we should've left immediately as dinner was rushed in an attempt to get back home and warm up.

This place is NOT ready to serve people. Avoid at all costs. Even when they figure it out, I will never be returning and will never recommend this place.

I was so impressed at Lilia. The value was incredible firstly. Our bill was under $200 getting four drinks, two apps, and three entrees. This is next to the second beauty--the food. Everything was fantastic. Hand crafted pasta with beautifully vibrant sauces, fine plating , and scrumptious flavor. It was hard to get a reservation and not without reason. It lives up to the hype. I have no reason not to go there (except that it's hard to get in!). Good wine selection. Great apps. Cool rustic interior. Love it!!

After feeling fortunate to secure a reservation on at Lilia on the first day of reopened indoor dining, we were sorely disappointed. When the restaurant called to confirm our reservation, they told us to wear warm clothes. They didn't tell us that there would be no heat in the restaurant. Really? Why no heat when its 22 degrees outside.  The entire staff were dressed for the tundra. Although current Covid regulation require mask coverage at all times other than when seated at your table, Lilia's rules require patrons to mask up everytime  a wait staff approaches the table. They do not coordinate service in order to minimize interruption, clearing plates and wiping the table incessantly. Every time in the middle of your meal, conversation and experience, patrons are required to stop talking, eating and enjoying themselves and put their mask on. Given the frigid temp inside the restaurant, the heat of the meal diminishes rapidly. The wait staff are not apologetic about the above and beyond mask policy and are actually very aggressively rude about it.  The food is average ... nothing appealing about cold, greasy al dente pasta and heaps of over-oiled roasted garlic consuming most dishes.Newsflash: Lilia is not doing anyone a favor by opening indoor dining. Your money is better spent at your local pasta join

Wow. I've been waiting to come to this restaurant since I moved to NYC 2.5 years ago and boy it did not disappoint. We did the Amex/Resy yurt dining experience and it was pricey but it was worth every penny. Everything felt very covid safe. We were wearing masks any time the staff was around and the staff was wearing masks the entire time. We were in a private yurt with a heater, blankets, and they even gave us hand warmers. 

The meal started off with some amazing appetizers. The cacio e pepe fritelle was obviously amazing (how can you go wrong?), but the roasted cippolini onions were a sleeper hit. I was not expecting them to be as incredible as they were. The prosciutto and Parmesan butter was also amazing as was the speck. Really loved it all. 

The pastas were incredible. I loved the malfadini with parm and pink peppercorn. It was kind of like classic cacio e pepe but different. I loved it. The beet filled pasta was so unique! It was borderline sweet and topped with butter, poppy seeds, and smoked ricotta. It was great. The corzetti was the sleeper hit from the pasta round. It was a super simple pasta topped with pine nuts, marjoram, and Parmesan. 

Then we had the mind blowing steak. Honestly I think it's the best steak I've ever eaten. It melted in your mounts but had a nice crust and was perfectly salty. The sides were great as well but the steak was the big hit here. 

Lastly, we finished with a chocolate torta with fresh whipped cream. Loved how simple the dessert was! And it wasn't overly sweet, which I also appreciated. They also had roasted chestnuts which were good but the tort and cream were my fave. 

I cannot wait to come back here, even without a preset menu. This was truly an incredible dining experience.

Lilia was hands down one of the best restaurants I've ever eaten at. Definitely #1 when it comes to Italian and maybe even my favorite in NYC among all cuisines. Each dish was better then the next. I arrived thinking it would probably be overrated but I couldn't have been more wrong! We got the fresh house made mozzarella, the broccoli side, two of their classic pasta dishes, and then the lamb. The lamb was my favorite but honestly all were incredible. We finished off with their olive oil cake. It was 34 degrees and there were no heating lamps in the area without the huts, but despite the cold it was one of the best restaurant experiences I've had. The wait staff was friendly, patient, knowledgeable and professional, they helped to made my birthday memorable and special. It was a lot of fun and definitely a meal to remember!!

One of the best meals I've had in New York. Everything from the service to the food was exceptional. Reservations are very tough to come by but if you live in the area, it's worth dropping by to see if they have any cancellations. We ordered a ton of things on the menu, and the saffron pasta and focaccia were clear winners. The italian surprise dessert was one of the best I've had in awhile, and extremely creative.

One of the best Italian meals of my life. We braved a 30 degree night and sat outside in order to eat here..and it was beyond worth it. The quality, freshness, and unique flavor combos makes this unlike any Italian food I've had. I will find a way to come back and do it all over again!

Lived up the hype! Reservations can be tough to come by but it's so worth the struggle. We had a 9:45 seating on a Monday night in November that we booked about a month in advance. We tried a little bit of everything and did it family style. The gnocchi and agnolotti are out of this world. In addition to excellent food, atmosphere and service, they nailed the COVID safety and cleaning protocols. This was an indoor experience during COVID times.
Delicious pastas, clams, and olive oil cake. One of my favorite restaurants in NYC

This place is solid. Their sheep milk cheese filled pasta was amazing but malfandi was okay... texture of these noodles  was amazing but it was not mind blowing. Their service is great and they seem to take covid-19 safety measures very seriously
Great Williamsburg Italian spot. Feels trendy but cozy at the same time. Came here for a birthday with a group of 5. We had a wonderful time sharing a bunch of pastas.

This place was ok. I hoped to like it more than Misi however it was much worse. Still a 7/10 not bad but not great. Would go again but to Misi not here. The pasta was dry and not as good as the sister restaurant.

Make a reservation early! Been on my NY bucket list for a while and I'm so glad I finally got to check it out. Had to make a res 5 weeks prior to actual date but well worth the wait. You can't go wrong with any of the food options and we actually saw Kevin Love & Kate Bock seated a couple tables from us as this is one of their favorite spots in the city as well.

All in all I thought the food was good. I was anticipating greatness, but was underwhelmed. The mozzarella antipasti was delish and I enjoy the Italian job gelato. The pasta dishes were just OK. I thought the pasta dishes needed more pop of flavor. They were very bland.

eating in the street is an experience by itself, but pair that with good food and great company definitely takes everything up a notch. Getting a reservation was just the first obstacle you would encounter... the next one would be which dish to NOT order... they were all sounding great. We went through the yelp reviews and ordered everything everyone highly recommended (a lottt of recommendations).
My biggest take away for the night was definitively the grilled Blower Fish dish. I would have never thought this tiny, cute looking fish (in my head), would taste so freaking juicy and amazing. The meat had a soft, fall off the bone; crisp, texture. I am not a big fish eater since i dont like to deal with bones and such, you will NOT have a problem with this dish. I would recommend it to everyone and anyone. Get it.

I've been waiting for months to get a res here and finally did tonight (my friend knew the general manager). All I really have to say is WOW. Every single thing we got was DIVINE. We ordered foccacia with heaven butter, clams, broccoli, sheep cheese pasta and rigatoni and the olive oil cake! My god everything is good.

While it may have been an off night, I had a very underwhelming and at times unpleasant experience. Probably the worst outdoor seating available which is surprising given the sidewalk transformations many restaurants in the area have bene able to achieve. On to the food:

Cacio e Pepe Frittelle:

8/10--the pasta in the fritelle was perfect and the exterior coating the same. Fritelle itself a bit dry.

Red and White Radicchio, Pine Nuts, Red Onion, Balsamic:

8/10--not coming here for salad but it was solid and a good way to cut the richness of the fritelle.

Rigatoni Diavola, San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano, Pecorino:

2/10--flavor completely lacking and pasta was underdone, probably a minute or two before al dente 

Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano:

7/10--rich flavor and excellent texture, may have been better if it wasn't served to the table so cold

Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Basil, Pistachios

6/10--pesto and pistachios verdant and  tasty and redeemed an otherwise flavorless gnocchi

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey

8/10--best pasta of the night, very well balanced and unique. May have been better if was not served to the table so cold.

Black Bass, Salsa Verde, Coal Roasted Yukon Gold Potatoes

9/10--best dish of the night, fish cooked perfectly and salsa and potatoes were nice compliments

Grilled Veal Flank Steak, Hot Peppers, Basil

4/10--probably one of the oddest dishes I've had in a while. Nice cut and tender but the condiments were too sharp, almost vinegary. Could only take a few bits.

Phenomenal. I've been to Lilia a few times but due to COVID hadn't been in some time. The food is just as incredible as I remember. The focaccia, one of my favorite breads, is the best I've ever had anywhere in the world -- including Italy. We got a second order! We also enjoyed the pesto gnocchi and malfadini. The malfadini is bar none one of the best pasta dishes you'll find. We finished with the olive oil cake which was good but not a highlight. I would skip this and try the gelato next time. Our waiter was helpful and friendly. Just be prepared there are no heaters so dress warm!

This was our first time at this restaurant and excited to taste everything. Of course due to this COVID pandemic we sat outside and unfortunately with a limited menu although most of the dishes that I wanted to try out were available. 

The appetizer were yummy:
Cacio a pepe: super peppery as expected but I liked it very much. 
Mussels: very good but very small portion- I wouldn't order again.

We ordered 3 pastas for me and my husband and they were very good but some were better than others. 
Agnolotti: My favorite.  A pretty dish and savory. Worth ordering. 
Rigatoni: it was okay but it had no kick to it. However the oversized shape of the pasta was interesting and unique. After I added extra Parmesan cheese and salt, it tasted better. 
Gnocchi: tasty and worth trying but no need to order it again if I return. 

For dessert I ordered the Italian Job and the olive oil cake to go because we were so full! Unfortunately, they refused the "to go order" because of the "whipped cream" but they said that we can have the gelato to go..... wait, that doesn't make any sense right? So I asked if we can have the olive oil cake to go without the whipped cream. They REFUSED again and they sent out a different waitress to deliver the news and she was nasty about it too. Our regular waitress however was super sweet and attentive. 

So would I go again? Yes. The experience might be different I hope! But I am not sure if setting an alarm to make reservations through Resy is worth my time? I would order Agnolotti again and try something different from the menu. BUT BEWARE, do not dare order dessert to go unless it's gelato! 

This restaurant overall deserves 3.5.... not 4.

Came here for a highly anticipated dinner. I had heard a lot about this place so was quite excited when we got a reservation.
We ordered focaccia, broccoli, salad, gnocchi, and several pastas. The meal started out incredibly with the focaccia--it was truly special. The broccoli was also very special as it was mixed with a light cheese that really worked well. The pastas were very good, but I wouldn't use the word "special," a word that I always ask waiters before I order. 
For desert we ordered the olive oil cake and it was  ok..a little bit dry however.
The wine we ordered was great and the service was very professional--changed silverware after every course.
Definitely a must try!

We were able to snag a reservation 30 days in advance for a Saturday night to Lilia. It was a chilly October night, but we bundled up and wore extra layers for outdoor dining. Upon arrival the host did a temperate check and we had to sign a waiver. They require masks to be wore at the table when the servers come by. 

We ordered quite a few dishes and everything was on point. The cacio e pepe frittelle were super cheesy and not greasy even though it's fried. The grilled clams were a little spicy, but not overwhelming so. I've never seen grilled blowfish tails on a menu before so we had to try it. It was seasoned well with herbs and the fish was tender and flaky.

On to the pastas! Of course we got the signature sheep's milk cheese agnolotti and it's worth the hype. The filling is creamy and pairs perfectly with the honey and dried tomatoes. The mafaldini was coated in a luscious pink peppercorn and parmigiano sauce. The pasta had a nice bite to it, which many restaurants don't master. The ricotta gnocchi with pesto was my least favorite of the bunch. The pesto was not flavorful and felt like it was missing something.

We were pretty full at this point, but we had to get dessert and the Italian Job was a great ending to the dinner. Vanilla gelato covered in honey, olive oil, sea salt, and fennel pollen was a unique take on a sundae. It wasn't too sweet and would be good to have on a hot summer day.

I've been to Lilia now well over a dozen times including several during the pandemic. There's a reason why they're still so popular. The food is consistently good. 

And for those who are concerned about how they've handled covid, I personally think they're one of the best. No where else I've been is at good at following the rules. You're not allowed to interact with the staff unless you're wearing a mask, so when they approach to serve you, please put on that mask. The outdoor dining it's beautifully spaced out and inviting. 

I have nothing bad to say about Lilia. I was worried that with less staff, as is the case in most places, the quality would go down. But nope, not at Lilia.
Anytime we visit NYC, we can't wait to eat at Lilia. Amazing dishes! Top 5 restaurants I've experienced. And we travel the world.

This is obviously the go-to spot for a reason. 

The service was excellent - the staff was happy to chat through the menu and offer up their recommendations. 

The food was on point - they're known for the focaccia and pastas for a reason. The focaccia is a MUST. 

The pricing was....high but explainable? 

I would come back and try the steak.

This place is extremely good. I went here with my girlfriend and the appetizers alone were to die for. I got some sort of squash with different tasty ingredients sprinkled on it and she got the most delicious bread with fresh mozzarella and spices on top. For our entree we both got different pastas (rigatoni and gnocchi) with various sauces and cheeses on them. Do not miss out on this place! Oh and make sure you get the chocolate gelato, it's a giant serving but you'll eat it all trust me.

RONA REVIEW FALL 2020

Wow. Lilia continues to impress.... even in the times of the rona. Here is what you need to know:

1. Yes, you still a reservation. Yes, it's difficult.
2. Lilia offers two of my favorite bites of food in NYC: that saffron sheep's milk pasta and the Italian Job sundae. You must get these. Full stop. Do it now. I'm still dreaming about the food.
3. The rest of the food is still delicious. Lilia offers elevated dishes using the highest quality ingredients and focusing on simple concepts. It works.
4. The lamb is also a must get. But really, the saffron pasta and sundae.
5. Delicious drinks.
6. Quality service. 

Lilia delivers on its food... if you can get the reservation and handle the outdoor dining through the colder weather, it's absolutely worth it.

A really underwhelming experience, both food and service. I ordered the housemade mozzarella on toasted garlic bread, Black Bass, Rigatoni and Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti with a couple glasses of white wine. The toasted garlic bread and Agnolotti were somewhat interesting, tasty. The rest was disappointing. They're heavy on the salt but a little bland on the flavor. The indoor CoVid experience needs some improvement. The waiter started by informing us that it would be a "contactless evening," but it felt like the opposite. I'd normally appreciate attentive service, however, given their request that you put your mask on each time someone approaches the table, interacting with the staff became more of a nuisance than anything. We had about 4 different server/waiters approach us multiple times throughout the evening (to bring plates, clear plates, etc.) I had to put my mask on mid-bite more times than I can count. I can't say that I'd go back or recommend it.

It's impossible to make a reservation, the phone is never picked up, never have answered an email. I was trying to get a party (10 people) in this place but when I asked for a prefix menu nobody answered and I just asume it was to risky. Tried to reserve for 4 people and it seems is booked for the rest of the year what is weird because I can see a few spots available everyday when walking around. I've sent more than 5 emails, tried to call everyday for weeks. Once I stopped by the door and with rudeness and disinterest, a female just told me to go to resy. It's impossible. I liked Lilia, the place, the food, but the service is not good.

Life-changing pasta, in that we didn't know it could taste this good, this complex, and this nuanced. 
Cacio e pepe fritelle: this comes in a pastry. Too many carbs, but the pasta is delicious.
Mussels: very nice, though heavily featured one main flavor, garlic. 
Mafaldini with pink peppercorn: tasted like we were eating meat, maybe squid, and the peppercorns were so light, almost like rose. Amazing.
Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey: really special, as delicate as a flower you could breathe the head off, and so much going on at once as the tomato interacted with the honey and the lovely creaminess of the sheep's milk cheese.

My husband and I were so impressed with Williamsburg that we decided to return. Lilia is in the residential section of Williamsburg and offers outdoor seating. We were able to dine outdoors on a fabulous evening and watch the Hipster world in motion. The food was exceptional. Our grilled Clams were divine, and the sauteed Mussel's delicious. We  enjoyed summer squash, and  Agnolotti  that were just fabulous. We drank Vermentino with our meal, and it paired perfectly with our dinner. Lilia is a must!

Although it's really hard to score a reservation, this place is worth the trouble.  The rigatoni Diavola is to dieeeee for.  one delicious pasta just isn't enough, at least for me it isn't, order the cheese filled agnolotti too.  And a gelato to seal a perfectly delicious dinner. Service is great. I will be back

Food is phenomenal, but the service was a bit too overbearing. Every time we got food or drinks to the table we were asked to put our masks on, even though we were in the middle of eating, which isn't unreasonable considering the reality we live in at the moment. However, at the end when we asked for the check, the server insisted on clearing the table before bringing the check, which again required putting on our masks, though we politely asked not to clear the table and just bring us the check, we were told that it's not up to us and the server stood and waited for us to put our masks on. It was the last sitting for the night, there was no rush to do that. Don't think this was necessary really, especially being rude like that.
Worth the hype! Been here a couple times and eaten most of the menu.. highly recommend all of the pastas! They are all 10/10

This is a 4.5 star rating. I really loved Lilia and don't even think this review is necessary. BUT I've anticipated coming here for a long time and finally got a reservation so I feel like I am writing this to those people who've been reading the menu over. 

I think a highlight was the focaccia with green butter. It was unexpected, when I read the menu I kind of brushed over this because focaccia? But the waiter recommended it and I had to try it. It was delicious and a MUST. 

Next we had the agnolotti is also a must try and definitely worth the hype. I would order this again if I came. 

After we had the mafaldini, honestly this wasn't my favorite. I know it's the Instagram you see but I would say skip it and try something else. 

Then we had the sea bass which was good although a tiny bit salty. I might skip this next time I go. 

Lastly we had the Italian job which was amazing, it's gelato and EVOO and honey. It was something different that I would recommend trying. 

The service was amazing, new table settings after each course and wiping the table down. They are really COVID safe (honestly more than any place I've been to in nyc). 

The only thing I would say I didn't love was my dirty martini and the g&t on the cocktail menu. We did get a chilled bottle of read the made up for the cocktails.

Came in here today. 

Food was 5/5
The Sheep Cheese Agnolotti - Amazing. Hands down best pasta dish I have had in awhile. 
Linguine with tomatoes - tasty, very simple. Compared to the agnolotti didn't seem as special... 
Sea Bass - Wow. I loved this dish. It was so flavorful and cooked so wel. 

Outdoor eating decor 1/5
For the level and quality of food, was really disappointed at the thoughtlessness of the outdoor decor. To be honest, I was kind of embarrassed to have brought someone to a pricier dinner and have the ambiance feel barren. I think some nice rows of bushes to enclose the space and a single flower on the table would have brightened the experience. 

Food Service 5/5
Waiters were really great and helpful and the service all around was excellent.

Like other commenters have said, servers come by fairly often to check in and customers need to put masks back on, which does get annoying. 

The Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti is a must try!! It is delicious and the honey and lemon add such bright elements to the dish.  I was pretty blown away. 

Also, if anyone watches the TV show Billions/is generally aware of chef Missy Robbins' greatness, she made a few appearances. Needless to say, we were all starstruck.

Lilia has long been one of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn. We were able to grab a reservation a month ahead of time (they're not acception walk-ins right now) and I was looking forward to this meal for a while! The food was all as good as I remembered! Only downside was that the artichoke wasn't on the menu and that's one of my absolute favorites - I hope it makes its way back on soon.

The service was as good as it was pre-covid. Lilia definitely falls on the more cautious end of restaurants as they ask you to put your mask on anytime staff is at your table (dropping off drinks, food, exchanging plates, taking orders). That doesn't bother me at all and I'm comforted to see Lilia to take precautions to protect their staff and customers. I'm kind of shocked to see other reviews complaining about that? It's honestly not that hard or disruptive to the meal and a small thing to show respect towards the staff.

Already booked another reservation for a month out! Can't wait to keep coming here!
My second time here - both times were good experiences. Friendly staff, good service, nice ambience (pre-COVID when you could sit indoors). The agnolotti is amazing - a must order dish.

I've been here a couple of times, and I'm always impressed with the quality of the food. The most recent time I came here was on a Saturday night during COVID. They have a good amount of outdoor seating and it is all very well spaced out. They take COVID precautions very seriously and even ask diners to put their masks up when severs approach their table, which is very considerate. 

Our waiter and all of the staff was very friendly. It did take a little while for them to first come over to give us menus and take our orders, but I'm sure things are a little more difficult due to COVID.

As for the food, we started with the cacio e pepe fritelle which is my favorite dish here! It is SO good and it was served nice and hot. I way over-ordered because I wanted some of everything, and then I took a bunch home. The wood roasted summer squash was really tasty. As for the pastas, my favorite was the mafaldini - it is almost like an elevated cacio e pepe. However, it wasn't hot which definitely detracted from the flavor. I also tried the agnolotti, gnocchi (loved), and rigatoni. They were all good. The one complaint I have is that several of the dishes had fennel pollen on them, which was not listed on the menu, and I dislike that flavor so it was a little disappointing. However, I still love the food here and would highly recommend trying Lilia at least once!

Let me start with saying, this is prob one of the best restaurants I've been to in NY. Food was insanely tasteful and service was phenomenal. We tried a few appetizers, a few main dishes and couple desserts as well as their wines. I gotta say, you have to try this place!!

Exceptionally mediocre. Like most you've probably been trying to get a reservation at Lilia for months. We were thrilled a few nights ago when we were able to take a canceled reservation. 

Food: We ordered all of the pastas. The goats milk cheese pasta was incredibly delicious and flavorful. The others were edible. We also ordered a few appetizers which were all just okay. Maybe the food was better before COVID but i wouldn't eat here again. 

Atmosphere: Uncomfortable. Even though the tables are outside the servers won't approach your table unless everyone seated is covering their faces. Even when you're eating. So if dishes and drinks are coming out sporadically, which everything did,  you are literally putting your mask on and taking it off the entire meal. And if you don't have it on the server will awkwardly stand 6feet away and just stare at everyone like they're contaminated until you notice them.

Our waitress Cecelia was fabulous! She was super nice and patient with us as we tried to navigate our way through the menu. She also gave suggestions and explained some of the Italian descriptions that we didn't understand right off the bat. She definitely added to the overall experience and it really is servers like her who can make the meal that much more enjoyable. We started with the cucumbers with sheeps milk, and the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle. The cucumbers where crisp and fresh in a slightly spicy vinegarette & covered in sheeps milk cheese. Reminded me of an Asian cucumber salad but with cheese.The cheese is light and fluffy & paired nicely in contrast to the cucumbers crunch. The Fritelle was good, basically a fried cheese ball of sorts. Very light and crisp, but with a super cheesy taste and a peppery bite. Tasty but my friend referred to it as a glorified mozzarella stick and he was right. 

Next we had the lamb leg steak,  black bass, rigatoni & agnolotti. Out of all of those- skip the rigatoni. Pasta was very al dente which was appreciated but pretty bland and lacking pizazz other wise. Now the agnolotti...that was pasta! Filled with pillowy soft rich sheeps milk cheese and coated lightly with honey & oil. Really good wish we would've gotten two instead. The lamb was also tender & nicely seasoned. But between the meats the black bass really stole the show. It was cooked perfectly *chef's kiss*. Firm yet super delicate and light, with the most perfect herb sauce covering every portion of it. It sat nicely on some soft potatoes. Reminded me more of a Greek style fish. 

Lastly was the dessert- do get the olive oil cake, do get the infamous Italian job ice cream. There's just something about olive oil and dessert that is delicious! All in all our waitress & the casual Victor Cruz sighting made this posh restaurant somewhat understandable of the hype. However,  some of the dishes do fall short. Still worth checking out... if you manage to get a reservation that is.

Overall a very good meal. Came here with a few friends so we could sample a bunch of things. First up was the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle which was excellent. Such a kick in the mouth of flavors, which I personally love. Next was the Tomato Foccacia, with Green Garlic Butter. Likely my favorite item. Super fluffy bread with great flavors. After that we shared the grilled clams which overall were good, and great for sharing. The Grilled Head on Prawns were tasty for sure but definitely something to avoid if you're worried about making a mess. I ordered the Mafaldini for my main, which was decent. Great al dente pasta with enough flavor to be memorable, but my girlfriend ordered the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti which blew my pasta out of the water. Flavors were amazing and the pasta literally melted in your mouth. Tried a bite of the veal flank and was very impressed. Great kick to it and super tender.

Lilia lived up to its expectations! Have been trying to come for years and was able to finally make my way and order everything off the menu.

You must come with a reservation - they're not taking walk ins during outdoor dining (I asked) 

Everything we ate was out of this world! The cocktails were OK we stuck to wine but the food was (chefs kiss)

Nice looking place, to get a reservation is nuts! People love the hype, esp here in bk, it's almost comical! The food was good but I don't think it was worth the month long wait! Apps I got clams, mushrooms, cauliflower, slice of bread with mozzarella, scallops pretty tasty. Pastas were decent portions and had good flavors !!!

I'll start off by saying the experience is okay at best. This was my second time here. The first time was alright. 

This time friends wanted to go so I made a reservation a month in advance for a 9:30pm dinner for four. We arrive promptly for our reservation, however, this restaurant lets people linger at their tables after they have clearly finished and paid. We weren't seated until 10:10pm! We asked the hostess to please explain why is there's a delay. All we got is I'm really sorry, but the group hasn't left the table yet. We are working on getting them to leave.  I'm really sorry. I'm really sorry. 

It doesn't make sense to allow one party to linger and diminish the experience of another party.  I suggested placing a maximum amount of time on diners similar to other popular restaurants, but all we got was I'm really sorry. Honestly, the least Lilia could have done was bought a round of drinks for our wait time. 

If you make a reservation be prepared to wait regardless of your reservation. Dinner was good, but I'll pass on Lilia in the future because of the lack of customer service and the disregard for people's time.

Glad I got to try Lilia - The limited contact service was the first I've encountered in NYC since the pandemic, which meant masking up every time a masked server came to our table, which my friends and I would have been totally fine with if they didn't come by at least a dozen times. Three apps were ordered which were dropped one at a time so you couldn't enjoy anything without interruption. We were told we had to order the rigatoni diavola, which at $28 was completely skippable and had no spice.  That said the ricotta gnocchi was delicious and so was their Bianco Bianco cocktail.

Went there a few days ago with some friends. I'm not a fan of sitting outside but in the advent of  COVID-19 I guess we have no choice. My friend walks over to the hostess and tells her that we need a table for 3, she looks at him and says in sum and substance "I'm sorry but before we start, I need you to put your mask on". He complied by putting his mask on as he had it around his neck. After he put his mask on, she then told him that they were booked and that they had no space. We tried to explain to her there were empty seats and  people whom came after we were rejected were given a seat. We were Spoken to as if we were dirt , others came in and were spoken to kindly. I guess they pick and choose who they want to treat kindly .From what I have heard from other people whom have dined here is that the service you receive is dependent on your skin color. My friends and I all have professional jobs in the criminal justice field. We aren't criminal nor do we dress like thugs. I wouldn't recommend anyone whom is black going here.

Contrary to what a couple recent reviews may indicate, pandemic-era dining at Lilia is perfectly pleasant. Lilia does request that you pull your mask up when your table is approached by a staff member, as some other restaurants have been doing as well. But they minimize the length and frequency of these interactions and are courteous when doing so.

And these simple/reasonable measures come nowhere close to overshadowing the food! The pastas are as delicious as advertised (we had the rigatoni, mafaldini and agnolotti). But an unexpected star was the tomato foccacia: basically the finest rendition of "bread-and-butter" you could imagine.

After lots of diligence on social media, I landed a reservation to the "prestigious" Italian dining experience known as Lilia. I was totally excited, after being hyped by their glossy social media marketing on Instagram. Little did I anticipate that this would be met with ABSOLUTE DISAPPOINTMENT and a sprinkle of trauma.

It seemed a bit strange as we initially approached the outdoor dining area. Diners seemed afraid and tense. I saw an older child sitting with their family, mask on their face, with absolute discomfort in their eyes. I brushed it off. Typical requirements? Maybe. 

Walking up to the reception table, there were two women in masks, peering down at reservation tablets. Instead of being approached with a "hello, how are you," I was greeted with "please put on your mask." I was at a pretty good distance, but I complied out of respect. My husband stood even farther away, more than 6 feet away and he was met with glares. I gave them my information, and our table was not ready. It would ultimately not be ready until 15 minutes from the actual reservation time. 

My husband walked up to me to ask me what was going on. He was asked to put on a mask. He did, but then after speaking to me, he walked away to the far point he was before- more than 6 feet away from any human contact. He walked up to me again, this time with his mask pulled down, because he wanted to know why we weren't seated and whether or not I was ordering a drink. We were then approached by what seemed to be a manger- an Asian or Hispanic male (only using appearance as a description, not being racially charged- I am a POC as well). In a very MILITANT manner he said "Sir, put on your mask." My husband asked "why? I'm not near anyone else but my wife, and I will be distancing myself now." He replied "THIS IS THE WAY OF THE WORLD. WHERE HAVE YOU BEEN?" in an even more militant manner. We were stunned. I'm presuming this "manager" took health and hospitality courses before working here, so I was particularly stunned about his concerns, as he was wearing disposable gloves, which has been proven to cause even more detrimental cross contamination during this pandemic, if you are wearing them outside of a hospital setting. My husband walked away again.

I decided to try a little experiment. Turns out, if you order a $15 Gin and Tonic with Juniper floating in it, you can stand on the sidewalk mask free. I sipped the drink twice and stood mask free, in very close proximity to others, and was not reprimanded. SO! If you are very determined to dine here, and would like to stand mask free on the sidewalk, ORDER A DRINK AND LURK. 

As we were seated, I asked my husband if it would be a more wise idea to order to go. This entire setting was now revealing itself to be extremely creepy. Diners eating and being forced to mask themselves, even if they were chewing. Already seated, we were then advised that we must put on our masks when waiters and staff approach the table. We have dined outdoor once during this pandemic and we were not asked to ever mask ourselves while seated. We were then approached by a higher waitstaff authority that militantly said to my husband "Sir, you MUST wear your mask. We understand that all restaurants do things differently." Fair enough, all restaurants do. That's why we chose to leave. We offered to pay for the drink but that person seem terrified at the thought of touching cash. 

This place should remove "Italian dining" from its record. Italian dining would never be so militant and uncomfortable. Maybe you should post your pandemic rules on your pretty instagram account? Maybe go over these rules with diners as they approach, instead of making it a Black Mirror-eqsue encounter? Notify the public. You are a MILITANT establishment, with rude staff and improperly social distanced tables. If you care so much about the health of your staff, have less tables, distance those tables and invest in face shields. Why not even consider closing off dining and doing solely take out? Maybe you need to overstaff to overwork and pay off that PPP loan? Who knows.

Finally had the privilege to dine at Lilia and holy $@!&!!!! If I could have ordered every single item off the menu I would have, although I did come close to it. For apps we did the grilled eggplant, housemade mozzarella, and the cacio e pepe fritelle (MUST TRY). The housemade mozz is heavenly and what food dreams are made of. I snuck in an order of grilled clams as an app too, and they did not disappoint! I'm pretty sure there was some parm sprinkled on them for fun, wow. We ordered four pastas for the table, all amazing! I really can't decide if I'm more in love with the Mafaldini or Agnolotti, both are beautiful in their own way. The Mafaldini pasta itself is delicious and is cooked perfectly al dente. We ordered the veal flank steak because why not. The fresh herbs and pickled hot peppers are excellent compliments and the meat was so tender even for a flank steak! DO NOT, I repeat, DO NOT leave without trying the Italian job. You won't regret it. It's got all my friends ordering fennel pollen and I'll never eat gelato without olive oil ever again.

This is my favorite Italian restaurant in the city. It's always amazing & worth the planning you need to do to eat here! The food is phenomenal . I've been here multiple times & it's always on point. All of the pasta is homemade& simply delicious. 
Start with the Focaccia with ramp butter- mind blowing good!  Sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti- absolutely delicious -literally melts in your mouth. The Riccotta Gnocchi and Mafaldini are delicious too!

Always awesome. The menu doesn't change much, but it's still worth coming back over and over because it is consistently fantastic. Get the cacio e pepe fritelli and the mafaldini for sure but everything is awesome. During the summer months the patio is amazing and no reservations needed (come early though). In the morning their bombolini and coffee are on point too.

This place is almost impossible to get a table for. Got to call a month in advance, early in the morning, and only then you have some chance of getting a table 30 days after the day you call. Regardless of this absurd process, this place is incredible.

Came here on a Thursday night with very high expectations due to the above crazy reservation process and strong reviews. Would be very tempted to give it a bad review due to the reservation process, but I can't, it was that good. Here are some of the details:

The service - Myriam - was very attentive, helpful and friendly.

The atmosphere - very pleasant, busy but not packed, romantic but not assuming.

Food - simply delicious. From starters, the chicken liver crostini and cauliflower with sopressata, over mains (any pasta from this menu) all the way to dessert (gelato, but especially the Italian Job), everything is delicious.

All in all, certainly one of the best Italian restaurants in the city. Would certainly recommend but with the caveat that you have to live in the city for this reservation to work. In a sense it's exclusive with this type of reservations so I would strongly recommend that the management rethinks the whole process.

Thoroughly enjoyed dinner at the bar here with a good friend where we were able to walk in early Friday evening and claim a spot for much much later in the evening. If you don't mind grabbing drinks and a snack elsewhere or doing something else in the meantime, I think it really is worth it as reservations can be hard to snag. Our bartender was (very) friendly and honestly wished we went with more of his recommendations. We had the grilled clams which were pretty good but not as amazing as I thought they may be. Then we had the artichoke...omg, amazing. Finally for the pastas we had the agnolotti, which was a bit lighter and sweeter than I want in my pasta but it was beautifully crafted and so soft and pillow-like, and the mafaldini, which was like cacio e Pepe on crack...truly next level. We finished with the olive oil cake which I'm always a big fan of and we weren't let down. Ah, of course, we sipped Negronis throughout and may even venture away from those next time because the things they were making and pouring out in front of us looked incredible too. Loved the ambiance and the space was actually quite mild when it came to noise which I am so very thankful for.

Cute place but Ewww Don't believe the Hype. I have been blown away by pasta at Paola's and Marea. and those places are on repeat. With all the hype and this place booking up so quickly, you assume it's going to be exceptional but  incredibly disappointed in the food. The only dish worthwhile was the black bass with pesto . We ordered Agnolotti , Fettachini with sausage  and special chestnut pasta with pork sausage and did not enjoy . The Agnolotti was ok but borderline dessert not savory. The fettachini was hard and tasteless . The pastas are served borderline cold. The service is slow . I can't believe it's a month wait fir this place.

It was my 60th birthday on 2/28, & there were no reservations available. However, an adorable hostess with almost white blonde hair found a table for me & my BFF since 6th grade, who has lived in Williamsburg since 1984. I'm embarrassed that I'm not better with names because that hostess is a gem. She gave me a table & a truly great hug, thus making the last hours of my 6th decade on Earth very special.

The service was impeccable & the food was divine. We had broccolini, chicken liver on toast, baked clams, & the special pasta with sausage & truffles. 

Go check it out! Make that reservation early.

Sorry, pains me to do this but I was very under whelmed. I have been dying to go here and honestly, for all the hype, it was just okay. I would first start off by saying service and servers were excellent. Here is a rundown on food. Appetizers were the best part of the meal. We were a party of 5 and ordered everything to share. Appetizers: Cauliflower, Spicy Soppressata, Sicilian Pesto, Majoram, Chicken Liver Crostini, Grilled Spring Onion, Balsamic, Cacio e Pepe Fritelle, Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon and 
Radishes, Whipped Ricotta, Sicilian Olive Oil, Sea Salt. They were all VERY GOOD. We then heard that the Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs were a must have. Definitely not worth it, absolutely no flavor. Pastas: Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano
Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Basil, Pistachios
Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey and the special pasta which was Chestnut and truffles. Pastas all very tasty but they arrived at the table cold which was very disappointing. For main course we ordered the special which was a 32 oz rib eye. That was good but again arrived cold and undercooked so we sent that back. It was accompanied by potatoes, both were good, again not blown away. Also, found a lot of the dishes were very salty. Too heavy handed on the sea salt for me. Lastly, coffee (not very good and that arrived  cold as well) but the 2 desserts we ordered were excellent, Olive oil cake and the Italian Job which was soft serve ice cream with olive oil and honey. I just don't get why it is so hard to get a reservation. It is good but not great. I much prefer their sister restaurant Misi.

OH MY GOOODNESS! is all I can say. I have never been more full from a meal in my life, but have no regrets! Go in a big group & share everything is the best choice. Pretty sure the waiter requested we order everything at the beginning - the only flaw of the dinner.

On Resy, reservations for Lilia open one month in advance at 10am. I booked for a month out right when they listed, but still only managed to get a 10pm dining time for 2 people on a Friday night.

I arrived right at 10 for my reservation, but was made to wait 18 minutes until a table cleared and I was seated. The hostess and servers were apologetic, but nothing more. I didn't think the service was great. 

However, the food is very delicious. We ordered:
-grilled scallops: $18, which I feel was rather expensive and not worth, would rather have just gotten an additional pasta dish
-sheep's milk agnolotti: $25ish, highly recommend; it was creamy and cheesy but didn't feel too heavy either
-one of their specials for the night, some linguini dish with pork sausage and black truffle: $25ish, really really liked this one! The texture of the noodles was a perfect hardness, and the pork sausage complimented the noodles very nicely. It was heavier on the truffle taste, but I don't mind
-Italian Job dessert, which they said was a special but I feel like they have it pretty regularly: $10ish, super unique! It's vanilla gelato with olive oil and honey, which sounds like a weird combination but it all comes together very nicely 

So although it's rather difficult to make a reservation, you will have to make a reservation a month in advance, and you'll probably end up with a not ideal dining time, the food is great, and at a very reasonable price point as well, and worth checking out for sure!

Tried for months to get a reservations for two at a decent time and finally was able to get one. It was well worth the wait. Probably had the best single pasta dish i've ever had. 
We started off with the Focaccia Special which was served with green garlic butter and the Whole Artichoke. Anytime they have the Focaccia on the menu i recommend getting it. For our entrees we got the Mafaldini, Ricotta Gnocchi, and the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti. The Agnolotti is absolutely delicious and highly recommend going to Lilia JUST for the Agnolotti. The combination of flavors were unlike i've had before in a pasta dish. The cherry on top of the whole experience was that the service was very good and the place felt warm and welcoming.

First time at Lillia, which was highly recommended by my son (a Raging Foodie).  And once again he was spot on.  The service was very welcoming and it never stopped. There weren't the usual signs of "burn and turn" table flip protocol. It was inviting and the servers kept it that way throughout the meal.  We didn't have reservations so we gratefully sat at the bar, which put us up close and personal with the wood burning grille and chef. We started with an app of chicken liver crustini, which just had a warm and wonderful taste and textures. Followed by the Sicilian style herring and the Grilled Clams, each providing layers of flavors that kept me wanting more. However, we were armed with the knowledge of how wonderful the Pasta dishes are, so we journeyed into the Fettucini with Spice Lamb Sausage and Lemon Spaghetti with Pine nuts. Suffice it to say we were not disappointed in any way.  With the little room we had left, we thoroughly enjoyed the Sword Fish, which was cooked perfectly and was awash in a pepper sauce. I really enjoyed each aspect of the meal and the attention the team played to any food issues and/or allergies. Bravo to the entire Lillia Team.

As mentioned in other reviews, the best thing about Lilia is the service and hospitality. These days, one walks into nice restaurants afraid of stepping on the server's toes, not the other way around. Refreshingly, the staff at Lilia were impeccably warm, kind, and considerate. Our waiter, Clay, was one of the best (if not the best) waiters I've ever encountered. Ever. 

That being said, the pasta wasn't worth the hype, in my opinion. The portions were small for the price tag, and the flavors, while interesting, weren't particularly spectacular. I had the spicy rigatoni dish and the pasta was undercooked. We didn't try any non-pasta dishes, so maybe those would've been better? It was disappointing, especially after all the hype.

Atmosphere and pasta is great! We had a Friday reservation which we waited a month for. We were excited to try this restaurant after reviews from friends. The vibe overall is dimly lit, romantic, perfect for an anniversary/special occasion. Our waitress was not extremely helpful whenever we asked for recommendations etc. but she did her job otherwise. As a main - I had The fettuccine lamb ragu which was phenomenal (if you like spicy). My husband had the fish which he said was mediocre at best. Overall a good experience, but missing warmth.

I have gone all over Manhattan in search of good pasta and have gone everywhere paying anywhere from $8 to $35+ for a single plate of pasta. Lilia has been the only place where I found the pasta dishes interesting, unique, and delicious. 
The tortelli in particular was genuinely the best dish I have had in the U.S. (unfortunately seems like they don't have it currently - I went in July 2019).

We had:
 - Cured Sardines, Capers, Dill, Fettunta
 - Grilled Veal Flank Steak, Hot Peppers, Basil
 - Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey
 - Fettuccine, Spicy Lamb Sausage, Tomato Passato
 - Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano
 - Tortelli, Ramps, Prosciutto, Parmigiano, Mint

The steak you can absolutely skip.
Agnolotti and tortelli were flavours I've tasted before but never in this way. Really interesting. The latter was life changing. 

I regret not trying to match these with any wines but that's something to look forward to for next time. 

I can only really speak for the pastas but I cannot stress enough how good they were. I think the madaldini was a bit dry and could've benefited from more pasta water to emulsify with the cheese/sauce. Still really good though. 

As for the experience, I came here with my girlfriend and had an amazing time. The restaurant keeps its structure from the original building but with everything renovated - it has a very classy Brooklyn feel to it. 
We couldn't get a reservation for ages and ages so my girlfriend went at around 17:00 and secured us a table.

The experience and service was absolutely phenomenal. The food -------- unfortunately, was a little bit behind. I wanted to love the food so much at Lilia, but there were ups and downs throughout what we ordered.

If you have never been to Lilia, then you should be warned that snagging a resy at this Missy Robbin's JBF winner is as tough as it gets. Reservations open up 30 days in advance, at 10am, via phone, and calling within the first 10 minutes is really your absolute best chance of landing that golden ticket of a table. Any procrastinating beyond that and you're pretty much out of luck. 

I was lucky enough to secure a 5:45 early Saturday evening reservation for my wife's birthday dinner and, as I said, the hospitality was PHENOMENAL. We were treated like royalty by the staff from the moment we walked in. It probably had everything to do with the fact that I had mentioned that this was a very special birthday for my wife.

Since it was our very 1st time at Lilia, we held nothing back, went all out and, in the end, definitely over ordered. The menu is broken up into 6 sections - Cocktail Snacks, To Start, Little Fish, Big Fish, Pasta and Meat. Having researched the living daylights out of the menu, we were ready for the experience of a lifetime and ordered numerous dishes, including what was deemed the best of the best on the menu. Here's some quick thoughts - some positive, some not so much:

CACIO E PEPE FRITELLE - This order of fried cheese balls came in 3. They were much bigger than I anticipated and were really crispy and cheesy. Honestly, to many, this is probably going to be nothing more than a fried cheese ball, but it's a solid starter.

ROASTED TRUMPET MUSHROOMS, ARUGULA, BALSAMIC, SICILIAN ALMONDS - The mushrooms were sliced thin and spread out over a plate with arugala scattered around. It wasn't what I envisioned and it was served with a lot of balsamic drizzled on top. For some, the vinegar might be overwhelming, but for us, the more the better! The mushrooms were good and the balsamic definitely helped.

ROASTED SQUASH, THYME, BREADCRUMBS, CORIANDER VINAIGRETTE - The pieces of squash were sliced into a boomerang shape. I can't believe I'm complaining there was too much food, but there was too much squash for an appetizer. Sprinkled all over the plate were breadcrumbs. The squash's texture was different and something we had never tried before. It had a taro/potato texture to it. It was good, but it filled us up. Word of advice - they do doggy bags.

GRILLED CLAMS, CALABRIAN CHILI, BREADCRUMBS - Rather disappointing. If I can say bluntly, it literally tasted like some grilled clams with breadcrumbs and not much else. We prefer baked clams because grilled clams lack flavor and these clams did.

MAFALDINI, PINK PEPPERCORN, PARMIGIANO - The mafaldini pasta was quite unique in that the pieces were LONG. Everytime we dug into the bowl for a piece, it was neverending. The pasta's lone flavor came from the peppercorn, but it wasn't great. It just tasted salty.

RICOTTA GNOCCHI, BROCCOLI PESTO, BASIL, PISTACHIOS - Probably our favorite pasta out of the 3 we ordered. The gnocchi was a bit too al dente. The pesto and basil provided a tang flavor to the pasta and it was actually good.

SHEEPS MILK CHEESE FILLED AGNOLOTTI, SAFFRON, DRIED TOMATO, HONEY - If you're into soft cheeses, this is going to be your favorite. For me, the milk cheese was too soft, to the point it was liquidity. I kind of knew what I was getting into when we ordered it, so it was bound to not be on my favorites' list. 

BLACK BASS, SALSA VERDE, COAL ROASTED YUKON GOLD POTATOES - The BEST dish of the evening - by far. The bass was so flavorful and tender. It was perfect. It sat on top of a lump of potatoes, which looked like a giant rock in the dark, but it was delicious. Unfortunately, by the time we reached this dish, we were beyond full.

OLIVE OIL CAKE - One of the must order desserts, according to many, but it was ok. The cake was dense and on the dry side. It was served with a mountain of thick whipped cream.

VANILLA SOFT SERVE - So here is the biggest mistake of the evening for us. Instead of ordering the famed Italian Job, we ordered plain ol' vanilla soft serve with a few toppings. Unfortunately, the toppings overwhelmed the soft serve ice cream. If we stuck to the Italian Job, which was simply vanilla soft serve with olive oil, we probably would have loved it.

As I said, the staff was amazing. The waiters, waitresses and, a gentleman we presumed to be possibly someone in charge, were so informative of the menu and accommodating. They were friendly x 100. In fact, they were kind enough to get the executive chef to sign our menu and the ENTIRE cooking staff to stop what they were doing and take a photo with us before we left. Even though we were disappointed with some of the dishes, we felt so welcome. 5 stars (6 if I could) for the hospitality, but 3 for the food, so an even 4 to balance it out.

Lilia is one of those restaurants that make you feel privileged to live in NYC.
This is my Favorite Italian restaurant in the city, the food is always spectacular AND this place introduced me to one of my favorite dessert combinations maybe ever. Vanilla ice cream and Olive Oil. OMG just so good.

Ice cream and Olive oil is a bit controversial but I promise you, If you're lucky enough to snag a table at Lilia just order "The Italian job" for dessert!! I just cannot see anyone not enjoying this creation, its sweet and a little savory. Really perfect and memorable.

As for the food i wont repeat what everyone else has been saying but please go for the Mafaldini with pink peppercorn, its just unique and delicious.
I also really enjoy that the service here isn't snobby at all. Lilia is a beautiful restaurant and is listed on so many "spurge worthy" lists of places to eat in the city. Given this, you do not have to spend a ton of money here to enjoy the experience. They make you feel welcome no matter what. You could be spending $1000 on dinner for a group or you're just a couple splitting some pasta and drinks- same great service.

Lilia, i cant wait to see you again soon and ill be ordering dessert first.
The agnolotti alone is worth the trip ...truly a culinary experience ...

Everything at Lilia was AMAZING - absolutely worth the hype and the hike to get there from Manhattan. You can't go wrong with any dish, the vegetables are just as delicious as the pastas. Our waiter also told us to try calling for reservations as they occasionally can find something that isn't on Resy if you make the effort!

I live in the neighborhood and been waiting for a year to get in.From the moment we walked in, every single staff was superb. Food was delicious, ambiance was simple but chic. I would 1000% go here again.

Food is about as good as it gets, prices are very reasonable for the quality.  Portions aren't huge, but are fair for what you pay.  I went for my birthday this past weekend and had to wait a bit for the table we reserved. We got a bottle of wine in the waiting area and they covered the bottle of wine due to our wait which was very nice.

Servers are all top notch, staff is excellent.

Easily my favorite restaurant in all of New York.  From the service to the food, it's all just amazing. I've probably been here a dozen times, and the food is always on point. It's my favorite place to bring people because you know they will always be "wowed" by the food. You won't find better homemade pasta, I promise. 

Don't be silly - always get the focaccia special. The green butter it comes with is so so so good. 

My 87 year old foodie grandma has deemed their housemade mozzarella the best she has ever had. 

Trumpet mushrooms - small but great dish.  I've had the cauliflower as well which is also delicious. 

Their mussels are also amazing, I prefer them over the clams. The sauce they come in is super unique, you'll want to drink it.

My friend and I both ordered the linguini special with truffle oil and lamb ragu (I think). There was not a single piece leftover it was incredible. 

My husband had the mafaldini - which is always just out of this world good even though it is so simple. If it's your first time here I would definitely recommend this dish. It's a classic. 

Save room and get the gelato, it's spectacular. Add the chocolate and cookies, you won't be disappointed.

I must say that I liked lilia but after going to Misi a few weeks ago, and waiting months to get a reservation at a normal hour, it wasn't as great as I thought it'd be. The sheep's milk agnolotti was incredible, but the rest of the pastas were just okay. I would not suggest the rigatoni. If you're between here and Misi, I believe Misi's pasta is much fresher and better. The vibe in lilia is nice though and the prices are fair.

Maybe it's just me, I was not thrilled with this place. I felt the dishes were plain and lacked flavor. We had the clams, I found them small and under seasoned. Mushroom salad was okay, beet pasta was interesting and so was the saffron pasta (sorry, don't remember the names) but again, not worth the price or effort to make a reservation. The focaccia bread was the star as was the Italian job. I visited the cafe and purchased the gelato again. I wouldn't come back to the restaurant side. I feel there are better options in the area.

Wow, what a great experience! Everything at this restaurant felt very well thought out. The menu was diverse beyond pasta, but that's basically all we had because that's what the chef is famous for. The pasta dishes ranged from pretty bad to exceptional. Details below -

We started with the focaccia bread, which was delicious. It came with a huge scoop of garlic butter, which felt like more of a spread than butter. Unfortunately, when we tried to order another one, we were told it was sold out (booooo!)

We also got the blowfish tails, which was seasoned perfectly, and we got five of the pastas.  Well, to be perfectly honest, we got five of the pastas, but one of them we ordered three of because it was just so good. Clams were also pretty good.

I'll start from the least impressive to the most impressive.
