Rigatoni diavola - this was hands-down, really, really bad and not tasty at all. There is al dente, and there's undercooked. I thought that this was definitely undercooked. Our group had to dip the remaining pieces into the lamb sausage sauce to finish it. That's how tasteless it was.

Ricotta gnocchi - this was nothing to write home about. Not only was the pesto bland, the gnocchi wasn't all the same size. I don't know why I even bother getting pesto anywhere other than at Costco. I can eat that pesto straight out of the jar. Shoulda brought the jar

Mafaldini - this had pink peppercorn on it, sprinkled everywhere. It was quite the beautiful dish, and pretty good. Small complaint that each noodle was so long that it was hard to share. But it was very good!

Fettuccini - this was the dish with the lamb sausage. Very good, and we all enjoyed it. It's a little bit on the spicy end, but the sauce is so good that it pairs well with the focaccia or, if you insist on ordering it, the rigatoni.

Sheep's milk cheese agnolotti - this dish was absolutely, 100%, knock your socks off amazing. It was so good that we ordered two more, and they all went very quickly. It's basically a little pillow of awesome that explodes in your mouth with the creamiest, tastiest, sheep's milk cheese.

The service was also great. Lauren was attentive, funny, and a great server all around. We had a great time.

Lilia lived up to the hype. From the staff, who were incredibly knowledgeable and helpful to the actual dishes themselves, it was all superb. I'm not typically a pasta lover, and the sheep's milk agnolotti was unbelievable. Other must have is the artichokes. Honestly For pasta we also had their lamb bolognese with fettucine and Cacio e Pepe... both of which were well done, but certainly not the stand outs on this menu

worth the hype. the angolotti was the best thing ive ever eaten in my life. its insane to get a reservation but if you can get one its worth it. we (2 of us) came hungry and got the foccocia (amazing) and 4 pastas. all were great.

I'm going to buck the trend here and say that Lilia is good but not great. While it's definitely worth a try, the meal didn't justify the efforts of getting a reservation.

I came this summer for the first time. For our group of 4, we had three starters, three pastas, and one fish dish, which was perfect portion-wise. We ended up getting three bread-based appetizers (mozzarella, chicken liver, and sardines), and they were all solid.

All of the pastas were well-executed and clearly homemade. I expected a lot out of two of the signature dishes we ordered, the mafaldini with pink peppercorn and the sheep's milk agnolotti, which they didn't deliver. The mafaldini was just too subtle, and I didn't find the interior of the agnolotti to be particularly interesting. My favorite pasta ended up being the spicy lamb sausage one. The fish (possibly swordfish?) was shockingly good.

Ambiance is nice; lighting is low. Service is good and in line for this caliber of restaurant. We arrived at our reservation time and had to wait in the side bar for maybe 5 minutes. No thoughts on the wine list-- we brought some special bottles (corkage must have been $30-40 each). Strong coffee service.

It wasn't an overly disappointing meal, but a few months out it failed to be particularly memorable. It's so well established that I still feel like there's something I'm missing here, but I'm short on energy for the mega-wait or trying to snag a reservation.

Second time coming here! Reservations are insane still for this place, so when my friend said he couldn't go, I snapped it up quickly. 

We got 6 dishes to share between the two of us and it was a LOT. We liked the Blowfish tails, the lemon spaghetti and the Malfadini. The blowfish tails were my absolute favorite of the night!

I didn't love the Bagna Cauda or Veal steak. The Italian Job - an off-menu dessert with vanilla gelato, fennel pollen, honey, olive oil, sea salt - was good. Definitely get the focaccia if they have it! It's so. Darned. Fluffy.

I was lucky enough to have tried both Misi and Lilia. While I loved both places, my new favorite pasta dish is found here! We didn't get a reservation on Resy, but the bf was able to score a reservation by calling!

We started off with one of the most delicious focaccia that I couldn't help but slather on their green garlic butter. The bread was so fluffy with a crispy crust. The Mafaldini, the texture and shape of this noodle was delicious, but slightly too much pink peppercorn for my taste. The sheep's milk filled agnolotti with honey and saffron is simply the BEST!!! Omg. Fluffy creamy pockets full of yummm that's topped with this incredible sauce! You must order this! Finally the dessert, we ordered the off the menu Italian Job, vanilla gelato topped with honey, olive oil and salt. Sounds weird? But somehow it just works. 

If you're ever in town, try and get a reservation here! I think you really must try the agnolotti here!

Super disappointed. After waiting for months we finally got a reservation and it's not worth the wait. The pasta was way too al dente! It was like rock hard. The server seemed annoyed with us after we ordered and he suggested we get more. We had questions since we needed to decide on something else and it seemed to pain him. The agnolotti that i had been dying to try was sub par. Wasn't impressed by anything else we got either. We are a huge fan of Misi but Lilia is not great at all. Won't be returning or recommending. The only reason i gave 3 stars and not less is bcuz I actually messed up the date. Our reservation was really for next week but the hostess was awesome and accommodated us at the bar. She was their saving grace.

COFFEE SHOP REVIEW
in the mornings and afternoons their cafe is open. The decaf americano with almond milk was better than Variety, Lella, Tarpit, Fortunato and other local cafes. The party is next level, real and beautiful northern Italian stuff. I enjoyed the cheese focaccia with my coffee. The music is hip but relaxing (Tribe Called Quest/Dis Generation). The young ladies behind the counter are very personable and professional, very nice. Stars very much earned. Drop a dollar in that tip jar, they have earned it.

RESTAURANT REVIEW Food here incredibly tasty. Service is warm and personal. Rock n Roll atmosphere (Bowie soundtrack). Old industrial garage decor. Cool. Great date place. The mafaldini pasta is the best dish. Blowfish tails quite good. Avoid liver--too salty. Usually it's perfect but last time we went the pasta came out slightly cold and what happened? --manager comped it. They are going out of their way to make sure you have a great time, and they succeed. Try the grilled things which amazing & famous **female** head chef is famous for.  (Support female chefs in this very male-dominated industry!!!!) Especially the bass, or lamb. If you don't eat meat, the artichoke is amazing. Book ahead like a month in advance or you won't get a table. Better yet, come in and book in person. The reservationists are very nice and friendly and want to help you!

4.5 stars for this delicious splurge meal.

The key to making a reservation at Lilia is to be on Resy and prepared right at midnight. Not 12:01, not even ten seconds after 12, but 12 a.m. SHARP. Those spots go fast. I was able to snag a reservation for 6:30, and my friend and I thoroughly enjoyed the majority of our dishes.

Seasonal focaccia bread with green garlic butter - The bread, sprinkled with parmesan, was absolutely delicious; really fluffy and fresh with a great crispy crust. That green garlic butter was creamy and garlicky and everything I could've hoped for. Honestly, this was my favorite bite of the night.

Radishes with whipped ricotta, Sicilian olive oil, and sea salt - I expected thin, cooked down radish slices, so I didn't really enjoy these big, chunky, raw bites. The bitter aftertaste was a little strong. I loved the whipped ricotta, though, and made sure to scoop up every bit.

Grilled scallops with walnuts, yogurt, marjoram, and anchovy - Delicious, perfectly cooked scallops. Great char and seasoning on these. I think the sauce was pretty good too, but not that memorable. You get two scallops for $18.

Mafaldini with pink peppercorn and parmigiano - I was most excited about the pastas since I'd heard that Misi ensures that her pastas are the definition of al dente, which is my personal purview. Al dente pasta is the one true method of cooking pasta. This didn't disappoint. I loved the shape and chew of these noodles, and the parmigiano and pink peppercorn really shined through without being overpowering. This was a simple yet elegant dish with a wonderful balance of flavors.

Sheep's milk cheese-filled agnolotti with saffron, dried tomato, and honey - I was ridiculously hyped for this dish, so there was no way it could live up to my expectations, but it came damn close. The pasta was so light and delicate, and the sheep's milk cheese was a fluffy cloudlike dream. Add on those subtle touches of honey, butter, and the tanginess of dried tomatoes, and this was a total winner.

Italian Job - This off-menu item sounds like it's actually a constant dessert option. They top their housemade vanilla gelato with honey, olive oil, sea salt, and shaved white truffles. It was $25, which is ridiculous for dessert (I would've preferred to remove the truffle shavings and pay less) but I was filled with an overwhelming sense of FOMO, so I had to try it. Welp, I'm glad I did, but I wouldn't get it again. As I suspected, the truffle shavings didn't really add anything to the gelato. They just felt like a fancy way to bump up the price. The olive oil was nice and nutty but became overwhelming after a while. Great gelato though, it was really smooth but not overwhelmingly creamy. My friend got the regular sweet vanilla gelato with all the available toppings (sprinkles, chocolate straci, and almond biscotti) minus the lemon walnuts.

The bill came to $135 before tax and tip. Do I think my meal was worth almost $90 after tax and tip? Definitely not. I'm hard-pressed to find any meal that is. Was it an indulgent and delicious meal? Yes, absolutely.

Came here for my friends birthday with a party of 6. We all had high expectations as we had heard great things and as everyone knows it's very hard to get a reservation. 

We arrived right at our reservation time and were told the table would just be a few more minutes. Went to the bar/coffee area and had a drink. The decoration and ambience is very trendy. Overall really cool atmosphere. 

For food we started of with a variety of appetizers. My favorite was the Blowfish, which was super yummy. We asked for the Focaccia bread which they were all sold out of. I was a little surprised that they would sell out of the bread and then when we asked for more bread they brought us just plain untoasted bread. We also had the artichoke which was very delicious as well. 

For the main course I had the Pesto Gnocchi which was okay but not anything amazing. My friends also ordered the Rigatoni, Spicy Lamb pasta, and the ravioli, which all were okay but nothing super special. 

The service was really great but overall was pretty disappointed with the food. I think we all had such high expectations and were sort of disappointed.  Not sure if I would come back for how expensive it was.

So anyone else get food poisoning here Saturday night 12/28?

Food was great otherwise, but man oh man the post-dinner experience not so much.

Always always always get the focaccia. Always save room for the Italian job dessert. Always. Always have get the chili basil veal. 

Every pasta is a winner but the mafaldini and lemon spaghetti are the stunners. Rigatoni is the only one that's not a 10. 

Did I mention to save room for dessert?

Really disappointed with this place. We were super excited to eat at this place, but the night ended poorly. 

We arrived at 7:15pm for our reservation and got seated immediately. Good vibes and décor at this spot. I will say the service here was also great. Drinks were good. Then things turned negative with the food. The food was 80% super salty and the 6 of our dishes came out room temperature. Who wants to eat room temperature pasta? That was really disappointing for me. 

We asked for one of our pastas to go and they said certainly. No one ever came back with anything (bag or tag) and we forgot about the to-go and never received it. Paid $20+ for a dish we barely ate and expected to take home. This was bad service and honestly shocked that this happened. This has never happened to me in my life where a restaurant did not give me my food.

AMAZING, and i mean AMAZING, authentic, Italian cuisine! Everything was PERFECT! 

Only down side is you need to put your ENTIRE order in when you first sit down. I don't like this concept because i was so famished that i ordered with my eyes and of course i ordered too much.  I would of liked to at least sent in some appetizers before my initial order but they simply "don't do it " and considering i've been in hospitality for over 10 years.. i find that odd. I guess its THEIR concept.

Sorry to say, but...overhyped. We came in for a 9:30pm reservation on a Wednesday. I was completely blown away by the rustic beauty of the place. My first impression was strong.

We were seated at 10pm, 30 minutes after our reservation time (no biggie.) Started with some wine. Have to say that the service is really good, we had a really attentive and nice waiter.

Started with a few apps - favorites included the baked clams, focaccia bread & fried fish. On to what matters most, the pasta.

This is unfortunately where my disappointment started. The "spicy" rigatoni was not spicy at all, and the pasta was so al-dente you couldn't even chew it. It was hard as a rock. Additionally, the pasta sauce was so bland & there was not nearly enough. Very disappointing.

3 stars for good apps and vibes, but the main meal was not up to par. Probably wouldn't return & not worth the hype whatsoever. Don't wait months for a res.

I'll just start by saying that this restaurant is NOT WORTH calling on the phone a month in advance to get a reservation. It's really good, I enjoyed my meal, but it wasn't so mind-blowing that I think makes it worth the hype. 

We had a lovely meal, good service and the price wasn't unreasonable. The food is fresh and tasty but I feel like restaurants with similar quality exist in a lot of places.

Incredibly bland food, terrible service, and long waits. Avoid this hipster trap.

  

.

This was my second time at Lilia. The service was 100% better than it was during my first visit and they really did everything in their power to accommodate my special notes and requests for an occasion, which I did appreciate. 

This time my guest and I found the food to be less than stellar, particularly because a couple of dishes arrived cold. 

What we ordered:
- Cacio e pepe fritelle -- amazing and piping hot
- Squash with breadcrumbs -- good flavor but arrived lukewarm and turned cold
- Malfaldini -- my favorite dish was perfectly chewy this time but felt undersauced and also arrived lukewarm/cold
- Spicy rigatoni -- delicious and hot, just like the first time
- Olive Oil Cake -- good flavor, but enjoyed the soft serve from last time better.

-- we also tried to order the special focaccia, but they were sold out

Nothing was egregious, but for the reputation this place has and the price, I expected a more consistent and stellar dining experience.

We came here on a sunday night with reservations. Make sure you get reservations when you come here because the wait is normally very very long. Everything we ordered was delicious and out of this world. We started with the foccacia bread that was a special that day. The green garlic butter that it comes with was unreal and the bread was so soft and delicious. Then we got the whole artichoke which was delicious and very different from anything we have ever had before. For the main course we got the angnelotti and the ricotta gnocchi. Both were extremely delicious, however the angnelotti was amazing. The flavors in that pasta are like any I have ever had in my life. I would highly suggest my friends and family to come here atleast once in their life to experience it for themselves!
Soo good the fresh pasta with homemade cheese is to die for -- and that wood burning oven/grill makes you think of cozy campfires. I highly recommend it.

Been here twice and will never go back. I have nothing against them. I want this place to be good because I live close by but it is so mediocre. I am happy to spend $$ for good food but this is bunch of BS.

All the good reviews are from tourists or people who believe the hype for no reason or never tasted good Italian food.

The space is beautiful but the food is just mediocre and not worth it.

Spaghetti with Lemon and Pine Nuts - didn't taste any of the pinenuts, just a creamy lemon sauce. bland.

Rigatoni with tomato sauce - boring. if you gave me the same pasta with canned tomato sauce, I would not notice the difference

the cauliflower appetizer was not edible.

Mafaldini with pink peppercorn - this is supposed to be their take on Caccio e Peppe. The pasta itself is nice but again no flavor. Who makes Caccio with pink peppercorn which has a lot less flavor than black peppercorn. the idea behind caccio is the flavor of the pepper, not the lack thereof.

There is much better Italian restaurants throughout the city (I Sodi, carbone etc) or you can go to a cheap Italian place in Greenpoint for 1/3 of the price (Scalino) and get better food without the attitude.
Excellent restaurant! The mafaldini is superb. Can be difficult to get a table but definitely worth the wait!

I had tried getting a reservation at lilia for so long and finally lucked out and snagged a saturday night table. What a treat this place is, from the food to the service everything is top notch.  Had the spaghetti, mafaldini, and agnolotti as entress and everything was delicous. Had the italian job dessert with shaved white truffle mushrooms and it was unbelivable. The housemade mozzarela on garlic toast was superb as well, hopefully have the chance to revisit

This was my first visit and I was excited and anticipating something special. I had read the reviews and drooled over the pictures. It certainly started well. We were greeted pleasantly and seated quickly. 

The staff was the best part of the evening. They are friendly and helpful with a thorough knowledge of the menu and wine list. The cocktails were delicious as were the Cacio e Pepe Frizzelle. Then it took a turn. 

We ordered a salad and two different pastas. The pasta was homemade and had a wonderful chew. Unfortunately they were all salty. Surprisingly salty. The "did I order the correct thing" salty. The "please bring more water" salty. 

The cake with fresh whip cream was not salty and I finished every bite.

Very tough to get a reservation, but once you do you understand why! The cocktails, pastas, and desserts were all amazing.  This is a great place for special occasions.

Call ahead to book reservations if you can't find one online!

To my great surprise, I liked Misi more overall than Lilia. Largely because I enjoyed the antipasti more at Misi - the pasta is definitely better at Lilia, but I'll almost always prefer interesting vegetable dishes to pasta dishes.

With Lilia, there's a much more expansive menu, but unfortunately didn't get the chance to try any fish or meat mains as we focused on the pastas. We got:

Leek focaccia - It's an off-menu item that was quite good, especially with the green butter. Personally not a cheese fan so found the cheese on the top a bit too overwhelming in flavor, but can imagine this being a crowd pleaser.

Blowfish tails - Interesting for the novelty but as it turns out, it tastes like any other firm white fish. Not bad, not that interesting either.

Mafaldini - My least favorite of the pastas. Nice chewy al dente texture but nothing special with the flavors - sure there's a tiny extra kick from the pink peppercorn, but it really just tasted like a simple pasta with cheese.

Agnolotti - The sheep's milk filling is rich and delicious. But for me, a bit heavy to eat more than a few bites of (I'm sure the rest of the world disagrees with me).

Beet filled casunziei - This was probably my favorite of the pastas because it was so interesting - super unique flavor of beet to cut through the richness of the pasta / cheese. 

Kind of wanted to try the Italian Job but it was shockingly pricy at $29 or something in that ball park, thanks to the truffles on top. I imagine there's a no truffle option but wasn't told about it. 

Everything adds up quickly here, so be prepared for a pricy meal. One that for me didn't really wow. Given the huge hassle of landing a reservation here not sure I'd come back.

Good food, okay service, unreasonable prices. Out of five dishes ordered we enjoyed one - Cauliflower. It was a great combination of spices and sweetness, crunchy and chewy. As for the rest (clams, artichoke, rigatoni, sea bass), it didn't strike as special. Textures were confusing, clams were undercooked, pasta was from yesterday, and sea bass was plain boring (served with potatoes - who does that??).

Best best best - and don't forget about misi another must try 
Clams Mussels and two pastas - everything was perfection

it was ok. we live equidistant from misi and lilia. the food is better at misi, it's simpler and the menu is more straightforward. the wait staff here was good but the door staff was uninviting and we were treated like cattle. no eye contact, no welcome, just basic barebones acknowledgement. we waited 4 wks for a reservation, pump us up, make us excited...

Hands down, THEE best meal I have ever had in my life...and I say that with no exaggeration. Im actually really upset they don't have a restaurant on the West Coast. Everything I had was just above and beyond what I thought a meal could be. Everything was also very affordable but could add up since the plates aren't very big. This place is extremely popular, you either have to get there before it opens or make a reservation months in advanced.

If you're a foodie or invested in the culinary scene in some form, I'm sure you're well aware that the James Beard Awards were handed out this past Sunday in Chicago, IL. For those who aren't, the James Beard Awards are considered amongst the highest honors in the American restaurant world; simply being nominated is an honor which typically leads to an uptick in restaurant publicity and if you win well that's your ticket to skyrocketing into fame. I'm privileged and honored to say that I had the opportunity to eat at Lilia in Brooklyn where Head Chef Missy Robbins just became the latest to win the "Best Chef: New York City" award. Simply put Lilia is fantastic; it's everything you want in an Italian meal. It's wonderful to see Missy getting her well deserved recognition for years of hard work! Until next time Lilia...  

Dish 1: Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti with Saffron, Dried Tomato and Honey
Dish 2: Rigatoni Diavola with San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano and Pecorino
Dish 3: Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn and Parmigiano
Dish 4: Grilled Clams with Calabrian Chilies and Breadcrumbs
Dish 4: Double Chocolate Torta with Espresso Zabaglione 
Dish 5: Olive Oil Cake
Dish 6: Chocolate Soft Serve

This restaurant is a definite must go! We ordered 3 impeccable courses. The ambience, service, and cuisine was nothing short of outstanding. Our waiter, Skyler was polite and available; the manager, Adam was pleasant and prioritized that our dining experience was stellar!!

I am writing my first ever Yelp review on Lilia because I have been so incredibly disappointed about my experience there. The starters were amazing and we were really looking forward to the main stars of the meal - the pasta. In short, the Rigatoni Diavola is one of worst pastas I have ever had at a restaurant - it was so under-cooked that it was almost crunchy. Thinking that it must have been a mistake, we sent it back to kitchen. 15 minutes later, the SAME dish came back - the only difference was that it was warmer. The top pasta bits were just as crunchy, and the bottom ones were slightly softer but still incredibly unappetising, because they were way too salty and soggy. It was as if the kitchen had just microwaved it.

Everything about this place is amazing. The dimly lit dining room and quiet atmosphere is great. The pasta are out of this world. Every single one is amazing but must get agnolotti. Cacio e pepe fritters for an appetizer. The homemade gelato for dessert is also a must!!
One word. Superb. Wine, food, ambiance, the people. Superb. Go. Get a reservation!

Place is a joke...hostess was extremely rude. Waited for two hours on the waitlist and kept getting told different things about when we would be seated and kept getting referred to their cafe bar which had no room to stand....Ultimately after 2.5 hours they said that unfortunately they wouldn't be able to accommodate anyone on the waitlist and just turned everyone away despite tables beings open for long periods of time with no one sitting.

I really enjoyed my pasta here like it is raved for. However, I was extremely disappointed in our wait time given we had a reservation. My friend made a reservation for 2 online right at midnight when they came available, and we were still only able to get a 10:00pm reservation for a Saturday night. We WERE NOT SEATED until 10:25! And the restaurant supposedly closes at 11:00. The stewardess kept saying they were just waiting for the party before us to leave... 

I ordered the clams with chili and breadcrumbs to start which I enjoyed. My friend and I also shared the fresh mozzarella, which was really great. Like they sister restaurant, Misi, they do not do substitutions on any dishes. This is a real issue for people who are allergic to nuts. My friend could not have the pesto pasta which is obvious but also could not have my Cacio e Pepe pasta because it uses pink peppercorns, which is part of the cashew family. There were also several other pasta dishes that had nuts in it, and the waiter said they could not be left off the dishes. She ended up getting the sheep's milk ricotta agnolotti, which was delicious and super soft and pillowy. But it was still frustrating for her that she could not try other dishes. 

Overall I recommend but probably would try to get there right when it opens rather than make the 10:00 reservation that will really turn into start your meal at 10:40pm when you're starving. I liked Lilia better than Misi, which I have also tried.

TLDR Lilia is like most of your friend's boyfriends: great, but slightly overrated. We ordered the fettucine with spicy lamb sausage, which was quite good and had the perfect amount of spiciness, but the star was the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti. The saffron and honey really work well together and the pasta is cooked to perfection. The sheep's milk pasta is a bit too rich to eat on your own so would recommend splitting it. The atmosphere and staff were all extremely nice; however, I still prefer Misi, Lilia's sister restaurant, simply because it is so difficult to get a reservation at Lilia (ours was for 10pm which is way past my bedtime) and I think the pasta is a better value at Misi. Definitely great pasta but unclear if I'd go through the hassle of going again.

Excellent pasta! When Ina Gardner (aka Barefoot Contessa) is seated next to you, then you know the restaurant must be good!  Highlights of the meal were the pastas...went with the popular picks of Mafaldi & agnolotti. The agnolotti was the star for sure! We also really enjoyed the scallops...grilled to perfection! Our server while not overly personable, was very helpful with the wine list and steered us to a nice bottle which we both enjoyed. We shared the apple crostata & "Italian job" desserts. I'm not sure what the hype is about the Italian job but the ice cream paired nicely with the crostata! If you can get a reservation, you are sure to have a delicious experience at Lilia!

So much hype about this place. A bit too much I think. Pastas we had were all delicious. I liked the peppercorns on it a lot. The clams were not bad but not memorable. The gelato with topping customization was pretty phenomenal as I'm a total hazelnut and chocolate fan. I don't think it's a place I would make plans for a month ahead. I'm not really craving anything I had now that it's been a couple months since I went. I just think there are plenty other Italian restaurants that are at this standard too. All in all, not bad.

Well worth the month long wait for the table! 
The menu is curated incredibly well, and all the dishes we had flowed nicely into one another.
We started with the Cacio e Pepe fritters which were sensational, along with the artichoke.
Second course was the blowfish tails which were tender and well seasoned, and the baked clams which were fantastic and very instagram worthy.
The pastas were the show stopper - perfectly cooked and beautifully balanced. We were lucky enough to try 4 varieties - the agnolotti being the favorite.
The chocolate coffee cake for dessert brought a wonderful evening to a fitting close.

Disappointment, wait 40 minutes, cold and unbearable wind for Brazilian Tupiniquins, hoping to taste the flavor that evokes the photos, but unfortunately we were barred at the entrance, reason: not being able to receive eight people at the same table ... unbelievable ...  sad ... we moved on and were given a nice reception at the Bamontes restaurant ... the only pleasant moment was to see my son play the white piano at the corner ... no more ... forget this passage ... Goodbye

Lilia was good, but I hate to say it: it's overrated. 

Between two of us, we ordered six plates and two desserts. It was definitely too much food for just the two of us! Four plates is probably ideal. 

We had heard rave reviews about the clams and olive cake, but were underwhelmed. The spiciness was overpowering and the olive cake was nothing special. We also ordered the mozzarella, scallops, artichoke, and gelato which were all delicious. The agnolotti was our favorite, making me think that we would have been better off ordering mostly pastas. 

Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to go back to Lilia's but if I did, I would stick to their pasta menu.

Unique and refreshing pastas in an open and airy ambiance!

You definitely come here for the pasta - the rigatoni diavola is very flavorful, the malfadini with pepper and parmesan is a lighter cacio e pepe, and and the sheeps milk agnolotti is very unique tasting albeit too strongly flavored for one person to finish, in my opinion. Our favorite pasta, however, is the simple spaghetti with lemon, pine nuts, and parmigiano. It's a favorite of the servers' for its lightness - I could definitely eat a whole bowl of this and not feel immobile. Both times I have come, however, I've been disappointed by the appetizers, hence the 4 stars. They've lacked flavor, felt overly-heavy, or have just been unmemorable. They feel like precursors to the pasta rather than dishes that can stand alone.

The hype for this place makes the wait somewhat unbearable; I came right around opening at 5pm to find a long line of walk-ins and didn't end up eating until close to 8pm. Lilia has great, consistently satisfying pastas, but it's somewhat over-hyped still.

I live near Lilia and I constantly see lines for this restaurant so I decided to give it try. It was overrated. The experience was nice but we got small portions, plus the food wasn't worth the price. The service was great but the food was okay. I wouldn't go again. For a fancy place to eat at with good food and great service I recommend Esme.

Let me just say it's worth the wait / hustle to come. We got the reservation exactly 30 days in advance through a hustle with the online reservation site. 

It's in a fun neighbourhood and the restaurant is a little out of place among some warehouses and apartment buildings. We got seated at the whole inside atmosphere is very lively and energetic. 

We picked 8 dishes for a party of 5 girls. It was more than enough!! The service was fast and friendly. My favorites were the clams and the "pillow" pasta bites! I also really really liked the secret off menu desert the "Italian job" - olive oil, vanilla ice cream and honey. Amazing. Would come back again in a heart beat. Would bring more of my friends.

I came here on a weekday evening and with reservations, I was seated right away. I got the reservations easily the night before as I had signed up for daily notifications for any cancellations on Resy.

I thought the ambiance was minimalist. I mean for pictures, it does require flash. I think I would have preferred if the place was more well lit but I understand that it was an aesthetic choice. 

The service was great!

For the food, I had the chicken liver crostini ($17). It was decadent, creamy, and flavorful-- it was absolutely everything I'd want it to be and more.

We also tried the clams ($18), which were disappointing for me. The spiciness had a sort of sour taste to it which I did not particularly enjoy. Also, I would say the spiciness did not pair well with the clams and it tasted out of sync somehow.

I also tried the Agnolotti pasta ($25). This is a must try for this restaurant and it did not disappoint. I loved the notes of cheese milk and honey. It was very rich, creamy, and filling.

I also shared the Fettuccine with lamb ($24), which we thoroughly enjoyed. It juxtaposed well with the other pasta as they were both so different and unique. The lamb pieces were flavorful and larger than your average Bolognese pieces of meat, which I enjoyed. The sauce was slightly spicy which worked as it was not overpowering.

For the dessert, I had the Italian Job ($11). The pairings of sea salt, honey, and Polifemo Sicilian olive oil were simply divine! 

I did see the similarity between Lilia and its sister restaurant, Misi. For the chicken liver crostini, it looked similar to the charred peppers with whipped ricotta crostini. *Although, these tasted unique from each other. The olive oil ice cream at Misi mimicked the Italian job at Lilia. Also, the butter and honey infused into the pasta held the same appeal. I am only mentioning this to say both are worth going to, if you are looking for that vibe! I loved my experiences at both of them.

I came here with a girlfriend for a friend date.  We were not able to get a reservation but showed up about an hour before they opened and were able to be seated at the bar.  There were others waiting in line before we got there.  We ordered a lot and loved everything.  Our favorites were the saffron pasta and the dessert.  The restaurant is small but with a warm vibe.  It is upscale but casual.  The food tasted fresh and the menu was exciting.  I would love to come again but wish it was easier to get a reservation.

BF and I were able to snag a table at this exclusive restaurant yesterday after arriving around 430pm (opens at 5). Due to the hard to get reservations, we were seated around 510 and had to be done by 7pm (okay, no problem!). We started with the Housemade Mozzarella and the Grilled Blowfish tails (recommended by our waiter). I personally really enjoyed the mozzarella but the bread was lacking. The blowfish tails were seasoned very well. I found out I don't really like the texture of the blowfish tails but if this is something you like it's a must try! The waiter also recommended the scallops which I would order if I'm able to snag a reservation in the future. Now the main course: Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti and Mafaldini pasta. The pastas are WHY you go to Lilia. Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti is a must try (as you can see from other reviews). The richness and flavor of this pasta is amazing.  The Mafaldini was interesting but I would not order again. I do suggest customers to get a meat/fish dish to eat with their pasta! Overall, I would recommend!

Yeah yeah... it is really that good.  I mean THAT good!  Hype shmype... you want a unique italian meal that covers many types of prep using the best ingredients, spices and flavors, creatively mixed and matched to make a memorable meal... then just go.     

Was there with a large group so we had a fixed menu and got to sample many dishes. Clams, foccacia, little gem salad, cauliflower (OMG), simple beautiful ripe and sweet heirloom tomatoes, rigatoni, gnocchi, grilled bass, anglotti.  ohhh... yes... the anglotti which everyone raves about is yes,  a must.  Delicate array of rich flavors not found previously and melt on your palate goodness.   

But virtually all dishes that came out were winners in my book and I have been to Italy a dozen times in my life and eaten many great italian meals and this is in the top tier.  And let me tell you the chicken drum and thigh were also amazing.  I know... you "chickened" out ,...  well have one more in your life and make it this one.  The marinade on this bird and the skin and the flavors were mind altering.  I'll never look at another bird the same way.  Ohhh and the eggplant app was different in that it was melt in your mouth almost a puree it seemed, with a marinade and flavor profile with the ricotta salata, thyme, garlic and chili oil that will make your eggplant future altered ( unless you like your eggplant on the raw side), then skip this.   

And of course the deserts also hit it out of the park, in particular some type of ice cream or gelato with god knows what drizzled on it just had a unique flavor I have never experienced.  And did I say the focaccia with green butter was also to die for.  Should I keep going.   We had a ton of dishes and I am fatter and happier because of it.   

My next trip to Italy now has a higher bar to reach in the food world.

Lilia feels like special occasion dining with its ambient buzz and open hearth-driven kitchen. The food mostly delivers. Dishes are ambitious and the flavors clean, pastas and vegetables highlight only a handful of ingredients at a time; Lilia shows simple is definitively not boring. Get the Italian job soft serve to finish.

Best dinning experience!!! Everything was beyond delicious! Best Italian food I've ever had! Had the homemade mozzarella which was superb. Tried both the sheep's milk and squash raviolis. We had the mussels which were the best I've ever had. The blowfish was amazing!! Basically everything was absolutely delicious! I can't say enough good things about this place, I'm sure everything on the menu is delicious. No complaints :)

Great spot! It's very hard to get reservations but if you can, it's worth it. The restaurant is upscale but casual. The menu is well priced for being such a popular in demand spot. Everything we ate was delicious. The fried cheese balls and blow fish tails appetizers were both delicious. For dinner we had two pasta dishes. The most memorable was the sheepmilk cheese stuffed agnolotti. Absolutely delicious. Great place, I recommend to anyone as a perfect date, birthday or anniversary dinner spot.

Lilia has been on my list FOREVER and the stars seemed to have aligned when a Resy reservation opened up last minute for dinner on the night my husband and I were going to go out to celebrate our anniversary. The service was amazing but there was no AC and it was mid August and sweltering. This really took away from us enjoying the meal. That and the somewhat disappointing appetizers like the artichoke with parmiagiano and breadcrumbs which sounded delicious but was way too salty. We were ready to write the place off when our pasta dishes came out and the meal was redeemed. The pasta was fresh, delicious, and devoured quickly. I would definitely come back for the pasta.

Not as good as I expected it would be. My husband and I went here one night thinking  it to be awesome because we had heard so many good things. We got the clams, gem lettuce, agnolotti, mafaldini, and for dessert the chocolate cake and soft serve. The clams and gem lettuce were okay but the agnolotti was delicious. The mafaldini was very undercooked. We both worked in an Italian restaurant so we know what al dente should taste like and this pasta was actually hard. The chocolate cake was pretty good and we loved the soft serve, but how can you mess up soft serve honestly. Perhaps it was a rough night and we will come back and try again another time.
Had my hopes up for this place and for its popularity. Good, but nothing to die for. Pasta was great, but wasn't a 'melt in your mouth' type of feel. The service, however, was excellent.

I came at 5:15pm to try to get it at open. There were already 10 people ahead of me. I didn't get a table inside but we were able to sit outside. 

This is the second time I came. 
Sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti is must order. 
Favs beans is summer special. It tastes light. I like the fava beans at Misi's better. 
Vegetables are raw. The sauce is flavorful. 
Collar was a special that day. I think Japanese cooks better collar. 

Now I want to go to Misi for another time..

I have been wanting to go to Lilia for a really long time and last night I finally did! I would give it closer to a 3.5 than a 4, but I'm rounding up because the service and pasta were both great. 

The restaurant itself is really cute and we weren't sitting on top of our neighbors which was a pleasant surprise for a trendy NYC restaurant. The one problem I had was that it was SO HOT. I had read some reviews that mentioned that and I didn't think it would be a big deal, but it was uncomfortable hot and humid. We heard the people at the table next to us talking about it as well. 

For appetizers we got the prosciutto (the parmesan butter was SO good), mozzarella garlic bread, and the clams. The proscuitto and mozzarella were good, but the clams were really disappointing. They looked a lot more flavorful than they tasted. If I went back I wouldn't order appetizers and I would just order an extra pasta. For pasta we ordered the Mafaldini and the Agnolotti which were SO GOOD. Totally worth the hype. The Mafaldini is really just cacio e pepe, but the pasta shape makes it more interesting. The Sheeps Milk Agnolotti has such great flavor, but it's a rich dish so split it with someone. We got the Olive Oil cake for dessert which was good, but next time I would skip the desserts. 

Lilia was very reasonably priced and good quality. For a bottle of wine, 3 apps, 2 pastas, and a dessert we spent $200. If I went back I would go in the winter and I would only order pasta.

the sheep's milk pasta literally changed my life - by the time I got home from dinner here I was already craving it again. 

also the service is incredible; they're super cognizant if allergies even if the ones you have aren't technically in the menu's dishes, and the space is absolutely gorgeous. Beautiful interiors and natural lighting.

Sad to say, but this was a very underwhelming experience. 3.5/5 but I'm rounding up in good faith. 

We've been meaning to come here because my husband read about the special oven that they have. Tried to make a reservation, but as I found out when someone finally picked up, they're booked 30 days in advance but you can come 30mins before opening and get a spot at the bar on first come first serve basis. So that is what we did. About 30mins before opening, as expected, a line started to form. At 5:30pm on the dot, they opened the doors. We were second in line and got a table that was reserved for 7:15pm, so we were told we had and hour and 45 mins. I'm not sure what the hype is and "the 30 day in advance wait" because I really did not find anything special about this place. 

We got a housemade mozzarella with grilled bread which was probably my favorite. The chicken liver pate was very flavorful, interesting but not my fave. The grilled zucchini with anchovies were weird, but surprisingly good. The mafaldini was okay, a bit too al dente that it was difficult to chew. Then came a 30 minute wait between the pasta and our entrees. Finally, we got our grilled bass and lamb steak. The fish was okay. The lamb was very fatty but my husband liked the flavors. I got a strawberry crostata for dessert and it was yummy. All in all, it's okay, can't say it was worth a trip to Williamsburg. 
Servers were very nice and attentive.

HYPED.

Was so excited and after spending $100 pp we left disappointed for so so tastebud satisfaction. Maybe too high hope from other positive reviews.

::: The Liked (yes only 1 dishes out of all) :::

Chicken Liver Crostini - all of our favorite, good flavor and texture, not too dry (sometimes can be)

::: The Okay----ed :::

Grilled BlowFish Tail - I it's not bad but nothing special.

Grilled Clam - not bad and you can tell the clam is fresh.

Whole Artichoke - as expected.

Linguini, Anchovy, Tomato sauce & Lemon - the more flavorful pasta we had, the mix of tomate and lemon was pretty good.

Strawberry Dessert - okayed

Italian Job - pretty good but even 4 people share it's still to much as it's pretty heavy in flavor. Was sold as it's their biggest secret menu dessert but well I see the post here and there ...

::: The Disappointed :::

Roasted Trumpet Mushroom - six thin sliced mushroom with few arugula laid on top, I thought this dish is a joke.

Cacio e Pepe Fritelle - so salty no one wanted the second bite.

Ricotta Gnocchi - I like the nuts texture in it but the whole dishes just bland. Not impressed.

Mafaldini - my fav noodle but sorry maybe I don't understand, this minimalism dish. Pink peppercorn and parmigiana only, we didn't enjoy it. Kept thinking about Scampi's Mafaldine as I ate this.

Save your money and go somewhere else.

Personally I thought it was fine. The pasta seemed kinda cold when they brought it... and it took a while to get it and I honestly think it was sitting there for sometime before we did. Skip the rigatoni definitely get the ricotta to put on the heirloom tomatoes. My issue was our waiter seemed way more interested in the table with the annoyingly loud chick next to us. He didn't seem attentive at all to our meal. My friend is very polite she's from LA doesn't realize NY you don't need to apologize for someone bumping into you on the train. Long story short we didnt need to tip an extra 50 bucks for not doing much and just because of the name of the restaurant. I've had better essential Italian wait wasn't so bad if you got there at 5. I just get frustrated when I put so much effort into getting a meal for the experience to not be every last bit of impressive. I'm glad I went since it's damn near impossible but I also could live with out it.

Overpriced and overhyped. Sat outside initially at a table with no light, had to pull out a phone light to even read the menus. The scallops were good but not worth $9/scallop (2 scallops per order). For $20-30 per small dish of pasta they were marginal- not bad but certainly nothing to write home about and not worth the price. I politely asked for hot chili peppers for the pasta. The waitress said she'd check with the kitchen as the "cooks don't allow it on some of the pastas." They eventually gave them to me, but really? For $120 for a 3-dish meal that leaves us hungry and underwhelmed, I'll damn well use the chili flakes if they're available, which they are.

It started raining at the end of din so they offered to move us inside to the bar. We asked if we could kindly finish our meal at one of the many open tables inside (most had turned over). They paused and asked their higher-up before reticently agreeing. We were polite the whole way through, and tipped well none-the-less. Bottom line, you can find better food for a more reasonable price elsewhere, with a less pretentious vibe, even in Manhattan. And this is coming from an Ivy league MD living in the upper east side.

Beautiful atmosphere, however, I do agree that this place is more hyped up than it should be. The food is incredibl - the grilled tuna and the lamb leg steak. We also tried their chicken liver crostini which was a favorite for me. I would definitely come back here and plan on it.

author.name: Foodie L.
author.location: Long Island City, New York, NY

reviews.review: Because I did not have a reservation, my friend and I had to sit outside where they are doing construction right next to the restaurant. However, the service was still wonderful, and the inside of the restaurant is gorgeous. We ordered the focaccia special to start and it was AMAZING. The butter on the side was delicious silk and the bread itself was buttery and salty and crusty to perfection. For my entree I got the sheep's milk pasta with saffron and honey and it was mouth watering delicious. My friend got the ricotta gnocchi which had good texture but I did not personally enjoy the pistachios with the dish, they were overpowering. We shared the chocolate and espresso dessert and it had good flavor but I think it was slightly over cooked. Overall this restaurant is fabulous, I would recommend getting a reservation to sit inside, and its not too expensive for the quality of the food!

Lilia has been on my hit list for well over a year. I had somewhat given up on going after having a less than ideal experience at its sister restaurant Misi and the difficulty of getting a reservation so I was very happy when my friend asked me to go with her after scoring a reservation for a Sunday night.

We started with the blowfish tails - I don't think I've ever had blowfish cooked in western style before. These were meaty and perfectly seasoned. I would have been happy with this as a main course.

We then ordered the sheep's milk filled agnolotti and linguini with tomatoes and anchovies. I liked both pastas but I think the agnolotti slightly more due to the originality of the dish. I was glad we got the tarter tomato based linguini to balance out the richness of the agnolotti. 

Lastly after reading the reviews of the olive oil cake - I decided to get an order for the table. Honestly, I didn't think this was very special at all - it just tasted like normal cake to me. I probably wouldn't order it again.

All in all, I had a good experience at Lilia but considering how difficult it is to get reservations here, I'm not sure if I would be back unless I was with someone who was very insistent about wanting to dine here. I'm glad I finally got to try this staple to New York's Italian restaurant scene and think it's definitely worth a try if you like modern Italian with an American twist.

The most frustrating thing about this restaurant is the food is quite good. But their desire to project an image of unrelenting popularity is a ridiculous falsehood. All staff are trained to tell you there is a 30 day wait limit. Staff will leave tables empty rather than seat people that didn't wait. It is my local, I even have the managers number but I have developed a deep resentment towards the front of house staff and their spiteful management. It's good, but guys come on it's not that good. snap out of your air of grandeur and be the neighbourhood restaurant that promised so much.

I've been waiting for this day for a month (made this reservation 30 days out for a family dinner during their visit), but unfortunately, I feel like Lilia is super overhyped. Cute space, but it was soooooo hot. I know a lot of restaurants like to open up their windows on nice days, but yesterday was way too hot for that...the place really needed AC!

Here's what we tried, family style:

Cacio E Pepe Frittelle $9
We got two orders since there were 6 of us and only 3 to an order. These looked really good but they were insanely oversalted.

Roasted Trumpet Mushrooms $16
Great dish, even though the portion is laughably small. These were super small rectangular slices covered in arugula. Thought the balsamic vinegar really created an interesting flavor combined with the seasoning on the mushrooms.

Whole Artichoke $18
A yummy dish, but note that most of the dish is inedible, so the portion is once again quite small for $18. The artichoke heart was extremely tender and the flavors were spot on (love the breadcrumbs), wish there was bread around to soak up all the juices at the bottom. My 3yo niece loved this dish.

Grilled Clams $18
The seasoning and bread crumbs were really good, but unfortunately these tasted a bit rubbery as they were overcooked. Disappointed :(

Grilled Blowfish Tails $16
I thought this was good but also slightly overcooked. I think the theme here is that all the dishes are seasoned to perfection, but the cook is somewhat off. Not a lot of meat, and definitely an appetizer portion. If you have a lot of people. I'd recommend getting multiple orders.

Rigatoni Diavola $20
Really boring dish to be honest. Some pieces were undercooked. I would not recommend. Slightly spicy.

Mafaldini $21
Cool shape of pasta! Texture was good, right amount of cook. I liked how simple this was, but you're kind of pleasantly surprised by the interesting flavors from the pink peppercorn.

Ricotta Gnocchi $21
Meh. I've actually never had gnocchi with this type of texture. It seemed really dense and the texture was blah, did not taste very good. I've actually never tasted gnocchi with this type of texture. The broccoli pesto with the pistachios was really good though!

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti $25
SO GOOD. If you come, please order this dish, this is a must get. Every agnolotti is cooked perfectly and the filling is just delicious. Such a delicate and simple dish.

Vanilla Soft Serve $10
I would skip this, nothing special :(

If you can get resos, I'd recommend their sister restaurant Misi over Lilia!

Pasta just as good as a I remembered it. Now bumped up to 5 stars because the service we had last night was impeccable - enthusiastic, friendly, and extremely helpful - was dead on with all of his recommendations, especially the wine pick.

Pasta rundown:
Agnolotti - must order, that sheep's milk cheese filling still owns me
Malfadini - still one of my favorites, perfect texture and bite, creamy/peppery sauce, but wish it was 1-2 deg warmer this time around
Cappelletti - that rich, sweet corn filling is soo good
Rigatoni - enjoyed it much better compared to my last visit; pasta cooked perfectly, such a fresh/sweet tomato sauce, and perfect hint of spiciness

Reservations seem much harder to come by these days. Trick is to just make on Resy 30 days out at midnight, and you should be able to get it. I rarely see cancellations show up on Resy.

There's a reason this place is still so hard to get reservations at this long into its existence. Still some of my favorite pasta in the city!

Fair prices, superb service, ok food which does not live up to the hype. 
Had some surprisingly greasy dishes, overpowering amounts of butter, cheese, and oil. Fish was definitely on the dry side. Still, well priced for the quality

Highly-recommend Lilia!! All of the food is delicious and the service is excellent. 

We started with 4 appetizers: 

-Housemade mozzarella on garlic bread with lemon & bottarga: Mozzarella was fresh and flavorful and the lemon and bottarga add to the flavor 
-Whole Artichoke with Garlic, Mint, Parmigiano, Breadcrumbs: I didn't even know that I liked artichoke (my friend ordered this dish), but I can assure you that I love artichoke now that I've tried it at Lilia
-Italian Broccoli, Parmigiano, Chili Oil, Lemon: The broccoli picked up the flavor of the chili oil to give it the perfect kick 
-Cacio e Pepe Fritelle: Fried cheese dusted with pepper-- can't get better than that 

For the main course, we had 3 entrees:

-Black Bass, Salsa Verde, Coal Roasted Yukon Gold Potatoes: The bass was crispy on the outside and perfectly-cooked on the inside. The Yukon potatoes were an excellent pairing with the bass 
-Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey: The sheeps milk cheese was rich and was perfectly-balanced but the saffron and honey 
-Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Basil, Pistachios: This was my favorite dish, which is saying something because everything was so tasty. The ricotta and broccoli pesto paired perfectly and the pistachios added fantastic flavor and crunch. 

For dessert, we had the double chocolate cake, which was fluffy yet rich at the same time-- delicious! We also had cortados, which was the best coffee I've ever tasted. 

Can't say enough about Lilia!!

Tons of hype surrounding Lilia and they did not disappoint. There was something left to be desired -- they didn't hit that "best of the best" tier, hence the 4 starts instead of 5. But hey, 4 stars is pretty damn good!

We started with the grilled stuffed artichoke which was excellent -- best I've ever had. We then split 4 pastas -- the agnolotti, malfaldini, fettuccini and spaghetti limone. 

The agnolotti was stuffed with ricotta and in a beautiful honey cheese sauce. Very delicious. 

The maldaldini was a wonderful ribbed noodle in a cacio Pepe sauce, also very good, though a tad heavy handed on the pepper 

The fettuccini was with a spicy lamb ragu and maybe my favorite of all. 

And the spaghetti limone was vibrant and delicious as well. 

The service was excellent and the ambiance was nice as well. 

Overall, an excellent meal and would recommend to all

An incredible experience.  After finding out about Lilia, I immediately put down our party of 4 to be notified of a table the next day between 6-9pm.  The next morning I got an alert that a table become available and opened the app, but it was already grabbed by someone else.  After this happened 2 more times, we secured a table for 6:00 for 4.  We arrived 17 minutes late, but they still welcomed us with open and relaxed arms.  The hosts and wait staff were very friendly and made you feel like you belonged there from the beginning.  We started with the garlic bread and herb butter, it was amazing.  We then ordered the mafaldine, pesto gnocchi, and 2 diavola pastas.  Mafaldine is now my new favorite pasta shape, and the dish was so amazing.  The chew of the pasta and the creamy but pepperiness was a great balance.  The pesto gnocchi was my least favorite but still good.  I thought the gnocchi was a bit to tough/chewy.  Not as pillowy as potato gnocchi.  We finished with an off menu dessert that was vanilla gelato, honey, olive oil and fennel pollen.  It was an incredible way to end the meal, but maybe a touch too much olive oil for my taste.  Overall, I'm glad we made the trip and am thankful to have gotten to eat there.

Beautiful space, incredible food and service. Really loved the simple but surprising flavors. Tried two pastas and both were delicious, the gnocchi was incredible. Also tried the bass and it was awesome. All the appetizers and cocktail snacks were also great. Their homemade mozzarella especially was really good and the cheese puffs. The food was filling but not super heavy like some pasta dishes can be. Had the chocolate torta for dessert and I swear it was somehow the perfect combination of light and rich. Also the waiters are awesome. So attentive, I never saw the bottom of my water glass, and they really try to create a beautiful cohesive meal with great pairings and impeccable timing. Will definitely be coming back.

Do yourself a favor and start with the ice cream! So good! The apps were all excellent. Some dishes are quiet spicy- so be aware of that. I didn't love my main dish (sea bass) but it wasn't a big deal because I was satisfied with all the apps we ordered. The host and the staff are all very friendly and nice. Totally looking forward to return.

Reservations are difficult to get, and now I know why. This. Place. Is. EXCELLENT. From the appetizers to desert, I was blown away tonight. Started with a glass of white wine (very good and moderately priced), then had the stuffed artichoke hearts (delicious), then spicy-lamb fettuccine (incredible) and, lastly, an assortment of desserts (mind-blowing). I'd go back every night I'm in town if I could get a table.

One thing I love to do at Italian restaurants is dip bread in the sauces that my dishes come in! I had been here once before and we ordered the focaccia bread and did this with it! The waiter was very nice and even brought us out seconds as a single order of focaccia isn't huge. The second time I visited Lilia, however, we were told they were out of focaccia- disappointing but not a big deal. Seeing as there were several other dishes containing other types of bread on the menu, we asked if we could instead pay for a side of bread for our meal. The waitress said no, that "we don't do that here." Annoyed and knowing they had bread in the kitchen, we asked the server who came to refill our water. He obligingly brought us out a plate of bread (3 small pieces but beggars can't be choosers). When our waitress saw this, she pulled him aside and we could tell she was telling him this was wrong. When we asked for seconds to eat with our pasta, he said no. If i am paying you $80+ for a meal and I ask to pay additional for a side of bread, and you have bread in the kitchen, then why be difficult about it? Bad customer service and the "we don't do that here" came off pretentious and snobby. Do better Lilia!

tl;dr: spotty service, decent food, I've had better.

Two of us walked in on a weeknight ~15 minutes prior to opening, and were seated soon afterwards. We shared the frittelle, the artichoke and couple of filled pastas. The issues started when the ceiling started crumbling and falling above our table, some of which fell on me (!) - the team apologised, but we weren't given the opportunity to move.

The artichoke dish was fun, but as first-timers, we ended up only eating half the dish. For all the other noobs out there, you kinda scoop the tender inside flesh away from each petal and discard the tougher outer. Our server didn't explain this at all - we only realized this when another server told our neighbour, after our (sadly only half-eaten) artichoke had been cleared. The pastas were elegant and good value, especially the agnolotti. 

RE: service, I shared my feedback and they gave me a free ice cream, which was nice - but to be honest the experience wasn't quite salvageable. Lilia is a good restaurant, and if there wasn't so much hype and finagling associated with it, I'd probably call it fair value and go despite the service. As it is... ehhh.

Incredibly tasty food, cozy and fun vibe, excellent service, everything felt like it was done with passion and intention. Had the mozzarella, clams, mafaldine, agnolotti, bass and veal. All exceeded expectations. A gem in Brooklyn.

Reservations are harder to get than I imagined but I finally got one and it did not disappoint! 

We had a late seating at 9pm, when we arrived we were seated immediately. We ordered the cacio e pepe frittelle, grilled blowfish tails, sheeps milk cheese agnolotti, mafaldini, fettuccini with spicy lamb sausage, and for dessert the off the menu ice cream called the Italian job.

We ordered a bit too much but every dish was delicious. I have to say the 2 main stars for me were the blowfish tails and the sheeps milk cheese agnolotti. They were my winners of the evening. I highly recommend.

Although I find the food to be outstanding, I'm consistently disappointed by the servers at the caffe and the hosts. It's a rare treat to have such an exceptional meal yet I feel very disappointed when I'm treated indifferently and rudely by the staff. I will say that our server for dinner was wonderful and we so appreciated her kindness and professionalism - but it seems she is a rare gem at Lilia. I'd come all the time if I felt more welcome.

One of our favorite places in New York. Everything we have ordered has always exceeded our expectations.

Favorite dishes: cacio e pepe fritelle (crisp shelled and cheesy, with plenty of pepper, yet maintaining lightness), seasonal focaccia with green garlic butter (most recently they topped it with parm and sungolds), fresh housemade mozzarella (so creamy), and any of the pastas (have had the mafaldini, fettuccini, sheep's milk agnolotti), lamb main, and veal main (probably the most tender version we've had, lightened with fresh herbs and Italian chimichurri). They also have a lovely olive oil cake and lemon ice

We normally get there around 430-445pm to get the first seating at the bar. When the weather is nice, they have more walk in seating (esp for groups of 4) outside. Service is always very nice. They also have a very good aperol spritz, as well as complementary sparkling water and predinner snacks (rosemary peanuts and spiced potato chips)

I think it's very easy to come here expecting Michelin-quality food and it's just not. BUT, it's also not Michelin priced. The pasta is great, the value is fine, the atmosphere is above-average.

We had a 9pm reservation on a Saturday, which yes I did make at midnight a month in advance. We were able to be seated immediately. We also downsized our reservation from 6 to 5 people and they adjusted the table without a problem. 

I had talked to a couple friends that had been to get recommendations. We ordered 4 apps: the prosciutto, the mozzarella, the zucchini, and the clams. Mozzarella and zucchini were great, the other two were good but missable. From there, we got one pasta per person: the mafaldini, agnolotti, rigatoni, spaghetti, and fettuccini. Agnolotti was a hit - by far one of the best dishes of the night. I also liked the mafaldini. Rigatoni (in my opinion) was a skip - it was very al dente and the sauce was just ok. 

For dessert, we got the olive oil cake and the off-menu Italian Job. Can not recommend the latter enough - it was incredible. We all joked that it would be our last meal if we were prisoners on death row. Olive oil cake wasn't bad but wasn't great either. 

Service throughout the night was paced well. Dishes came out quickly. Total per person was around $70 with two drinks each, so pretty decent considering the quality of the food.

All in all, I'm glad I went. I'm not sure it's worth the hype, but probably worth a visit.

Lives up to the hype. 

Wow... I know you see this place all over Instagram and think it has to be overrated, well it's not. Since you have to get reservations so far in advance, we went all out and ordered two starters and three pasta dishes because we couldn't pass up the opportunity to try all that we could. 

Overall - would definitely recommend anyone to go, while a bit more on the pricey side, it definitely has some amazing pasta. 

Grilled clams - super tasty and fresh. They taste as great as they look. 
Bread (can't remember what it's called!) - a special that night, though I believe it's a special most nights, definitely a must order. 
Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti - melts in your mouth. I knew it was going to be good... I didn't know it was going to be THAT good!! Must try! 
Mafaldini - Good dish, could pass on next time. 
Ricotta Gnocchi - fresh and yummy! Definitely can taste the green :)

Food was great ! Little Thrown off on how the reservations worked. Waited an hour and a half for a table outside because inside would have been a
Longer wait. Got a text at first about seating at bar which was never an option for us. But the host fixed everything. She was amazing and found us a table outside quickly! 

Our server was attentive but not as much as Paul who i think was a back waiter And he picked up all the slack and made our first date dinner better than we expected. Thank you Paul! 

Fresh mozzarella on garlic toast great. Chicken thigh and leg was fantastic so flavorful. Looked forward to the ricotta gnocchi. Was decent. Did the job. Great wine.  The view from the outside patio table was not up to par because of the construction but again. Paul killed it so we didn't even care. 

All around i would come again. But i would make a reservation in advance for sure to get a table inside !

After spending day after day staring at Lilia's always fully booked reservations page I finally snagged a slot one month out and dreamed of the night I'd finally be in pasta heaven at the place the NYTimes awarded a rare 3 star review just weeks after opening.

Located in a former auto-body garage, Lilia's space is filled with wooden accents, high ceilings and features an open kitchen. Even with a reservation I waited 30 minutes to be seated but came prepared to order straight away, starting with the burratino toast, featuring housemade mozzarella, lemon and bottarga on toasted garlic bread. While mozzarella on toast would be a safe and unexciting order at a lesser restaurant, Lilia punches it up with the unexpected flavor of bottarga, a salted anchovy-like cured fish which even my seafood averse dining companion appreciated. The bottarga was very subtle, just dotting the soft mozzarella cheese with salt grain sized flecks of umami flavor. Crushed garlic in olive oil deliciously bound the cheese and bread together.

The ruffled edges of the Malfadini pasta create the perfect wavy shape for gathering up generous shavings of Parmigiano Reggiano cheese, melted butter and pink peppercorns. These three simple ingredients alone season the pasta, which for a dish that was as hyped up as it was, came across as pretty underwhelming. The pink peppercorns added a tiny kick and the texture of the noodle was fun and nicely al dente but otherwise there was nothing to write home about this dish.

The Sheeps Milk Agnolotti with Saffron, Dried tomato and Honey was undoubtedly the most intoxicating dish of the meal. Each pocket of the smooth egg based agnolotti pasta was filled with a light, creamy filling of sheeps milk cheese. The buttered honey saffron sauce drenched each bite with a pleasant sweetness that made the "pasta made by Ms. Robbins is a direct route to happiness" line from the NYTimes review ring very true.

While you really go to Lilia for the pasta, the desserts look to be the most creative part of the menu, with items like Italian Bombolini doughnuts, Prosciutto Brioche and Rosemary Shortbread. The Olive Oil Cake felt like a very adult way to satisfy my sweet tooth. The cake, while very rich, was not cloyingly sweet, as cake can so often be. The whipped cream was almost as dense as the cake, and tasted great with the also subtly sweet blood orange that comes on the side. This was a generous slice of cake, which I appreciated after the comparably small portions of pasta.

The dishes at Lilia are all executed very well but in a city where good food is the standard for restaurants that survive, the food fell short of being impressive among the many red sauce joints of New York. While I wouldn't be upset to dine at Lilia again, there's plenty of more exciting and unique options elsewhere if you're unable to get a reservation.

Amazing, make sure to book a table in advance, or you will have to wait for a bar stool. Portions are small but the dishes are so good that it is worth trying multiples. Slightly pricey but worth it, also in a nice spot in Brooklyn.

This is a classic case of HYPE alone leading to popularity. I worked in the neighborhood when Lilia was being built. I remember being SO excited. Since then i've been seeing consistent social media hype about it. To the point that it took months and months to even get a resi. I'll say this, the vibe of the restaurant is amazing. The food itself is beautiful to look at. My friend and I tried the little gem lettuce, the black bass, the mafaldini pasta & the veal flank steak. The salad came with cheese, even though we asked for it without, and the staff seemed so perturbed by us mentioning something. The pasta came out cold, they took it back to warm it up, and it was still cold. Overall, everything tasted fresh, but to be honest, not very good. The pasta looked so beautiful but tasted so off. Same with the bass. And oh my god the prices! So incredibly expensive. I definitely will not be back. So many better restaurants in BK, especially in that area!

Lilia is one of my favorite Italian restaurants- it is worth all the planning you need to do dine here! 

Getting seated: We planned all our restaurants we wanted to go to during our trip to New York and Lilia was one of them. We couldn't get reservations at a reasonable time so the only other option was to come early. We arrived at the restaurant at around 4:50pm on a Wednesday night, 40 minutes before they open and we were third in line. They have seats outside so you can wait and just chat with your company. It was a nice warm summer night so the 40 minutes just flew by. When the restaurant opened, we were able to get a seat immediately on the patio. We were happy our wait paid off and were ready for our meal

We were a party of three and ordered two appetizers, three pastas, and two desserts- it was more than enough food! We ended up spending about $50-60 per person, but it was completely worth it! The service was also amazing and we had the best waiter. He really described each dish and truly made our experience memorable.

Appetizers: Cacio e Pepe Fritelle and the house made Focaccia Bread with Ramps Butter. Both appetizers were incredible.
- The Cacio e Pepe Fritelle was just too good for words. They were balls of cheese-dusted dough, stuffed with melted pecorino and asiago cheese. They were prepared perfectly, with a crunchy exterior and a delicious and creamy interior. 
-The Focaccia Bread with Ramps Butter: The focaccia was high quality and authentic- baked to perfection and not overly oily like you find in many focaccia. It was the butter, however, that stole the show.  I can't really put in words, but I could defiantly eat a whole tub of butter by itself.

Pastas: Peppercorn Mafaldini, Spaghetti Lemon Pine Nuts, and Sheeps Milk Agnolotti
- Mafaldini: This was my favorite. I loved the al-dente twisted noodles as it really captured the flavor of the peppercorn and parmigiana. The peppercorn flavor was intense, but it was balanced perfectly with the parmigiana and the thickness of the pasta
Sheeps milk Agnolotti: Another excellent pasta dish. While I am used to dishes in which the agnolotti is stuffed with meat, the sheeps milk was so delicious that no meat was necessary. You could tell that the sheeps milk inside the agnolotti was high quality and prepared really well; each bite was light, creamy and filled with so much flavor

Spaghetti Lemon Pine Nuts: This was a nice simple pasta that we all enjoyed. It wasn't unique or stood out like the other dishes, but it was a good pasta to have to balance out all the flavors from the other dishes. 

Dessert: Our waiter convinced us to order the Olive Oil Cake and the Olive Oil  Gelato- Also known as the Italian Job. Both were so yummy, but the Italian Job was incredible. It's not on the menu, so make sure to ask for it. Its a Vanilla Gelato with hardened honey mixed into it, and topped with olive oil, sea salt and fennel seeds. Its a combination of ingredients you never really, but it all came together wonderfully. Finding chunks of the hardened honey throughout the gelato was absolutely delectable, and while it may sound overly sweet, the high quality olive oil and fennel seeds balanced it out with a savory kick
BEST food I have ever had!!!!!  Everything was phenomenal! The focaccia was fantastic! To top it off the waiter, Marcus,  was exceptional!!!  BRAVO!!!

HOW TO GET A RESERVATION THAT'S NOT AT 10PM ON A WEDNESDAY: Call for the reservation, rather than using Resy. I know, it's 2019 and we all hate talking to humans on the phone, but in this case, it pays off - they'll take reservations over the phone for two days further out than you can reserve on Resy. Reservations open at 10am, so start calling at like 9:58 and keep trying until you get through to a person. I stalked Resy for days trying to get a reservation and finally tried calling - and it worked on my first try.

Onto the actual dining experience! We started with the garlic bread + mozzarella and the roasted trumpet mushrooms. Both were delicious - nuanced in both flavor and texture. Must orders. For the pastas, we went with the sheep's milk cheese agnolotti and the rigatoni diavola. The agnolotti were to die for - despite all the hype I had read/seen on Instagram going in, it was truly wonderful. The rigatoni, on the other hand, I was really disappointed by. The pasta was VERY al dente - and I like my pasta al dente - but it was almost undercooked. The sauce tasted like a one-note spicy tomato sauce - I honestly prefer the tomato sauce I make at home over it.

All that being said, the appetizers and agnolotti were worth the price of admission. I'm hoping to return so we can try the mafaldini!

To start off with, if you're like me and can't be bothered to make a reservation a month in advance at midnight on the dot, let me say that in my personal experience, it is very easy to get a spot at the bar provided you're willing to get there 15-20 min before the restaurant opens on a weekday. 

Service/ambiance: 5/5, lots of windows with lots of natural light. Servers could not have been more friendly and attentive. I don't think my water glass got more than half empty my entire night. 

Food: Quite good. Of course, I had to get the famed malfadini and the sheep's milk agnolotti. Of the two, the latter was my favorite (although the malfadini was very good as well-- nice texture and good flavor). Biting into the agnolotti though was like biting into the softest pillow you can imagine; I don't think I've ever had cheese more soft and fluffy (I should warn you though, it's very rich. I couldn't finish it but that's why we invented leftovers). 

My favorite dish of the night though was the dessert, the Italian job gelato. It's not on the menu and it has quite possibly the weirdest assortment of toppings I've ever seen (olive oil and fennel in addition to sea salt and honey on top of vanilla gelato) but as many other reviews have mentioned, it works. The saltiness and sweetness blend together perfectly. 

Overall, is Lilia worth a visit? Definitely. I wouldn't call it the kind of place I'd /regularly/ go to but it's certainly worth checking out.

We ordered almost every pasta in on the menu, absolutely delicious! We also ordered steak, potatoes (with a ton of cheese on top- amazing), grilled clams, and Cacio e Pepe fritelle. I can't complain about a single item that we tried. I would highly recommend a visit to Lilia!

This place has a lot of hype so I had big expectations going in. All the dishes we ordered were very very good but lacking the wow factor.  Definitely would recommend trying the place though. Service was phenomenal, my favorite dish of the night was actually dessert. Italian job ice cream ... that one did make me say wow this is unbelievable so they get five stars :)

This is the kind of restaurant that when your manhattan friends learn you're moving to Williamsburg, they say "ooh we have to go Lilia!"

After going there, I totally get why. 

It's in a bright airy space in a quiet part of Williamsburg. They could have crammed a lot more seating in, but they didn't which I really appreciate because it feels like they are trying to maximize your experience rather than their headcount. 

The service is fantastic, I came with a girlfriend and it felt like at least four people helped us - but not in an overbearing kind of way.
