I was committed to going but was a little nervous because it's one of those restaurants that doesn't post the prices on its online menu. I was pleasantly surprised! We got two appetizers, two entrees, two drinks and a dessert to share and the bill came (pre-tip) to about $120.

The only "knock" on the service I would say is that our waitress made it seem as though we should be ordering more because of portion size, but in our opinion the portions were totally normal (you definitely don't need two to three mains per person!).

I got a pesto gnocchi. The pesto was delicious, very fresh. The gnocchi is ricotta gnocchi rather than potato, which gives it a lighter feeling. 

Definitely get the homemade mozzarella - I was a little hesitant about the fish roe on top, but it was delicious.

The only thing that was mildly disappointing was the dessert. We got the chocolate cake, which was absolutely fine but when I go again I'll get a second glass of wine instead!

Overall it's a definite repeat, though I'll have to plan in advance because they book up fast!

This place was a standout.

I don't usually like pasta but the food was a standout. We had a variety of dishes - caccio e pepe, butter beans, and Italian broccoli were exceptional. My sister had been there previously and she suggested avoiding the fish. I found the angolotti a bit too sweet or saffrony, not sure, but it was a bit odd to me.

Service was top notch. Attentive and mixed up a beer choice once but quickly made it right. Very friendly but didn't get in your way. Did a great job of steering us to some dishes and the right count for a table of 6. 

For a restaurant in Brooklyn, I greatly appreciated having a bit of space in the restaurant- great layout and not claustrophobic or falling over other guests.

Love love love everything about this place. Food was delicious! Veggies to die for. Went with 3 other people. We got 4 antipasti and 4 primi (pastas) everything was so delicious. Beautiful place to go for a romantic date or a nice drink after work by the bar. Service was amazing as well. Wanted a drink that was refreshing like a taste of summer and the waitress had the bar make me a drink off the menu. It was exactly what I wanted. Would definitely go back

My favorite restaurant in NYC, a close second to their sister restaurant Misi. You can not go wrong with anything on the menu, but I recommend starting with the Bianca cocktails and fresh burratta. I love the trumpet mushroom appetizer in addition to the broccoli and cauliflower (veggies never tasted so good!!) we usually order 4-5 pastas to share family style on the table - it's homemade daily and you can taste the gloriousness of that freshness. Whatever you do order the sheep's milk agnolotti. My mouth is watering just typing that....if you have room for desert enjoy the olive oil cake and homemade gelato.

Did it live up to the hype? Welp I'd say menz a menz.. the pasta is absolutely homemade goodness and incredibly well done. However the sauces just too much. Too many opposing flavors competing against one another. Also- asked the waiter if I could have the mozz app sans fish eggs because my husband is allergic and I was told no because the roe is the salt component of this dish.... FAIL 10% tip for u bud!

I have traveled through the midwest and live in Maryland. I often wonder how blissfully satiated people become only smelling the roses in  their stagnant environment; never leaving their borough or region. This Michelin Star restaurant had Great table Service, back bar service very slow, but the food? 

Focaccia bread with pesto butter-this was triple deli. Soft almost melt in mouth with tasty spread (almost eat by itself)

Fettuccine with lamb sausage-good flavor with the sausage, but the noodles were far too firm for my taste (Like Hamburger Helper-ish)

Goat cheese algonotti--Perfection! 
The thin pasta was scrumptious, and the goat cheese creamy greatness; would have been fantastic if i didn't have to send it back for having a single (one) roasted tomato-shocking when reviews abound show 5-6 of them!  

Veal-this was Carpaccio-like sliced with onions, dill, and mint-also quite delicious, but paled in comparison to the similarly priced quite large lamb shank option-which my son claims is absolutely delicious; but I insisted change upon him ;) as I do you!

No desert thank you. 

Nice memory with my son, but at $175 for 2 people would I return?....Next please! 

As someone else said, there are comparable fine dining options in the local area; for those so restrained and limited.

Second time here. Not nearly as good and quite disappointing. The fritters were not light and airy as the first time. They were dense and heavy. The garlic bread with mozzarella was delicious however. More so the bread, than the cheese. That was the highlight of the meal...good bread. The clams were good and my husband enjoyed the scallops (all 3 of them). Big disappointment in the pasta. The agnolotti was creamy and light. Continues to be the choice pasta. But the rigatoni diavola sucked. The pasta was too al dente and thick, with a sauce that did not do the pasta any justice. It was too thin and tasteless. Yeah, it had a hint of spice, but that's about it. Quite dry. Are they trying to duplicate Carbone's spicy rigatoni perhaps?? Back to the drawing board if they are. Dinner was so lackluster that we skipped dessert. Couldn't deal with another disappointment. Lilia, what happened?

I don't understand why this place is so highly rated, it's overhyped.  The service is garbage, and the food is mediocre at best.  I have been here before and it wasn't great, but I live around the corner and it is a late-night spot that has a dog friendly patio.  We got there just after a rain storm so I figured it was the perfect time to avoid the line, and I was informed VERY rudely by the host(esses) that they would seat me in an hour because of the rain.  I saw employees outside cleaning off the tables and I told them that I just wanted to grab a quick bite and rain doesn't scare me away, and if they wanted they could bring my check with the food- but I was treated so rudely that I will never come back to this overpriced place that thinks it's amazing.  Save yourself some money and go to a real italian place.

This place cannot be described. A line out the door before it even opens up should tell you everything right there. 

My boyfriend and I traveled up to NYC from Virginia - we've waited almost two years to finally try this and it did not disappoint. The richness of the food made everything so filling. I love sitting at the bar and being able to observe them cooking As well as being able to interact with the bartender. Highly recommended to anyone visiting the area.

I want to start with the service that was pretty good and professional about the food what can I say nothing special I wasn't impressed from the apps and especially from the pasta dishes there is better italian restaurant in nyc !

Amazing food and love the vibe - so cozy and casual.  The ricotta gnocchi in broccoli pesto with crushed pistachio nuts may be the best pasta ever!  Another must have is the cacio e pepe fritelle.  Hard to score a reservation but well worth the month wait!!

28 minute wait for a cocktail, but my date got his right away (same drink ordered).  Not even kidding. 28 minutes for an Aperol Spritz. 

This was the second time visiting this overhyped establishment. And no joke, from the time my friend and I ordered our drinks, he got his right away and I got mine TWENTY-EIGHT minutes later. I even pointed this out. They didn't care. 

We proceeded to order pescatarian/vegetarian items from the menu. All were fine, if you like all of your food covered in salt. I do love salt, so I enjoyed it but it was bordering on too salty, even for me. 

As nice as they were, after I waited TWENTY-EIGHT minutes for my first drink, they don't even bother to take it off the bill. 

This was my second bad experience at this place and I will NOT go back. I don't understand why anyone is waiting in line for this place when you have Aurora, Naked Dog or La Fanfare with actual good food and good service nearby.
Very good, however, i think the sister restaurant MISI has better food. the wine list here is large and has a great variety

i've literally been seeing pictures of the mafaldini for years on instagram, and i finally got to come and try it!! we ordered 3 pastas and two of the starters, both starters were amazing, and the chicken liver crostini is something i'd definitely say is a must have. clams were maybe skippable. out of the three pastas we ordered, it actually turned out that we liked the mafaldini the least (still great) but the real stars were the tortellini and sheeps milk pasta. sooooooooo goooooood. also we had an olive oil cake at the end and that was sOoooooooOOoo goood. i ended up taking home some of the mafaldini and olive oil cake and they were both still so great the next day. glad i finally got to try this restaurant and glad that it lived up to the hype!!!

I live around the corner and have admired the buzz about Lilia. I finally got a seat at the bar. Service is efficient, but not friendly. Our bartender was terse, bordering on rude. I wanted to know a bit about the Italian wines on the menu, but was given harsh retorts. I understand that it's a busy atmosphere, but I enjoy feeling hosted by the restaurant I'm patronizing. At Lilia, I felt expected to bend to their expectations, which is: know what you want, order it all at once, and don't keep menus on the bar (I was a little confused why I couldn't keep the beverage menu with me and was wondering if this was a matter of aesthetics or the bartender needed to have control over every little thing). This is the only time I've felt compelled to leave a negative review at a restaurant. But with the service being what it is, I'm having a hard time thinking I would return to dine on their delicious pasta. I ask, is it worth it?

Great ambience, service, and generally fantastic food and drink at appropriate prices... just not up to the hype. My main criticism is that the majority of dishes, particularly the apps and fish, were way too salty. I would definitely go again though for a couple dishes in particular - the agnoloti pasta and the italian job dessert were unreal. 

Would definitely come again and enjoy however i wouldn't wait hours for it or slave to book a reservation

Wowww! This has got to be one of the best Italian restaurants I have ever eaten in. Everything was absolutely delicious!! We started of with the fresh mozz appetizer. It was on top of a fresh garlic bread. We also had some snow peas which were amazing. For our main dish we had the sheeps milk agnolotti! This was the best pasta dish that I have ever had!! We also had the special rib eye steak which was better then any steak house that I have ever been too! For desert we had the special olive oil vanilla gelato, which was very interesting. Our waiter David , did an amazing job explaining everything and helping us choose our dishes and drinks! Overall, my husband and I had an amazing dining experience!!

Had a better experience my second time coming here. Three friends and I shared the prosciutto dish, cauliflower and off-menu bread with pesto butter to start, all of which were amazing. We then split the mafaldini, aglonotti, gnocchi and spaghetti, the latter of which is now my second favorite after the mafaldini. For dessert, we had the off-menu "Italian job" which is vanilla soft serve with olive oil, a rhubarb tart thing and the chocolate soft serve with all of the toppings. Definitely some of the best pasta in NYC.

Edit 6/2019: Got a reservation for 6:30 on a weeknight (thank you, Resy alert) for 4. I had the Milano sour cocktail, which was great, and we all shared:

+ Toasted focaccia with ramps and ramp butter 
+ Gem lettuce
+ Mushrooms 
+ Spaghetti
+ Mafaldini
+ Tortelli
+ sheeps milk agnolotti 
+ Strawberry crostata
+ Chocolate gelato 

Would give this place 5 thousand stars if I could. Lilia continues to be my bar for pasta in NYC and I will return as often as I can for the rest of time.

I just don't get the hype. Maybe it's because they are located in  Brooklyn that generates the buzz, but this restaurant just does not deserve the adulation it has been getting. I have been there two times now and the food is just not that impressive. 
More precisely, it is incredibly inconsistent. The kitchen can, on one hand, roll out an appetizer that is new and heavenly like their blowfish tails and then simultaneously deliver a cold hard mozzarella appetizer unworthy of the effort to try and cut into it. 
Their entrees follow in line. Some of the fish dishes were excellent but a rigatoni dish was inedible. I scanned the other tables and noted a number of the rigatoni dishes pushed to the side. This is unacceptable for a purported fine restaurant. A comment to the waiter that perhaps the dish be removed from the menu was met with a shrug. 
I feel the same.

Not worth the hype and all the wait in line. Food is good, but doesn't meet the high expectations of someone that waited almost 2 hours in line. We seated in the bar and felt that the whole experience was a little rushed.

Went to dinner here this past Saturday night. The place is very popular and small so you def need a reservation well in advance. They were very crowded the night we went so we had to wait a while past our reservation time. The food was delicious! We ordered a few appetizers- one was basically fried cheese balls which were amazing! They make all of their pasta noodles fresh so would recommend ordering off the pasta menu. We ordered gelato for dessert which was also delicious. Overall great evening and great dinner!

I can't even begin to tell you how amazing this meal was!
If you don't make reservations (like us), be prepared to stand in line BEFORE Lilia opens if you want to snag a table without a further wait. We got there around 4:30pm and there were already a few people ahead of us.. but we just waited 30 mins for them to open, and we were seated right away.

To begin with, I'm not a huge fan of Italian food because it's usually heavier and I haven't found great pasta dishes. BUT LET ME TELL YOU. Lilia will blow your mind.
All their dishes are pretty small, so you can order a few to share. We had such a hard time deciding because there were so many we wanted to try, but only two of us!!

We ended up getting and ENJOYING:
- Grilled clams: buttery, tangy from the tomato sauce, and nicely cooked. Did not feel rubbery at all
- Roasted trumpet mushrooms: a nice light dish with roasted mushrooms on the bottom and covered with arugula and a light vinaigrette on top. Could've passed on this
- Little gem lettuce: perfect salad to prepare for your main entrees! but it was a litttttle heavy on the dressing
- Mafaldini: MUST TRY at least once, because no other restaurant serves this.  BUT I do think once is enough just because they have so many pastas.. I'd want to try something different next time. Creamy/buttery with an interesting taste from the pink peppercorn.
- Linguini: I was hesitant to get this because it sounded so simple.. but the sauce was so FRESH and a total SPRING season pasta! I really enjoyed this and was a good complement to the heavier mafaldini
- Italian Job: last but not least, DESSERT. Vanilla gelato with honey, olive oil, fennel powder. a savory dessert was the perfect end to our meal.

I can't wait to come back to Lilia and check out their sister restaurant Misi
Highly recommend . Everything from the service, ambiance, and food was 5/5

Was in NYC for a quick trip and was able to score a table at Lilia through a customer of mine...Friend m start to finish one of the best meals I've had in a very long time...We ate way too much but everything was too good to leave even a single bite on the plate...We started with a lovely bottle of white that the sommelier recommended, and than had the cacio e pepe fritalle. Delicate fried balls filled with fresh cheese and black pepper = heaven. Than the butter beans w/fava and a gem salad  both delicious  We shared the tortelli with ramps and the mafaldini pastas and both were scrumptious. We also shared the lamb shank which was tender and delicious  We ended with the olive oil cake but the real stand out for me was the gelato with olive oil and honey...seriously was tempted to lick the glass  Our server was as super sweet and helpful, and the sommellier was knowledgeable and attentive. Great atmosphere and the food was perfect  You won't be disappointed

The food is good but it wasn't memorable or that much better than other good Italian restaurants nearby. I don't understand the hype and why this place chooses to be pretentious and act like they don't have tables. I've walked in when the place was empty and they said they'll only seat people with reservations.
Amazing atmosphere and a true gem in Brooklyn

I have eaten here once and while it's solid contemporary Italian food, I truly don't understand what makes it more hype-worthy than the many very similar restaurants in New York City--many of them at a slightly lower price point, and friendlier. 

I am dropping in here to report that I tried to call about large party accommodation, albeit at the last minute, on two occasions. It was my fault that I didn't plan far enough in advance, but while other high-caliber New York restaurants (union square cafe, diner, Oxomoco) worked with me to make this possible (or were at least nice when they understandably couldn't do it) the staff at Lilia was openly mean and condescending about how I had not inquired through the proper medium and essentially told me how insane it was for me to even try. I don't know, just something to work on since I don't think the nice-enough Italian food is worth the arrogance and  hostility! Thanks for reading!!

One of the best in Brooklyn for good reason. Even if you can't get a reservation, on a nice night, you can wait online before they open for outdoor unreserved seats. The lemon-garlic chicken is a favorite, even over the pasta most nights. Just so perfect. Don't sleep on the soft serve either or daytime cafe sandwiches.
Amazing, obviously. So good and good price considering reputation and nyc expectations. Impossible to get reservations, so good luck!

Lilia is definitely not a place to spend your time and money if you like good italian food. The overall experience was very disappointing, due to poor service with a lot of attitude and no attention to details (table not set properly, tap water not filtered, etc). Going back to the food, the appetizers were not tasty and the attempt to make it interesting/spicy fell flat: Specifically the grilled clams tasted like they were frozen rather than fresh - rubbery and inert. Then, the pastas...we ordered 4 different pastas: The sheepsmilk agnolotti was the only bright spot, while the rest was very average.  You know the pasta you make after a long day at work and you have no inspiration for cooking. So bottom line is Lilia is certainly well located and the decor is pleasant (the one star of this review), but the food is terribly overhyped and not worth he wait.

Without a doubt, a 5 star meal. Was unable to secure a highly demanded reservation at this Missy Robbins jewel prior to my trip to NYC. Believe me, I tried a month in advance and securing a resy at a reasonable hour can be tough. 

Showed up at 430pm and waited in a 10 person line at the time. By 5pm, the line must have been about 50-60 people deep. This was on a Sunday. 

Me and my party (3 of us total) were able to secure some
spots at the bar as soon as the restaurant opened. 

Going straight for the food. I probably could spend an hour describing all of the dishes and how perfect they were. I want to let the photos describe the experience because it was absolutely superb. 

We ordered and shared: 

Appetizers: 

Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga

Focaccia bread. I can't remember the butter spread but it was sooooo delicious 

Pastas: 

Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey (BEST PASTA DISH IVE EVER HAD)

Rigatoni Diavola, San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano, Pecorino

Meats: 

Grilled Chicken Thigh and Leg, Fingerling Potatoes, Grilled Lemon, Garlic 

We also were able to try the rib eye that they had on special, cooked to a perfect medium rare. The couple next to us graciously traded us some for some bites of one of our pasta and chicken dish. 

Desserts: 

Olive Oil cake

Soft serve. 100% get the vanilla with the fennel pollen and olive oil. Amazing!

I honestly think about this dining experience all the time...lol

Loved Lilia. Even though I had to make a reservation one month in advance, it was worth the wait. The pastas are fresh, light and full of flavor. Favorite was the olive focaccia which was a special that night. Leave room for some gelato

Let me start by saying, I was beyond excited to get an Italian dish from this restaurant. For months, I saw reviews on Instagram. I saw all the gorgeous pictures with so many people commenting and expressing their deep contentment with the cuisine here. I was thrilled to finally get a day off to go; I was craving a great Italian dish as well. However, that bright sunny day ended in gloom. The "focaccia" was decent tasting but it was not real focaccia. The bread came with a green butter that made my stomach feel uneasy after a while. I wasn't concerned with that though. I knew the pasta would be amazing. To my dismay, the first bite of pasta abruptly turned my smile completely upside down. It was a complete disappointment. I was in complete shock. The pasta was 100% unpleasant and awful. It was so bland and had no taste. It was so unenjoyable that I could not even finish eating it. It was like torture putting that pasta in my mouth to swallow. I left that day feeling such sorrow and woe. My experience was so anti-climatic. All the build up of excitement just turned into a complete debacle. . I would never EVER recommend this restaurant to anyone. The cuisine here is not good at all. This was by far the worst Italian food or pasta I have ever had in my life. Please do yourself a favor and do not even bother going here. It's not worth the letdown, despair, stomach pain, or regret after.

We made a reservations weeks ago and when we got there they told us they didn't have our reservations. Then as the waitress goes to pour the waters I noticed my glass had something on it so I wiped it and instead of her getting me a new glass, she asked is something wrong with your glass? I wanted to respond what do you think if I'm taking the napkin and trying to clean the inside of it , but I just smiled at her... she continued to pour the water. Then she never brought our appetizer but remembered to bring it after we were almost done with our tiny portion entrees. I really don't know what the hype is about this place ... the food is good but the portions are very small, the service isn't that good or at least that night and they list our reservation. If they redeemed themselves by giving us the late appetizer for free I would of gave them 3 stars but that didn't happen.

Lilia is absolutely my favorite restaurant in New York! The food is great, the atmosphere is lovely, and the service is generally excellent. 

I went last night (not my first time going) and had a good time. The only negative experience of the entire night was my interaction with the hostess, who seemed to be weirdly frustrated with me for no apparent reason. I had come at 5:30 to try to get a table right as they opened, but my boyfriend wasn't there yet. She told me I couldn't be seated until the rest of my party arrived, which I was totally fine with, but when I asked if there was a place I should wait she just stared at me blankly. When I returned with my boyfriend, she was helping other customers, so we waited until she was done, and then I said "we're back!" She very quickly shut me down and snapped that she was busy. This experience was confusing, because I was trying to be friendly and I understand that at a place like Lilia, there is bound to be a wait, but she seemed aggressive for no reason. 

Anyways, after we were seated, the rest of our night was awesome. We started with cocktails -- the G&T and Negroni were both stellar. They tasted fresh and interesting. Even the potato chips they served as bar snacks were delicious (they have fennel on them!). We got the ramp focaccia with ramp butter and ramp tortelli (we really leaned into ramp season). Both were INCREDIBLE. The food here always tastes so fresh and flavorful. It's legitimately pasta made with passion. I've also tried the mafaldini, agnolotti, and the clams, all of which have been insanely delicious. I couldn't recommend the agnolotti more, I think it's the most interesting and beautiful pasta dish I've ever had. The mafaldini is fun to eat and the pasta is perfectly chewy. The only thing on the menu that I find kind of disappointing is the cacio e Pepe fritelle, but I think that's more on me for not loving fried food. 

Also, the atmosphere and service of the restaurant are generally spectacular. Our bartender was super nice and other than the hostess from last night, I have never had a negative service experience at Lilia. I love how the restaurant is always humming with energy and filled with beautiful light. It's truly my favorite spot in NYC.

I feel very passionate about Lilia. Even before I was able to actually dine at Lilia I felt passionate about Lilia. What does this mean? I have been wanting to go to Lilia for upwards of a year now. I finally buckled down and ventured to Brooklyn with friends to dine at this charming establishment. You know when you have high expectations for a restaurant because you've read countless reviews and then you get there and everything is just "meh"? Lilia isn't like that. Lilia is genuinely great. Everything from the service to the atmosphere to the food is great. I'm going to do something I rarely do and write an individual review for each item we ate.

Cacio E Pepe Fritelle - I don't love deep fried food, its a personal thing and I'm sorry, I know this is controversial. Non-the-less, I loved this. This is the perfect hybrid of a doughnut and one of my favorite pasta dishes, Cacio E Pepe. It has the texture of a dutch pancake and the flavor of the perfect blend of cheese, butter and pepper. Its wonderful.

Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga - I loved this so much I ordered it again when the waiter came back around. 

I'm going to preface by saying I don't think you NEED anything from the Antipasti menu. You'll like everything you eat, but I think we can all agree when eating at a restaurant like Lilia, your energy and stomach space should be reserved for carbs. 

Sugar Snap Peas - Tasty, light, and refreshing 

Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs - Yes. 

Little Gem Lettuce - if you insist on eating a vegetable, this is a very good salad and I would recommend it.

Cured Sardines, Capers, Dill, Fettunta - Not necessarily a crowd pleaser but I personally enjoyed this very much. If you are not a fish fanatic, do not order this. I thought it was one of the most beautiful things we ate, I was alone in that opinion. 

Bagna Cauda, Spring Vegetables, Warm Anchovy and Garlic - This might have been the biggest waste of stomach space and energy. Skip it 

Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano - If you do not order this I will judge you. You have done Lilia wrong and the pasta gods are looking down on you disappointed.  

Tortelli, Ramps, Prosciutto, Parmigiano, Mint - This was my favorite thing we ordered. Each Tortelli is made with love and it shows. Biting into these was honestly a special experience that I cherished.

Rigatoni Diavola, San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano, Pecorino - These are the tomato sauce pasta you have been waiting for. 

Black Bass, Salsa Verde, Coal Roasted Yukon Gold Potatoes - Delicious, this came second to last. I don't think we needed it but I don't regret ordering it. 

THE OLIVE OIL CAKE - HOLY YUM. If you do not finish your meal with this cake, you are doing it wrong.

This was the best experience in Williamsburg so far. 
We really don't go out in Williamsburg really often but this place was worth it. 
Delicious pasta with red peppercorn and well cooked clams. Perfectly cooked if I may say so. 
A really nice thing is that you don't have to wait outside if you arrive earlier. They have a hidden bar to wait for your table. 
Even tho that experience was perfect I still do not understand why? and again WHY is the wait list a month? Provide at least one walk-in day a week.
Overall, not bad at all

Every year we visit the Brooklyn area for great food and drink spots. There were so many good reviews about this place we marked off our calendar alert 30 days in advance to make sure we got a dinner reservation. With only about 2 second after midnight we could only manage a 9:30 seating. How could that be? We figured it was so incredible it would be worth the late dinner. When we arrived with our party at 9:30 we waited in a dark cramped bar area until our table was ready. We only waited about 10 minutes so it wasn't a big deal. The atmosphere was cool and the open kitchen was nice to see.  The appetizers were ok. The blowfish tails could have been cooked a little more under the wood fire grill to make them a little crispy and to make the cartilage more palatable. The scallops and walnut yogurt was great as were the 2 salads we ordered. So far so good.  Unfortunately 3 out of 4 pasta dishes we overly salty and one was inedible. Something about using sea water to cook the pasta in? Might have been the Dead Sea?
We had a good bottle of wine and the desserts were excellent. I think we just came on an off night and would probably try again. No real complaints on the service.  I can't imagine this is how it usually is. My recommendation would be to lay off on the salt concept and bring a nice grated cheese and pepper to the table and let us choose our desired levels of added salt.

My friend and I started off with the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle and Roasted Trumpet Mushrooms. The Cacio is very rich and cheesy. I realized it ate perfectly with the mushrooms as it toned down intense cheesiness. 

For entrees we decided on the Malfaldini and the Fettuccine with spicy lamb sausage.  Our favorite was def the fettuccine.  Fill transparency, I had a terrible meal with pink peppercorns like a week or 2 prior. That flavor trauma didn't set me up to really enjoy the Malfaldini since that is one of the main flavors in this. 
I wish we went for the agnolotti instead. 

Also note they do not do substitutions or additions that don't come with an item. I wanted whip cream on the side with the chocolate cake and got a "No" so solid, I thought server was joking lol. He was not; also suggested to get the olive oil cake since thats the only thing it came with.  Kinda sad but the taste of the cake made up for that.

Id love to come back to try other items on the menu. It's pretty hard it is to secure a reservation.

*This is a review of their caffé.

The Overview: 4.1/5 

Amazing coffee, pastries and paninis. All flavors are well-balanced, taste fresh and nothing is ever too sweet. The space is small, so it can get crowded (especially on weekends), so if you're looking for a quiet coffee shop, this probably isn't the place for you. Try to get there well before 4pm if you want a panini or more than a plain coffee to avoid angering the baristas. Prices may seem a little out-of-budget for some, but it's well-worth trying at least once. Would absolutely recommend. The Breakdown Below...

The Food: 5/5

1. Almond Milk Latte, $4.50 - A nice balance of well-done espresso and almond milk. Would recommend.
2. Bomboloni, Tiramisu-style, $4.50 - Light and fluffy Italian pastry reminiscent of a doughnut with a spiced cream filling and topped with a dusting of bitter chocolate. It's has a really nice balance of flavors. I love that it's only slightly sweet. I loved pairing it with my almond milk latte, but would also be really great with a clean shot of espresso. Would recommend.
3. Burrata Panini with Chilies and Basil $14 - Good god, this is the most perfect sandwich. It's so simple, yet so mind-blowing. Again, a perfect balance of toasted bread, soft and gooey burrata (rumored to be made in-house), sea salt, basil and a chili spread. I could eat this sandwich daily. Would absolutely recommend. 


The Service: 3.5/5

The service is always a little hit or miss in the caffé. If you come a little too close to closing time (4pm), you'll most likely be met with slight passive aggressive hostility, especially if you're looking to order a panini or anything but  a plain coffee. Also, they will not accommodate any changes to the coffee menu aside from milk alternatives (I've been present when a barista has denied a customer request to add chocolate to a latte), but they know what they're doing and concoct amazing drinks, so mix-and-match concoctions aren't needed. Service is reasonably fast, but if it's crowded, there will be a little bit of a wait, which is well worth it. The caffé recently stopped providing loyalty cards for an unknown and unannounced reason. I wish those would come back, as it was a nice incentive for the regulars.


The Ambiance: 4/5

Small, cute and casual. Inside, there's a high bar table top facing the window. If you need to stretch out a little more, there are a few round tables. Both are great for people watching while you sip on your coffee. 


The Price: 4/5

The prices for the coffee, pastries and paninis may be a little high for some, but their food and drinks fresh, perfectly balanced flavors are well worth the price.

I finally got to snag a reservation, right in time for my birthday. I went in with high hopes. We started off with the Sicilian olives and right away I knew I was in for a good meal. They were covered in chilies and garlic and were amazing. Also be sure to get the focaccia, ours was topped with ramps and came with ramp butter and OH MY GOSH SO GOOD. Then came the pastas. We had to get the sheep's milk agnolotti- the cheese was light and the sauce was sweet and perfect. The pink peppercorn Mafaldini was a little peppery, but in the best way. The spicy rigatoni was indeed super spicy, but holy wow it was yummy. For dessert, we ordered the Olive Oil Cake with blood oranges- very yummy. Also got the Italian Job- Soft Serve Vanilla Gelato with honey, olive oil, sea salt, and fennel. It sounds super weird but it was somehow incredible. I hope I get to go back sometime soon (also shoutout to our lovely waitress).
I was seated at the bar because i was a walkin with no reservation. We were greeted and served with hospitality. The food was very good. Highly recommendable and will return.

Waited so long to try this place and couldn't have been more disappointed.  The cacio app was dry. All 4 pastas were dry, overcooked and salty.  After visiting many of the top Italian restaurants in the city, I honestly can't believe people still want to come to this place.  Probably my least favorite restaurant in NYC.

I had no idea this place was as popular as it is. My friend and I were just walking and came upon this place and it looked good so we stepped in. They had a 4 hour wait for a table inside but allowed us to sit outside immediately. it was a solid 40 degrees outside but we still decided to do it because we were soooo hungry. The staff at Lilia's was so nice, they gave everyone sitting outside thick blankets to bare the cold. 

We ordered the roasted cauliflower appetizer, ricotta gnocci, and lamb sausage fettuccine. 

The service was fast, the food was delicious, and we really enjoyed our time. I would definitely put in a reservation weeks in advance to dine here again!

Lilia definitely lived up to expectations! My aunt and I had a rez for 5:45 pm on a Sunday evening. We got there 20 min and they sat us right away. For apps we ordered the focaccia with ramp butter and the cauliflower soppressata. Both were AMAZING. For entrees we got the sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti and the lemon chicken. While the pasta was pretty it was a little off - the cheese reminded me of ricotta and the honey made it a wee bit too sweet. The chicken on the other hand was to die for. How was the skin so crispy and the meat so tender?? For dessert we got the vanilla gelato with all of the toppings and it was great. Definitely recommend!!!!

Was so excited to go but very unimpressed
Food was not hot.  Some things were good - we ordered a pretty good variety.  Felt as if the pretentiousness was more important to convey than service.   I understand that the kitchen can't accommodate every dietary request but we asked for - dressing on the side - and no whipped creme in our desert - not big asks.  We were told they would "have to see" and the speech about "the integrity of the meal".  Seriously? Dressing oil and vinegar instead of what they put on? 
Don't need to go again

I wanted to go here because a review stated that the only way you're doing Lilia wrong is not going enough. We couldn't get reservations. So we got there 45 mins before they opened.  My bf and I got the escarole (vegetable), blowfish tails, veal, squash ravioli, mafaldini. The escarole was very salty but good texture, hard to break apart in pieces. The blowfish tails had bone in them and were whatever. The veal was pretty chewy and I was expecting them to be more tender. The mafaldini is crazy popular and has great texture, but slightly too salty. The squash ravioli was SO FREAKING GOOD. I should ordered another one. This dish is the only reason I'd come back. think this place is overrrated. Great service though. The day we went, they only took 13 groups without reservations.

I discovered Lilia shortly after it opened, and I visit whenever time permits. I like everything about this place. the food is excellent, the servers are polite and solicitous, and the room is bright and airy. If you go try the pasta's, everyone that I've tasted was delicious. Clam's and Sardine's are equally impressive. If you go reserve well in advance, and hire an Uber to drive you there. Parking in this section of Williamsburg is very difficult.

70/100

I'm trying to implement a rating system for myself so I can explain why I round down or up a star in accordance to my 100 rating - so.... my experience was fine.

The food was okay, there are some great dishes and some not so great dishes. But when you have a James Beard award/national recognition, I don't think I should be settling for a like, 60% accuracy. Also, this place is unfortunately... kind of soulless? I suppose this is what happens to a lot of restaurants that are part of restaurant groups, but still, it's kind of sad to see this very hype, very beautiful place become only okay after some time. 

for 2:
Chicken Liver Crostini - good texture with very nice richness but extremely salty (though honestly it was quite good with a lot of wine)
Bagna Cauda - incredible! a little heavy on the fennel (but it works) and I would've loved to see a bit more of the other veggies but on god this was so delicious 

Grilled Scallops - honestly fine, the scallops were too salty and felt like kind of an imbalanced dish to me
Grilled Blowfish Tails - also delicious, this was like, perfectly cooked and all the flavors that needed to be there were there. *kisses fingers*

Rigatoni Diavola - pretty good? but emphasis on pretty...so like, it was a bit better than fine
Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti - killer! this dish is so great
Linguine Anchovy, Corbari Tomatoes, Lemon - this was really good! it's reminiscent of something I'd make at home but like, Lilia. 

Wines were great, I wish I remembered what wines we had but it's been too long, we had glasses of mainly whites and they all paired very well with the seafood heavy meal. 

I wish I could put half stars because it's at least a 3.5 but not really a 4 for me; I would come back here and give it another shot but I was kind of disappointed unfortunately. I decided to give it a few months before publishing this review and fortunately my heart has softened but unfortunately my palate has not.

Need to give this 3 stars because of how very underwhelmed I was compared to all of the hype that exists around Lilia. Yes, good Italian place. BUT not good enough for there to be a line at the door at 4:50pm....... I guess I was expecting cream of the crop and that is definitely not what I got. Would come back if a friend happened to get a reservation but wouldn't trek there and wait for a table. 

Best appetizers:
1. Grilled clams - yum yum yum
2. Their focaccia special with ramp butter - so fresh and yummy !

Best pasta:
1. Spaghetti with lemon parm and pine nuts - I think this pasta was for sure the best dish.


The rest:
Malfadini- very pretty pasta. Agreed. But the flavors were kind of whatever nothing sooo special. 
Rigatoni- very basic. My first couple bites the pasta were undercooked. You can tell from biting into it and can see the inside of the noodle hadn't been fully cooked.
Agnolotti- good but good for one bite. Slightly too sweet for me. Couldn't eat a whole dish of this.
None of these 3 pasta dishes were stand out dishes by any means.

Lilia lives up to the hype. My partner took me here on a Friday night. There was a line that wrapped around the block even though it was raining out. I've wanted to check out a Missy Robins's restaurant ever since I listened to her podcast on Bon Apetit. I had high expectations and they were met. 

The restaurant is a lot larger than I pictured. It's clean and modern. I loved the open kitchen format. It's nice to see the chefs cooking and see where your food is being prepared. 

We started with radishes over ricotta, clams, and butter beans. The butter beans were my favorite appetizer - they throw a healthy amount of fresh basil on top which was delicious. 

Let's get to the pastas. We ordered their two most featured on Instagram. The agnolotti and the mafaldine. Wow! Loved both, think I liked the agnolotti because of the rich saffron taste and the sweetness of the honey. I usually don't like stuffed pasta but this was phenomenal. The madaldine's texture was so good. 

They have a nice wine list and the bartenders make a mean cocktail. We ordered a few drinks that paired really well with our meal. Definitely will come back and will also have to check out Misi.

I have no idea what all the hype is here.
Service terrible and slow.  Waitress couldn't be bothered to acknowledge our table.  
Food is wildly average, my guess (and hope) is we caught them on a bad night.  Unless like so many other businesses they buy these positive reviews to create hype.
I will definitely be back bc the place has nice style and feel.  Desperately wanted to like it more.

Average Place- overpriced with ok service
We celebrated my wife birthday, it was during the week around 6 pm. We order one Artichoke which was nothing special $18, a bit of cauliflower for $16 - none of them were organic. Lam steak was great size and well priced that is where they deserve a star. The homemade spaghetti were ok nothing spacial. Desert chocolate cake dry almost no flavor. I had a black bass which was a bit of potato and tiny bit of bass for $30 small plate - rip off. Our server M. B. start ok but them it go just dry not friendly, we ask three times for desert menu people passing around us until it took her almost 10 min to deliver it herself - not sure why. At the end when she deliver the check she finally said Happy Birthday. Toilet garbage cans were overflowing with paper and etc. I don't recommend this place

Ugh I love it here. Every dish is better than the next. 

Annoyingly difficult to get a reservation and I had to get in touch with the Maitre D weeks in advance to get a table. 

That aside, it really is worth the wait. Lilias pastas are perfectly balanced, incredibly creative, and just overall delicious. We ordered five pastas for three people because we just couldn't choose :) (plus pasta makes for great leftovers!) 

They also put a pretty lovely spin on vegetables. Their baked artichoke is probably the single best vegetable I've ever eaten. 

Worth the trip to Brooklyn and work the wait if you can snag a resy!

Excellent dishes.  My favorite is the agnolotti with safrron and honey. I'm not a big fan of veal, but a friend of mine ordered it and I tried it- it is absolutely delicious. Everything tastes exceptionally fresh. Highly recommend.

Overrated. Small plates very expensive. Waitress was a brat. Food was just ok not worth the price. Cute atmosphere but that's all. Will not be coming back here. Did not enjoy it enough for the amount of $$ spent.

We loooove this place. Every dish was amazing. Great presentation. Fresh ingredients aThey are all well seasoned. 

Only down side for this place is that they are all booked for few month despite the fact it's in Brooklyn. Only way to get a table is to walk in there early in the evening.
Very good pasta, but they very much have a "cooler than you" attitude here, and are one of those places that refuses to make changes to any of their dishes, no matter the circumstances.

In my thousands of restaurant experiences over the decades I've witnessed less than ten perfect meals. This rare phenomenon is so few and far between that when it does happen it catches you by total surprise.

My first perfect meal was at the French Laundry in Yountville, CA over 15 years ago. My last perfect meal was Pujol in Mexico City about 2 years ago; then came Lilia last night!

When you set foot into Lilia, you catch a positive vibe that something special is going to happen, and believe me it does.

We get ushered to the very back of this restaurant to a stark bar type waiting room as our table was not quite ready. There we we're served some outstanding gin Martini's. 
The hostess comes back and fetches us after a few minutes and now was when the real magic starts to happen.

The superbly trained staff immediately sweeps you up into their vortex of how a patron of their restaurant should be treated. This attention bids well for what's ahead.

The menu is so well constructed with so many diverse items in which to choose from it's almost impossible not to put together a cohesive and well thought out dinner.

We had on this night:
*Mozzarella Toast with mozzarella cheese that was so fresh it had to be made minutes before serving. This was such a treat, I could have gone home at this point and I would have been happy
*Chicken Liver Crostini - Now we're talking my peeps food, the only exception is we chop our chicken livers. But, this Tuscan version of my food just smothered the Jewish / Yiddish rendition. I loved the way Lilia prepared this dish. It's gonna be rough going back to Katz's Deli for chicken livers after having eaten this one
*Roasted Artichoke oozing with aged parmigiano - reggiano /  just fantastic
*Trumpet Mushrooms with aged balsamic and Sicilian Almonds - what can I say about this "Perfect" dish other than "Perfect"!
*Grilled Clams with Calabrian Chili - Never had clams so good Ever!
*Fettuccine with Lamb Sausage - crazy good.....Loved this pasta
*Linguine with Anchovy and tomatoes - one word " Memorable"
*Rigatoni with Chiles and Pecorino - took the leftovers of this one home by for lunch....can't wait to finish it.
*Olive Oil Cake - came with whipped cream - my wife's favorite dessert of all time! And as the saying goes " Happy Wife, Happy Life".

To get a perfect score in anything, from an Olympic event to a 300 game in bowling, it's gotta be PERFECT, right? 

I give Lilia a score of 10 out of 10 as a restaurant. Pretty impressive I would say!

Underwhelming to say the least. We waited about a month or so to finally get a bar seat at Lilia for my hubby's birthday. We ordered 3 apps and 2 pasta dishes. I always saw their mafaldini all over the gram so I was sooo excited to finally try it, but all I tasted was peppercorn. It wasn't crushed up peppercorn but whole peppercorns, quite the crunch. It really overpowered the mafaldini's intended flavor. 

I was at Misi last weekend and really enjoyed everything. 
P.s- I'm a huge fan of Missy Robins, but Lilia was a huge flop for me.

Boyfriend was determined to come here on last visit to New York City to dine out with family who lives in town. I understand that there is a lot of work that goes into handmade pasta but at the price proposition along with service besides our wonderful server, wasn't worth the wait. The portions are smaller than an entree and tasted like what my mother from the Midwest would throw together because she had not had time to make it to the grocery for something more substantial. Granted the space is very sexy, I felt it all to be so over rated. Also, why are the managers and hosts standing around with their arms crossed like body guards the entire time?
Absolutely Fabulous. Go with a group to order as many dishes as possible to share.  Arrive and delicious food. Great service. Austere space but the focus should be on the food. Gotta go back. Soon

I have been dying to eat at Lilias in Brooklyn for a while now as friends, critics and blogs have all raved about the restaurant, especially after Missy Robbins winning best chef in NYC in 2018. I knew I'd be staying in Brooklyn this week and I had reservation reminders for any openings on Resy for over 3 weeks. We never got an opening for our party of 4 so we decided to try and do a walk in on 3/4/19. We showed up at 5:15 a little before opening and attempted to put our name in. I spoke with one of the hostesses who said they were fully booked for the night, I asked if we could sit at the bar and she pawned me off to another hostess. The second hostess informed us that they do not sit parties over 1 or 2 at the bar, to which I told her we would gladly split into two parties, since we were two couples -  with separate bills and everything. She said "unfortunately we don't do that, we don't split parties up" to which I said again "we'll gladly split into two parties , separate check & everything - if I had walked in the restaurant stating we were 2 there would of been no issue but because I said we're four people now you refuse to sit us OR split us up into 2 parties?" . The hostess then turned around and asked her manager who was behind her, who said it was no problem as long as we were out by 7:30. Fine no problem.  We were shifted over to the cafe area to wait until the restaurant opened. While we waited many other couples and parties flowed in.  Perhaps the only highlight of the evening was your wonderful sommelier who happily went through the wine list with us to pick out a bottle for our party. The 2017 i Fiori Cannonau really shined. She was very knowledgable and helpful and picked a bottle we all loved. 

We were eventually seated at the bar and our server went over the menu and the specials. We ordered the focaccia special, whole artichoke and grilled clams for appetizer, and each of us got a different pasta as an entree: the mafaldini, Sheeps milk agnolotti, fettuccine with lamb sausage, and the squash ravioli. 

Our party all chatted and drank while we waited for the appetizers to come and took in the beautiful ambiance of the restaurant. Everyone around us had received the complimentary freshly roasted warm peanuts and fennel chips...except for our party. We asked our waiter if we could get some and he replied "oh I thought they were too hot" to which 5 minutes later they then served us the chips and peanuts with our appetizers and they weren't even warm? 

As for the appetizers, the focaccia was the highlight, but the artichoke and clams were not hot temperature-wise. I love when my food comes out hot, not warm, especially when they're "grilled" clams and "grilled"  artichokes coming from the kitchen that I'm staring at no less than 20 feet away. The artichokes weren't tender at all and the clams were like just eating luke-warm spicy breadcrumbs. No one in our party was impressed.

We eagerly awaited the homemade pastas, our hopeful highlights of the night. Again, all the pastas came out and not one of the pastas were hot. I understand fresh homemade pasta doesn't have to boil long, but again if its coming directly from the kitchen 20 feet away it should be hot and steaming. We all had the same comment about the temperature of the food to the point where one woman in my party asked if they could reheat her sheeps milk agnolotti only minutes after it coming out. The waiter said he'd happily have the chef make another batch and she agreed. Keep in mind she had only tried 2 pieces of the agnolotti... the waiter then came back a short while after with a new, WARMER, not hot, smaller dish with only 4 agnolotti after taking away her previous dish with a full serving. They took her food away, that wasn't hot, and replaced it with ...less food? The new agnolotti was definitely hotter and the sheeps milk inside really shined when the temperature was right but we were all rubbed the wrong way by the service and food experience. 

Also keep in mind that the hostess claimed we couldn't be seated at the bar if we were over 1 or 2 people and that they were "fully reserved" for the night , and we were seated next to TWO parties of 3 people and there were multiple empty tables in the restaurant the ENTIRE time we ate up until when we left. I feel like we had to fight our way to eat at Lilias and then had a poor dining experience on top of this. It's almost like we were targeted. I eat out constantly in NYC, & for the price point, hype & poor experience, I feel cheated. I don't know if the "B" squad was working or if it was just an off night but our party was very disappointed.  Before I wrote a poor review on yelp or another site, I wanted to write directly to the restaurant to let you know for the future so other guests don't have similar poor experiences. 

Feel free to reach back out or give me call

Came in 8PM on a Sunday. Waited 20 minutes for a single seat at the bar. Therefore, plan ahead as it is busy.

Started with the Chicken Liver Crostini. The bread does wonders as it is not overly toasted, slightly hard on the crust as the bread should be. Creamy well season duck liver mousse as spring onions offers an extra complexity and onion flavor the dish.

Then came the Fettucine. Fresh pasta that I recommend eating quickly as this allows it to keep its slightly bouncy texture for its generally soft and chewy quality (albeit for fresh pasta). A forwardly spicy, peppery sausage crumble is included as well as a simple tomato sauce.

Oxbow Luppolo Dry Hopped Italian Style Pilsner pairs well with this dish. Light grainy malt flavors match the pasta as the forward lemon rind hoppiness lifts up the fattiness and spiciness of the sausage. Citrusy hops and peppery sausage harmonize obviously.

Amazing and attentive service by the bartender. Very knowledgeable as he recommended amaros for dessert for a guest. 

Right before I left, I noticed Action Bronson had sat down at a table. A fine celebrity sighting.

As a bartender, dealing a questionable issue that is not solidly agreed upon, I leave people's check/tips on the bar until they leave. Quickly after I had left my cash tip after closing on cash, I had my holder snatched quickly before I was ready to leave. A personal peeve although I understand this can simply be a difference practices by bartenders. Cheers.

Resy made it very easy to make a reservation. Just refresh at midnight on the dot and you'll be able to get a reservation 30 days in advance. Otherwise if you set alerts for a specific day, you'll probably be able to snag a reservation due to last minute cancellations. I had to turn off the alerts in the end because I received too many of these notifications. 

The textures of the pastas were just outstanding. They have some interesting appetizers, but their pastas are truly worth the hype, for me at least. Despite how good their pastas were, my favorite turned out to be their focaccia bread special.

* Focaccia with chive butter - This was one of their specials, but if they have it I recommend ordering this. The bread was extremely rich and cheesy without the butter, but the chive butter makes it really special.

* Whole Artichoke, Garlic, Mint, Parmigiano, Breadcrumbs - What a great way to make artichoke as unhealthy as you can possibly make it. The artichoke was sitting in a lemon butter sauce. It was tasty, but I wouldn't order this again.

* Grilled Blowfish Tails - The fish was meaty and cut in a way so you can eat it like a chicken leg. I also wouldn't order this again.

* Sheep Milk's Agnolotti - The filling was so soft and pillow-like. The butter sauce was slightly spicy from the chili peppers and had a somewhat funky taste to it. Overall, I thought it was delicious.

* Pink Peppercorn Mafaldini - I loved the chewy texture of this pasta. Taste-wise, it mostly tastes like peppercorn, parmigiano, and butter. The sauce wasn't anything too mind-blowing, but with this kind of texture it was addicting all the same.

* Chocolate Torta - This wasn't the best dessert in terms of texture. The cake was dense, almost like a cake donut. The espresso cream paired really well with the chocolate.

We ordered their more popular pastas and appetizers, but I would love to come back to try more of their dishes. Unfortunately, we were seated in the area secluded from the kitchen, so we didn't get to see the chefs cook. I would try to get a reservation at the bar or request a table near the  kitchen.

I had recently heard the hype but I was BLOWN AWAY by the food (and wine). We were very lucky to get a table for 3, considering their reservations are booked a month in advance. My advice: get there right as it opens and put your name in. The bar is only for parties of 1-2 and tables are 3+ if you don't have a reservation (or so that is what was communicated to me). The starters were delicious but the lemon spaghetti was the best pasta I've had in my life! Can't boast enough about this place and fingers crossed I make it back soon.

Not too long ago my friends and i went to Lilia to basically try everything on the menu since that's...kinda what we do.  I arrived early and grabbed a drink at the rear bar while waiting for my friends.  Once they arrived we were seated near the front entrance round table and i finally got a chance to absorb the ambiance.

This restaurant, while having a cozy atmosphere also seemed somewhat cold as their high ceilings drew heat away.  The kitchen was something to watch though as you can see every dish being cooked.  There's also a middle bar area where people were dining as well which looked fun to eat at. 

Drinks were fun and tasty, food was really good and i especially enjoyed the appetizers, although some were better than others (looking at you blowfish).  I had a good time.

Lilia is worth the hype. The ambience is trendy with friendly service and great food.

The food could be described as a contemporary flare of classic Italian dishes. Overall, on the pricier side, but everything was tastefully plated with unique flavor. The sheep milk agnolotti was our favorite pasta dish, and, although simple, the rigatoni was cooked to al dente perfection with just enough of a kick from the spice.

Be aware, reservations do not come by easy at this place. Be prepared to look weeks in advance for even odd times.

Was a bit underwhelmed tbh. Food, drinks, service, and ambience were all great. There was nothing wrong with Lilia. But I guess I walked in expecting to be mind-blown, except I wasn't. Really really wanted to love this place but don't think I'll be coming back.
Appetizers were really good but I think I actually liked the pasta dishes Misi a little better!

Really a disappointing experience... service was abysmal... the bartender doubled as a waiter and wasn't interested in us at all. I was visiting NY and my friend was super excited to take me (apparently you have to make reservations a month in advance) and we went and lined up thirty min before it opened so get seats. The service wasn't bad because the bartender was the only waiter - nope, folks to the left of us as a super sweet waitress. What also really left me disappointed was that both couples left and right of us got food "on the house" and it was brought out in front of us. I didn't need the free food (we left food cause it was a lot and wasn't amazing), it left us feeling discriminated and shitty. Food-wise? The mussels were amazing but the broccoli and the pastas were okay. As I'm writing this review I'm truly realizing how disappointing an experience it was and how I wasted a valuable NY meal opportunity here. Honestly the food wasn't that bad but the service just left me feeling really upset...

The vibe/ambience was warm and lively, the food was simply exquisite, and the service was exemplary.
Had a wonderful time. The team had Lilia are on top of their game; Kudos to the team - Alicia Blegen for affording us the opportunity to experience Lilia, and to our experienced and lively server Alex Kim.

I wish I understood the hype but it escapes me. The front of house staff is lovely and kind but I truly wasn't impressed by the food. I've been three times now so hopefully I've weeded out the possibility of it simply being a bad day in the kitchen. The sheep's milk agnolotti is definitely a high point, but for me the rest of the pastas fell flat. I was especially disheartened by the mozzarella made in house. In fairness I make mozzarella by hand as well so perhaps my standards are high but it was unfortunately overworked on multiple occasions, overworking it like that really defeats the purpose of making it in house. The wines by the glass and cocktail list were also a big let down for me, it was all very one note. I love a negroni as much as the next guy but when every cocktails predominant flavor is bitter and the wines skew pretty heavy it's hard to navigate and tailor your experience. Glad others enjoy this place so much but it's not for me.
The Agnolotti pasta is probably one of my favorite dishes, the buttery saffron sauce is light yet rich of flavor. I wish I had more to share, however nothing was as memorable.

Very underwhelmed at this spot, which really bums me out because I was looking forward to it so much. 

Seated promptly when we arrived. It's very dark in there so just beware! Minimal interior decorating- looks very "brooklyn"

i found our apps (cacio e pepe and cauliflower) overly salty and nothing that special. The cacio e pepe fritters' flavors definitely work better as a pasta. 

As for our pastas, we ordered three (mafaldini, fettuccini, and the agnolotti) and I found all three uninteresting. maybe i was expecting too much from this place, but overall i'd say i was disappointed in the flavors although the pastas were all cooked pretty well. The mafaldini in particular tasted uninspired. 

Maybe it was an off day? I'm not sure, but I don't think I'll be making a trek out here any time soon.

If I had to choose a top 3 Italian restaurant in the city Lilia would make the cut. As most have mentioned, snagging a reservation is tough and requires a lot perseverance. If you're a party of two and don't mind an early dinner, show up 15-20 minutes prior to opening and your almost but guaranteed to land a spot at the bar counter. 
All of the pasta is delicious, my favorite is the malfadini with pink peppercorns. My second is the sheep's milk filled agnolotti, highly recommend if you don't mind pasta with a little sweetness due to the honey. 

All of their appetizers are extremely delicious as well - housemade mozzarella on toasted bread, spicy cauliflower with soppressata, clams, sardines, scallops and the list goes on. 

Whenever I crave some pasta, I just find myself coming back to Lilia.

Lilia Lilia Lilia! Saw this restaurant pop up on a ton of foodie articles and have been waiting FOREVER for a chance to get a spot. Everyone I try to get a ressie even a month before it's always full! Only times they have were late late at night or early. Finally after a good three months I got a spot for an early dinner on Monday. Terrible timing, but I had to try it. Maybe my expectations were so high since it's virtually impossible to get a ressie, but i was sadly disappointed. 

Let's first talk service/decor/ambiance. Beautiful spot in the heart of Brooklyn with the smell of fresh wood fire burning. Sadly though that beautiful fresh burning smell stops at the door. The attitude on the hostess in person to the severs is way to fru fru for me. Not a fan. I get it that this spot is a hot thing right now, but doesn't mean you gotta serve attitude with it. Their website clearly states "warm hospitality to come together"
And the only thing warm was that fire... 

Now for food, this is not your traditional Italian spot so if you're looking for classics this is not the place for you. However, if you are adventurous and want to try creative mix of flavors this is for you. We read a bunch of reviews and they said to order a bunch of anti pastas to start and the main pastas to share as well. Our table was veggie eaters so keep that in mind. We got the cacio e Pepe fritelle which look like little doughnuts. They were really dry though..  Italian broccoli was yummy and the whole artichoke with parmigiano and breadcrumbs is a must! It's beautifully presented so gram worthy. Serving size def good for 4 people to share. 

Pasta was next and be warned these are not heavy family share style. We got the recommended mafaldini which we rated the lowest of all the dishes. The pink peppercorn left for an odd after taste. The ricotta gnocchi was the highest for us. Sever with broccoli pesto and pistachios. Really beautiful. 1st runner up, squash filed ravioli with hazelnuts and fresh rosemary. Perfect dish for New York winter. 

Would I give these a 10 out of 10?? No. Maybe a high 7 or 8. 

The star of the night, surprisingly was the olive oil cake served with blood oranges. Seriously best olive oil cake. We also tried the house made soft served gelato but ehh tases the same as 16handles. 

Perhaps my palette isn't sophisticated enough or the service really turned me off, but it's hard to give Lilia 5 stars. I would def try it to cross it off your list, but warm hospitality it is not.

Came here with my family for my dad's birthday, and we all had a lovely time! Happy to say that the restaurant lived up to the hype! 

Appetizers: 
Cacio e Pepe Fritelle - super creamy and cheesy, although I think I like Cacio e Pepe better in pasta form 
Roasted Escarole, Anchovy, Garlic Chips, Ricotta Salata - very interesting combination but good (a little salty though)
Cured Sardines, Capers, Dill, Fettunta 
Grilled Blowfish Tails, Lemon Samoriglio, Cracked Coriander - wasn't sure what a blowfish would taste like, but this was probably my favorite appetizer! I loved that it wasn't salty at all and had a perfect blend of flavors. 

Pastas:
Rigatoni Diavola, San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano, Pecorino - your classic tomato sauce pasta 
Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano - This is one of their most popular dishes. It's very similar to cacio e pepe and tasted very creamy and delicious. 
Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Basil, Pistachios - good soft and delicate consistency of the gnocchi with a lovely pesto/basil flavor (though a little salty as well)
Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey - our favorite pasta of the night, and another one of their most popular pastas for good reason!

Our waitress was extremely friendly and enthusiastic, and our family had a great time! Even though Lilia is not my favorite Italian restaurant in NYC, this restaurant is definitely solid if you're looking for a nice Italian meal with a lot of creative menu options you can't find elsewhere.

Most rude treatment I ever encountered. Stopped by at 5:15 and place was empty. When I asked to be seated with my daughter and her 2 friends, was asked if I had a reservation, which I didn't. I was then told that I would have to wait with no guarantee of being seated. When I pointed out that the restaurant was empty and that we had to get to a concert and would therefore be quick, I was told that tgey get reservations 30 days in advance...clearly did not want to serve us...extremely rude and showed us the door. We were well dressed and clean. Would never patronize that place

My boyfriend and I came here for our anniversary dinner and while the atmosphere and location were decent, the food itself fell short. 

What we had:
Olives - tasty and fresh but not warm
Prosciutto appetizer - prosciutto & bread were tasty but the butter/mustard served with it were a little rich
Mafaldini - super rich sauce, this was good but I don't think I'd get it again
Rigatoni - my favorite dish of the evening, the sauce had a great spice to it and you could tell the pasta itself was fresh but unfortunately very undercooked - way past al dente

The service is what gave this place its fourth star. The staff was incredibly friendly and accommodating but sadly I would probably not return.

TL;DR: as Pete Wells notes, come here for the pastas and you can't go wrong. Definitely a $$$ splurge for special occasions.

SO and I came by for his birthday after Pete Wells waxed poetic about the pasta in the NYT, and we were not disappointed. Our starters were fine - the full artichoke is more or less just a bland a steamed artichoke and the cacio e pepe fritters are, well, fried cheesy rice balls. Nothing to write home about. 

The mafaldini, though, was incredible. I got the gnocchi with broccoli pesto and my SO had the mafaldini, which IMO was the star of the show. Each mafaldini strand was soft but still just a bit chewy - the elusive, peak al dente state. Ricotta gnocchi were so so pillowy soft, but I found the broccoli pesto a little bland.

I think the way to go here is to skip starters - srsly do not even bother - and share pastas.

I've come here twice and despite the hype, it is not a 5/5 place because it doesn't live up to it. Even though it's good I only give it a 3/5 because I'd expect a restaurant so nationally recognized to be, well...better. 

For a Best Chef nominated restaurant, I'd expect more. The Rigatoni was slightly too al dente. The gnocchi pasta lacked some flavor. I get what she was trying to do with the artichoke but it's honestly just kind of hard to eat and there isn't much artichoke. The special ice cream dessert - nothing impressive. Last time we got the olive oil cake and the chocolate torta and both were not impressive. The torta was not creamy/rich, more flaky like a chocolate cake. 

When it's so hard to get reservations, you'd expect a once in a lifetime kind of meal. Sorry to disappoint but that month long wait might not be worth it!

For a place booked two months out, I expected so so so much more from Lilia. We were able to get a table after another party canceled earlier that day, which made this experience better because if I'd waited two months for that, I would've been sorely disappointed.

Our table was for 9pm and we were not seated until 9:20. Not really sure I understand this system, but fine. They walked us to our table which was a booth among many others. We were about five inches away from the tables to our right and our left. Not the best atmosphere, but I was eager for the night to begin.

The server was not particularly enthusiastic about anything in the menu and barely explained anything to us. We ended up going for a bunch of appetizers, three or four pasta dishes, and an entree. I remember liking the cacio e pepe but not thinking its price tag was justified. This was the theme for most of these dishes. And to pile onto that, the extensive wait after every course was a little ridiculous; literally drinks, long wait, apps, longgggg wait, pastas, longgg wait, secondi, and then we couldn't we the check fast enough. This meal that shouldn't have taken over an hour took almost two and a half hours.

Honestly a pretty forgettable experience. Imagine going into a high-brow restaurant (maybe like I Sodi or something) and having your cliche hipster Williamsburg server semi-pay attention to your table because??? not sure???, and having that be the vibe of the entire night. Stuffy not in a midtown Manhattan kind of way, but more like our party was an after thought kind of way and everything is gonna be half-assed.

Paid that full-ass bill tho. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Just had a wonderful dinner with friends here. This service was top notch and the food was incredible. I was overwhelmed with the vast menu and the waiter was able to give us amazing recommendations. 

Definitely worth the wait.

The wait time is brutal but totally worth it! We sat at the bar next to the giant warm oven. Bartender/waiter Ryan was so nice and made the best drink the Milano Sour definitely recommend. We ordered the pesto gnocchi which are to die for and the mafaldi pasta 10/10 for both dishes. Exquisite flavors. As an app we got the mozzarella garlic bread which was also, amazing. Food blew us away tonight as well as the service. Will definitely be back!!

Great atmosphere and very nice clean minimalist design. Light and airy! A bit too loud for my taste. I tried Pork ragu and Broccoli Rabe pasta, both were delicious! Would come again. Only if the reservations were easier, its a bit ridiculous.

I had to make reservations over a month in advance and I was really looking forward to my first time here but I don't think it lives up to the hype. The ambiance was great and so was the food but the portions were small (why do restaurants think they need to up charge small portions to be relevant?) and the service sucked. Ordered the mozzarella app and it was amazing but there were four of us and you'd think the waitress would mention that it's on one piece of bread. Wasn't all that filling and probably won't be back but it was worth a try. Also, no Cabernet?

Food was good, but overpriced and small-portioned. Pasta was the best thing on the menu, but small. Service was overbearing and pretentious - we never had three minutes alone without being interrupted by a question or an arm between us, etc. Did not live up to the hype or our expectations. Decor was too hipster-typical and predictable. 

I should have known, in a city with hundreds of Italian restaurants, the best ones are not going to be in Williamsburg.

Lilia was such a fantastic dining experience. The atmosphere in the restaurant is lovely - it is bright but not too bright, and very classy without being stuffy. The Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti is by far my favorite pasta dish, it has a hint of honey that makes it so flavorful. Personally, I thought the Mafaldini with Pink Peppercorn was too peppery, so if you don't love pepper, I might try something else. Additionally, I definitely would save room for dessert! The espresso chocolate cake was unbelievable, and honestly one of my favorite parts of the meal. I can't wait to be back.

After a year of trying to get a reservation I was finally able to score one for 5:30 on a Monday evening. The space itself is beautiful and the service was friendly and professional. We shared the cauliflower, clams, mafaldini, agnolotti, and cappelletti with corn. My favorites had to be the clams, agnolotti and the gelato. In all the dishes were incredible and definitely surpassed the hype!

Tl;dr: Creative and well prepared Italian that lives up to the hype, though sometimes a little heavy handed on the salt 

GETTING RESERVATIONS: Unless you have a credit card with concierge services, most of us plebeians must settle with trying to nab a coveted reservation. We called exactly 30 days ahead of our desired date on five lines (enlist your friends) starting at 9:58 AM EST. Keep calling until you're told to hold -- normally you'll hear voicemail -- we got in for a reservation at 10:04 AM EST. 

IF YOU ARRIVE EARLY: We got in 20 minutes early and we're directed to the back for drinks. I ordered the spritzer, which was light and sweet. If you prefer not to taste your alcohol in your cocktails, this is your choice. They will add your drink to your table's tab so you don't need to pay/tip twice. 

Our server split up our meal into three courses after we ordered. STARTERS: We started with the clams, which lived up to the hype. Delightfully well balanced with a hit of acid; the small, hard breadcrumbs allowed for a crunch without taking attention away from the clams themselves. We also ordered the frittelle, which were sharply cheesy without being greasy. PASTA: The malfaldini was cooked just right. Great taste with the pink peppercorn -- but depending on the bite, the dish was sometimes outbalanced by the salt. The sheep's milk agnolotti was great. The flavor of the sheep's milk  shines through the dish, and fills your mouth with the warm and tart filling. As expected, this was a heavy dish. MEAT: The veal was tender and done well. Piled with herbs, the dish was flavorful and had just enough acid. ICE CREAM: We got the off menu olive oil ice cream with fennel. The olive oil ice cream and fennel itself had a great flavor when paired with the honey. However, depending on the spoonful, sometimes the salt added to the sides would overpower the dessert. Rather than scooping down the sides like you might do at normal ice cream shops, definitely cut into the ice cream so the salt mixes into your bite. It still might be a little too salty -- but it's better.

SERVICE: Attentive. Also really cool to see Chef Robbins visiting with her patrons. She must have had friends visiting, because she rotated between sitting down at their table and going in to check the open concept kitchen.

Does not live up to the hype at all. Was so excited to go only to find slow service and mediocre food. Ordered many top recommended dishes and they were underwhelming. Pales in comparison to L'Artusi or even sister restaurant Misi.
The service was excellent and the ambiance was great! I am glad we were able to catch them before they closed.

From start to finish, Lilia provided the most excellent service and most excellent Italian cuisine I have ever enjoyed in my life. From the host, to the café servers, to the bartenders, servers and everyone in between, this restaurant made me feel treasured as a diner. The sweet Sicilian olives were delightful, bagna cauda was a bounty of delicious seasonal abundance, and the crispy little fish with gremolata were addictive (sadly, I don't see them on the menu anymore). The black bass was p-e-r-f-e-c-t-l-y prepared, and so was the rigatoni diavola. I wish I lived across the street so I could dine hear every day like the glutton I am. 

The ambiance somehow is welcoming yet fine at once. When we couldn't make up our mind about our entrees, we learned that the chef likes to receive your entire order at once to create harmony in the presentation of your meal. This reassured me as I was worried about delay. Again, as I said earlier, the service here is outstanding, and the dining experience is seamless and full of joy. I cannot wait to return.

My boyfriend and I waited over a month to go there and finally went this Friday night.  The heat must have been broken because the entire restaurant was freezing!
