The hostess was giving out blankets and tea- to which I was charged $3.50 for!!! We also asked to switch tables because the wall right next to us smelled newly painted but they had no other tables. The pastas came out room temperature, probably due to the lack of heat. Definitely overrated and not worth the $$!

One of my all-time favorite Italian restaurants in NYC. I have been here about three times now, and have never made a reservation. Came as a party of two about 30-45 minutes prior to opening, and was seated at the bar. If you are a larger party, I suggest to make a reservation. 

Staff is friendly, and environment is aesthetically pleasing. The bartender was helpful on suggestions and recommendations. 

What I have tried:
- Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga
- Cauliflower, Spicy Soppressata, Sicilian Pesto, Majoram
- Grilled Scallops, Walnuts, Yoghurt, Marjoram, Anchovy
- Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano 
- Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey

Everything was savory and delightful, but the sheeps milk cheese was my least favorite. Malfaldini is a must try, pasta is cooked perfectly.

Allow myself to introduce myself.  Names Papi G and I locked up the yelp game a long time ago.  I do this shit to change lives.  And sorry fattys, but based on food what you have here is a solid 3 star spot.  And the prices, oh lawdyyy lawd the prices are enough to bring a grown man to his knees.

I waited 3 hours at the coffee bar area to be seated at other bar area which was expected. Food (Cacio e Pepe Fritelle), drinks and service at small coffee bar area were great! 

Once seated at other bar for dinner, I was ignored by bar staff. It took a long time to get a glass of water and even longer to order a glass of wine and my meal. When I finally got the bartender's attention, he said he could not recommend a dish. I ended up getting the Rigatoni Diavola. The dish was luke warm and chewy. NYC has the best Italian restaurants. This is rated as one of the best. I was extremely disappointed. Everyone go to Frankies 457 Spuntino, Evelina or Rucola for incredibly better food, service and ambiance.

This has been on my list since I moved to Brooklyn--my food obsessed friends all raaaved about it, so we did a walk in and the service was great and the place is beautiful. I can't decide if it's because I don't have a palette for Italian or the plates I chose were underwhelming, but I was super disappointed with the meal and it actually made both me and my boyfriend feel kind of sick afterward (we're not lactose intolerant).

Honestly the chips in the beginning were a highlight for me + very good. We tried the cacio (the server recommended it), malfadini, and gnocchi. The cacio was essentially very cheesy bread-- good but a bit too cheesy and salty for my taste. The malfadini was also too cheesy and salty, but the noodles were nicely cooked (I think?) Nothing super special. The pesto gnocchi was the best dish. The pesto was fresh, but I didn't think it was anything I haven't had before. 

Overall, I wanted to love Lilia. I didn't hate it, but unfortunately the love wasn't there.

Yikes! This may have been the biggest let down of a restaurant I've ever been to. This place was so tough to get into and so hyped up, I was expecting a delicious italian fiesta for my friday evening.

The waitstaff was very attentive and pushed us hard to buy everything and anything because their food was 'so amazing'.  I was so convinced, we did end up selecting 4 apps and 2 mains between the 2 of us.

Outside of the prosciutto, which was delish, we had:

The wine, the clams, their bass, their malfaldini. If you love bland tasteless dishes, order any of these items!  

Perhaps their sister restaurant sees their better chefs & more attention these days. Please save yourself spending on overpriced and underwhelming Italian and go anywhere else.

Ate here the other night and the food was very good but our waiter took away our bottle of wine before it was empty. It still had about a glass left in it, and we paid for the whole bottle. It looked like they took it over to the bar to serve to someone else. We should have said something, and I of course regret not doing so (too shy and confused), but I thought I should publicize it. Not cool, Lilia!!

We came here on a weeknight as walk-ins and put our names in for a table. It was a 4 hour wait and we explored Brooklyn while waiting. The wait was absolutely worth it! Fantastic service at the bar, great food suggestions (mafaldini, lamb fettucini, burrata and topped off with the olive oil dessert). Wow - we were blown away by the meal. I wish it was easier to get reservations! Will be coming back as much as we can!

Don't miss out, one of the best meals I've had in New York in a while. Everything is light, fluffy and obviously made with love. We made our reservations 30 days before by setting an alarm at 11:59pm and calling until we got through, it's the only way! Look at the Instagram before you go for recommendations and specials- get all the pastas. Skip dessert though or just get gelato. They know they're not pastry chefs considering the most popular dessert is ice cream with olive oil on it.

Just got back from Lilia. The food/service was very good and the hype is well deserved. It was not the best meal I ever had but it was a very solid meal. We were a party of 3 and order quite a bit of food but we were still hungry when we left. The bill was around $300 including the tip. If you plan on driving, there was plenty of parking in the area (Thursday evening). 

Starters:
Artichoke w/ garlic & mint - Spectacular. I'm used to traditional Italian stuffed artichokes... loaded w/ garlic & breadcrumbs. This was a fresh take. The presentation was unique as well. The artichoke was flattened out and every leaf had great flavor. I couldn't taste any garlic though.

Grilled Clams - In the same way I'm used to the artichokes a certain way, I'm used to traditional baked clams. This hit all the points of baked clams but the calabrian chilies bring a unique acid/spice element to the dish. After seeing all the photos of these I was expecting these to be epic. I felt they were just OK.

Entrees: 
Malfadini - Executed perfectly. Cheesy, peppery, al dente. Adult mac and cheese. I'd order this again.

Fettuccine w/ lamb sausage - Executed perfectly once again. Flavors were pretty straight forward.

Veal Flank Steak - Best veal I've ever had. Super tender... A lot of brightness from vinegar or lemon. I ordered this because it's a cut of meat you really don't see too much. I like going to restaurants and ordering something I can't make on my own. I'm glad I ordered it.

Escarole - Tasty but a little too salty. Also it would have been a little easier to eat if it was cut up a bit more. It was all connected at the stem.

Dessert: 
Italian Job - The standout dish of the night. I loved this dessert. Salty and sweet. The combination of vanilla gelato, olive oil, honey, salt & fennel form a balanced dessert. It was not too savory. I would eat this every night if I didn't care about gaining weight!

Apple Crostata - Average - reminded me of a pastry you may get from starbucks with some sour cream on top. I'd pass.

Overall - The highs at Lilia were very high and the lows weren't really too bad, just average. I don't think it's quite a 5 star restaurant but it's definitely better than average and is great for a special occasion.

Overall this is a solid 4-star meal. 

Dinner at a table inside the restaurant (3 stars) followed by dessert and coffee in the cafe (4 stars).

Why only 3 stars for the dinner? 

Cons:
-service was slow
-sommelier to came out to talk about wine offerings was actually quite underwhelming. With all Italian origin wines on the list we were informed upon sitting down there there were cousins of Pinot Noir's to try (Pinot Nero's). We were excited to be wowed by an expert explanation of the subtle differences between choices and instead just received one description of one option and then trailing off like a deer in headlights without anything to note on the other 3 options.... kind of bizarre to make a special point to send out a wine expert over to the table who really could provide no value to us making our choice
-we were excited to try the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle but we're actually pretty disappointed by the one note texture and lack of real texture in the dish (would not order again) 

Pros: 
-both main courses ordered were scrumptious. 
-The Mafaldini is made in house and absolutely delicious! The pink peppercorns add nice depth and spice to the dish, which strikes just the right balance in flavor and subtlety 
-Veal was cooked to perfection. Extremely tender meat and garnished with fresh herbs that really enhanced and balanced the dish. 

Cafe experience: 
-olive oil cake with homemade whipped cream and candied blood oranges was great! 
-lattes were made to order

Ordered the following:

Focaccia Bread ---- The herb butter served with this bread is so delicious, I could eat it with anything! 
Cacio e Pepe Fritelle ---- Creative take on cacio e pepe, still retains the flavor even when fried.
Cauliflower with spicy Soppressata ---- Didn't stand out to me but a good vegetable addition to balance the rest of the meal. 
Whole Artichoke ---- Perfectly cooked, flavorful
Mafaldini ---- Light and simple, al dente pasta. Goes with any dish. 
Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti ---- The honey and saffron were not too overpowering, added just a touch of sweetness.

The only downside to our experience was that we had to wait for half an hour before the table was ready. Normally this isn't a big issue, but given how long ago the reservation was made- I would have hoped to be seated sooner to that timing.

Again a great dinner at Lilia. This restaurant offers everything for a fantastic dinner. Excellent food, service is top notch and the ambiance is very pleasant. I particularly like the pasta and the fine selection of desserts. Also like the mention the great wine selection.

Lilia has mutton dressed as lamb syndrome.  I'm not sure who ate here and decreed that Missy Robbins, whose pasta I do believe I've enjoyed previously at Andrew Carmellini's far superior A Voce, was in fact the goddess of pasta, or that Lilia was some sort of Nirvana for Italian Cuisine, but whoever this person was must have been at an entirely different restaurant, having an entirely different experience.  Maybe he or she was on acid.  Who knows.  

Now, to start, I had a 6:45PM reservation on what was admittedly the coldest day of the year thus far, a balmy high of 10 degrees with a wind chill factor that made it feel like Antarctica.  When my husband and I were able to score this table after what has been something akin to witnessing the Vision of Lourdes, we figured this was due to people thinking it was too cold OUTSIDE to handle a gorgeous dinner at what has been a hugely lauded place and one of the hardest reservations to score in all of NYC.  What we didn't know, is that we likely landed this table because the patronage knew what we did not.  That restaurant has MAJOR heating issues, it has NEVER replaced the very flimsy glass windows that the former auto body shop it was had prior I suppose in order to maintain that "New Brooklyn Charm" but the thing is?  It was maybe 20 degrees in there.  All the patrons were sitting in their winter coats, gloves on, FREEZING THEIR EVER LOVING BOOTIES OFF.  As a gratis, the staff offered blankets to the customers and told us "we have a space heater doing its best guys."  A SPACE HEATER?  I'm sorry, isn't this supposed to be one of the hottest tickets in town?  Am I really to understand that I'm about to share space with a space heater?  Why, is this restaurant so cold?  I'm absolutely sure that Martin Picard's Sucre just outside of Montreal isn't this cold and that place does business all throughout the MONTREAL winter.  Already I was not feeling good about anything. 

There is a lot I'll withstand as a foodie and insane person to enjoy great food.  So with that, your food better be GREAT if I'm already starting out my evening shaking in my coat and wearing my winter gloves at the table.  If Missy Robbins and staff think that this is cute in any way, that because she is from Wisconsin this is some adorable hipster play, I am here to tell you as a resident in the neighborhood, that this is not only not cute, this is downright disrespectful to your patronage who you know is all but contorting and genuflecting to get a table.  The least you can do, is heat your space properly and if you are having HEAT ISSUES on the COLDEST DAY OF THE YEAR, maybe call your customers?  Get someone in to fix the problem?  Maybe don't put your patronage through a really uncomfortable experience?  What's to be gained at the expense of a few dollars more if people like myself can't enjoy the food and then come here to complain?  

Let's get the gorilla in the room out of the way first, the ever-blogged photographed and humble bragged about, "Mafaldini with Pink Peppercorns."  If you've never had Cacio E Pepe, this is likely going to knock you out and you'll hear the angels singing, Aretha Franklin maybe she the goddess rest in peace is personally going to greet you as you walk through the pearly gates.  If you've HAD Cacio E Pepe, by virtue of just how many people have been all GAGA about it since Lilia opened shop roughly 3 years ago, should minimally be the GREATEST Cacio E Pepe experience, the one that puts all others to shame.  Well tonight, I was able to partake in the experience, admittedly barely enjoyed through gloved hands in a room the suitable temperature for a tawdry Las Vegas SubZero Vodka Bar.  I love Cacio E Pepe, it's one of the perfect examples of how great Italian cooking requires nothing more than 3-5 ingredients, cooked with great technique and with ingredients that are the best that can be sourced, so I expected something akin to the most perfect ayahuasca trip, guided by a glittering shaman.  I'm here to say it.  It's good!  Is it the best pasta dish I've ever had?  Not by a long country mile, not even in this NEIGHBORHOOD or close to it, Naked Dog does gorgeous pastas and amazing food in a room that doesn't make me feel like an extra in Dr. Zhivago.  Faro in Bushwick dazzles!  Rosalina and Al Forno in Providence dance rings around this place.  

Honestly?  The best thing?  The FOCACCIA.  Served warm and pillowy with tons of butter, and then they give you a quenelle of even MORE butter, with garlic and chives.  

I had the misfortune of having to use the Ladies Room while there, and you could see your BREATH in the bathrooms, and well...I won't even discuss what it felt to sit down on the seat.  I let out a yelp I'm pretty sure they heard in Canarsie.  Was going to go to Misi, but I think I'll skip it.  Maybe instead of another joint, spend the money to heat the one you HAVE.

Generally lives up to the hype. My friends and I had to claw our way to getting an 8:45pm reservation on a Thursday approx. 3 months in advance. We were a party of 6 and when we came we were immediately seated. The ambiance is pretty incredible. The restaurant is in an old automotive warehouse building and the way they have redone the interior is pretty incredible. Our server was super polite, nice, gracious. She knew the menu inside and out and answered all our questions. 

We ended up ordering approx. 4 appetizers, 3 pastas, and 2 protein dishes. I have to say that the mussels in cashew and yoghurt sauce and the squash ravioli were two stand out dishes that tasted absolutely incredible. The yoghurt sauce was so unique and authentic, I have honestly never had anything like it. The sheepsmilk pasta was another dish that I can honestly say was something I've never even seen on another menu. This restaurant and the chef that runs it clearly cares about offering nontraditional and unique Italian dishes and are putting in the effort to make their food worth waiting for.

The only reason I took off a star was because so many of the dishes were too salty. We ordered focaccia bread with basil butter and it was absolutely phenomenal except the bread was so heavily salted. Same for the salad I had, it was like lettuce with oil and salt. Also had to take off a star because of the obscene wait time to get a reservation, but I guess what are they supposed to do in a restaurant so popular and trendy.

Wow. How can I even begin to explain the magical evening we had at Lilia? I want to start off giving a (virtual) standing ovation to our server Marcus who made an already fabulous dinner into a show. Listening to him explain the intricacies of the menu made us feel like we were at a slam poetry reading, it was incredible. We got excited every time he checked in on us because we got to hear even more poetic details about the dishes. Safe to say it was the best and most exciting service I have ever received.
Now onto the food. I want to preface this part with saying that EVERYTHING we ate was delicious. There was not a single dish that disappointed, so I want to highlight our favorites (and there are plenty). I didn't take any pictures because I was so consumed with how incredible the meal was!!
The special app of the day was a housemade focaccia with a chive butter, which just melted in your mouth. The roasted escarole with anchovy and garlic chips was a fun play on a Caesar salad and surprisingly ended up being one of my favorites of the night! The scallops with yogurt sounded like an odd combination but I'm so glad we ordered it-what an inventive blend of flavors. The spaghetti was recommended by Marcus and was BOMB. The flavors sound simple (lemon, pine nuts, Parmesan) but holy crap I have no idea how they made it so delicious. The malfadini is a necessity to order-make sure you toss it around to get all the peppercorn sauce that pools in the bottom of the plate. Lastly, my favorite pasta was the agnolotti which was filled with a flavorful and creamy sheep's milk cheese. My mouth is watering thinking of it.
Sounds like a lot of food, right? Plot twist - we ordered dessert and WOW it was unreal. Vanilla gelato with olive oil and sea salt served with an olive oil cake. I have never tasted anything like it-the combination of sweet and salty was to die for. What a perfect way to end a perfect meal!

I think i found my favorite new restaurant in Williamsburg. I heard it was notoriously difficult to get reservations at Lilia so i figured i would wait for the hype over this spot to die down and then make them. The hype hasn't died down, it's still notoriously hard to get reservations butttt I came here on a weekday with a friend and managed to snag seats at the bar. I asked the bartender for food recommendations and was told the Grilled Veal Flank Steak with hot peppers and basil was a favorite. Never a fan of veal, i decided to try it due to my curious nature. It did not disappoint! Absolutely delicious, the perfect amount of seasoning and just the right amount of spicy. My friend got the grilled swordfish and wished she ordered the veal. Both dishes were delicious but if you're more of a meat kinda person, i would definitely recommend the veal dish. 
Can't wait to try more things from the menu, now i definitely understand the hype.

Given the hype, this was very disappointing. The food was decent- maybe slightly below average for an Italian restaurant in NYC. But the combined experience made our visit here an epic fail.

First- the service... To seat us 20 minutes late when we have a reservation is really not cool. Worse yet, asking us to wait outside... And the IDGAF (I don't give a f*ck) attitude continued after we were seated with long waits between, 1)  when the waiter first took our order, 2) when we received our drinks, and 3) finally when the food was brought. 

All-in-all, this was a 2.5 hour dinner on a Monday night when our average, on a normal Monday night out, would be a little over an hour. I mean, get it together...

Then there was the food. The best part I guess was the pastas. They were good- but not mind blowing by any stretch. I've had much better of the two versions we tried in much lesser known (certainly less hyped) NYC establishments.

But the really bad part was the chewy veal main entree, the overcooked clam app, and the chicken liver crostini app which was just very, very bad.

So in summary, decent pasta dishes can't overcome poor service and a menu full of underperforming entrees and apps. We would never go back.

Love it or hate it the trend of Restaurants featuring high volume and dim lighting has got legs, and on Sunday night in Williamsburg it was as a party of three that such things were tolerated to see what the buzz was about at Lilia, Missy Robbins' still white hot space that is almost ready to celebrate its third anniversary.

Located at 567 Union Avenue and thus highly convenient via subway from Manhattan, the Bedford Avenue station just a few blocks walk, it was arriving fifteen minutes prior to a reservation booked exactly thirty days prior that guests were whisked away to a table, service pleasant but grating thanks to both over-explaining and recommending *everything* yet somehow failing to mention several daily specials.

No stranger to Robbins' Cuisine, visits to both Spiaggia and A Voce occurring during her tenure, it was after brief perusal of labeled sections that the decision was made to order in four courses with a focus on Pasta, though first it seemed pertinent to take a look at Lilia's oft-praised Cacio e Pepe Frittelle which eat like cheesy Popovers plus a plate of imported Charcuterie that comes with far too little housemade Bread for the sizable quenelle of Butter infused with Parmigiano-Reggiano.

Forced to ask for more Bread, three slices arriving room temperature almost fifteen minutes later with the first pair of Pastas, it was within one bite that surrounding annoyances including two diners making out were easily ignored, the tubular Agnolotti stuffed with Sheep's Milk and perfumed by Saffron beautifully juxtaposed by Honey and Sundried Tomatoes while springy Ribbons of Pasta called 
Mafaldini lived up to accolades as Robbins' best dish both in terms of taste and texture despite fairly simple toppings of Cheese and Pepper.

Certainly not a place that will ever be accused of rushing to turn a table, nearly half-an-hour between clearing course two and the arrival of another duo, it was unfortunately a bit too much Basil that compromised creamy Gnocchi while pockets of Squash were offered more subtly with Rosemary and Hazelnuts, the choice of just one Dessert to finish largely based on the late hour and a long day of eating but mostly enjoyable as crumbly Cake offered a gently sweetend base for Figs, a splash of Grappa plus plenty of Whipped Cream.

My bf and I dined at Lilia's last month.
I kept hearing such great things about it so I called them up to make a reservation and scored one but had to wait a month (which I had expected)

We had dinner there late on a Sunday night are 11pm. Regardless of it nearing closing time, everyone at the front of house was super attentive and very friendly and did not rush us at all. 

We tried a little of everything on the menu.

For appetizers we had
-Cacio e Pepe Fritelle
-Roasted Squash, Thyme, Breadcrumbs, Coriander Vinaigrette
- Grilled Scallops, Walnuts, Yoghurt, Marjoram, Anchovy

For dinner we had

-Rigatoni Diavola, San Marzano Tomatoes, Chilies, Oregano, Pecorino

-Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano

-Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey


For dessert we had
- Olive Oil Cake with figs
- chocolate gelato 


Everything was absolutely delicious ! Still thinking about the sheep milk agnolotti, was out of this world

Came here on a Saturday with my girlfriend. I'd made reservations a few weeks in advance, and was told the only availability was at 5:00 p.m. (right when they opened). No problem. A few days before our trip - we were only there for a night - Lilia messages me to confirm the reservation, which I appreciated. I get paranoid about these things, especially when anticipation's had time to work its painful magic. 

It was raining lightly when we got to Brooklyn, and, in a miscalculation, we got to Lilia thirty minutes ahead of schedule. Across the street was a lovely desert bar, where we started our night with a glass of Prosecco. As it turned out, this part probably could've been skipped. We ended up drinking at Lilia. A lot.

Okay, enough foreplay. Lilia was effing incredible. One of the best Italian meals I've had in my life, if not the best. We had the Cacio e Pepe Fritelli, the Treviso, the Mafaldini, and the Agnolotti. We also had a grilled fish which was a feature, but I forget exactly what it was. I want to say Snapper neck, but I could be wrong, which is embarrassing because it might've been my favourite thing we had. Given how much we had to eat, I'll write a couple of sentences for each. The Cacio e Pepe Fritelli was a cheese-lovers dream - heavy in theory, lovely in practice. This dish is all about the perfectly balanced textures, with a special emphasis on goo. Gooey in the best way. The Treviso was brilliantly conceived, with elements that played off of each other in a way that somehow contained the bitterness of the Treviso with cheese and pine nuts, while building on it with capers. The Mafaldini was the standout dish for my girlfriend, who described it as "her favourite pasta dish, ever". This one doesn't shy away from its richness. In fact, the ribbed shape of the pasta itself seems designed to not only capture as much of the salty, fatty sauce as possible, but to add to the dish's richness through mouthfeel. The Agnolotti was great, but combined with everything else felt a bit unnecessary. I'd say either get the Agnolotti or the Mafaldini, not both. Instead, opt for a more acidic sauce for your second pasta. You'll need it. And then the fish. I really wish I'd written down what it was, but by that point we'd finished a bottle of wine, two aperitifs, and two digestifs (the alcohol was all lovely). The thing I do remember though was how much I loved the fish. Each component had its own flavour and texture, so that combining them was a revelatory experience. The skin was oily, charred, and somehow both chewy and crunchy. The flesh, in contrast, was buttery and light. Just delicious.

The place itself is a perfect date spot. Very romantic, with a dash of modern and separate dash of rustic. Our server was amazing - we both agreed that he felt like a friend. I should've written down his name. He walked us through everything, made great suggestions, and generally was super nice without being overbearing. 

Overall, Lilia was excellent. Would definitely go again.

You. Need. To. Come. Here. 

I've been about 7-8 times since September, and I don't plan on stopping anytime soon. I've tried most things on their menu, and these are my go-to's:

-homemade focaccia (they've had the leek focaccia since about August but switch it up depending on what's in season): it is to die for and comes with a creamy pesto butter
-Calabrian Chile clams: despite the name, they are not TOO spicy! They come with breadcrumbs on top as well. There are about 11-13 half shell clams per order (I know because my boyfriend and I have to count them out since we fight over eating them all!) 
-Sheep's milk ricotta agnolotti: I've had it as a meal before, and it is great. However, I often like to put it in the middle for both of us to share since it is so sweet. It's a must try though. 
-ANY TWO PASTAS: I've tried them all and it really just depends on what you're in the mood for. My favorites though are the mafaldini, gnocchi and corzetti. If you don't want to take home leftovers and are looking for something lighter, go for the corzetti. The rest of the dishes you will take home half. 
-Olive oil cake: a denser cake that comes with whipped cream and a seasonal fruit (usually fig or orange). I thought there was a 0% chance I'd like anything olive oil involved in dessert, but they have changed my mind for good. 
-Gelatos: chocolate or vanilla with several toppings to choose from. If they have the Italian Job, definitely try it. It's an off menu item that they only have certain nights, but it is vanilla gelato with toppings like olive oil, fennel seed, and honey. UNBELIEVABLE. 

I've also tried the prime rib, which was HUGE, as it should be for the cost of $100 (meant to be shared by two). We put it in the middle of the table and everyone enjoyed it. 

I have a million photos of the food and will attach later.

This restaurant is amazing. 
I went with my family and everything we ordered were incredible.

The service was awesome. The staff is really nice.

It was SO hard to get a reservation there, I had to wait almost 2 hours and I had to seat at the bar. Besides that, everything was perfect. Service, ambience and food.
I started with a garlic bread with homemade mozzarella. Excellent!
Then, I got sheep milk cheese filled agnolotti with honey and dried tomatoes, to die for. Now the best, the dessert you HAVE TO ORDER: the Italian job. It's vanilla soft serve with honey, olive oil and sea salt. The best I've ever had!

I knew nothing about this place but went for a friend's birthday.  Apparently it's hard to get a reservation.  

Everything that needs to be said about this place has probably already been said.  But.... 
There were 4 of us and ...
we had... 7  appetizers
3 pastas
5?!!! desserts
a bottle of wine....    

Your take on a place is very much dependent on the aura of the event... I didn't have to make a reservation.  I just showed up and was given a great seat. Service was impeccable. Company was outstanding.  Food was good - great (depending on dish). We all had a fabulous time.  But I went in with no expectations.  I hadn't heard of the place, I knew nothing of the hype... so what's not to love?

I'd go back. But now that I know that it's super hyped and hard to get a reservation... would I appreciate it so much? probably not.  

The nifty kicker at the end of the eve was my expectation that it would be at least $200/couple... but it was a lot less.  Bonus for everyone.  

Why is it so hard for NYC restaurants to pull this off?

Had to book a month in advanced to come here with my girlfriend and it was definitely worth the waitstaff was fantastic as well as the food! We ordered the homemade mozzarella, grilled clams, Mafadini and Rigatoni Diavola. Truly fantastic dishes and we are definitely going to return. 

---update: returned multiple times and Lilia continues to be one of my favorite restaurants. If you're ever in NYC definitely check it out. It's worth the trip to Brooklyn. 

Pictures are a collage from the multiple trips. Can't go wrong with this menu!
Outstanding food and delicious aperol spritz. Everything we ate was fantastic. The pastas were exceptional. Can not say enough good things. Eat here. You won't regret it.

Very disappointing service and food. We were really excited to try this place, but the preparation of the pasta was subpar as was that of the dessert. There is far better Italian food and especially pasta in NYC. Go elsewhere!

Had a lovely dinner at with a Piedmontese friend visiting from Italy. The food was fantastic. 
The servers knew the menu and wine list backwards and forwards and upside down. Besides being knowledgeable, the staff is friendly, warm and intuitive. Would highly recommend to anyone.

Cacio e pepe fritelle were sooo good. We slightly preferred the mafaldini to the gnocchi, but both were delicious pasta options. Our Italian friend was happily surprised with the authentic flavor of the bagna cauda. Can't go wrong with anything you order at Lilia.

I have been absolutely dying to try Lilia since the raving Pete Wells review in 2016 where he couldn't stop talking about the pastas. I've very much the same person: if there's something on the menu that I find unbelievable, I'll spend the entire meal (and possibly the next day) talking about it in this breathless, stream of consciousness rambling, to the annoyance of everyone around me. In Lilia's case, that honor actually belonged to the home-made mozzarella rather than the pastas but I'll get to that soon enough. 

Oh, and the Michelin stars don't hurt either. 

However, I've always been intimidated by the reservation system where seats only open up 30 days in advance and they're gone in a blink. Plus, Lilia is all the way out in Williamsburg and I'm on the UWS and I had always planned on eating through the West Village first if I'm in dire need of pasta. Lucky for me, I have dear friends who are able to book this most prized reservation (and I suppose it helped that most people are out of town this weekend anyway).

Much of the menu has already been debated ceaselessly in the reviews and accolades heaped on Missy Robbins but here's my contribution anyway. I think, as with most places with killer menus, you should come with at least 2-3 other people to try a little of everything. 

(1) Home-made mozzarella: 15/10. This was so good to the point where I was seriously debating if I should get a second piece all to myself for dessert. Three slabs of the best mozz I've ever eaten on a piece of perfectly toasted Amy's sourdough bread. I really wish they had offered more of this bread to dip in the leftover pasta sauce. 

(2) Sheep's milk agnolotti: Incredible. 

(3) Malfadini: I've never come across this pasta shape before but it was so addictively chewy. The one thing I will say for the pastas is that they were all uniformly a tad saltier than my liking and came out on the lukewarm side. I usually prefer my food on the other side of boiling especially in the freezing wintertime but neither was an issue that prevented me from gobbling down. 

(4) Rest of the appetizers (grilled clams, cauliflower with soppressata, trumpet mushrooms) were tasty but nothing topped the mozz. 

(5) We tried four of the ... maybe five desserts. What you should get: the vanilla soft serve with candied pecans and the toasted apple crostata. Add together. Rejoice. The double chocolate torte with some kind of espresso creme was too dry (and might be why I'm writing this review at 4) while the Italian job with the olive oil was so strongly floral that it stung a bit. 

The enormous platters of meat looked intriguing. Photo credits of the stunning pastas go to my friends - mine came out looking like dark shadows around a candle.

Good pasta and very nice vibe. The pasta isn't overly complicated, but you can tell the quality of the ingredients is high. It's very hard to get a reservation, though, and it's probably a little overhyped; I've heard people say it's the best pasta they've ever had, whereas I think I've definitely had comparable pasta elsewhere in the city. That being said, very happy I went, and if it were easier to get a reservation, I'd go back
Try everything. Lilia has great oysters, great pasta, fine wine and is the perfect date spot!

We received a gift card here from our foodie friends when we got married. While it took a bit of work getting a reservation, it was well worth it. Our evening was special from food to service.

We arrived about 15 minutes before our reservation time and were directed to the bar, located through the restaurant and past the kitchen in the back. We sat there and had delicious cocktails - negroni and aperol spritz. When our table was ready, a hostess found us by name and even carried our drinks to the table. This simple touch really set the night at such a high bar.

Our server was incredible - attentive and knowledgable about the food and wine. We began with the focaccia bread special, truffled rice balls, cauliflower and scallops. Everything was delicious and melted in my mouth. The rice balls were creamy on the inside and crunchy on the outside. The bread was piping hot and the special butter served with it was very well seasoned.

We split three pastas, including the popular mafaldini with pink peppercorn, ricotta gnocchi, and linguine with anchovies and spicy tomatoes. I actually found the mafaldini to be the weakest, with a less than al dente texture (too crunchy in the middle). The linguine was was fabulous and was the right amount of spicy and salty. The gnocchi were nice and light.

Dessert wasn't particularly memorable, but was still great. I believe we had the chocolate cake (can't seem to the find desserts on their website) The coffee and espresso served with dessert were so delicious, too. At $3 for a cortado, they were reasonably priced as well.

Everything was served at an appropriate speed, with silverware and plates changed often. We left stuffed, but managed to stop at the hostess on the way out to make another reservation. There was so much on the menu we didn't get to try but know we need to come back for. 

Looking forward to my second meal here soon!

Lilia, I was so excited to try you, however I must say, you were VERY disappointing.

After all of the hype, my friends and I were calling a month in advance for a reservation. After calling 30 days in advance, we were able to get a 9:15pm reservation.

We arrived a few minutes before 9:15pm and were told it was going to be a few minutes. A few minutes turned into a half hour and we weren't seated until 9:45. Besides a few apologies, nothing was done for us.

We ordered 2 appetizers & 4 pastas. All 4 of our pastas came out cold. After the meal we asked if that's how the pastas were supposed to be served, the waitress said no.

At the end of the meal, all of the pastas were comped. Although we had a great waitress, and the restaurant ended up doing the right thing in the end, the food was subpar. Not worth making yourself crazy trying to get a reservation.

Waited a month for this reservation. Even saved my anniversary dinner for it and i have to say i was a bit underwhelmed.  Waitstaff was great and very attentive. Just felt that the food didnt have the wow factor that i expected. Portions were small and definitely over priced. I dont mind spending the money,  just ask that the meal is worth it.

Came on a Saturday night with the girlfriend - stopped by at 5pm when they opened to put my name down for a party of 2; was eventually seated at 8:30. Between the hype and the long wait time (though plenty to do in Williamsburg to kill the time), the bar was set pretty high.

And the verdict? The food is pretty good, but not outstanding. Breadcrumbs on the clams were nice texture, but felt the clams were a little overcooked. The rigatoni, on the other hand, was a little too al dente, and erred on the side of being too simple.

Agnolotti was a home run - can never complain about creamy goat cheese. And the olive oil cake was tasty and substantial.

Would probably come again (and order differently) but only if I didn't have to wait!

Ugh I could cry writing a review about this place. Posting my review from my Instagram account @carbiesanon:
"If I could only use one word to describe my meal this weekend from @lilianewyork it would be WOW Of course, this would be of no surprise to anyone who has been lucky enough to snag a res to this place. From the service, to the menu, to the PASTAS this place went beyond my expectations. We started off with the cacio e pepe fritelle (not pictured because I was hella hungry) which was SOFT AS HELL & covered in tons of shredded mountain of parmesan. Next we had all 3 pastas at the same time. Peep descriptions below;
*Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti: the most perfect noodle briefcases stuffed with sweet sheep's milk. Could I ask for anything more?
*MAFALDINI: the best thing I think I ever ate. Like I couldn't stop talking about it. I'm going to call everyday to get a reservation so I can have this again. I'll go alone. Idc
*Ricotta Gnocchi with broccoli pesto: these soft little gnocchi pillows were everything. They just melt in your mouth
*Me being a thirst monster 
*Vanilla/chocolate gelato swirl: topped with amaretti cookies, chocolate stracci, chocolate-espresso powder & salted hazelnuts. We first said no to desert until we saw them walk by with this & we called our server back to take our check back because we were not DONE.
@missyarobbins LOVE YOU BABYGIRL let's have a convo over white wine (I got the Malvasia Salina Biano (2017) - Caravaglio)"

Side note: our server was the most phenomenal server ever, I took a note to take his name down on the receipt so we can give credit where credit is due, we had Marcus M!

Lilia, you have let me down this time. I have been here a few times before and have had stellar meals and service. This time was a bit different. We arrived for a 9:15 reservation on a Wednesday night. After 30 minutes, we were finally seated. We were told time and time again that the table was finishing up and paying, which is totally fine ....as long as the restaurant is willing to grab our party of 3 a drink or do something worthwhile to make up for their booking error. It was my birthday dinner and after making 4 reservations at just as highly rated places, I chose Lilia for the sheer fact that the service and food are great and for the fact that I would not be rushed. Well, I was very wrong. When we began the meal, we commented on how displeased we were with being shoved in a corner waiting for a half an hour. A staff member brought out a complimentary fritelle that was luke warm and so rich we could hardly stomach it. As the meal went on, we had waiters standing over our shoulders waiting to take our plates. A guest with us counted 6 times that a busboy came over my shoulder to see if I was done. Towards the end of our meal, our waitress just stopped coming to our table. A new woman appeared and wrapped up the meal. I understand that shifts end, but I have been to diners at 4 in the morning  where the waiter has come and told us their shift has ended and that we'd be with someone else for the remainder of the meal. I expect more from a restaurant like this. The new woman who took over said she knew we were celebrating something and dropped the check. Very bizarre? 

All in all, probably will not return here for quite some time - if ever. One of our guests who had a fantastic dinner here last spring noted that she would never return for any sort of occasion after tonight's disappointment. There are too many great restaurants in New York City with fantastic service. This is no unicorn, proving to be just another overpriced restaurant that thinks their name speaks for themselves. To maintain customers, you have to do so much more than what was shown tonight.

I don't really get the hype. Overall the food was just ok, nothing special and the prices are ridiculous. If you're going to charge $23 for a few bites of pasta it better be some great pasta. Also by the time the pasta reached our table it was cold so this place is a no for me. 

The cacio e Pepe fritelle were a bit overwhelming. The chicken liver crostini were good. The mafaldini came to the table cold and the peppercorn in the dish makes you feel like you're eating shards of glass. The fettuccine also came cold and the flavors were nothing special. The sheep's milk agnolotti were very good and the only reason this place didn't get one star from me. This meal cost $115... not worth it at all. 

The service was ok but the time between when we got the appetizers and when we got the pastas was 40 minutes... a bit crazy for a place with such good reviews. 

Would not come back, would not recommend.

I love love love love Lilia. I understand now why it's so hard to get a reservation. I went in September and have a few upcoming reservations in December. All i can say is wow. I was blown away by the service and the food. Every single thing there was delicious i can't say enough good things about this place. My favorite appetizer was the Grilled Clams and (this is a tough one) my favorite pasta was the Sheep's Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti. As for dessert i don't care how full you are do not leave without having the Olive Oil Cake.

We all know that you come here for the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle. They are definitely a must as a starter. This is the second time here and this time we were able to get seated at the bar right away, which is probably my favorite place to sit anyways. 
This day they had a special on focaccia bread with whipped up seasoned butter that would just melt in your mouth. Together with the Cacio e Pepe, we were set for a great start to our dinner.
For our mains, we got a bowl of pasta, obviously. More specifically the spicy lamb sausage fettuccine. Together with the mussels and ricotta radishes which were both great, we finished our meals stuffed and happy.

The bartender/waitress was very attentive and friendly. The atmosphere is always delightful. Crowded but just the right volume and enough space. Sitting at the bar is just as nice as being seated at a table with their open kitchen concept. The no reservation policy is a downer and the menu isn't diverse enough to make this a frequent date spot. But overall if you're able to get seated right away (or your uber hasn't left yet), the wine and drink selection will keep you company until your food arrives.

First meal of the night of our trip in NYC, it started with a bang of a meal. We started with the roast mushrooms it had a balsamic glaze marcona almonds and arugula. Next was their housemate focaccia served with a green leek butter it was so fluffy and whipped it was like eating a cloud instead of knowing you were consuming flour and oils. A fitting aepreol spritZ accompanied me through the meal, to do as the Italians do. The scallops in a yogurt bath were a big portion than your usual scallops and I could've done with 5 bowls of that for my meal it was so good. For the main pastas we did a red sauce and white sauce perfectly al dente. Then ended with a veal we were too full to finish but mustered up the strength because leftovers were not an option for us. Then dessert was an olive oil cake that was a little too dry.

When I first ate at Lilia I truly loved their food. Ever since then the food has gotten saltier and saltier. The wait times are absolutely insane for what this restaurant is. I should have to wait 2-3 hours for one person to sit at the bar.

One of the nicest Italian dinners I've had in Brooklyn! Came with a friend around 4:30pm on a Sunday and we were first in line outside waiting for it to open. There is a small enclosed vestibule we were able to stand in out of the cold, but only a few people for there. We got a table for two, no reservation!

Started with the cacio e pepe fritelle, basically cheesy little parmesan fritters. They were absolutely melt in your mouth delicious. The gooey cheese filling is richly flavoured with parmesan and the fritters are lightly fried so they crack apart when you bite into them. None of that thick, bready fried coating usually found on arancini and other fried apps. 

My friend said the mussels were some of the best she's ever had. 

We tried the lemon spaghetti and squash filled ravioli for main course. The two pastas were excellent in different ways: the spaghetti was like elevated comfort food. Pasta was super al dente and chewy. The sauce was slightly creamy and coated the noodles like a carbonara. The lemon and pine nuts saved the dish from being too heavy and decadent, and along with some roasted garlic, the whole concoction was really well balanced. 

The ravioli, in contrast, was very light and delicate. The pasta dish was incredibly thin and well balanced with the sweet squash filling. The ravioli was bathed in a buttery sauce and sprinkled with hazelnuts, which added a surprising crunchy texture and also even more buttery, smooth flavor. 

Finally, we ended with the vanilla soft serve, which was a pretty fun and unexpected dessert option. You can choose as many of the toppings as you want and the ice cream comes in a big glass cup so there's plenty to share. The soft serve was extremely sweet with strong vanilla flavor. A little watery and less creamy than I would have hoped, though. The mini amaretti biscuit topping was amazing! 

The atmosphere is very romantic and industrial with low lighting and lofty ceilings. Service was good, not overly cordial/friendly, but pleasant. One downside was that the single, tiny bathroom was kinda of smelly and gross - out of character with the high quality of the rest of my experience.

This place absolutely lives up to the hype! Everything was fantastic from start to finish and you could taste just how fresh everything was. We ordered the fresh mozzarella, baked clams, grilled squash, malfadini, and sheep cheese pillows - would highly recommend it all! The pasta was some of the best I've had and is competitive to what you'd get in Italy. If only this place wasn't so hard to get into, I'd be coming every week. Well done!!
brunch was amazing. all I remember was I kept ordering more. If you want a Manhattan style brunch, but a Brooklyn feel - this is your place.

Worth all the hype - ambiance, food, service and just about everything brings this to the very top of williamsburg's food scene. It's almost impossible to get a reservation but the bar counter is just as great (plus you get a sneak peek through the kitchen)

Uhhhhhh, this place is so geeeeerd.

Make a reservation ahead of time, recommend for parties of 2-4 but they can certainly accommodate larger parties.  They have a nice little coffee shop in the back of the restaurant where you can order a drink and wait for your table. 

Drinks: Wine and cocktails, and coffee, their cappuccino was ever so delicious.

Appetizers: The Little Gem Lettuce was yummy and a good simple base salad, get a little veggies in that belly prior to piling on that pasta.  I really loved the grilled clams with breadcrumbs and chiles, so flavorful and crunchy with the breadcrumbs, they complimented each other so nicely.  You must get the prosciutto, balsamic mustard, and parmesan butter as it will knock your socks off.  Bottom line, I don't like mustard but can eat this for days.  The housemade mozzarella, toasted garlic bread and lemon could take me to heaven, knowing I died and saw the light.

Pasta:  One word and one word only "Mafaldini".  The adult version of mac and cheese on crack.  Not a big fettuccine person, but this is mind boggling on how delicious this is.  The ricotta gnocchi was so light and fluffy, just wonderful.

Dessert:  BIG fan of the chocolate soft serve with espresso powder on top.  It is more on the icy side than creamy side, but sooo good, just preference on who you are and how you like your soft serve, as I know people are opinionated now in days.  The olive oil cake was good, but too dense and heavy for me.  DON'T FORGET to order a cappuccino :)

I have to say Lilia definitely lives up to the hype!
 
I came here with three other friends and got to sample a bunch of different things. For starters, let me say we had Marcus as our server and he was INCREDIBLE. He was beyond impressive on not only his knowledge of the menu/drinks, but was able to give us a detailed description on the flavor palate to expect with each food, where the wines originated and the tones the grapes gave, and so much more. Marcus really knew his stuff and made our experience incredible!
 
For appetizers we had the whipped riocotta radishes, stuffed artichoke, cacao e pepe fritelle (fried pasta ball), and the herb focaccia bread w/ garlic herb butter (not listed on the menu, but ask for it!). I highly recommend all! Everything was filled with flavor and cooked to perfection. The stuffed artichoke and cacao e pepe is definitely for those who love cheese! It has a strong cheese flavor and may be slightly overpowering for those who don't love heavy cheese. If you do, then it's a must!

For the main course we had: Lemon Spaghetti with Pine Nuts, Rigatoni Diavola, Corzetti, and the bolanease. All the pasta was cooked perfectly and very seasoned. I would say my favorite was the lemon spaghetti- simple, but delicious.
 
The desert was a definite must. We were so full but I'm glad we splurged because the desert was on my favorites of the night. We had the vanilla sobert with sea salt, honey, and olive oil. It was the perfect blend of sweet and salty! This is a must !!
 
This place is a must! Apologies for the poor pic quality. It's very dim lit!

I brought my boyfriend here for his birthday. Everything was done really well (service, food itself, vibe) but it did not live up to all the hype we've heard. It is the perfect option for someone looking for a slight twist on modern Italian cuisine, but not for people looking for a new twist or re-invention of Italian food.  

For wine, my boyfriend had Veneto, which he said was good and went well with red sauce. I had a Negroni, which lived up to its expectations. We had the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle as apps which were great. Then the Agnolotti and Gnocchi. The Gnocchi was ok, but pesto overpowered the dish and the Saffron on the Agnolotti did the same. 

Portions were a good size, but everything meant for sharing. 

Service was fast and inviting.

I feel like I won the lottery when I walked in and got a  seat at the bar at Lilia with no reservations.  We took a big leap walking in on a Tuesday at 5:30.  

Lilia is beautiful. The music has a great vibe. The atmosphere and ambience is romantic with dim lighting and a beautiful open kitchen. We were seated at the end of the bar, right by the kitchen. We saw the chefs preparing all the dishes with precision.  Along with sitting at the bar we saw the bartenders making all the wonderful cocktails. Overall, it was such a pleasant and interesting night. 

We looked over the menu and heard the specials and decided on:

A special of focaccia with leeks and a chive butter. It was soft and served warm. It was flavorful and a great start to the beautiful meal.

We also ordered Scallops. Which was cooked on the wood grill and seasoned perfectly. They were accompanied with a yogurt, walnut and anchovy sauce. It went so well together.  This a small app but so worth trying! 

We ordered two pastas.  The agnolotti was with a saffron, honey and dry tomatoes. This dish was just amazing. The filling was creamy and delicious. The sauce was so flavorful. It is a def must try! 

We also tried the corzetti with speck and parmigiano. This pasta was al dente discs and on top are succulent mushrooms in a beautiful sauce!  I really enjoyed this dish.

Lastly we ordered swordfish with sweet and hot peppers with mint. This was a small piece of fish But it was seasoned perfectly. The sauce was just amazing.  Unfortunately, I didn't like the seeds of the peppers in this dish. 

For dessert We ordered cappuccinos and chocolate gelato with espresso powder. I thought this was a great combination. It was creamy and super decadent. 

We also order the chocolate torte. I found this to be okay it wasn't my favorite.  It was a tad dry. 

Also for wine I spoke with the sommelier and she suggested a lovely white wine that was light, crisp and fresh. It was a tad expensive. So ask for the price before committing lol 

In summary Lilia is a bitch to get into but, we finally got in and enjoyed dinner here! It was a delightful meal with  great wait staff and ambience. Anything you order here you probably can't go wrong with. So if you are lucky and can get in with out a reservation, high five! Enjoy! 

Parking is somewhat difficult! (327)

Reservations can be a little hard to get but we found a last minute opening the night before on Resy and grabbed it before it disappeared. Walk-ins for the bar are available but the line can start before the restaurant opens. Our reservation was for Monday night and there was at least a dozen people waiting in the rain.

To start off:
1. Chicken Liver Crostini - this was super light and flavorful. Chicken liver mousse is one of my favorite ways to start a meal and the dish here is no less than excellent
2. Grilled Clams - unique because they're grilled with crunchy breadcrumbs that are clearly by Missy. Chili gave it a nice kick too
3. Grilled Scallops - only two scallops but they were big, buttery and delicious

The appetizers were great but the our two entrees were the stars of dinner:
1. Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti - incredible! It was so luscious. Each bite was tender, the filling was creamy, and the pasta was bathed in a honey-based sauce. It's no wonder all the tables around us ordered the same dish!
2. Wood Fired Dry-Aged Ribeye - this was one of the specials that night, $118. Not a pasta but it sounded like something really special -- 32oz (2 lbs) of steak dry-aged 30 days and cooked perfectly medium rare over wood fire... we were not expecting to find the best steak we've ever had that night. 

For dessert, we shared a vanilla gelato with all the toppings (lemony walnuts, amaretti cookies, sprinkles, and chocolate stracci) which came with a birthday candle. We were stuffed but still devoured it way too quickly. 

Would absolutely come again because it lives up to the hype!

Tuesday night at 8:45pm, table for 6.

The ambiance, service, quality of ingredients in both the drinks and the food, together with the surprisingly (for New York) well-spaced out timing between courses rather than the usual rush to turn tables, make it an understandably top-rated restaurant. 

My only advice would be to not focus entirely on the pasta, despite all the extremely appealing photos being regularly circulated over blogs and social media. My reason for this is two-fold: firstly, setting unnaturally high expectations always leads to a slight disappointment; secondly, because the pasta is simply not that good compared to all the other delicious and varied items on the menu. Take one or two of the pastas just to say to yourself you tried it (my favorite was the corzetti with chanterelle, speck and parmigiano) but then make sure to select a few antipasti and a fish or meat to follow. I also highly recommend finishing off the meal with the olive cake and an amaro. 

Good luck trying to get a reservation!

So our meal was good, but when I opened our leftovers the next day we found a short black hair in the sea bass. I get that it happens in kitchens and could have happened when they were wrapping up the food to go, but what a turn off. See attached photo.

Everyone comes here for the pasta, but dare I say they stay for the veg?! By far, the best, most unique things we ate were the simple radishes with ricotta, the broccoli and by g-d the artichoke. The artichoke was the standout for us - it was one of the best things we both have ever eaten. 

Out of the three pastas we got (rigatoni, lamb fettuccine and the green gnocchi) the lamb was my favorite - very flavorful but not overwhelming. My husband loved the gnocchi for its interesting pesto/nut flavor - it was of course perfectly cooked.

What a joke. Not ready for prime time. No better than any Wburg hipster spot. Loud. Kids dragging on Juuls. Waited 20 mins past the reservation. Waiting area at the bar is op top of the bathroom and about as comfortable as hovering by the serving galley on a 2-aisle airplane. Food was largely mediocre. Lemon spaghetti? Meh. Spicy rigatoni? Bad. Service was attentive, so that's worth something. Mailino, Marea, even Morini and Emilio's are much better. Wells is smoking something, if this is a three star restaurant.

So...I tried coming here back in August and couldn't get a seat. My friends and I left and went to another location for dinner. Ever since, getting a reservation has been a total nightmare, lol. I decided to come back on a whim, by myself, lo and behold, the outside patio was empty so I was seated right away. Food and service was amazing...especially the service. Wish I can remember my waiters name but he was outstanding. I'll be back with my friends, this time we have a reservation, lol.

Place is BS. Impossible to get a reservation. Was in the area when they opened at 5pm, went in and the place was about 90% empty. We went to the hostess and she said there was a waitlist and that the earliest we could potentially be seated was 8:30 (it was 5:15). No way every seat was booked on a rainy, shitty Saturday @ 5:15pm. Why would you turn away customers that are already in house?! If it were prime dinner time, I'd understand that those empty seats could quickly fill up but 5:15pm?! Get over yourself.

After trying to get a reservation that works for my schedule for nearly 2 months, I finally was able to secure a 10:15pm reservation on a Wednesday. There is a great deal of hype surrounding Lilia and its star chef, Missy Robbins and I can definitely see why. The food is amazing, the ambiance is nice and cozy, and the service is very attentive. 

We came about 15 minutes prior to our reservation and they were able to sit us a couple of minutes after our arrival. The space is former garage with dim lighting and a very relaxed vibe. 

We started off with the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle, followed by the Roasted Squash with Thyme and Breadcrumbs. The Cacio e Pepe Fritelle were delicious and extremely cheesy both inside and out. They had a bit of heat to it when you bit into them, but they were awesome. We went with the squash as our Antipasti because it is a fall vegetable and we expected it to be amazing. Well, the Squash was nothing short of perfection. The squash was roasted on the outside and was soft on the interior, the bread crumbs provided a great crunch and had an awesome texture pairing, the Coriander Vinagrette provided a nice bit of citrus acidity that was the glue for the dish. I was blown away by this appetizer.

For our main course, we opted to try two of pasta dishes. The first was the famous Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, the other was the Spaghetti with Lemon and Pine nuts. We were going to try the Mafaldini but we had incredible lemon spaghetti in Amalfi over the summer and wanted to see if we can get something similar in NYC. The Agnolotti was awesome, the filling was super soft and had a bit of a spicy kick to it, the sauce was sweet and paired nicely with the spiciness of the filling. I just wish that there was more sauce and maybe a piece of bread to soak it all up. The spaghetti was also delicious and perfectly Al dente (the only way to eat pasta). The lemon sauce was creamy and had an abundance of pine nuts that also added a nice textural element to the dish. 

Overall this place absolutely lives up to the hype as everything was amazing. The meal wasn't all that expensive and we left feeling feel and completely satisfied. Missy Robbins, you are a genius. Can't wait to try Misi!

Went in for a coffee break, stayed for dessert. Service was top notch. Coffee is served in carafes to keep it hot. Every detail of our dessert experience was beyond impressive. Can't wait to go to dinner and try out their savory menu.

The hostess was the rudest woman ever. We didn't have reservations and she treated us like second rate citizens. She said "I can seat you at 11 but that's when our kitchen closes so you won't be able to order or eat any of the food". What?! Why not just say you're fully booked for the night, sorry.  Horrible. Don't even want to try this place. Btw her new restaurant Misi is awful. I went there last week and didn't finish even one of the dishes we ordered!  Don't even bother with Misi. It's all hype

Lilia's has taken simple dishes and made them even more delicious and pretty. Everything feels very fresh and simple, yet also elevated.

It's tough to get a reservation. But, you can show up before the restaurant opens for dinner, get in line, and put your name on the list. It's worked every time for me, when I've gone on a weekday. 

If the weather is nice, sit outside if you can. 

Start with the whole artichoke for an appetizer. Trust me, it's beautiful and delicious!

You must get some pasta dishes to share. Specifically, the Ricotta Gnocchi with pesto, Rigatoni Diavola and Malfadini with Parmesan sauce and pink peppercorns. All so delicious! These come in a "small plates" size, so get a few bowls to share. 

Honestly, everything on their menu is delicious, so you can't go wrong.

Lilia, I love you.

I come here to eat sticks of butter. You won't taste anything like this anywhere else. You have my word!

Let's move onto the artichokes with a mountain of breadcrumbs to accompany the sauce or the tasty roasted trumpet mushrooms. Have the Rigatoni Diavola, the fish of the day and make sure you get the Steak if it's the special of the day. You won't regret it.

Did I mention to order the butter?

Missy Robbins is a genius. Love everything about her and her pasta is NEXT LEVEL. The service is always beyond friendly. Can we take a moment and realize that when people complain about waiting while there are empty tables, that maybe, just maybe, there isn't enough staff to cover that table or can't seat it without encroaching on another reservation? LOL

After going to lilia several times last night was the worst ...... we arrived and was told we can only be seated outside within 20-30 minutes we accepted to wait by the bar located in the back of the restaurant,  while consuming , an hour had past and we decided to check on our table the host stated it was 10-10:30pm what she had told us when we all perfectly heard 20-30 minutes ... we finally get seated in the cold outside while there were 2 empty tables of 4 inside. However, they claimed they were "reserved" . I had told the host if the reservation no showed to please seat us inside since we where shivering of the cold and enjoying our meal was uncomfortable.  The Host totally ignored us since when we were done I decide to go inside and the same 2 tables were still available .  Not to mention the "I don't care "attitudes of the hosts ,the cold fillet that had to be taken back to the kitchen  and the long wait on the food . 

Positives : our waiter Cory was amazing !!
Hands down, one of the best places to eat in NYC.   Been coming for years and the food has never missed a beat

Fabulous Italian Food and Fabulous Service- Wow!

Dinner at Lilia was an absolute joy!  The food and service were fabulous.  We were lucky to had a 6:30 reservation on a Saturday night thanks to my son, who is a regular customer.  We were a party of six and we enjoyed sharing all the dishes together, ordering family style.  We got several appetizers including the chicken liver crostini and our favorite item of the evening, crispy, tasty focaccia which was a special item for the evening.  For our main courses we enjoyed several pasta dishes, the Rigatoni Diavola, Malfadini Pink Peppercorn with Parmigiano, Fettuccini with Spicy Lamb Sausage, and the Grilled Lamb Leg Steak with Roman Spices which was tender and deliciously seasoned.  For dessert we enjoyed an apple strudel and double chocolate cake.   The service was first class, with the food coming at a good pace, and the servers clearing our dishes and silverware, and providing us with clean dishes and utensils at least 2-3 times during the evening.  They frequently filled up our water glasses and we also enjoyed several bottles of Lambrusco wine.   

We loved our dinner at Lilia and look forward to returning in the future when we are in Brooklyn again.

I stumbled across this restaurant while I was location scouting for one of my films. I really loved it and connected with one of the hosts (didn't get her name but she was very friendly). I told her it seemed like a great place for one of my scenes and I asked her if they allowed filming in the restaurant. She was really excited and said yes. I was then referred to contact the general manager, Alicia Bergen, to discuss the possibility of renting the space for my film. Days went by without a response from her. So I then went to the website and submitted a second inquiry after realizing that "Film/Photoshoot" was an option on their drop-down. A day or so went by and still, no response. Finally, one of my Producers called and they were very short/dry with her until she shared that she was contacting them regarding a film. There was then "excitement" again. Except, we couldn't speak to this mystery woman named Alicia. Lol...ok fine. So then, Alicia finally e-mails us back at 4am saying that she was unable to offer their dining room as a shooting location. That was it. No explanation, no reasons why. So, I followed up and asked her if that would be the case for the future so that my team knows not to consider her business as an option. And that it is so clearly written on the website that they offered that. No response. Not only that, her "team" of employees seemed very excited at the prospect and said Alicia has allowed filming there before. Thus I am led to believe that we were discriminated against. And I would never dine nor recommend anyone dine in a place that is not welcoming to all guests/artists.

Waited a while to try this place out. I and the person I went with ordered the malfidini & fettuccini. We had a few bites and couldn't finish the rest. Several hours later and extremely ill with nausea and vomiting. I don't know why this place is so hyped up. NEVER aga

Let me paint the picture for you....While working in the office the other day, I was exposed to the tantalizing aroma of someone's pasta during lunchtime. At that moment, I said to myself "Boy, would I enjoy some of that right now instead of this sandwich"!-lol. Fast forward to the end of the work day and constant thoughts of eating pasta swimming in sauce compelled me to locate an Italian Restaurant for dinner. Lilia is a place that came highly recommended for their great tasting food. Yes, getting there as quickly as possible was top priority when 1.) One starts looking at the great online pictures of some of Lilia's signature dishes and 2.) This causes one's stomach to start growling in anticipation of eating one of these delicious looking meals!

It was such lovely weather the other evening so patrons were enjoying Lilia's outside as well as inside dining/seating options. The hostess stated that it was an hour and a half wait for indoor dining versus a 20 minute wait for outdoor dining. It was mentioned that the wait is long for indoor dining because patrons can reserve seating up to 30 days in advance (this is good to know and that information is being kept in my mental rolodex-lol). Well, of course the easy decision was to sit outside. The hostess mentioned that customers can sit inside Lilia's Cafe which is towards the back of the actual restaurant. It is such a cute cafe and the freshly squeezed Orange Juice quenched my thirst while waiting for an outside table for dinner. Lilia's Cafe serves beverages such as juices and wine as well as appetizers. 

Lilia has elegant decor which includes everything from their tables, seating arrangements to the candles lit on their individual table settings. Gray, white, beige, cream colors are here and there which includes their nice/simple dinner and cocktails menus. Cafe Bartenders and Servers were all so gracious, warm and kind as they check on you often to see if you need anything throughout your entire dining experience. 

I ordered Prosciutto w/Bread as my appetizer and  Fettuccine w/ Spicy Lamb Sausage for my entree. Sure I had another glass of freshly squeezed Orange Juice...Yes, it was that good. Flavorful Proscuitto w/ chewy bread, fabulous tasting Fettuccine in a sauce w/ sausage that was well-seasoned but not overpowering and fresh juice = an awesome meal in my opinion. It definitely satified my pasta craving. 

The hostess extended goodnight greetings on my way out after using the bathroom and asked about my experience. I let her know that it was wonderful, that I will be back but next time I will make reservations to try indoor dining so that I can say that I had the best of both worlds-lol.

Horrible service.  Management packs the house with their friends and people who know them. If you are a member of the hoi polloi coming in for a reservation, beware - service will be incredibly rude. They rushed us through our meal, made us order everything at once (i.e. no starters first), and then kicked us out of our table for another reservation. They promised us a free drink at the bar for kicking us out, but the bar was so crowded there was no hope of getting a drink, plus the manager disappeared so how would the bartender know not to charge us? Not worth it at all - don't waste your time.

I finally got a reservation at the perennially full Lilia! Unfortunately, it was much later than I like to eat and they couldn't (wouldn't?)  accommodate us earlier so, off we went. There were 2 of us and we ordered an app, (grilled clams) & two entrees; agnolotti & grilled bass. Immediately, we were informed by our waiter that "other patrons usually order more food" and we should too. Not only was it already almost 9 pm, we always order in this manner & have never left another restaurant hungry before. I politely declined explaining that I had peeked at the dessert menu online & wanted to save room. He didn't seem pleased. Food was delivered at a good pace. The clams cried out for bread but none was served. I finally asked the bus person if they served bread & he brought over 2 small pieces of cold Neapolitan style bread.  The clams were good. Nothing to croon over. We were then served the agnolotti which were small, light, rectangular pillows of deliciousness! I could have lived without the honey but it was subtle  enough as not to ruin the dish. Lastly, the bass, which was served over Yukon gold potatoes & bathed in a luscious herbaceous sauce. There was a faint hint of smokiness from the grill. Excellent. We decided to order the apple crostata for dessert. Our waiter once again tried to up sell us by insisting that the soft serve was "a must" over the crostata or olive oil cake. He was openly annoyed when we declined. I actually overheard him give the same spiel to another table & then say "you want to do the right thing, don't you?" If it's such a "must," why doesn't the chef serve if that way?  Intimidation, bullying & shaming a customer to get them to spend another $15 is a major turn off to me. Sadly, the end of the meal was a complete miss. The apples were scarce & undercooked while the pastry was cold, hard & tough. At first I thought it may just be an "off" night but then realized it was served with a big steak knife which to me, means it is meant to be that way. Overall, it was very good with the following exceptions: none of the food was hot which is a pet peeve of mine, portions are small so if you are a big eater, you may indeed want to order "more food," the prices are too high for the portion sizes, the dessert was awful and finally, the service was pretentious & a bit obnoxious. I'm glad I went for the experience but will not go thru the insanity of getting a reservation again anytime soon.

I had a great experience for my birthday but dropped in on a Sunday night and was really disappointed with the service. If it wasn't for Missy's superb pasta, not sure if it'd be worth the BS at the front of the house.

Upon coming in around 8pm there were 6 tables open inside and about 6-9 tables open outside all "reserved." Fine. Informed the waitress we'll do first available, she told us 45 minutes. After 25 minutes of waiting the tables outside dwindled to maybe 4-5 empty tables and a handful of tables inside that were STILL unoccupied. We finally were seated at a two seater outside that was OPEN the entire 45 minute waiting experience.

I get it, Lilia is "it" everyone "wants" to go here but this is some B.S. city-service.

My experience reminds me of a crappy/unhealthy relationship that my friends don't support where I'm not treated well by a partner but there's that ONE THING always makes me come back...for Lilia it's the pasta. 

If the pasta wasn't so good, I'd give it 3 stars.

Everything I had here was phenomenal! Arrived around 630pm on a Thursday night and still had to wait about 1.5 hours for the table but the food proved well worth it. Finish the meal with a slice of the olive oil cake!

My friend and I planned a trip to new York, our first stop being Lilia because my friend wanted a pastry that we could only find here. We arrived after a 30min metro ride and was told by the barista that she already send the pasty back to the kitchen. When asked if she could get it she flat out said no. There was no reason as to why she could not get the pasty. She was just too lazy to do so. Horrible customer service.

Somehow managed to get a reservation for last night and was worth the wait. We ordered a bottle of red wine plus apps to start. Got the clams, artichoke, and mozzarella. The mozzarella dish was my favorite.  We each got a different pasta which was to die for and ended the night with the chocolate ice cream desert. Will have to try Missy's new restaurant, Misi, next!

There is a stark difference between the food and the experience here. The food here is obviously the selling point. Everything we ate was spectacular! However for a restaurant of this caliber where you need a reservation a month in advance, I expected more from the overall experience. We arrived on a Saturday night at 8:50 for our 9pm reservation. We were told it would be a little while before the table was ready and were offered a spot at the bar in the back. We ordered drinks and while mine came out in a couple of minutes, it was about 15 minutes later when my friend received hers. At around 9:30, we realized how long it had been and went to check if our table was ready. We were told they were paying their bill and it would be ready soon. We weren't sat until 9:45 (45 min after our reservation and almost an hour after we arrived!) I'm not sure what the purpose of a reservation is it you have to still wait that long. Also we were not offered anything to make up for the fact we were seated so late and had to wait so long for a drink at the bar. I would have expected a place like this to do the right thing (maybe a complementary second drink at the very least). We sat at the table (needless to say we were starving) and while it was about 66 degrees outside, the fans in the place were going full speed which made it freezing inside. I wore my jacket and scarf the whole time. It was also quite loud in the place making it difficult to have a conversation. While we didn't have any issues with the server, he was at best, average. I was underwhelmed with his descriptions of the food when we asked questions. He basically recited what was written on the menu with little elaboration. Again, for a place with this reputation and at $120 per person, I expect more. Thankfully the food came out and was a god send!! However the experience is not on par with the quality of the food. The chef deserves better than this!

My boyfriend and I arrived at Lilia at 5:05PM to put our names down. We of course anticipated a wait and were seated at 7:20 at the bar.  We got our appetizers and pastas with no issue. For a main we order the lamb steak which was clearly forgotten to be put in as we were presented dessert menus prior to receiving out meat portion. We had to remind our waiter that we had ordered a meat. 25 min later..... we had to follow up as to where our meat dish was. There seemed to be a miscommunication between the kitchen and wait staff and 15 min later were presented extremely rare main course which we sent back because it was inedible. Our whole meal should've been comped, instead of just that once very raw dish, given the overall poor experience we received, especially for a place in such high demand.
