Caution when ordering their meat as they are clearly feeling the pressure of being in such high demand.

Been here twice- once for dinner and once for take out. I honestly do not understand all the hype! The food in both the restaurant and to go area are lackluster and incredibly overpriced. The sandwich for 16$ has maybe one piece of prosciutto on it? You can go to a cheese store and buy 1/2lb for that much and it will taste better.

Same with sitting down in the restaurant- pasta is OK. Nothing memorable.

Think this place is all about being trendy and hip when it's just a waste of time and you leave hungry. 

1 Star for a good espresso!

Great Service. Wonderful Space. Focaccia was great. Olives were ok. Artichoke was horrible. Dish was more cheap cheese than artichoke. Really awful. Linguine with anchovies was inedible. Sent it back. Very expensive night to go home hungry.

Last night, with much anticipation my friends and I went to Lilia for dinner.  We were very disappointed.  I'll break down what we had.  The focaccia, clams and cauliflower were OK nothing special. there was also an appetizer called broccoli rabe. I would like to know what they were thinking.  This was not broccoli rabe but rather broccoli rabe leaves not good at all.  The agnolotti were good, the rigatoni, mafaldini, and spaghetti with anchovies were marginal at best.  The lamb steak was good.  After reading all the reviews on how great the food we were not impressed at all.  On a positive note the staff were extremely professional and pleasant. We have eaten in many restaurants in all of the boroughs that are far superior than Lilia.  We will not be returning.

I honestly can't believe this place is close to a michelin star. Artichoke undercooked, fra diavlo pasta undercooked, sheep milk rigatoni tastes parallel to the mushroom ravioli I get from the supermarket, clams....I can make a buttery break crumb and red sauce at home that's parallel and the cauliflower is just a little oil and spices...5. 

Go to L'Artusi or a million other Italian spots in Manhattan if you want a unique Italian experience. Oh and if you want an authentic, down and dirty home cooked Italian meal w a bomb red sauce do Max's in tribeca...or go see my buddies at Randazzo's in Sheepshead Bay.

Honestly, I just don't get it. I haven't had this much anticipation to than be than be SO disappointed for a meal in a while. Come on Michelin...this place isn't even close.

Best birthday dinner last night! I am a manhattan girl through and through, so you know its worth it if i'm venturing to BK. I had been hearing about Lilia for over a year and finally was able to score a reservation on my birthday. For 2 people, 2 appetizers and 2 pastas will definitely suffice. My boyfriend and I did 3 and 3 and it was way too much food.

In terms of the food, the focaccia special is a must order. It was warm and served with this delicious garlic butter. The must order pastas in my opinion are the agnolotti (do NOT skip this) with honey and dried tomatoes and the rigatoni diavolo. 

The service was also impeccable and attentive without being overbearing.

Amazing amazing experience!

Went back for the 2nd time to give it a chance before writing this review.  Both our experience is consistent.  It confirms that while the food is good, it is not mind blowing where I would recommend my out of town guests to go there.  

The service during both our visit hasn't been good.  It wasn't bad.  We were served but not waited on.  In this last visit, we felt the waitress was trying to up-sell us on the food; she mentioned that we ordered a light meal.  We got an app, pasta, lamb leg steak, dessert.  We questioned ourselves for a second but then remembered how large the lamb leg steak.  At the end of the meal, we still had doggie bag the lamb steak, so we had no idea what she's talking about with our light order.

Adding to the chorus of admirers - my meal at Lilia was one of the best Italian meals I've ever had. Missy Robbins (formerly Chicago's Spiaggia and NY's A Voce) is back and making some serious pasta in Williamsburg. 

Reservations have been impossible to get since this restaurant was voted one of the best in NYC and my party of 2 attempted to walk-in. We arrived at the restaurant 10mins before opening at 5:20PM and a line had already formed outside the door and around the restaurant. We put our names down after waiting on line and were called by the staff in about an hour - we were seated for dinner at 7pm. My advice is to get there at the 5:30 opening or earlier, get your names down, and then go somewhere nearby for drinks to wait for the best Italian meal of your life. 

We inhaled the two fried balls that make up the "Cacio e Pepe Fritelle", a delicious appetizer and creative approach to the traditional cacio e pepe. The dish is on the heavier side - creamy, cheesy and bursting with carbs. 

We dug into the "Mafaldini with Pink Peppercorn" next. Mafaldini means 'badly cut' pasta but this dish was far from badly done. The malfadini is similar to a cacio e pepe - imagine melted butter and parmigiano-reggiano with a dash of pink peppercorns. The pasta shape is very unique and the flavors blended to create a creamy, wholesome dish with a bit of spice and heat. 

The star of the night was the "Sheeps Milk Cheese-filled Agnolotti"- I could eat this again and again and forever if I could. A supple golden-yellow dough gently wrapped around a sheet of sheep's milk ricotta and feta sits in a broth of melted butter, honey and saffron. Soft dried tomatoes dot this velvety landscape, adding a sharp, acidic element to this otherwise very creamy dish. The flavors, textures and smells just worked so insanely well - I was blown away by the creativity of this agnolotti. 

Highly recommend this dining experience with anyone who has an afternoon to kill waiting for walk-in opinions. It's near impossible to get a reservation here for good reason.

My significant other and I sat at the bar for dinner this week. The waitress was not particularly keen on explaining the items in the menu nor the wine by the glass so I'm not sure if this approach is specific to this server or to the restaurant; she also wanted all the food ordered in one go which seems unreasonable if you don't know how hungry you'll be after you eat a few plates.  The food was good and the ambiance was good but it was not a stellar experience for us.
Aw man this stuff is to die for I love it and everyone should check it out! Tell them I sent ya lol

Lilia has been on my radar for quite some time and I finally had the opportunity to go on a Friday night for dinner a few weeks ago. A friend and I stopped by around 6:30pm to put our names on the wait list. The hostess said it would be around 10pm until we would be called, which was perfect because we had somewhere to go in between. I received a text around 9:30pm letting me know that our table was ready. 

We sat down at a table outside and it didn't seem to be overly busy where we were sitting, probably because it was so late. After looking at the menu, we decided we wanted to try so many items and it would be best to share a bunch of things. 

For starters: 
-Cacio e Pepe Fritelle: Fried balls of cacio pepe, which were delicious but a bit heavy and probably not necessary if you're ordering a bunch of pasta dishes. I definitely liked but  could've done without them. 
-Roasted Trumpet Mushrooms, Arugula, Balsamic, Sicilian Almonds: SO great and really unique. Wasn't that large of a portion, however, the mushrooms were excellent and definitely worth trying. 
-Whole Artichoke, Garlic, Mint, Parmigiano, Breadcrumbs: EXCELLENT! one of the best things we ate. So delicious and simple. 
-Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs: Really delicious and unique as they're grilled. Most places bake clams and the chili gave them a nice kick. 

For mains: 
-Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano: So delicious and tasted like cacio pepe. The pasta shape was really great and we enjoyed this pasta! 
-Ricotta Gnocchi, Broccoli Pesto, Basil, Pistachios: Really didn't love this dish. I'm a HUGE pesto fan and it just really didn't do it for us. Maybe the broccoli made the pesto sauce taste a bit bitter, but in comparison to the other dishes it wasn't that great. 
-Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey: The best pasta we ordered. The milk cheese filled pasta was soft and delicious. Really loved it and would highly recommend.

Overall had a great experience and really glad I was able to try out Lilia. It was quite pricey with drinks ~$200, but now we know what we like for next time. We were overly full at the end of the meal that we didn't have enough room for dessert. Definitely try out Lilia if you have time to put your name on the wait list or if you're lucky enough to get a reservation!

I was super excited to try this place, as I had heard GREAT things from others who had eaten here. We had the clams, mozzarella, cacio e pepe balls and gnocchi. The clams were definitely my favorite of the mix. I really enjoyed the other dishes, but I found they were a bit salty. I'm a huge salt lover to a fault, so for me to say that means there's probably a bit too much. I also see there's mention of the same in other reviews.

As for the ambience...it's beautiful. The space looks like a renovated warehouse with worn touches throughout the walls and floor. The service was also great, we received attention to detail that you'd normally see in a Michelin rated restaurant.

Overall, I'm giving 4/5, because although we had a nice time, they really should cut back on the salt.
One of THE best pasta dinners we have ever had! Came here for date night with the hubby. All of our dishes were delicious! Highly recommend coming here. Worth the wait. Definitely make reservations.

I think this is the best meal I've ever had in my life. I can't begin to describe how wonderfully complex the most simple of dishes are. 

Getting there: did not make a reservation. Arrived on a Friday night at 5:15 (they open at 5:30). Were probably ~15-20 people in front of us (basically enough to fill the bar and a table or 2 outside). We could've been seated right away but said we wanted to come back for a more normal hour so they took our name and said ~7-730. Then got drinks at William Vale.

Starters: radishes w ricotta, focaccia, grilled blowfish tails
Pasta: Mafaldine, agonolotti 
Main: veal flank steak

For Pete's sake order the focaccia. I usually am not one to fill up on bread at restaurants but it's heavenly.

Usually love this place but visited tonight for a friends birthday and had a not so perfect experience:

- it was unbearably hot. we asked multiple times if they could adjust the temp down but was told that's just how it is there where we were sitting. very disappointing when you're trying to enjoy a heavy Italian meal. later in the night they could have easily moved us to another open table but never offer d and just brought ice water to placate us.

- our waitress was very rude and not at all attentive.  We saw her once every blue moon and we caught her rolling her eyes at us multiple times. she's obviously too cool to work there and should live her best life outside the customer service world.

- service was incredibly slow. I've been here many times in the past, seems to have really gone down hill. We had about 45 min between dishes.

2 stars because the food was great but the experience was subpar.
-

Came here on a whim during a day trip to NY after finding it on a bunch of food bloggers lists and IG posts. Arrived around 4:40 to try our luck as a walk in and the line was about 20 people deep. The restaurant itself isn't very large and reservations are about 30 days out so walk in at opening is your best bet. We ended up waiting about 30 min for outdoor seating once we got our names on the list. The indoor seating option was a 5 hour wait since that's reserved for the reservations. We started with the night's special, foccacia with a ramp garlic butter that we gave a 5/5 we followed with the spicy lamb fettuccini 4/5 and the malfadini 3/5. Both pastas were fresh and tasty but nothing wowed us like the bread. Service was amazing, very attentive and gave recommendations. Not sure it would be worth the month wait but would come back to try other things.

Absolutely amazing. All the food is unique and well prepared sourced from some of the best ingredients. This will definitely not be my last time visiting. Service food and ambiance were all outstanding.

Nicely prepared, interesting dishes in a sleek space with courteous service.

Get the mozzarella toast, clams, and linguine. The dishes are pretty small so great for sharing and tasting lots of different things. 

Great for a nice dinner for two or four.

I was given a gift certificate for my anniversary in April 2018 so my husband and I could celebrate our anniversary. It is now 4 months later and I can never find any available reservations to this restaurant. When I call I never get a human voice. This is absolutely ridiculous. If they cannot accommodate reservations, they should not sell gift certificates. I am ready to go and collect the money that was paid to them and go and enjoy a long awaited dinner with my husband in a less popular but accommodating restaurant. I hope they refund gift certificates that they cannot accommodate.
The food and service was excellent! Everything was seasoned to perfection. Great date spot!

I wanted to like Lilia more and maybe it's because my expectations were so high but I was slightly disappointed. We couldn't get a reservation for ages and then finally secured one for 10PM on a Sunday. We were seated outside but the tables were really rocky and the chairs were extremely uncomfortable (think not great patio type furniture). 

We got the mushrooms and cacio e pepe croquettes. The mushrooms were really good and the croquettes were pretty good too but they were really dry and there was no sauce or anything to help it out. For mains we went with the mafaldini, agnolotti, and rigatoni. The rigatoni and agnolotti were pretty good but the mafaldini was a little salty. All the pasta was cooked well but nothing was as amazing as I expected it to be. 

We had gelato for dessert and it was actually horrible - weirdly icy and just icky. Plus side, service was really great.

4.0
Month: August 2018
Day and time: Saturday evening

Food: 4-5 stars
We ordered the cacio e pepe fritelle, the cauliflower, the mafaldini, the gnocchi, the agnolotti, and the black bass. The fritelle are essentially fried cheese balls, and I highly recommend you start your meal with the trio. While not stuffed full, each ball comes with plenty of soft cheese. The coating is heavily seasoned with black pepper, providing a salty start to the experience which suited my palate. The green and white cauliflower came with spicy soppressata and was pleasant but uninspiring. The fish was soft and melted in the mouth, but the salsa verde was a little overwhelming and I found myself pushing some away to allow the bass to shine. The three pasta dishes were good to outstanding. The agnolotti was filled with sheep's milk cheese, and paddled in a shallow pool of honey and saffron. I enjoyed the creamy cheese but the pungency of the saffron soured the honey. The gnocchi came with broccoli pesto and pistachios, and was the heartiest of the three pastas. The mafaldini came with pink peppercorn and parmagiano and was my favorite. Usually, the pasta sacrifices itself to bring out the flavor of the other ingredients, and rarely does it steal the show. Not so here. The ribbons were oaky in flavor and tough in texture. The peppercorn and parmigiano provided light variety. I wish I had ordered a bowl to myself.

Setting & Atmosphere: 4 stars
The ceilings are high, the windows, are long, and the lighting is low. The combination creates a soothing atmosphere, and the noise level simmered but never boiled. The walls are light in color and are paired from above with distressed wood rafters.

Drink: 3-4 stars
I drank a boulevardier which was a little light on rye. Most of the cocktail list is gin-based, though the presence of mezcal in the Milano Sour caught my eye. There are 5-6 whites and 5-6 reds offered by the glass, and my partner tried a couple of the latter before finding one that matched her tastes.

Service: 2-3 stars
We had no complaints about our service once we were seated, save for a little tardiness in bringing the appetizer. Our server was polite and helpful and added value when choosing wine. However, we were disappointed by the service from entering the restaurant to being seated. Despite arriving on time for our reservation, we waited 35 minutes for our table with no indication given for its ETA, and no apology provided afterwards. 

Value: 4 stars
There are barely any dishes - if any - over $30. For a restaurant of this reputation and standard of cooking, that is somewhat staggering. We over-ordered slightly, and took some home. The pasta dishes are a little small to eat as individual entrees, but three between two goes perfectly.

Return: Yes
You could come to Lilia and choose five dishes at random and I guarantee you would enjoy your meal; or, you could come to Lilia and choose five dishes carefully and really enjoy your meal. Lilia's food has a high floor and a high ceiling, and that's hard to find. I trust the poor table management was a one-off.

Lives up to the hype! Be warned - the wait is usually incredibly long, unless you arrive at 5 or 5:30 and can be one of the lucky 10-15 people who are seated right away (as we did). We sat at the bar, which was very pleasant and a perfectly good alternative to actually getting a table at this trendy hot spot.

Definitely recommend sharing as much as you can, as everything is delicious, and you'll be limited if you only order for yourself. We started with chicken liver crostini (rich, meaty, and incredibly indulgent), roasted mushrooms (briny and packed with umami flavor), cured sardines (accompanied by curls of cold butter on thin crostini), mafaldini (a modern twist on the classic cacio e pepe) and mezzaluna (creamy, light and bursting with the flavor or spring). As unbelievable as each dish was, I got food envy at the other dishes I saw being served nearby. I know we could have ordered an entirely different set of dishes and still been as wowed by the food.

Service friendly and down to earth. Would love to come back!

Taking into consideration the hype, the pricepoint, and the difficulty of getting a reservation here - I found my experince at Lilia to be pretty unremarkable.

Atmosphere: While the vibe inside seemed pretty cozy, we chose to sit outside as the weather was pretty nice. However, (and I can't believe I'm being picky about this but it actually affected our experience) the furniture outside is extremely uncomfortable - I would not recommend sitting outside.

Food: The Cacio E Pepe Fritelli was good, but would have been better if it was accompanied by some sauce to dip it in. Thought the Mafaldini and Rigatoni Diavola were both pretty average (the flavors were good but nothing to rave about; pasta noodles themselves were pretty thick and chewy). The one item that I thought really stood out was the Sheeps Milk Cheese filled Agnolotti - the pasta was so thin, it felt handmade, and the taste was unique and delicious. For dessert, we opted for gelato, which ended up being pretty icy/watery and disappointing.

Maybe we just didn't orders the right items? But again, overall, thought my experience here was pretty average.

We arrived shortly after 5:00pm on a Sunday and waited about 1.5 hours for a table for two which wasn't so bad. I read a few Yelp reviews that mentioned you should get here before or right around 5:00pm to put your name in because they stop taking names fairly early in the night. That was a very helpful tip that probably helped us get a table! Anyway, despite being sat at the bar, we received fantastic service throughout our dinner. Our plates and silverware were cleared after each course and the staff was very attentive. Now I'll get down to business and list out our food choices and my personal favs.

Starters
We had the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle (fried balls of goodness that are surprisingly light) and the Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga. Both are amazing and the perfect portion to hold you over for the main show without filling you up too much.

Pasta
The Agnolotti (Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey) is a MUST. This is amazing and my only regret is not getting my own order of this. We also had the Fettuccine (Fettuccine, Spicy Lamb Sausage, Tomato Passato). This was good but honestly, it was VERY salty. I would skip this.

Meat
We ended our meal with the Veal Flank Steak (Grilled Veal Flank Steak, Hot Peppers, Basil) and this was AMAZING. We had no idea what to expect but we truly loved this dish.

In addition to the two starters and three entrees, my boyfriend had two cocktails and I had two glasses of wine. The bill with tax and tip came to around $100 pp which is what we were expecting. This is certainly on the pricier side for Italian but you should also know what to expect before dining here.

Overall Lilia is great to try at least once. Because of the price, I likely won't be back for awhile but I would definitely recommend Lilia if you haven't been here yet!
Everything about this place was fantastic. The vibe is just right, the food special, and the service very friendly and on-point. Don't forget to order the soft serve.

Loved everything about this place. Two of us got there at 4:30pm on a Saturday and there was already a short line formed. We waited and then got a seat at the bar upon opening. Service is sharp, knowledgeable, and friendly. We could see Chef Missy in the kitchen tasting food, expediting, etc. The food was outstanding. We had the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle, Housemade Mozzarella, Mafaldini, and the 32oz Ribeye with Crispy Potatoes. The only downside was not being able to order more food because we were full, the food we had was all delicious and the plates we saw coming out looked great too. I've been to many a Steakhouse and this steak was up there as one of the best I've had anywhere.

This review is only for the cafe part as I did not dine in the restaurant portion.

Staff was rude. Asked about vanilla flavoring and was met with a harsh response of not mixing flavor in with their coffee as if it is so good it should leave untainted; Yet there is sugar and cream available, ingredients used to alter the taste of their precious coffee. 

I do not like this trend of holier than thou coffee establishments that are pretentious AF, as if their coffee is a gift to me and I should be humbled to be allowed to try it. The coffee wasn't even good (this is my opinion of whatever blend/bean I was given).

Avoid this place unless you are a glutton for punishment.

Good food, good service but tries a little too hard to be an exclusive restaurant. Plenty of tables available in the bar and patio which are available for walk ins yet they stand by their "hour and a half wait time." 

If you want to wait a month out to get a reservation, go to Carbone instead.

My wife and I stood in line at 4:30 to get a seat at the bar.  There were a lot of people waiting in line, looks like this place became popular cause they won an award, so we definitely wanted to check it out.

Very nice staff, prices are reasonable, and the food was good, but not worth the line or wait.  The focaccia bread was probably the favorite thing we ate.  The Cacio e Pepe balls were good, but the little gem salad was overly acidic. Pasta was decent and cooked just right.

Honestly, I prefer La Pecora Bianca over this place, if I was forced to choose.  But all in all, congrats on the award and looking forward to come back one day!

I recently came here with 2 friends on a Monday night after we had made a reservation a month prior. It's pretty hard to get a spot, we had to call exactly 30 days before at 9am and even then got the last one. 

First things first, the ambiance is great. It's warm yet trendy, and just far enough away from the Williamsburg main stretch that it feels quiet. 

I'd heard great things beforehand so was super excited to try it, especially the pasta. We started the freshly baked bread. It was honestly some of the best bread I've ever had, and the green butter (!!!). I don't even know what it was but it's amazing. The cucumber appetizer was good, but nothing extraordinary. 

Now onto the pastas: we ordered the mafaldini, ricotta gnocchi, and the agnolotti. All were delicious, but the best was without a doubt the agnolotti (not pictured because we had no patience) - it stole the show and was truly amazing and unlike anything I've ever had. SO good. Second favorite was the gnocchi, then the mafaldini. Would order everything again except that probably. 

We finished with the chocolate torta. It was decent but the pasta was for sure the highlight here. 

Definitely give it a go if you're able to get a reservation. And if not, it will be worth the wait.

I went in with the highest of expectations headed in recommendations. This probably would have been a 5 star review had it not had as much hype around it. The blowfish tail was one of the best and most interesting things I've ever eaten. I wish the pasta was a little tougher and most variety of spice. It felt as if every dish had the same kick. Artichoke was great and interesting to eat.

OH MY GOSH, top 10 restaurant I've been to in NYC. If you go, you must ask to be served by Marcus. He makes the experience THAT much better with his knowledge of all of the dishes and his passion and authenticity as he describes dishes and flavors... it's truly like he's putting in a show. On top of that, all other management and staff we interacted with were unbelievably charming, kind and professional. Cacio e pepe fritelle Balls - get 2 orders (that good). OH and the vanilla gelato with olive oil... never heard of a weirder combination that tasted like a million bucks. 13/10 Lilia!

I've waited months to get a reservation here as most of you know it always packed. This was the most disappointing experience to date. We started with the focaccia. It's house baked and honestly to die for. I wish the rest of the meal followed suit. Next was the whole braised artichoke. It's braised and tender, coated in breadcrumbs and stale chili flakes. I don't get it. No salt, no acid, no flavor. It's just a mushy artichoke that's so drenched in breadcrumbs. Next was the cured sardines. They would be tasty if not served over a roll literally a cigar worth of butter and a pound of lemon zest. You can't taste the fish just butter and lemon on toast. I hoped the pastas would be better. Broccoli pesto gnocchi is tough and chewy. I would have thought it's store bought potato gnocchi at best. Lamb sausage fettuccine is also pathetic. Sausage is crispy shreds as if they scraped the crumbs off the pan of previously served rack and the fettuccine, not house made - not cooked enough. The worst part is the manager brings over a soft serve ice cream sundae with a candle, says " I heard it's someone's birthday" (it wasn't) then admits "well I brought this because I heard the meal wasn't enjoyed." We kindly declined and left. I don't understand why Lilia is busting at the seams with reservations. Chef of the year never. You couldn't pay me to eat here again.

This place reminds me of LA's Bestia - super exposed, industrial looking restaurant with lots of well sourced ingredients. Unfortunately, besides the clams (which were delicious), everything else, including the famed pastas, just wasn't that tasty or great. And the price wasn't gentle either. Reservations are hard to come by, but walk-ins are possible, just be prepared to wait at the bar in the back and you'll probably be seated outside (if it's nice weather). Lilia isn't worth the wait.

Went for the first time. Waitress had a chip on her shoulder- we had more fun with the assistants and servers. Portions small, sometimes cold and very salty. Dash of red pepper flakes on most dishes- we had the artichoke, zucchini, mushroom, scallops, anchovy spaghetti, rigatoni... Rigatoni is super spicy. House butter is fantastic -still wondering how it's green!!

Today's our anniversary. We were so excited to eat at Lilia. My boyfriend had planned for us to get there at 8. In hopes to at least be seated by 9:30. 

We tried to put our names on the list and the HOSTESS LAUGHED at us and said you can but we may not be able to seat you. Earliest possibility is 10:30. 

I just think the customers service was terrible. No interest in eating here based on insensitive staff.
The food was excellent, the service was good, but all of the employees look sad :(  The artichoke was the highlight, I'd come back.

Tried the cacio e pepe fritters, blowfish tails, malfaldini and sheep anglonotti. Everything was great, service was attentive. We started with a dirty martini which was underrated-ly amazing.  For me the MUST TRY was the blowfish tails. You pick it up and eat it like chicken wings. They were to die for. Would definitely come back for a special occasion

This is hands down one of my favorite places in Williamsburg! We got four different pastas but my favorite was the spicy sauced pasta. The dishes are reasonably priced and very delicious. We had to wait 3 weeks for the reservation but it was worth it.

Ambiance was nice but food isn't worth the hype. The foods was all served lukewarm, not really what I'm into when you order grilled blowfish tail (obviously it was sitting out for sometime. Pasta was cold and microwaved to be hot (the bowl was then super hot and the food still not. Waiter was rude. Smallest pours of wine I've seen in nyc (literally half glasses). Not worth the hype.

The hour long wait is worth it. While I turn a blind eye on Italian food because I prefer food that has bold and spicy flavors, this place exceeded my expectations with every dish bursting with flavor. We ordered the foccacia bread, scallops, chicken, and sea bass. I didn't take any pictures because I was in a food coma when I took a bite of the bread; it was garnished with fresh Parmesan and truffle mushrooms. Sea bass was cooked until perfection with the verde sauce.

Came here for my birthday two months ago and forgot to write a review ! I know everyone is probably wondering if the food was worth the price and it most definitely is!

The ambiance is very intimate and would be perfect for a fancy date with your special someone! and also to get here it's gonna take you a month so make sure if you have an event you book in advanced ! The location in Brooklyn is nice although it's on an odd corner but who cares !

For the food: Amazing, fresh and AUTHENTIC. The Cacio e Pepe balls are a MUST When ordering appetizers. For the entrees I had to try the spicy rigatoni (I believe that's what it is) they cooked it perfectly, the sauce tasted like it was from a garden and they put amazing seasoning that you could clearly taste. My boyfriend got the steak and they put some type of vinegar on it that complimented it PERFECTLY. 

I would also try the wine as they have a great selection, they even try it before to make sure it's good which is very impressive to me. As for the dessert, I got the chocolate gelato which was good but when comparing it to actual gelato from Italy, nothing to go home about. 

The only thing I wish was better was the service. My waiter was very nice but I didn't see him much and he didn't check up on us to see how our food was (something you expect from an expensive restaurant) Other than that I had a great experience and I will DEFINITELY be back.

Don't go there !! Beyond rude hostesses!!! I 
Totally not worth it !!!!call ahead .. is this Chile's ?? Poorly handling of the customer.. bTW there were empty tables

I just did a random walk in.  

I read about the place and was walking past an they were about to open - so lined up at 5 and got seated at 540. I was solo and sat at the bar it was cute, and had a nice bar mate.  

The bartender was nice at first but he ket ramping up the hassling - i asked for a wine suggestion - of course he suggested the most expensive one - hmmm - i ordered 3 courses and and he put down one course - then added the second so there were  2 together in front of me - i was feeling rushed - which i didn't love -  but i said 'ok' it was only 6pm at this point - then he asked if he could add my entre to the other 2 dishes still sitting in font of me... to sit in front of me -- why? Let me eat and enjoy... and he kept asking if i wanted another drink... i finally told him i just wanted to eat in my own time  - still not even 630 pm - my bar mate was rolling his eyes at this point about the bartender.  this is not cool.  

Then i finished my first 2 courses - and my entre was placed in front of me IMMEDIATELY - woah - can you let me breathe for 2 mins.  And he was whispering to the manager - clearly about me (IN FRONT OF ME) - 

Again NOT cool.  I hope they read these reviews... i was out of there (disgruntled) - by 6:45pm - $130 lighter - for one person....feeling v hassled - if you are having a $15 dollar burger yes ? Maybe?  Ok hassle me... if i sit there beyond 45 mins but really? - it was a  crazy - one bar seat ... A massive turn off (!) and the food was ok - tasty  - nice homestyle Italian ... Nice simple food - but no better than NAKED DOG in Greenpoint -  northern Italian delish in a modern setting -  i felt so rushed honestly it was hard to enjoy -  i am not sure f the bartender is just a jerk looking for more $$ pr he was told to do this by management either way rude and annoying.  for context i am a middle aged adult - who has eaten in the best restaurants around the world - ....i hope they read this and adjust -  it was a little shocking...

I really did love this restaurant- the food is wonderful, the setting is divine and the service is always great. But tonight I had an experience that left me very upset and I do not plan to return to your restaurant.  

I've been here countless times, I recommend it to friends whenever they are in town and have had some lovely meals at Lilia. Last night, I went with my sister and her boyfriend for a quiet late night bite and a negroni. Our server was a total sweetheart and very attentive. The food was delicious, especially the spaghetti limone and the salads we tried. 

At the end of our meal, we paid our bill and my sister and I walked to the bathroom together as she lives across the country and we rarely have the opportunity to see one another and catch up. She also had a tampon in her bag and I was in need of it. As we close the door to the restroom a woman with short dark hair abruptly rushes and opens the door and says "sorry girls, you can't do this here- only one person in the bathroom at one time." I said, "Oh, ok. Well, we are sisters and she was giving me a tampon, we will be quick!" Woman to woman, I thought she would see that I was a girl in need. She instead chose to scoff at me and loudly, in front of other diners at this restaurant said, "That's not what you are doing and your "sister" can give you a "tampon" out here." Mind you the out here she was referring to was the middle of the restaurant. I was so shocked, I just walked out of the restroom and stood awkwardly while all eyes looked over at me! I could not believe that this woman who I assume must be a manager there as she was not in whites or the server uniform, who works at this fine restaurant would try to publicly shame me and insinuate that I was doing or using drugs. 

My sister and I were very upset, we told the bartenders who were working there and asked them, "Is that a policy you have?" They replied, "NOT at ALL! We are so very sorry." 

Bottom line is, after spending a not insignificant amount of money at this restaurant we were basically shamed by this woman who spoke to us in a truly awful and accusatory tone.

A group of friends and I enjoyed an evening here recently and it was totally worth the hype. We made a reservation a month in advance as we were a party of 6 and we couldn't have been happier with our experience. Our serve was attentive and helpful with suggesting menu items and the space was nice with lots of natural light and not too much noise. 
We ordered several appetizers. That was hands down our favorite part of the mean. We ordered the split peas, cauliflower, home made mozzarella garlic toast, and clams. Absolutely delicious. Only wish we'd have ordered the artichoke. 
For main dishes I ordered fettuccine, spicy lamb sausage, tomato passato. It was just the right flavor with the tomato based sauce and not too spicy. The fettuccine was fresh and cooked perfectly. 
For dessert we enjoyed chocolate soft serve with salted hazelnuts. Yum! 
We will definitely be back.
@wtelle

This cute Italian spot in Brooklyn is a must try. But you'll have to earn it- we arrived right at 530pm on a Tuesday when the opened, and the wait was two and a half hours! You CAN make reservations 30 days in advance, but I hear they go within minutes. You can walk in and put your name on a list for bar seats, though. There's a small little bar area in the very back you can have a glass of wine and snacks at while you wait. Wait time is very accurate, we sat at about 745. 

The food - fantastic. We got two apps - the artichoke and the cauliflower, both spectacular. And three pasta dishes- the rigatoni, the Mafaldini, and the Agnolotti. The latter is a MUST- savory and sweet delicious pillows of pasta. Probably wouldn't get the rigatoni again as that felt pretty standard (like a make at home type dish, pasta and red sauce), but would get the Mafaldini again. Portions were also much bigger then I expected. Decent size bowl for a tapas esq place. 

The bartender wasn't that great so I took a star off for service / friendliness. 

The L train is around the corner so was a quick subway ride from the city.

We had a tough time getting into Lilia. We tried walking in a couple times only to find that their waitlist was closed. We decided to make a reservation which had to be a month in advance. I'd recommend planning accordingly.

We started with Cacio e Pepe Fritelle. This was a hallow ball of fried dough with cheese that was dusted with pecorino cheese. It was an interesting item that I haven't tried before. I thought the crispy outside juxtaposed with the hallow, airy inside made for an interesting contrast.

Next, we shared chicken liver crostini. I'd highly recommend this dish. The liver was light and moussey. It had a light, delicate flavorful. It was topped with a grilled onion which helped mellow out the flavor making it more palatable for those who haven't eaten chicken liver before.

For our main course, we shared two pasta dishes. I picked the mafaldini with pink peppercorns while my girlfriend selected the ricotta gnocchi with pesto and pistachios. Both were good, but I'd recommend the mafaldini. I enjoyed the smooth yet jagged texture of the pasta. The  sauce and seasoning was delicious and savory.

We had a great time at Lilia on a Sunday night. We were seated right away and pretty much liked everything we ordered. Ambiance is nice but it was almost as warm inside as it was outside on a hot summer day. Service was excellent from the host to the busser. Our waiter Taulant was great and very knowledgable about the cooking process and flavor profile of every dish on the menu.  
Now on to the food- The cacio e pepe fritelle were soft and flavorful but a bit salty. We also enjoyed the artichoke and mozzarella garlic bread. The agnolotti was definitely the standout for us. Tender pasta and filling that melts in your mouth and the saffron honey sauce is subtle. The mafaldini and cappelletti were also well received by our table. I've had better gnocchi though so I would pass on that next time. The veal was also very tender and well seasoned.

The hype is real, but it is not perfect. Clams were boring and I expected a little more for the price. Pastas are great as was the fish but overall I think I was expecting more because of all the press.

A true gem in Brooklyn, this creative Italian restaurant exists in an eclectic old auto body shop. With its latest addition to the James Beard list the reservations for this place fill up fast, a month in advance but the food is well worth it. The wood fired Italian specialities are full of flavors. Got the homemade mozzarella on garlic bread, pesto & pistachio gnocchi, striped bass with golden Yukon potatoes, spicy lamb sausage pasta and finished with chocolate gelato on the hottest day in New York. Perfect evening paired with great wines. Must try!!

I have had dinner here about 3/4 times.  

Service is a 3.  For the attitude they have they should be more knowledgable on food and wine.  They act like they are too good to make a drink or be in the service industry but yet... here they are.
Kitchen staff is knowledgeable and seems truly interested in the the industry (We stayed late enough one night to close down the place)

Food is a full 5.
Cacio e Pepe Fritelle- these were a surprise for me and really good.
Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga- Pass you can make this at home.
Radishes, Whipped Ricotta- Crisp and refreshing would suggest as an In between courses.
Artichoke- Love but not a must.  Love the butter and lemon broth to dip. 
Clams-Can't stop thinking about.  Crispy breadcrumbs and juicy clams. A MUST
Little Gem Lettuce- A must really perfect salad.
Roasted Escarole- delish.  Sloppy goodness! Charred escarole with a delicious dressing.
Sardines- Cured and just what they say they are.. Tasty pickled onions
Veal Steak- Loved the fresh raw greens on top. Peppers/Basil
Rib Eye bone special- I would definitely have this a table for 4 even to have a few pieces of.  It comes sliced with the bone on the plate- great presentation and grilled perfectly. 

This place is a real show stopper for the food.  If the kitchen could serve it this would be a full 5.

Very sad experience over all. Had such high hopes for a delicious meal. Unfortunately we were never seated.  Came in at 8:20 for what they told us would be an hour wait, and were able to get a seat at the bar and later moved outside to wait a bit more.    We ordered a delicious app of fresh mozzarella. And so looking forward to more.  And three drinks a piece.  The bartenders were lovely but it seems like the front of the house fell short in finding us a table, even after sweet bartenders tried to find out what was holding us up. More than two hours later we called it a night. While it seemed that many others who came in after us got seated.  A great disappointment given that we had flown in from Illinois for our 25th wedding anniversary and wanted the full Brooklyn  experience. Actually spoke with and saw Missy briefly when we first arrived and knew she was there, but clearly not managing her front of house staff well.  We have reservations at meadowsweet tomorrow and anticipate much more accommodating service.
Great food and service I was so busy I forgot to review but it's a great spot and they deliver to the Hilton and any hotel on Collins strip. Enjoy
First time ever! I was very impressed with the taste, look, texture of all the foods. I recommend all of them. Enjoy!

Really don't understand the hype with this place! Pasta is nice but pretty average.  Drink measures seem very small, a friend joked it was like getting a shot of wine as opposed to a glass and the service was rushed.  I was so excited to go there and really disappointed overall!

One of the best restaurants I have been too.  We got the artichoke starter, raddiches, focaccia special and gnocchi ricotta pesto.  All the dishes were amazing.  Highly recommend this place.  We were fortunate to walk in and sit at the bar right when opened. Recommend a reservation or show up early and be patient. It also seemed as thought  there weren't reservations for sitting outside so that's an option without a reservation.

Its a solid 4/5 for food

Its a solid 1/5 for noise and acoustics :(

Pass on the Cauliflower......but I could eat a starter order of both the mushrooms and the grilled scallop dishes and will have problems trying something else as they were that good and I'd insist on ordering them again :)

Everyone seems to rave about the fettuccine and lamb.....I'd pass BUT the Rigatoni was excellent (we had the agnolotti as well....which were good....best would be better in bigger size pieces.

Try and go during the day/nice night so you can sit outdoors as even the quietest table inside has noise issues.......

I got in line (it was pretty long) a few minutes before 5 PM on a Saturday, and the line just kept getting longer and longer behind me!  I was maybe 15 tables back in line and the couple in front of me had a 15-20 min wait time quoted to them. Again as a single diner, I got lucky and snagged a spot at the bar. There are an odd number of sears at the bar, so assuming mostly couples come in, if you come alone, you might be able to get a seat like me! 

Everyone sat down at the same time, and the bartender was busy fixing drinks so it took him a few minutes to get to me to take my order. That was okay with me as I was busy trying to figure out exactly what to order.

I started with the stuffed artichoke. Because I've never had one as good as my Italian grandmother made, and this looked like it could come close. I was right; it's the closest I've ever had!  

Next I had the Mafaldini (Pink Peppercorn, Parmigiano).  The pasta was perfectly aldente. The pink peppercorn was more mild than traditional pepper, which I liked, and it added a saltiness as well.  This was a solid dish and my favorite of the 3 pastas I ordered. 

Next came the sheeps milk filled agnolotti and the pesto gnocchi. 

The gnocchi was a bit denser than I personally prefer for a gnocchi.  The pesto was okay, and the pistachios added a nice crunch but they were hard to taste. 

The agnolotti was creamy and the honey was sweet as you might imagine. It wasn't a combo I ever would have thought of. It was okay, and was good to try once, but I didn't like it as much as I hoped I would. 

Finally I had the chocolate soft serve with chocolate espresso powder. Man was this good! I love soft serve!! 

Overall this was a solid pasta spot and I would tell my friends to come check it out!

We went on a Thursday night without reservations and were seated approximately 2 hours later. The grilled clams were delicious but it went down hill after that. Our second appetizer was the mozzarella bread which was nothing special. All the entrees were disappointing. Linguine with lamb sausage was overly salty. The diavlo pasta tasted like deli food. The lamb steak was extremely bland. Food took a while to come out. Service was good.

I had been looking forward to going to Lilia with my boyfriend for months. We would set alarms at midnight to try and book reservations at this trendy spot as calling in or booking online a couple weeks out is a no go for this place. Finally in May we got a 9:30pm reservation for my birthday in June. That was the absolute earliest time we could get and that is for us booking a full month in advance. Finally my birthday comes around and I'm so excited to finally try Lilia. We grab drinks to kill time beforehand by my office in Manhattan and at 8:30pm he receives a text saying that we've been pushed to 9:45. Okay, only 15 minutes late but still i'm a little annoying seeing that we did our due diligence by booking so far in advance. Then we get to Lilia a little before 9:40 and they tell us our table is "being prepared". They told us we could get drinks at their cafe but we were so hungry at this point that we did not want to go far from the hostess area. It then took another 20 minutes for them to seat us. We were not sat until 10pm! And we originally booked for 9:30.  As someone that works in the Hospitality industry at a luxury hotel, I found this to be incredibly rude. This was not hospitality at all. No apologies either - I couldn't believe it. We then were sat (right next to the door) and we asked our waiter for a bottle of wine that was similar to a Riesling since I did not see one on the menu. He comes back five minutes later with the bottle already opened and he started pouring out red wine! I politely asked him if this was his choice close to the white wine that I had asked for and he mumbled something saying it was a mistake and he must be tired. While the food was definitely great (the spaghetti in particular), this entire seating situation followed by the wine incident left a bad taste in my mouth. Definitely not the birthday dinner that I had been dreaming of.

Lilia in one word: exquisite. I'm not sure why anyone described the service as pretentions, the hostess and wait stuff were so friendly. Our server described every dish so perfectly, we knew exactly what to expect with every course, which was super helpful when we were on the fence about some items. We had the mozzarella and focaccia. The garlic dotedfocaccia was like a cloud on the inside and the green tinted butter just made it. Be ready to carb load because the pasta is a must! The agnolotti and the gnocchi were outstanding. It seems that every ingredients had a purpose and things aren't just thrown in to make a dish. The agnolotti was probably one of the best pastas I've ever had. My husband and I also split the grilled bass topped with salsa verde, divine and so tender. There was definitely nothing missing from this meal. Prices are reasonable for the quality.

I will say the portions are on the smaller side, which is to be expected at a restaurant like this, but still. Getting a reservation can take months, at ease, but of you make it here, you'll see why!

It is really hard to get into the resturant but if you can get a seat it is more than amazing.  The food and ambiance are top notch.  Try to arrive ~10 minutes before it opens for the best chance to just walk-in and get a seat.

I managed to score a Monday reservation on resy a month prior to my visit and gosh, did I feel lucky. 

This is one of the few Italian restaurants in nyc that I can confidently say is mindblowingly delicious and also unpretentious. The servers are patient and knowledgeable. 

We started off with the erbaluce wine, which I haven't had before. It was a uniquely minerally dry white. 

The chicken liver mousse on toast was probably not the dish I'd order again but I liked the fresh lemon flavor. The artichoke heart was fun to eat- I hadn't been to another restaurant before which serves the little leaves for you savor every bit of the artichoke. Blowfish tails were decadent and worth trying. The baked clams were smaller than I expected but love the heat from the chili. 

Now the pastas are a must. We tried the pink peppercorn mafaldini and the famed sheep cheese agnolotti. I savored every bite. The mafaldini was perfectly al dente and had the best chew I could imagine. It was a great twist to a cacio e pepe. I don't typically love stuffed pastas but the agnolotti was bold and heavenly. The honey, saffron all complemented the sheeps cheese. 

Finally, the Italian job (olive oil on gelato sorbet!) was the perfect end to our meal. 

I can't wait to come back. Highly recommend.

Pretty amazing meal. If you're without a reservation I'd recommend getting there at least 15 minutes before they open (either for lunch or dinner). My boyfriend and I arrived at Lilia at 4:30p on a Saturday, 30 minutes before they opened up their doors for dinner and there were still about two dozen people waiting around to walk-in without a reservation. Luckily we ended up snagging a good spot on the line and were able to be seated at an outdoor table pretty swiftly.

The service is quick and efficient, polite and helpful. The food? They were just honored with a James Beard recognition so enough said.

Bravo!

Now that I've read the reviews and didn't get the agnolotti I am thoroughly disappointed and can no longer review this place as I didn't follow the directions correctly. 
No but really this place was fantastic. Ended up coming on a whim and it took 45 minutes to sit at the bar (considering reservations were booked out, that's not too bad). Our server was really nice, getting to know our names and explain what half the menu was. Gave wine recommendations as well. I had the fettuccine and my partner had the veal steak. Both were incredible and filling. The asparagus appetizer was really good and had a unique taste I never experienced with it. A great combo of flavors. 
Left with full bellies and definitely would love to try some other pastas. The girl down the bar from us was sharing everything with two patrons that walked in at the end. She cracked me up. Just pouring stuff onto their plates. The feels when you sat in the wrong spot

so this was for the overall experience today. Lilia is definitely still our go to, a restaurant we know will not disappoint. with that said, the line has definitely become longer now with the patio open. we arrived 10 mins before 530 pm on a Friday. by the time we got to the door to put our names down, for the patio now, since the bar was all seafed. they said it would be another 20 mins before they could seat us - we understood given that they had a huge reservation and they wanted to ensure the kitchen didn't fall behind - fair. we got sat maybe 30-35 mins later, fine. it was nice out but it was our first time sitting outside and not right at the bar. 

once we sat, we ordered our usual, 2 claim starters and 3 pastas. the food took much much longer .. service was okay, nothing memorable but no complaints. the biggest disappointment was when the claims came our and the portion. was legitimately cut in half. it looked like the took ONE portion and split it in TWO. not 2 separate orders, i even have old pictures to reference that the plate was in fact full and you couldn't see the bottom of the plate. i wish i took a full picture of today's claims but there was definitely HALF of what we usually get, there was barely enough clams to fill the dish .. we're very confused and we didn't even know what to say. the price did not change so why did the portion get cut in half?

we weren't going to say anything until the end of the meal - fortunately the pastas were still delicious and just as consistent. but Lilia was a no brainer for us, completely based on its quality and consistency - now we're not sure we would go back, especially after the wait, not really pleased with the wait and the portion cut :/ the service was flawless and smooth when we sat at the bar (at least 2-3x we've sat there) so it's hard to go backwards from that.

When friends call and say that they have two open spots on their reservation at Lilia tonight; would you like to join them? You say yes. 

There was a literal rainbow out the window of the restaurant as we enjoyed a blissful dinner here - a perfect representation of our experience. 

The cacio e pepe donut hole-esque things are magical. Get at least one order. All of the pastas were crave worthy, but the agnolotti with saffron butter stood out as the clear favorite. 

The next time you find yourself up at midnight, make a reservation a month out (preferably with a few people who like to share) and start counting down the days.

After visiting Lilia, this restaurant has made its way to my top 5 restaurants in NYC. Anything with their salsa verde is worth ordering. I wish I could have eaten the whole menu. I don't even begrudge them for having a difficult time getting a reservation or a walk-in. This place is worth it.

What a wonderful experience!!! From A to Z this restaurant is one you cannot miss! Even though it is one of the most popular restaurants in NYC the staff treats everyone like royalty. I've been to restaurants all over the world and tonight my wife, daughter, and I experienced flavors that I have never had. The amounts they served were perfect, the pasta was perfectly al dente, the service was the best! Lilia is truly a well oiled machine! Missy Robbins you are blessed!

Massive pain to get a seat in this place but ended up being well worth it. While they do allow walk ins be prepared to wait a couple hours. 

After that highly recommend the clams, rigatoni and malfaldini finished with their ice cream.
We had a rez @ 7, but didn't get seated till 7.45.  Pasta was overcooked and salty.  This place is over rated.  The cocktails were good.

Were I judging Lilia on food alone, it would earn five stars, but with a caveat or two. The cacio e pepe fritters were a little loud, the gnocchi merely good, the pasta was superb...sophisticated...lighter than air. What pushes Lilia into holy-cow territory is the service, which was legendary. Our waiter was part storyteller and part teacher. He advised us thoughtfully as we made our way through the menu and served as cheerleader when each course came. 

By the end of this meal, I felt like I had really learned something about food. I'll be back.

If you're expecting for a stuffy restaurant experience, Lilia is not for you. Many of the other reviews are criticizing the place for their service. I for one do not need or want a server asking how's everything going when my mouth is full of food. I would have to agree with one thing, the place is NOT pretentious at all; but the hostess can give off that vibe from time to time. It's NY, I'll give it the pass for great food.

If you're just trying to eat simple delicious Italian, this is the place. Get the entire menu if possible.

the food here is just OK. we had two very unexceptional pasta dishes - one with anchovies and one with sausage. we left most of it. the chicken liver on toast was good but the brocollini was so chewy i couldn't swallow it and had to spit it out. very expensive very good wine made it all tolerable but no need to return.

The hostess, Rachel, was incredibly rude to us after waiting 2.5 hours for a table. She told us to get a glass of wine, that our table would be ready shortly and that she'd come get us in the bar area once it was available. We headed to the bar and she then texted that our table was ready and that we must return to the hostess stand or we'd risk losing our reservation. We returned urgently, canceling our drink orders so we didn't stress the bartenders on a very chaotic night. All that was fine. However, when we returned to the hostess stand we let them know about the text, but they then proceeded to ignore my husband and I for a solid 10 minutes (we timed it, bc it seemed so insane), as they proceeded to greet others, check them in and bring them to their tables. The craziest thing is that they legit would not make eye contact with us. It felt like we were annoying them? I mean, if we were going to wait for 10 minutes in a high traffic area of the restaurant, they should've just sent us back to the bar, where our presence as paying customers wouldn't somehow offend them. I finally asked if we should just go somewhere else and explained that we came running back under the threat that our res would be canceled and then were ignored. They simply said, "we're waiting on water glasses." I asked if we might possibly be seated without water glasses and they said, "We're not allowed." Any restaurant they prioritizes structure over customer satisfaction has it completely backwards. I understand the need to keep standards high and follow a regiment, but perhaps they might extend that to attitude and customer service? They reassured me that the table would be ready soon, that it HAD to be set properly, then the main hostess, Rachel, stormed off and came back with two water glasses on a tray and handed them off to her minion who led us to a table that -- guess what --- wasn't set at all! Once outside, she began awkwardly complementing my outfit and asking me where it was from and all these shallow attempts at pacification. We just needed an apology, or -- hey, to be treated kindly in the first place. When she approached the table she intended to take us to it appeared someone else had already been seated there and she instead seated us at a completely empty table (although THANK GOD, we had water glasses). Our meal was fine and the server was fine, if not a little disgruntled. Overall, I feel like the food is not nearly good enough to tolerate the terrible attitude of the employees. I would write this off to a bad night, but for the fact that the last time we tried to come here, I waited for 4 hours because they hostesses forgot to call me for my table instead giving it to someone else (They later provided the manager's card and phone number to request a table whenever we would like to make up for the bad experience. Please note, we still had to eat elsewhere that night at 9:30). Basically, I would never recommend this restaurant. We have a $250 gift card to the restaurant that we received as a gift, but we've hated our recent experiences so much so that I highly doubt we'll ever attempt to use it. Frankly, I'd rather pay $250 than ever go there again.
One of my favorite restaurants in Brooklyn. The service, the atmosphere, and most of all the FOOD was incredible. Couldn't recommend this place more. Good luck getting a reservation though...

I work in the area and stop by during lunch to make reservations for dinner. We like to eat at the bar me and my wife dinning out twice a week at the best restaurants in Manhattan and Brooklyn. Heard a lot of hype about thisplace. The hostess said 1st come 1st serve, But there's a waiting list. So we came at 5 o'clock, there was nobody in the restaurant, We asked the hostess to if we can eat at the bar she said, There is a wait, I said but there is nobody here nor waiting outside, She replied but there is a wait, So we waited at the back bar for a cocktail, The staff was very polite we ordered an appetizer the fresh mozzarella. It came out quite cold and  Dusted with some sort of spice. Why would you spice fresh mozzarella. Anyway as delightful as the back bar help was the to hostesses were very rude when they looked you up-and-down and kept saying there is nothing available even know the bar turned over twice. I was a restaurant general manager in Manhattan for 20 years. No matter what hype you're trying to make. Unless you're at the door of Studio 54 rudeness doesn't work at the front desk... I truly hope when we eat there, the podium is not reflected on the rest of the staff.
It is the first impression to you experience
Very good espresso. Actually excellent compared to the crap out there for any of you espresso connoisseurs. Friendly, polite service.

We came here on a Friday night pretty excited to try their food after seeing that Missy Robbins (chef) had just won a James Beard award.

Our initial experience was quite poor, the two hostesses working that night were both rude and unhelpful, we showed up a few minutes early for a 8:45PM reservation and were sent to the cafe area to wait for our table.  Forty minutes later we were still waiting for our table and the hostesses were unapologetic and curt.  Even when we were finally seated over 30 minutes past our reservation time the two hostesses had not apologized or explained why we were delayed once.

As upset as we were over the bad start to the night the food and service following were actually quite good.  We enjoyed the ramp bread with ramp butter (though quite expensive at $12), grilled clams, artichoke, and a few of their pastas (though the signature rigatoni was quite standard).  Our waiter was helpful and friendly when navigating the menu with a nut allergy!

If you are in Williamsburg already and there's somehow a short walk-in time feel free to give it a try but otherwise there's plenty of good/better Italian restaurants in other boroughs that you can go to without trekking here.

This place deserves the hype forreals. You come expecting too much, and maybe those expectations won't be met - but I truly don't think you can say that you didn't have quality food that's been prepared properly.

cacio e pepe fritelle, clams, ricotta gnocchi, sheeps milk agnolotti. Agnolotti and clams were def the standouts and honestly, I think I'll try their other pastas next time for good measure. They all seemed delicious..

Will definitely be back (if I can get another reservation)

For anyone thinking this place is over hyped - they are crazy. This place deserves all the flattery it gets, and now that James Beard award has been given, good luck getting a spot, as if it was any easy feat before. 

Hypes:
- So I have never had anything so good having to do with pasta or italian food, and we basically tried almost everything on the menu. the dishes are listed below as hypes bc they are ..wow-status
- Cacio e Pepe Fritelle - Hot, crispy on the outside, and delicious
- Housemade mozzarella on bread - get this also - its refreshing
- Grilled clams - omg. Large portions, and delicious. Great for sharing in a group of 4
- Mafaldini - amazing. This was devoured in seconds, maybe not even seconds.
- Agnolotti- MY FAVORITE - sheeps milk cheese, saffron, dried tomato, and honey. I ate this sooo slow to savor every bite. And i dream of it at least once a day. 
- Steak - awesome - the only thing was that i was so full i couldnt eat enough of it. but it was mad good.
- olive oil cake - hands down....get.

Gripes:
- Chicken liver crostini - we were recommended this by the waitress, but if you're not a chicken liver person - you're not gonna like this so dont bother with it.
- when i come back next im going to have to come on an empty stomach, time the wait so i dont have to wait so long, and order everything i ate this time - bc it was so freakin amazing.

NO MORE. This place is questionable. Although the food is good as I had eaten here when it first opened, now whenever I go there is either a 2 hr wait or a closed wait list. I think it's poor business as they do not take reservations, no one else was waiting, plenty of empty tables not reserved and yet the wait list was closed? I'm not sure how a wait list is closed when no one is waiting but ok. I'm done attempting to patronize any longer. Just take reservations and stop acting pretentious over pasta. People make the trip there only to be turned away every time. I think that is ridiculous. If people cannot plan a night, a date or a celebration to have dinner what's the point? I have tried different times and days so it's not just busy times. There is also no known dress code. This is what Williamsburg has become.

Overhyped. After a long wait for reservations we were finally able to get a table. The food was mediocre and disappointing especially for the price tag. The service was rude and impersonal - our waiter brought the check before we asked for it or even had the chance to order desserts. I get that restaurants want to maximize turnover but there's a way to do it without being rude and pushy.

A touch overhyped, but lovely meal.

We came for a group date and ordered every dish our friendly waiter recommended. The wines are lovely and the vibe is very "date night". The foccacia, pastas (agnolotti), Chicken liver were standouts. The bathroom situation leaves a lot to be desired- expect a prolonged time away from your table and bring reading material- there is quite a line.

I'm not sure I understand the hype surrounding this restaurant. It's fine. The first time I went they over-salted one dish and severely undercooked one pasta (I understand al dente--this was not that). 

I gave it a second chance last night. The mussels were a little fishy. The Foccacia was good because, well, bread. The cauliflower was very average and a little heavy on the citrus. 

The pastas are the stars. The saffron agnolotti are delicious and special, the spaghetti with lemon sauce was simple but good. The gnocchi were pretty good. 

The service too was fine, up until the RIDICULOUS cake-cutting fee which was not disclosed to us. A group of 7 was there to celebrate a Birthday, one of us brought a homemade cake as a gift and they offered to cut it. We went back and forth because we weren't sure we wanted to pay for someone to cut it, but as they would not let us eat it otherwise we complied. It turned out to be a $9 charge PER PERSON. Totaling almost $60+. I thought that was crazy. We could have each ordered a single dessert and it would have been the same price. The cake itself didn't even cost that much. 

I think it's distasteful and unnecessarily expensive. 

Come for the pasta, sure. But in my honest opinion, it's not really worth the hype or getting a reservation months in advance.

A lot of hoopla about this place. 
My trusted foodie scouts had eaten here and had gone through some gymnastics to get us a reservation here. They really wanted me to check this place out.
So I will cut to the chase. 
The food was overall average. Maybe my expectations were too high or it just isn't what it's made out to be. 
The pasta was over cooked: almost rubbery. 
The fettuccini was excellent. 
The gnocchi was average. Nothing to write home about. 
The cauliflower was very good. 
Almost every dish was over salted. 
On top of these disappointments we were seated in what I would call the "annexe" of the main dining room. No ambiance and pretty damn hot in there. 
Service was impersonal as if we were an imposition. 
Not sure this is a sustainable operation. The hype is carrying this place. 
And, by the way, prices are on the higher side. 
I would never wait for as long as the wait times have been reported.

Ridiculous how you can never get a reservation for this place

You would think they are giving out free diamonds

Worth all the Hype. 

Had a 9pm dinner reservation on Saturday. We came a bit early and were directed to the back café for a drink while we waited. The space is small and rather dark but  we were able to get a seat at the bar. I had the Negroni Bianco which was refreshing and delicious. 

For dinner my boyfriend and I shared the radishes with ricotta, grilled clams, the special ramp focaccia with ramp butter, the fettuccini with spicy lamb sausage and the veal steak. Our favorites were the ramp focaccia and the veal steak. I could have eaten that whole container of butter with a spoon!  Not blown away by our pasta selection, it was tasty just nothing extraordinary. Wished we would have tried a few more pastas. 
Overall lovely service and delicious food. Can't wait to come back

My daughter wanted to go for her 27th birthday. Family of six. We all
order different dinners. We started with the focaccia, which we all
thought, it was too salty. The pastas came and though the portions 
where small ( size of a small soup bowl) their were heavy. We never
have room for desert but everyone did, still hungry.  All the service 
was fantastic ,love the atmosphere, the table space for six was tight. All and all nothing really jump out at us to want to go back?

If I could, I would go back here everyday to eat their focaccia. I love bread and this was damn good bread. It was perfectly crispy on the outside, warm, fluffy and spongey on the inside. I can't remember what the green butter was but it had some herbs in it. Yup, be finished all of it and didn't leave any crumbs. The sea salt was the cherry on top. 

Honestly I can't remember anything else about my meal except for the amazing focaccia we had. Well also the clams! There's a lot, so don't fight over it. It has a slight kick but enjoyable. Those two dishes were the most memorable. Apologies that this review is short but I don't recall having a bad time at all. Just know that I ate a lot and still wanted the focaccia at the end my dinner!

This is one of the few one places on Brooklyn where you can go to eat amazing pasta, great wine and listen to juvenile's back that ass up and little Jon's 2000 hits. Love it or hate it the food is off the charts amazing. Artichokes that will change your life. 
Service is spot on. Bar is amazing. Wine list and food pairing is perfect.

Pro Tip: there are several off-the-menu items including desserts like the Italian Job. 

While ramps are in season, the ramp focaccia is good but the ramp butter makes the appetizer worth while. While the ramp pasta might sound interesting, it's very one note, underwhelming, and overall not very good.
Very tasty, and high  quality food, and extremely friendly , helpful, knowledgeable staff.  The grilled clams were a real standout...

If you want hipster Italian, look no further. If you like this place you probably also like waiting for 2 hours to get a mediocre brunch at Five Leaves. But I digress...

I went here when it first opened and have not been back (except for coffee from the side cafe, which is excellent). The food is ok, but nothing is extraordinary. The service was subpar. 

leuca is a superior Italian restaurant in the neighborhood, but I guess this one has the eater hype machine behind it. Hell, I think I even liked the pasta I've had at Fiore or Testo better.

I struggled whether to give them two or three stars. I ended with 3 because I just hate being mean. First, they were never going to get more than 4 stars for their reservation system. The whole idea of 'we will give you a reservation when we have one available' doesn't suit me. They kept saying they had nothing on their online reservation system except maybe a 1030pm a month from now on a random date. We had a gift certificate that we wanted to use. It took over a year to figure out how to get in there. The service was impeccable. Seriously. Some people are like, "Service is just a small part." It's really not. I felt like the staff was nice, knowledgeable, had their timing spot on. The food though... was eh. Everything was slathered in cheese. No wonder everyone likes this place. Everything is good with cheese. The pastas were boring. I won't be back. I might have considered it it if it wasn't for the terrible reservations.

For a place that requires a reservation exactly 30 days in advance, I would've expected a lot more and even when I got there right at my reservation time, there was still a 25 min wait. When I arrived, I was told by the hostess that the table wasn't ready and she RUDELY and AGGRESSIVELY made us go to the cafe to grab a "wine or cocktail." For all she knows, I don't drink alcohol. The best items we had were the clams and olive oil cake. Given that it's an Italian restaurant, I definitely thought they'd perfect their pasta. They tried to serve it al dente, but it was just hard to chew.

First let me start off by saying how hard it was to get a reservation here at a decent time. (AKA something before 9pm - we're old now lol). Literally took us months...not exaggerating. So I thought I was going to have a meal that would just blow me away but i wasn't super impressed. Everything to me was just good... 

Appetizers: We started off with the mozzarella & toasted garlic bread. The mozzarella was fresh and the garlic bread was perfect amount of garlic and not too oily. 
Next up was the radishes with whipped ricotta. Not a fan at all. The radishes were raw and hard. But I heard good things which is why I tried it ‍
My favorite app of all were the grilled clams. HIGHLY recommend getting these. Such a large portion and just so delicious. 

For dinner we split 3 pastas: 
The ricotta gnocchi - AMAZING! But it is a very small portion. 
Mafaldini - also amazing. Decent sized portion. The pasta itself was perfectly al dente.
Agnolotti - this was so good but kind of on the heavy side. 

Dessert: 
I tried the olive oil cake and didn't leave a crumb behind. It sounds a little on the weird side but it was delicious. 
Also tried the "Italian job" which also sounds a little weird but it was just as good as the cake. The fennel gives it a nice touch 

I would visit here again ... try a few different things. The restaurant itself was very cute and the staff was on point! Very friendly and informative.

Very pretentious. A group of friends and I entered through the back, as we have not been here before. We were led to the front by an employee who pointed to a number of empty tables (indicating we could sit there) until we were rudely flagged over by someone standing at the host stand, in the manner that a principal would discipline an elementary school student.

I then proceeded to get gawked at for having the audacity to think I'd get a table without reservations. At least that's what the host's tone implied. We were looked at like peasants, which is pretty ironic! But very embarrassing. 

Can't rate it on the food, but I'll certainly never be back and will ensure none of my friends or family will ever be here.

I'm happy to give one of the thousands and thousands of other restaurants in New York City my business who actually care about customer service. These places are a dime and dozen anyway!

OVERRATED. I've been a customer 2 times. Decent food, fine vibes. However, after today's attempt to dine there, I'm disappointed by the unprofessionalism of the receptionist (and the blonde manager who was right beside and didn't intervene at all?). Unskilled to handle her role and incapable to accommodatingly interact with the customers. Either this place has lost its touch, or they have become so arrogant with the inflow of money and lost respect to the people.
Also, last time, we faced the arrogance of not accommodating us in our need to have some grated parmesan on our pasta, because the CHEF didn't agree that parmesan would fit on her creation! MAMMA MIA......

The fritelle was a little too salty for me and the outside wasn't as crisp as I would have wanted. The artichoke was great and cheesey but make sure you know how to eat it! They provide an extra empty bowl to put the outer leaves in that are too tough to eat. The sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti was the star of my meal. They were little pillows of cheese goodness with a hint of honey. The mafaldini was more on the chewy side of al dante (I liked the texture) and had a very interesting flavor. Note that the pink peppercorn is not the same as pepper -- the waiter described it as a type of cashew flavor. I only wish that there were more toppings on the malfadini. 

The service was amazing. The table was cleaned after each course and the waiter was so nice and happy that I left feeling very happy as well.

Definitely OVERATED. Why is there such a long wait for this place? Don't usually review many places but have to on this one given the hype. 

Just to set expectations - Pasta was really salty, apps were meh (altho veggies were indeed very fresh), entrees were sub-par (veal over cooked) and service was very rushed (gotta turn those tables I guess). Definitely much better Italian spots. 

The affogato was the star of the night tho.

Reservations can be tough to come by but we managed to get a Saturday night slot about a month in advance for a night in late January after hearing a lot of buzz about the pastas here!

We waited for about fifteen minutes for our reservation - the restaurant has a nice wine bar with a small plate menu you can order off of while you wait. When we were seated, the service was really good throughout - we were initially put at a two-seater that had no room at all (a side chair had been squeezed in at the next table, so there was a person basically leaning back onto our table) and when we looked uncomfortable, the waitress immediately noticed and seated us at a nook around the side.
