Our favorite dishes were the persimmon salad and the agnolotti, which were so soft they practically melted. These were both incredible and absolutely made the meal for us. We also got the cacio e pepe fritelle and the mafaldini, which was much-hyped - the mafaldini was a bit too chewy / al dente for my taste, though still good. Dessert at the end wasn't quite in the line with the rest - we got the olive oil cake at the recommendation of the waiter - though definitely solid, and a nice way to end the meal. 

All in all, the restaurant space is really nice, and the food was amazing - definitely a must-try experience.

This is a really cool spot. My table tried many of the items on the menu and we had no complaints. All of the food was delicious and plated well. The Chef was kind enough to let a Chef at my table discuss culinary things with her. Really enjoyed the drink selection!! I tried a Pink IPA from my family's region in Italy which made me happy! Looking forward to going back to dine alfresco when the weather is warmer!!

Pretty disappointing, considering the rave NYTimes review and month-long wait for a reservation. Went for 2 at 9pm on a Tuesday. 

Started with the frittelle, which was a super salty and dry. The escarole was an interesting idea but destroyed by an overzealous administration of anchovy.  The cauliflower was edible but of unremarkable flavor--though its possible the tongue-deadening saltiness of the first two dishes had diminished our ability to taste this one. 

For mains, I had the spicy lamb fettuccine and my wife had the agnolotti. These each fared better. The fettucine was basic and good, like the kind of oily-meaty comfort plate you'd get at a trattoria in Italy, albeit for 8 euros. The agnolotti had a more delicate and intriguing flavor. We skipped dessert.

The wine was priced what you'd expect although their selection was underwhelming. The beer however, starts at $10/pint (ugh).

The place itself is attractive looking, although the atmosphere was lessened by the sound tracking of an incongruous best of the 80s playlist of Falco, Madonna, Cyndi Lauper etc.

Overall: prob nice for a date, especially for someone who doesn't know or care much about Italian food. Pricy tho not crazily so. There are many better Italian restaurants though including Antica Pesa, and most of them don't require the song, dance and wait for getting a reservation that Lilia does.

Yes getting a table here can be a pain, but once you're there, it really is a wonderful, homey feeling experience.

Tip - the tables outside (in warmer months) are first come first served, so if you head over fairly early in the evening (on a balmy September eve we got a table for 4 at 7pm on a Friday with no wait), you can be seated easily. In cooler times, making a reservation is necessary, and sometimes they ask for a month's notice, which seems a bit nuts, but hey they're busy, good for them! Just make the reservation, and you'll find someone to go with when the time comes!

Favorites - roasted escarole, trumpet mushroom starter, pink peppercorn mafaldini, ricotta gnocchi, and the salsa verde bass (sounds simple but my oh my it's awesome).

Avoidables - whole artichoke (ours seemed a bit underdone and tough), bagna cauda (a little watery).

I was more hyped up about Lilia than I was when Beyonce and Jay-Z went on tour together and BOY, I have to say Lilia is NO BABY BOY of mine. Honestly as I am writing this review I'm a tad tipsy and a lot poorer so I'll get to the nitty gritty.

First things first here is what I ordered+ my conscious thoughts:
1) Cacio e pepe: warm, gooey, SALT SALT SALT. Upon first bite these little fritters tasted like delicious puffs of cheese sent from God. But, as I ate more I felt all the fluids draining from my body as I felt like I literally dipped my tongue into a salt bath.
2) Red Celery salad: HARD PASS. It was the one item I let my boyfriend pick, and then I quickly remembered why I always order for us. It was not memorable. It was not tasty. It was something I could easily whip up in my kitchen at the fraction of the price and with less clumsily cut c-stalk pieces. 
3) Little Neck Clams: These actually had decent flavor. Unfortunately they were overcooked and tough. 
4) Malfadini: WHAT IS THIS?! The texture of the pasta was swell, but it literally was a small bowl of glorified butter noodles with a 19 dollar price tag slapped on it. Worse. It came out lukewarm. 
5) Agnolotti: THE ONLY THING WORTH EATING HERE. This was actually very good. The sauce was exquisite and at the same time oh so simple. The only downer was it came out lukewarm/cold. It could have been a total home run if it came out hot.
6) Olive Oil Cake: Meh. It was pretty light for an EVO cake. It just simply did not hold a candle up to L' Artusi. 

Conclusion: The food was half assed, for the most part cold, and just not that impressive. Especially when there are so many truly incredible Italian restaurants out there to satisfy any carby cravings. If you want a REAL bowl of pasta head over to L'Artusi, Don Angie's, or Gaia Italian Cafe and you will not be disappointed. 

SIDENOTE: The waiter had way too much pasta stuck up her asshole. Her red glasses were filled to the brim with judgement. She was cold, just like the food and made the whole experience unenjoyable. DARIA CALLED she wants her specks back. At least when she had them, she had a smattering of a personality!

Although reservations are hard to get, it is worth it. The Mafaldini is amazing, and so are the cacio e pepe fritters and the lamb sausage pasta.  The agnolotti was good but we would not order it again. I also love the whole artichoke- if you love cheese and butter, this is for you.

Pasta! Pasta! Pasta!
We went as a group of 7 and decided to attack the menu by gettin 5 starters, 5 pastas and a 32 oz steak to give us some proper protein. 
To be honest, the starters were fine (albeit a bit salty). Between the Bagna Cauda, Cauliflower, Grilled Clams with breadcrumbs, Roasted Trumpet Mushrooms and the Sardines, I'd probably go back for the last two if I had to, but the real stars were the pastas!   
We were all in agreement that the Fettuccini with Lamb Sausage was the weakest and many of the group enjoyed the Malfadini with it's lightly drizzled Peppercorn, but from there onwards the favorites were spread between the sheeps milk Agnolotti (with it's sweet aftertaste!) and the potato filled Ravioli with creme fraiche. Just remember to order bread to wipe up the sauces by the end!
And yes, the steak was the perfect ending!
PS: The olive oil cake was brilliant too!

I had to book this place a month in advance, and went online to book when reservations opened at midnight. It was impossible to get a reservation here otherwise. 
I'd booked for 6pm on a Sunday. When we arrived, the place was very full, and we were seated immediately. The wait staff were polite and friendly and took care of us from the minute we stepped foot inside. We were a party of three, and ordered a number of dishes which were presented in a timely manner.
The radishes with ricotta and honey was one of the most average dishes. The ricotta was creamy and delicious, and contrasted well with the texture of the radishes, but overall, wasn't amazing. 
The grilled clams provided a better taste sensation than the radishes, but the pasta dishes were the stars of the evening, in particular, the sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti. All the pastas were cooked al dente, and were delicious. The pink peppercorn malfadini was my least favorite of the three. 
We finished up with the veal, which was served with  basil, providing a fresh contrast to the meaty flavor of the veal. 
We had a very animated and attentive waiter. 
The ambience here was very basic, and fit in with the Williamsburg neighborhood that it is situated in. All in all, we had a great meal.

We've been here twice for dinner, each time exceptional. Their pasta is no joke, especially their agnolotti in butter saffron sauce -- it's a sensual experience :) the dough is perfectly silky and stretched thin so you can enjoy every asset of the dish. Of course the malfadini is also great with a much thicker texture and bite -- it's mainly about the pasta. We've also tried the ricotta gnocchi with broccoli pesto which I felt was less memorable -- still good though. 

For appetizers, get the cacio e Pepe fritelle. I can also recommend the Housemade mozzarella which has a bit of a seafood flavor but it really does work, and I don't love fish.

The only let down was dessert. The chocolate cake was just ok, with the espresso cream being the best part. I prefer my cake to have more chocolate flavor and I noticed some unmixed egg whites. Still, I'm willing to give 5 stars for the pasta.

I don't know how anyone can leave less than a 5 star review for this place. I got the reservation a month in advance for a Sunday at 6:30. We arrived a bit early (10 minutes), but the restaurant had no problem seating us right away. The food was just heavenly. We started off with their spring garlic focaccia and the cacio e pepe fritelle. Out of everything, the focaccia was a 1000% a highlight, and the fritelle let us down. We just didn't feel like it was anything that special, but I know people love it, so maybe it was just not for us. For our entrees, we got the mafaldini and the ricotta gnocchi. The mafaldini was so silky and perfect, and just completely delicious. The gnocchi was just melt in your mouth good. The broccoli pesto was heavenly. For dessert, we got the vanilla soft serve with various toppings and took the olive oil cake home because I wanted to try it after hearing how delicious it was. To say that I don't want to come back here, well, that's wrong, because I don't think I've had food this delicious before. Also, the service, god the service, I don't think I've had service like that ever in my life. Never was a water glass empty, and our table was cleaned between each course. I cannot believe how wonderful this restaurant is, and we cannot wait to come back here!

First: if you are reading this a month in advance, get on that reservation list.  You are going to need a month in advance to reserve a spot and decent time.   My tip is to call in actually rather than wait for any of the online reservation methods.  Remember this is east coast time. 

Now onto the food.  Here's what we ordered:
- Cacio e Pepe Frittelle (it was ok, don't need to order this one)
- Mafaldini with peppercorn (this one's a good one)
- Sheep's milk cheese filled agnolotti (our fav!) 
- Gnocchi pesto (on the lighter side)
- Grilled lamb steak (done extremely well and flavorful)
- Sundae (the make your own sundae was actually pretty good)

If you love Italian it is worth the battle to get a reservation at Lilia!

Scoring a reservation at Lilia had been a hot commodity from Day 1, so I was thrilled that my brother was able to secure a table for us at 8:30 on a Sunday evening.  However, my joy faltered a bit when we walked into the crowded restaurant and wound up having to wait 45 minutes past our scheduled seating.   The restaurant had a café in the back that served beer, wine, cocktails, and traditional coffee shop beverages to hungry diners waiting on their tables.  However, we were unable to enjoy our time in this expectant area, as it was completely packed with little room to move or sit.  Yes, the bartender/barista checked in on us and offered us beverages, but the wait-time was ridiculous, given that we had reservations, and that it was already late on a Sunday evening.  When our time finally came, we received the table right next to the door, where other patrons were also standing about waiting for their time to sit as well.  Needless to say, it was not the most comfortable table.  

Despite our tight quarters, we were eager to jump into our meal.  We started with two appetizers - the mushrooms and the scallops.  The warm Roasted Trumpet Mushrooms had been sliced lengthwise, resembling thin planks of wood.  The fungi pieces were topped with salty Sicilian almonds, peppery arugula, and sweet balsamic vinegar.  The comprehensive flavor profile hit every possible note, elevating a simple dish to something more intricate.  The Grilled Scallops were tender, easy to cut, and perfectly cooked.  The two pieces were served in a deep bowl, surrounded by a creamy sauce made from yogurt and anchovy.  Sprigs of marjoram and chopped walnuts were sprinkled over the top of the dish.  We both found this course to be just OK.  While the mollusks were great, the sauce was heavy enough to seem more like a mayonnaise than a yogurt.  Walnuts also seemed to be the wrong nut choice that did not mesh well with the other flavors.  In addition, we had asked the server if they had a traditional bread service that we could enjoy with our meal.  She stated that they did not, but that she could toast some of the bread that they used for the mozzarella appetizer.  We said that that would be perfect and were presented with one thick slice of Italian bread that had been grilled, buttered, and cut in half.  It was delicious, but one slice for two people was a bit stingy!

Next came our pastas, which were simple in creativity and execution, but full of taste!  The Ricotta Gnocchi were soft and fluffy, potato-filled pillows from the heavens.  They were topped with an earthy broccoli pesto, fresh basil, and sweet pistachios.  The sauce was a tad salty, but still robust and enticing.  The Fettuccine with Lamb Sausage was out of this world!  The meat had hints of spice that were further emphasized with the addition of fennel seed.  The tomato sauce was well-balanced and possessed the slightest kiss of sweetness.  

After seeing an abundance of desserts exit the kitchen, we simply had to indulge.  We selected the Olive Oil Cake, which was moist, but had been a bit overdone on the top, leaving the crisp crust slightly dry.  There was an elegant hint of orange rind in each bite.  Since it was my birthday, the kitchen gifted us with the Apple Ginger Crostata, which had a perfectly flaky crust, but could have used more apple to boost its flat appearance.  It was topped with a scoop of whipped mascarpone.  The tart was our preferred dessert of the two.  

We had paired our meal with some wine, settling on the 2015 Rodano Chianti Classico from Tuscany, after tasting that and the Vermentino.  My brother requested the half-bottle, but we did not realize that we had accidentally been given a larger carafe, which wound up costing us $50, rather than the $25 we were expecting.

In the end, the service (excluding the wine mix-up) and the pastas were the real highlights of our visit to Lilia.  The modern and trendy atmosphere was also delightful.  However, the lengthy wait-time and mediocre appetizers and pastries left us only mildly driven to return.

Very rarely does a resto live up to its hype, but Lilia exceeded it. The atmosphere is chic-casual, and relaxed. My party enjoyed our appetizers (trumpet mushrooms, artichoke, and the clams), and we LOVED our pasta. Our server was super knowledgeable and enthusiastic, and provided us with a fantastic wine recommendation to accompany our meal. We also ordered the chocolate cake for dessert, and the special "the Italian job" which was a gelato soft serve with olive oil, sea salt, and fennel pollen which was delicious and unique. I would hands down recommend Lilia to anyone, and am eager to return.

So, we heard about Lilia about one week before we ended up there for dinner. We heard that it was the "best Italian food in the city."

Apparently there is a four month wait for reservations. Luckily, a friend of ours had gotten reservations several weeks ago but some friends dropped out so we jumped at the chance to try this place out.

This place is a short walk from the L train. 

Supposedly, the chef that runs this restaurant is Obama's favorite chef.

The vibe is industrial chic--exposes concrete-based decor. On par for Brooklyn.

Their speciality is pasta. And there were eight pastas on the menu--and seven of them are vegetarian. And we ordered them all!

My favorites were the mafaldini and the spaghetti. Special mentions go to the pesto and the rigatoni. 

The agnolotti i did not like because of the garlic which I really hate.

Just note, that this restaurant will not accept alterations or substitutions.

So, did it live up to hype? Yes, I still harken back to that mafaldini on cold, wintry nights. Would I wait four months to eat there again? No.
I had dinner here and the food was fantastic! Everything came out so fast and tasted fresh and delicious! Great service! Will def come back here

This place is awesome, period.   

It's the Italian restaurant you've always been looking for  

- warm, attentive and non-pretentious service 
- kick-a$$ food and wines 
- a sexy and intimate space 
- reasonable prices (for the quality) 

Is it hard to get a reservation? Yes.  Is it worth trying until you do? Absolutely.  Its worth the hype.  While all the food is not mind blowing the menu is well balanced, consistent, well-executed and delicious.  

We were a table of two and tried the following (don't judge, diet starts tomorrow):

Focaccia bread (its a special) - you must order this - the green butter it's served with is what dreams are made of.  

Trumpet Mushrooms - Very tasty but nothing special 

Roasted Escarole - If you like anchovies, this is a great "green" dish to accompany all the pasta you will be shortly eating 

Crispy Fish - Fried fish with a dash of lemon, it was lovely. 

Spaghetti, Lemon, Pine Nuts, Parmigiano -  Simple yet delicious, was one of our favorites. 

Rigatoni Diavola - Spicy, perfectly cooked, so yummy.  

Mafaldini - Very tasty, perfectly al-dente, but maybe a little too heavy on the pepper.  

Agnolotti with Saffron - the flavors were amazing, though the pasta was slightly over-cooked and mushy.  

Ricotta Gnocchi - was very tasty but was our least favorite of the night.  

Overall it was a lovely evening and I cannot wait to come back soon!

We wanted to love this place. After all we waited almost a year to get in, and it took a nasty note to them on Facebook to get a reservation. It's got to be amazing right?  We also wanted to hate this place - I mean how presumptuous can a place be, right?

In the end, honestly, it was meh. The server was really great, and the wine list had some amazing choices. The food was good (just good), but remarkable not creative. The artichoke was the same as every other grated parmesan and butter artichoke you've ever had. The mozzarella was tasty - just like every other Brooklyn Italian restaurant's mozzarella. 

Here's the bottom line: Everything was fine. Nothing was bad.  But at these prices and with all this hype, I expected Del Posto quality and creativity but found that the most impressive feature is the reputation.
This was a great spot to celebrate a birthday. Pastas were exceptional and outstanding. We all enjoyed our meal and service was very attentive. Hope to go back again soon
Just lovely space cozy and the food is simple but superb. The pasta dishes are delicious and can be a good family dinner location

Wow. A special restaurant indeed and one of my favorites in all of NYC. The flavors are so balanced, fresh, and popping. I want to say it's a Cali style but I've never had such great Italian in Cali so???  What gray use of breadcrumbs and citrus zest. Yum. It's just hard to get a reservation.

For our wedding anniversary we went to Lilia Ristorante in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. We will have to go back to try the pasta, but what we did have was delicious. Highlights - the focaccia and the coal roasted Yukon gold potatoes.
.
Casio e Pepe Fritelle - I'd describe these as little Parmesan donuts. They're light and crisps and cheesy. Delicious.
.
The house made focaccia - this was a special so I'm not sure of the exact details (I'd love to know what makes the butter bright green!) but it was superb. It had roasted caramelised bits of garlic on top & was probably my favourite dish.
.
Sweet Sicilian olives with garlic and chilli - perfect olives. The green Sicilian ones are always a winner for me.
.
Whole artichoke with garlic, mint, parmigiano, and breadcrumbs - there was a delicious pool of sauce in the bottom for dipping & it was heaven in a bowl.
.
Grilled lamb steak with roman spices, fennel, and celery. This was a beautiful dish, but didn't come with any sides, so it was a lot of meat. I'd have preferred half the lamb and some of the gold potatoes that my husband had with his fish. They were superb. 
.
Black bass with salsa verde, and coal roasted Yukon gold potatoes - so delicate and the roast potatoes were amazing. My husband loved the salsa verde.

The staff were attentive and polite and we had a lovely experience. We would love to visit again.

It is fair to say that Lilia's reputation proceeds it. From the first time I heard about the place, it shot up to the top of my to-eat list. Lo and behold, Resy came to the rescue when I got a notification that a reservation had opened up for a Wednesday dinner at 8:45pm. I jumped at the opportunity and was rewarded with arguably the best Italian I have had in New York to date.

COCKTAIL SNACKS
The Cacio e Pepe Fritelle is one of a few dishes that find their way onto every review. Mine will be no different; these are like arancini but instead of risotto it's parmesan cheese and fresh pepper.

The Housemade Mozzarella is well-prepared, but since we had it after the much heavier and spicier Fritelle, this dish failed to shine. 

APPETIZERS
The Cauliflower with Spicy Soppressata emphasized sour as a counterpoint to the spiciness. The roasted parts of the cauliflower also provided some savoriness to the dish.

The Grilled Clams avoided the fishy taste that too many clam dishes suffer, instead providing bold flavors and textures from the Calabrian chili and breadcrumbs, respectively. 

ENTREES
Lemon Spaghetti is not something I usually see on or order from menu. However, my sister insisted and was not let down. Again, the sour theme continues!

The Mafaldini was a welcome contrast to the acerbic notes of the spaghetti, countering with not only the muted spice of pink peppercorn but also a striking ruffly, ribbon-like shape. Arguably the best pasta I have had so far. It did arrive a few degrees cold, however.

Somehow, I found room for the Grilled Veal Flank Steak. This dish was a case study in seasoning. Though the veal itself was a perfect medium rare, it would not have reached such heights if not for the long peppers, basil, and fennel to bring each bite to life.

DESSERT
Olive oil cake is a classic, and the one here will remind you why. The crust is a little tough, but once you fight past it the interior is just firm enough to provide some resistance to your fork. The surprising star is really the whipped cream, which is somehow airy and dense at the same time. Personally I could do without the companionship of the orange peel.

SERVICE
You will hear it elsewhere and you will hear it here. Lilia's service is as attentive as it gets. Not a minute will go by before your water glass is refreshed or your table cleared. Our server Marcus was very amiable, from shepherding us through the menu with panache to checking our opinions on each first bite.

Lilia is a restaurant that rewards the discerning eater. Perhaps coincidentally, every dish of ours played some variations on a theme of the two tastes: spicy and sour. The thing is, every dish appears so simple as if to suggest that you, too, could prepare it. In the end, I can honestly say that my appreciation of Italian cuisine has changed thanks to my meal here (which I hope explains the length of this review). Make no mistake, I will be back for more soon.

Food: 4
Vibe: 3
Staff: 3.5

Had a lot of excitement and expectations coming here, as the wait is more than a month! And the chef is rumored to be Obama's favorite chef! 

Unfortunately, the dishes just seemed okay. Only the desert really was something to be remembered.

The price is very high, and the taste did not match. 

The vibe is quite pretentious.

Overall disappointed, but may be okay for someone who wants to go more to say they went, than for the food.

Better options:
1. L'artusi for pasta
2. Lucali for pizza 
3. Leuca for ricotta appetizer
We waited 2 hours, didn't have a reservation and decided to just go for it. It was worth it. Service was great, staff was welcoming, and the food was delicious. We will definitely be coming back.

Lilia probably doesn't need more five star reviews, but... They are still killing it in Williamsburg. So, another glowing review can only assure you that they are NOT resting on their laurels. Chef Missy Robbins is slaying in the kitchen, sending out insanely delectable combinations like sardines done tapas-style with capers, dill, and citrus. She also had specials which were basically there to feature black truffles freshly shaved onto your dish (can't go wrong here). Full disclosure that my Chicago roots may (mayyybe) make me a little biased here, but I'm a full convert to her fine AF Foods. Other notable notes include a grade A wine list full of Italian bangers and game-changers (Occhipinti Grappa anyone?) 

Special shout outs to our amazing server Jesse who timed our meal to perfection () and Jeremy the MOD who made even our delay in seating seamless (we had a lovely aperitivos in the cafe).

Insanely good.  

Cacio e Pepe Fritelle - similar to a risotto ball.  A bit hollowed out in the middle though.  Could use some more filling.  But really good.  3 in an order. 

Little fish - take the risk! Get it.  Yes a bit fishy like most small fish but really well prepared.   BUTTERFLIED style.   I though I'd be eating small little deep fried fish.   Was very surprised with what came, and happily so.

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti - so good, rich.  They remind me of cheese blintzes. 

 Mafaldini with Pepercorn and Parmesan - they are lasagna shaped noodle s just not as wide.  Pretty light sauce - I actually may have liked this best. 

Rigatoni - very good.  Just not that unique.

Great great meal.

We dined at Lilia on February 7th and had an absolutely incredible meal. 
It began with an excellent wine recommendation at the bar and proceeded with exceptional service, food and wine throughout the night. We dined in the small dining room to the left of the entrance and had a server named Marcus who truly heightened our experience. His passion for the food, drink and overall experience of the patrons was what brought our experience at Lilia to the next level. We will absolutely be coming back.

We were so excited to learn that the chef we loved from a restaurant near our home had opened a great place in Williamsburg. Here is the thing, service can turn a mediocre meal into an amazing experience and poor service makes a great meal seem like just ok pasta with a little lemon.

After paying our $1000 bill for 6 people, a tall woman came over. We were smiling and complimenting as we THOUGHT she was there to ask how our meal was and thank us for our business. But no, she came to tell us in an arrogant, abrasive and bitchy way that we had overstayed our reservation. We had LITERALLY just taken the last bite of dessert, finished our champagne and we're finalizing the amount of TIP on the bill. For future training, a simple "can we buy you an espresso at the bar?" would have clearly signaled the same message without making us feel like you took our money, $250 tip, now get the hell out. To stand outside for 10 minutes as our group waited for coats and used the restroom with the table still empty, added further insult to injury as your smug hostess made no attempt to smooth over the situation while rolling her eyes with a resting bitch face. 

I realize your waitlist may allow you to treat people this way, but your brand is all you have at the end of the day. We had an incredible experience and meal. The last 10 minutes left us sad and disappointed. I would never allow my staff to treat customers as they had just ordered a burger at a Shake Shack. Actually, we have received better service at Shake Shack because Danny Meyer knows the importance of his brand even if you are just serving a $10 burger from a hut in the park.

With so many amazing restaurants throughout Williamsburg, Brooklyn Heights, Cobble Hill and lower Manhattan my recommendation is to spend your money elsewhere.

TLDR: Don't worry about getting a reservation. If you're not a late diner, show up a few minutes before they open, walk in and sit at the bar, and have a grand time.

It's probably not a surprise that one of my favorite restaurants in NYC (so far) is this trendy eatery in Brooklyn that just so happens to do noodles (and many other things) really, really well.

When one of my favorite dining partners, Rachel, said she wanted to try Lilia, Chef Missy Robbins' ode to classic Italian cuisine, I was stoked. I had been once before, about 18 months ago, and the food was so good, I don't know what had taken me so long to return.

Snagging a reservation is much harder now than when my husband and I first chowed down at Lilia back in February 2016. These days, reservations open up 30 days in advance, and if you're not stalking Resy at midnight a month before your target date, chances are, you're going to come up empty (like I did a few weeks ago when I tried to lock down a coveted Saturday night booking.)

But, don't fear! One of the really (okay, only) great features of Resy is that it allows you to get notifications on the rare occasion that someone cancels and a reservation miraculously opens up. Just set the time range that you're willing to dine (I picked 5:30-9:00 p.m.) and you're good to go. (Pro tip: Make sure to allow push notifications if you want timely alerts. Resy emailed me about an opening that came available, and I didn't see it until 6 hours later -- and of course it was too late).

And, if you can't get a reservation, there's still hope -- as long as you don't mind sitting at the bar. Lilia bar seating is first come, first serve. Rachel and I came in a few minutes before they opened (5:30), grabbed a drink at their little wine bar/cafe next door, and as soon as we were able, grabbed two prime seats at the bar in the main restaurant space. I would say, as long as you show up by 5:35/5:40, you stand a pretty good chance of catching the first round of seating.

I highly recommend taking the L train (while it's still running) out to Brooklyn and giving Lilia a try. My second experience didn't disappoint, and I definitely won't be waiting 18 months until my next visit.
Delicious food in a very interesting space with a nice vibe and a lively crowd.  A nice wine list and great service.  My wife and I loved it.  I highly recommend Lilia.

Food is amazing! Service is bad. No smiles and very arrogant. Which is a shame, as that is not a nice compliment to the exceptional food. I don't expect to be judged when I ask for a toothpick. Obviously people who eat in this restaurant don't eat food stuck in their teeth.

We were able to grab a reservation late on a Sunday night to celebrate a friends birthday. Very knowledgeable wait staff and a diverse menu. Mentioned I was vegan and they were able to accommodate - the gem lettuce, trumpet mushroom dish, and rigatoni with tomato sauce can all be modified to be vegan friendly. Since the focaccia of the day had butter in it our waiter brought us some grilled bread with garlic and olive oil to start, and we ended the meal with a lovely lemon sorbet (minus the cream). Simple dishes but packed with incredible taste. One of the best pastas I've had!

Definitely worth coming by for date night or with a small group (it's not a huge restaurant). Love the open kitchen.  Came here for my hubby's birthday and made a ressie 1 month in advance. You literally can only make it 1 month in advance. You can look online at Resy, but I found it easier to call once month in advance and have them do it for you. Once i called, it wasn't too difficult unlike what some people say here. 

Lilia is a pretty decent price point for the quality of the food you get, and I just find that so refreshing. Granted it's in Willamsburg but not difficult to get to by any means.  We had: 

- the cacio e pepe fritters. Not at all greasy or heavy. Fluffy, light, with good filling flavor, and flavorful pecorino 
-the clams casino type thing with Calibrian chili and red sauce, breadcrumbs - great spicy kick, flavor, and mouthfeel with the breadcrumb texture 
-the rigatoni pasta which had a light red sauce, mildly spicy and again great mouthfeel given how al dente the pasta was. Great thyme flavor too
-the malfadini - love this unique squiggly pasta (kind of like skinny lasagna noodles), and while it seemed simple in nature, it was very cheesy and cream-like, almost like a light mac and cheese with breadcrumb texture. Yum. 
-We shared the leg of lamb steak. I'll be honest, I don't love lamb. But this was well seasoned/salted and not gamey so not strong on the meaty aftertaste you usually get with lamb. Can't say I'd order it again but I did it for hubby who is a lamb lover. It was pretty rare, but they know they're doing. I'd come back for the veal steak which is more agreeable for me but note that that's probably fatty whereas the lamb was pretty lean ish. 

For dessert we had the raved about soft serve - a swirl of chocolate/vanilla with crunchy Amaretti cookies (yum), and chocolate straci (shavings).  We also had the delicious olive oil cake which was charred on the edges and not overly sweet or greasy. It depends on what you like because sometimes the said is good (I'm a big olive oil cake lover), but this was atypical and different. It could have been perhaps more citrusy but overall great desserts. 

We shared a bottle of a spicy red Italian variety (forget the name) - but they will guide you if needed. For $60. Which was pretty reasonable. 

Overall, dinner was about $200 post tax/tip. Which I felt was pretty good given the quality of the food and how trendy the restaurant has become. The servers were very helpful, service was timed properly. It's not an overly formal type setting or pretentious. The only suggestion I'd have for the service is that they should bring out pasta while they bring out the mains cause we were eating lamb along without anything else - but I guess the tables were a bit small so it would have been hard. They divide their menu items up in sections.

Some of the best pasta around! I tried this place a few months ago, on a Friday night. It unexpectedly started to rain, and we were worried since we had been assigned an outdoor table, and knowing how popular this place was we figured chances of getting  another table were slim, but the staff was very helpful. They had another table that was reserved for around 50 minutes later, so they told us that we could eat there so long as we were mindful of time, which was perfectly ok with us. 

We started with the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle, which I liked, but I feel like I didn't love as much as everyone on Yelp. Perhaps my expectations were too high. However, the pasta dishes surpassed my high expectations. We ordered the Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti with saffron, the Ricotta Gnocchi, and the Spaghetti with lemon and pine nuts. All were outstanding, but my favorite definitely had to be the Agnolotti, I haven't tried anything like it before.

The service was very good, even though we were on a time limit, we never felt like we were being rushed by the staff. They just brought us our food promptly, and we left quickly and happily.

I don't even know how to explain how good this food was. Everything that was put on my table was some of the best food I've ever had. A truly incredible experience. You HAVE to get the focaccia bread if you go to this restaurant. The best bread I've ever had in my life.

I have dined all over the world. I take celebrities to dinner regularly. Regardless if it was in the South of France, Florence, casual or Michelin, I've never experienced a worse dining experience. You walk in the door and nobody greets you. You ask for the host and it's more difficult than getting a studio head on the phone. The coldest, most obnoxious staff from entry to exit. As an executive, company culture is formed by and starts at the top. I think the favorable reviews combined with demand created by only allowing under a dozen tables to be reserved has misled the chef/owner to believe they can have a staff that's only worry is the check and tip. Here's a tip, most of the executives and others i know have had the same experience.  The food is good and slightly overpriced. But, who wants to deal with self-absorbed people are attendant when the check is waiting for your tip and payment.
So bad! I'm confused about the hype. Every dish had an odd flavor to it and I left thinking there's not one dish that I actually enjoyed. Save your money!

We were headed to a rock show at The Warsaw And stopped here to grab dinner very last minute. We had no reservations but were able to be seated at the bar right away. Would love to go back and have a proper full meal. 

The ambiance is great--very light and airy. The service was good. Cocktails Great! Loved what we had.

The management at this restaurant is equivalent to the quality of the cuisine - absolutely phenomenal. I come from a long line of Brooklyn natives. We have seen many restaurants come and go - some who seemed to truly care about Williamsburg and its long-time residents, some who failed to notice anyone was there before them. Lilia handles the absolutely challenging task of marrying care and concern for all of the residents in this neighborhood, flawlessly. Because of this, I think it will be here for quite a while.

You can't go wrong with the menu. Having lived in Italy for years, this was the closest I've ever come to eating pasta as fresh and wonderful. Atmosphere is awesome, especially in the summer. 

Big shoutout to Sean, who welcomed our family with open arms and treated us like we were part of his own. Of course, a shoutout to Chef Missy Robbins. For a bonus treat, follow her on Instagram!

Unfortunately I can't rank lower than 1 star. The friendliness of the staff is dismal. The woman handling phone reservations was extremely pretentious, and will inspire me to save my money for restaurants with better service. There are many places with friendly service AND great food in New York City.

I have been trying to make reservations at Lilia for A LONG TIME. Every time I tried it was sold out for months. FINALLY I got a reservation for a table for three at 9:45 PM on a Wednesday night about a month ahead of time, and I was thrilled.

We arrived at exactly 9:45 PM and were told to wait in the cafe area. About five minutes later we were taken to our table, tucked in the alcove in the back. The space is very attractive, minimalist, and the ambiance was cozy for a winter night. The restaurant was at full capacity and a little loud.

We sat down and ordered a few cocktails. I got the G&T ($14) which was smooth, chill, and delicious. We ordered the Cacio e Pepe Fritelle for starter and it was unbelievable. Three fried dough balls filled with parmesan cheese and pepper. Delectable. We then ordered five pastas for a family style dining experience--I would recommend this because there are quite a few different options and many are worth trying. The waiter recommended we break up the plates so we could keep the pastas hot and this was a great idea.

First round: Rigatoni Diavola, Mafaldini w/ pink peppercorns, and the Ricotta & Tuscan Kale Filled Cappelletti. The Mafaldini was my favorite of these three. Cheesy, squiggly, and flavorful, I was increasingly impressed with each bite. A crowd favorite was the rigatoni which was the perfect amount of heat and freshness. The fresh pastas were all extremely well made. A server kindly noticed us dipping our forks into the cappelletti sauce by the end and brought us some fresh bread. I recommend heartily that you request bread when you order the pastas, each sauce is worth enjoying with a piece of bread.

Second round: Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti and Fettuccine w/ Spicy Lamb Sausage. The Agnolotti is THE ORDER. Extremely creamy filling, the sheeps milk cheese was to die for. We were a little disappointed by the fettuccine--I felt as though there wasn't enough flavor, it was a little bland. 

For dessert we got the olive oil soft serve and the olive oil cake. The cake was rich and moist, excellent flavor profile. The soft serve was creamy and delightful but I felt the olive oil was a bit overpowering (my friend, however, claimed it was his favorite thing of the night--I would recommend a soft serve order for sure). 

Overall our experience was delightful but I would take the hype with a grain of salt. The pastas are delicious but some stand out more than others (my favorites: rigatoni, mafaldini, and agnolotti). The reservations/wait times are a little frustrating but I do believe you should get yourself to Lilia and give it a try.

author.name: Maria W.
author.location: Princeton Junction, West Windsor Township, NJ

reviews.review:
This place has nice food but is pretentious.  I called ahead to be told that they had no space in the restaurant but had space at the bar.  So, we went down there 30 minutes later and at the door, I asked again if they had space (as you do - people cancel or no show).  The guy on the door says (in a rude manner) "as I told you on the phone literally just now, we're full but you can go check the bar".  So we walk in (me fuming) and the bar is full.  As we leave he gives me a smug grin and I want to turn around and slap him but am told to leave it by girlfriend.  He is one of those people who think you should be thanking him to walking into his average restaurant.

Anyway, I was told to try it again by the GF and the food is nice to be fair, the service from the waiter staff was good as well.  However, because of their "we got a good review so we're pretentious" door people - it gets a three from me.

Third time here. Very disappointed in the food. All heavily salted. While the ingresients are fresh, it is highly salted and doesn't have any depth of flavors. Food feels like a mass produced product.
Trying to be clever and unusual in combos rather than concerned about depth of flavors. Worst part  hot chocolate and coffee was served cold. a definite sign of the quality of the service and care given to the food. Will not come back.

All of the food here is top, top and definitely worth the wait for the month long resi. If you haven't tried making a reservation yet, good luck - this place is always booked up.  **TIP: they open the online reservation calendar 1 month in advance for the next day. Stalk online for an opening at midnight or after midnight. If you end up with a resi past 9:30 pm - take it! It's well worth it. **

The atmosphere here is chill with a trendy, upscale vibe. The staff is very friendly and kind, they care about their customers satisfaction and they are knowledgeable about all things on the menu. If you come and your table is not ready, you'll have the option to have a drink at the cafe in the back.

Here's what we ordered: Whole Artichoke baked with garlic, mint, parmigiano, and breadcrumbs, Grilled clams seasoned with breadcrumbs and Calabrian chili (these are delish, the chili has a kick to it but is also sweet), sheeps milk cheese filled agnolotti - these are GOD SENT! like little cheesy clouds with saffron and dried tomato. They have honey in them as well, which makes them slightly sweet. These are must, must, must! And last the grilled leg of lamb that is seasoned to perfection and topped with fennel and celery.

Everything here was absolutely delish, but I would say the agnolotti was my favorite. I really wanted to try the blowfish, but it is only in season from the spring into the beginning of October. I will definitely be back to try it (if I can get another resi!)
The sheep's milk filled agnolotti are like the softest, sweetest pillows and I wanted to fall asleep on them and and never get out of bed again.

Place is phenomenal. Broccoli and cauliflower apps are really tasty. I also think the ravioli stuffed with pillows of delicious cheese are the best thing on the menu. All the pasta is good but the pesto gnocchi is my #2. Can't go wrong with anything on the menu, meats and fish are also exceptional.

Awesome. Awesome. Awesome. Every dish was simple and delicious. We tried half the menu and had cocktails. All were very well executed. The service was professional and efficient. Great vibe from a converted garage to a rustic Italian feel.

I was sooooo excited for this place. Don't get me wrong the place is awesome. The ambiance, the service, the open kitchen, the anticipation of getting an actual reservation in the middle-of-nowhere Brooklyn. However, I was a bit underwhelmed with the food related to the hype. 
Even the Menu was hyped. I saw persimmons and my mouth watered, I picked out artichoke and I felt like a dog waiting for a holiday treat - but neither of these was as good as my imagination made them out to be. They were great but I knocked off 1 star for the gap between my the hype vs. reality. I will manage my expectations better and go again next time as their menu is filled with seasonal ingredients. 

Fav eats - Foccacia bread and bar chip (omg the taste of fennel in these babies are incredible!)

Rezzi hack - get there between 5 - 6 and grab a seat at the bar. Full dinner menu woot-woot.

This restaurant was such a pleasant surprise. The service was friendly, the drinks were delicious and the food was outstanding. I would come here again in a heartbeat. I recommend the cacio y pepe fritelle and the Agnolotti cheese filled pasta.

As you'll see lots of other guests wrote: food is incredible, but the hostesses almost ruin the experience. Rudest hostesses I've ever had at any restaurant in Manhattan or BK. The manager needs to do something about them. But the pasta is so good that it's worth going anyway...

One of the best restaurants in NYC, hands-down. Missy's food is incredible (pasta, obviously, but try the radishes with ricotta, and pretty much anything on the bar snack or antipasti menu). The service is also a highlight, from the host, to the waiter, to the wonderful sommelier. We keep coming back again and again, with no plan to stop!

This place is worth the hype. I arrived exactly at 5:00pm on Christmas Eve with no reservation. I got on a line to speak to the hostess. The hostess had room at the bar. When I asked for a table she said the restaurant was fully reserved for the night. I stayed from 5:00-7:45 and saw many empty tables. I don't understand how this restaurant claims to be fully reserved when I saw mostly empty tables in the restaurant. The food was absolutely spectacular! Service was typical (nothing outstanding.) I am giving Lilia 5 stars for the food alone. The Aperol spritz was one of the best I've ever had. The whole artichoke and gem lettuce salad were dreamy. The lemon spaghetti had just the right amount of lemon. The olive cake was a bit dry, but the cream helped. I will be back to try additional dishes.
Beautiful and Romanic Atmosphere! I can totally see this's the best place for date. Food are all delicious. It's more like a new Italian style and it's not expensive. Enjoy!

Waited 2 months to eat here, absolutely worth the trek to BK, amazing food and ambiance. 

LOVED the cacio pepe fried balls, and the pastas.  Wine list was on point.  Overall a great restaurant and at par if not better with all the new York top Italian spots. 

Will be back!

We fought tooth and nail to get a reservation here on our trip, and we ended up with 10pm on Sunday. Needless to say, we are not dinner-at-10 type people, but we made an exception and are immensely glad that we did.

We each started with cocktails. I had a classic cosmo - not on the menu, but seriously the best cosmo I've ever had. BF had the Boulevardier (rye cocktail) which he positively loved.

Now starters. The cacio e pepe arancini was a must; those are two of my favorite things. But the real scene stealer was the grilled persimmon salad. The grilled fruit with the cheese and the honey was positively phenomenal. I could've eaten it for days and days and days. 

For entrees, I had the mafaldini with pink peppercorn and Parmesan. The pasta is long, curly noodles (think the edges of lasagna noodles) with a perfect bite (cooked al dente). The pink instead of black peppercorns really elevated things, and the Parmesan rounded everything out. It was the best version of cacio e pepe I've ever had, hands down. BF had the fettucine with spiced lamb sauce which he loved equally (although he stole several bites of mine as well). 

For dessert I did the double chocolate torte and BF had the apple crostada. The torte was rich without being heavy (I don't know how they did it - the texture was like a cake and soufflé had a wonderful baby) and oh so chocolately. It comes with some sort of espresso foam that really rounded things out. BF's Apple crostada was delicious as well - the crust was sugary and buttery without being over the top, the filling was sweet but tart in the best way, and the lemon gelato topping rounded everything out. 

Finally - the service. A far cry from our dining experience the night before, Lilia is service done right. Our coats were taken when we arrived and returned promptly when we left, our table was constantly maintained without being overbearing - water always filled, crumbs wiped, napkin folded when I went to the bathroom, dishes bussed in a timely manner, new silverware provided after every course (and specific to what you ordered). The food was prompt but we didn't feel rushed, and even though they closed at 11 we never felt like they were hurrying us. 

Next time we're in NYC, reservations at Lilias will again be the utmost priority.

My wife and I called ahead to check if there was any availability and the hostess made it sound like the wait was minimal. She said there is a wait at the bar but you should still come. 
We decided to head straight to the restaurant and 30mins later we arrive and are told the wait at the bar is 2.5hrs long. 
I get that this is a popular restaurant but there is no reason to have made us come all the way just find out the wait is that long. We could have been told on the phone.

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey.

This plate will redefine your relationship with pasta. Your taste buds will detect new flavor profiles and send signals to your brain triggering a new form of euphoria. It's one of the better dishes I've had in recent years, and the flavor combinations were as complex as they were delicate and unique. 

But even without ordering this dish (arguably still a crime, though) your meal here will be incredible. I was drawn here for a while from a steady flow of hype, *that* NYT review and my personal hobby making hand-made pasta, and was not disappointed. We also enjoyed (like basically every other New Yorker) the cacio e pepe balls. They're basically a fried flavor bomb with that sharp taste you get from good pecorino and/or parmesan. A negroni (or two) pairs perfectly with the meal. 

We were seated next to friends of the owner, which was initially difficult because they were basically given the entire menu (leaving us salivating and with major fomo) but we ended up meeting her and heard about how a recent visit to Spain had inspired her seasonal dish with persimmon and some type of artisanal cheese. Typical chef being gourmet af and fabulous. 

Not an inexpensive meal by any means but the quality is there. Eager to go again.

Food was 4-5 stars, but the waiter really spoiled the experience.

He started the pressure early. We'd had a long day and just wanted water. He was really surprised, no drinks, are you sure? And then started listing drinks. No drinks, thanks.

When he was describing the menu, he suggested 3 appetizers and 3 pastas. That felt like a lot, but maybe the plates are small. We decided on 1 appetizer and 2 pastas, figuring that we'd get a dessert and could always order more.

Again he pressured us. That's it? I suggest at least another couple of dishes. Again, no thank you.

We got the dishes and they weren't small. We ordered well, despite the advice of our server. And after all, including our dessert, we still spent 85$, so I don't feel too bad about our waiter not being able to make the rent check thanks to us.

It was abundantly clear what he was doing, he turned cold after we didn't get drinks. The gall to suggest we order another couple dishes. We're fully grown adults that both have the right to order as much as we like, and have a good idea at this point in our lives how much we want to eat. Not cool.

AWFUL.  Service was ridiculous.  Told it would be a two hour wait from hostess with attitude.  We returned in two hours, forced to wait almost another hour, meanwhile several seats stayed empty at the bar "being held for friends of the chef".  Then as other seats opened we were shuffled closer to the door and icy cold wind coming in from front entrance.  Food is decent Italian but nothing approaching the overhyped reviews. More troubling, blowfish tails were upsold and tasted fishy.  Unacceptably, TWO of three pasta dishes were COLD.  We returned one.  They didn't clear the plates, just left what we'd taken there, stirred the remnants around in a pot and returned them to us - STIILL COLD.  Worse yet, didn't even offer to comp the dish.  Meanwhile the chef personally greeted people next to us and then later hand grated truffles over her friends' plates at the warm end of the bar.  Might have been a better meal if she had been paying closer attention. Esp. at an overpriced $220 for 2 ppl.

I want to ramble on about my last meal here but I won't. It's the best restaurant in Brooklyn. Get a pasta, get a Lamb Steak, drink wine. Enjoy the great service. Ignore the slightly bitchy hostesses and have a pukka dinner. The end.

I've been reading amazing things about Lilia for months and it took me just as long to finally get a dinner reservation there. After all of that, I really wanted to love it when my boyfriend and I went on a recent Monday night, but sadly, it fell short for us.

We showed up for our reservation exactly on time and were told the table wasn't ready and we would have to wait in the back cafe area. We weren't interested in getting a drink there, so we just stood around for 10-15 minutes until they came and got us. Not the biggest deal, but not a great first impression, either.

I had done my research before arriving and had written down several "must-try" dishes mentioned in the NY Times, Eater, and elsewhere. We ordered the following and shared all of it:

--Cacio e Pepe Fritelle (my boyfriend found these to be too salty, but I liked them pretty well)
--Cauliflower, Spicy Soppressata, Sicilian Pesto, Majoram (solid cauliflower preparation, but didn't knock our socks off)
--Grilled Clams, Calabrian Chili, Breadcrumbs (HUGE miss. The clams were ridiculously gritty and rubbery. I didn't care for the seasoning, either.)
--Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti, Saffron, Dried Tomato, Honey (delicious, unique, and memorable)
--Black Bass, Salsa Verde, Coal Roasted Yukon Gold Potatoes (overwhelming lemon flavor)
--Olive oil cake (solid, but maybe a little crusty in parts)

The pasta was far and away the best thing we had and we both regretted not ordering a couple of other pastas as well. We were trying to get something from each part of the menu and clearly that was a mistake. 

No complaints about the service once we got to our table. Another plus was the price, which was quite reasonable after all was said and done.
However, the food was simply not stellar enough to warrant the hassle of trying to come back.

Ive been here twice and both times have been great experiences. The service is fantastic. 
As is the food!!
The special focaccia and garlic butter is AWESOME. The cacio e Pepe frittelle are basically pasta donuts which I'm very into. 
The baked clams are good but I didn't think the best thing, as many others have said. 
Beyond LOVE the agnolotti, and the mafaldini is good. Finally, I thought the olive oil cake was a star!!

After hearing all the hype from both friends and reviews, I decided to take the BF to Lilia for his birthday dinner this past weekend.  By no means was the food bad, but unfortunately we were both let down.  The highlights of our meal were probably the two appetizers we shared - the roasted escarole and cured sardines.  None of the three pastas we shared were noteworthy (the rigatoni, mafaldini, agnolotti).  The Mafaldini which I was most excited for was probably the most disappointing - texture was on the denser side and lacked full bodied flavor.  And finally for dessert, we shared the soft serve which was again nothing great.  I really am sad that we didn't love our experience at Lilia knowing that so many people do.

Fourth time at Lilia, and the food was exceptional as ever. However, if you are going to make diners wait a half hour in the cafe for a reserved table, please consider offering an on-the-house drink or offer at least some acknowledgement of the inconvenience.

LILIA is a popular place for good reason. My personal experience was arriving at the opening hour only to find there was only one seat left. I could see by the active, attractive crowd that was true. I was pleasantly surprised by the wonderful service. I thoroughly enjoyed a terrific grilled fish and long to go back to try other offerings. Great place, met several cool people. Preston

Ok so here it is : got there 5:20pm sharp, folks are lining up as if they are giving away free yeezy's. Food is ok tried about 4 diff pasta's a few appetizers. Agnolotti is by far the best thing I had, it is absolutely out of this world. Everything is good not mind blowing. Do your self a favor get the blow fish the agnolotti don't share and call it a day.

This is one of those places that puts out really good food across their menu and doesn't need a star dish. Their pricing hits a really sweet spot with everything aside from main meat entrees being under $20. 
I really like this place. Top 5 in NYC. 
Will be back, even with the 3 hour wait.

Very unprofessional. My girlfriend and I went here for my birthday this week, and they NEVER GAVE ME MY BAG BACK from their pseudo coat check (which isn't really a coat check. A waiter/waitress grabs your stuff and insists they'll remember whose is whose, but clearly this failed. Would recommend a ticket system that most decent NYC restaurants adopt). What's worse, I had to call them FOUR TIMES just to get them to look for it, and after A DAY of back and forth they finally discovered it. I had to commute all the way to Brooklyn to pick it up. 

As for the food, it was good but not great. To be fair, pasta is difficult to perfect compared to meat/veggies/etc, but overall nowhere near the hype Lilia currently has. Add terrible customer service to the mix (see above) and I doubt this place will hold its reputation for much longer. To be a great restaurant in NYC you need to provide exceptional service all around, and Lilia misses the mark.

best spot in brooklyn. simple and perfect

missy's pastas are next level.

pink peppercorn mafaldine...sheeps milk agnolotti....

game over

The restaurant here is amazingly delicious but be prepared to wait for a long time if you walk in without a reservation. Also, come during the day and get the paninis from the cafe. The prosciutto on focaccia is amazing.

I've been to Lilia twice now, and I agree that their many accolades are entirely deserved. The space is warm, contemporary, and inviting, and I love the smell of firewood wafting from the kitchen.

Reservations can be tricky, especially on weekends. They do 30 days in advance on Resy, but sell out of prime times within minutes of midnight. Last Saturday I took my chances with a 5:55pm walk-in, and waited 2.5 hours for bar seats. For me, 8:30pm dinner at the bar on a Saturday night is actually ideal.

On to the food! I highly recommend the cacio e pepe frittelle; it's really a must-order. I've tried the baked clams, cannellini beans, and crunchy shrimp with gremolata too, and all are perfectly executed. For my main course, I chose the sheep's milk agnolotti, which is accented by sweet drips of honey. My husband raved about his lamb dish.

If you can deal with the hassle of getting a table, Lilia is one of the best choices for Italian hearth style cooking and fresh pastas right now.

Second time around was much better. Yes, reservations are still impossible to get, so book a month in advance and watch Resy's openings! The Italian wine options were excellent. Service was fantastic. The roasted Trumpet Mushrooms appetizer was fine, not great. I thought the mushrooms were a little too chewy and undercooked, and could have used more cook time. It was simple and tasty, but nothing spectacular. I enjoyed the mixture of textures. The Ricotta Gnocchi and Spaghetti Alla Chitarra were excellent. Between the two, I'd choose the Spaghetti (and my only complaint was that it was-- surprise surprise-- super salty). I would return again but I still strongly prefer other Italian restaurants in New York.

Sorry I lived down the block from this place and I cannot validate eating and paying these prices in what used to be a mechanic shop, filled with grease and dirt.  Food decent, portions very small, went home and cooked.

Finally snagged a reservation at Lilia in Brooklyn and the food truly lived up to expectations. All really simple but well-done with good ingredients. First time having blowfish tails and it so good and somehow reminded me of frog legs. 

The malfadini pasta is done simply with just pink peppercorn and Parmesan reggiano and is spectacular. Lovely restaurant!

Absolutely wonderful neighborhood restaurant - loved the plate of raw vegetables with anchovy sauce, the blowfish tails (never had this before and it was delicious), sardine toast, and baked clams. The spaghetti with mushrooms was good but too salty. Friendly service, kid-friendly. Can't wait to come back!

Technically, my rating is a 3.8/5 though I'm rounding up to 4 because overall, I had an enjoyable dining experience with above average food. Here's why: 

Ambiance (5/5). The space is nice and intimate. It's perfect for a date or even a birthday. That said, reservations are tough to get, so plan accordingly. I was lucky enough to score a same day resy due to a last minute cancellation, but reservations are typically booked a month in advance. 

Food (3.5/5). Like I said, the food was above average, but for the price, we were expecting more. 

+The cacio e pepe fritters (which come 3 to an order) were disappointing. 2 of the 3 fritters were overcooked, leaving us with doughy fried balls. I know this wasn't the intention because the third fritter was divine, oozing with cheesy cacio e pepe-flavored goodness. I just wish all 3 of the fritters were cooked this way because that one ball (which my GF and I shared) was the highlight of our meal. 

+ the artichoke appetizer was great. It's hard to go wrong with veggies smothered in cheese and bread crumbs. Yum. I would order this again. 

+ For mains, we shared the sheep's milk agnolotti and the mafaldani. Both pastas were perfectly al dente and for the most part, the flavor was on point (side note: if you're not a fan of pepper, I would pass on the mafaldani, which is topped with a heavy helping of pink peppercorn). My biggest complaint was that the food became cold quickly, which made the pasta almost unpleasant to eat. The mafaldani was very light on sauce, so it just tasted dry and chewy as it got cold. 

+ We shared the chocolate soft serve for dessert. The ice cream was served with hazelnuts, espresso, and candied lemon zest. It was a lovely flavor combination, though there were a few bites that were unbalanced. The lemon zest can be overpowering if you're not careful about the ratio of ingredients in each spoonful. 

Price (3/5): Lilia is a three dollar sign establishment, so it's certainly not a cheap meal. For two appetizers, two pastas, one dessert, two vodka sodas, and tip, our bill came out to $125. This wouldn't have bothered me if the food blew me away, but it didn't. 

Given all the hype around Lilia, I was surprised to experience the aforementioned issues (inconsistent cooking, cold food, etc.). These are all things that can be easily addressed, and if/when they are, I will gladly come back. But until then, I will satisfy my Italian cravings elsewhere.

This was our second time visiting Lilia. I have to say I was a bit disappointed for the hype and price. We sat at the bar both times and the bar tenders were great for drink recommendations but really had no valuable input on the menu when asked recommendation. We found all of the dishes to be over seasoned with salt losing the core flavor of each dish. The saffron Agnolotti is the best dish on the menu, its really unique and delicious. The rest of  pasta dishes come out luke warm and below average for the competition in that neighborhood.  Looking for a good Italian meal in Williamsburg go to Barano.

Disappointed . Expensive and not even good food . 18 $ for a small bowl of pasta with tomato ...i make better pasta at home and I am not the best cook !!! Two stars , one for the service that was good and one star for the design of the place . That's it .....

Had dinner here just last night. Booked the reservation online about a month ago. Had to settle for a 10:45PM reservation because the advance booking was full. My husband and I were looking forward to it because of the hype, publicity and proximity to home. 

We arrived 10mins early and were led to the back cafe for a drink and/or snack while we waited. The waiting cafe was fine, had to wait a while for our drink bc the place was busy. Small space, but thankful for any proper waiting space in this town.

Only waited for about 15mins before we were sat. We were told the (Italian) restaurant was out of BREAD and a couple of other things from the specials list. It was late, but that was the only time we could book. The waiter was nice enough, I could tell we were one of his last tables and he was perfectly professional and patient. 

The service was lovely (the red-headed hostess was really sweet) but the food was just fine. Just ok. Had the Fra Diavolo pasta and my husband had the lamb pasta. It was fine. Our appetizer was the prawns and they weren't impressive, just ok--passable. It seemed like we had to jump a few hoops, make a reservation far too ahead in advance for something "just fine." 

Seems like a lot of hype for little reward.

Disappointing. I woke up early multiple times trying to get reservations for this place. I was so excited to come her but the food was underwhelming. The best dish we got was the scallops. Unfortunately the dish only came with 2. We got the rigatoni, pink peppercorn pasta and sheep milk pasta. The sheep milk pasta was definitely the best. The rigatoni was very undercooked. The pink peppercorn pasta was way too peppery. The pasta dishes were definitely unique but I didn't love it. We also got the veal. It was cooked well and the flavor was good but I wouldn't order it again. The ambiance and service was a+.

What a terrific place!
Had dinner with four others and, between us, we order just about everything on the menu and enjoyed them all.
Staff was very friendly, helpful and accommodating, as well.
Especially enjoyed the Caulifower, Slow Roasted Tomatoes, Grilled Scallops,Agnolotti, and the Grilled Lamb Leg Steak. Found the Mafaldini a bit spicy for my taste, but others enjoyed it.
Dessert was good but nothing special, but maybe it suffered by comparison to the earlier parts of our dinner. 
Eager to return on my next trip to New York.

Can I give this place a 10 star? Oh my god - I have been in New York City for the past two years and have always been eating out and recently gotten into an Italian place. I live in Greenwich Village and there are TONS of amazing Italian places around but this place blows everything else out of the water - it was AMAZING. Went there with two friends and sat outdoors on a breezy Monday night. The waitress was very attentive. We got Grilled Blowfish Tails (amazing flavor, interesting in a good way food!) and that Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti OH MY GOD - we got one order first and HAD to add a second order right after even though the prices are on the higher end but everything was just SO good. One thing - desserts were kind of mediocre but overall I was very very satisfied and so were my two friends. Have a friend visiting next March and I'm already planning on bringing him there (He's a super huge Italian fan!)

The restaurant is beautiful, to start. Dim lighting,wood buttressed ceilings, and wall decor make this a very cozy spot despite its vast ceilings and generally large size.

The food is incredible. Noteworthy favorites include the cacio pepe fritters, the sheep's milk pasta with the saffron butter sauce, and the spaghetti with lemon pine nut sauce (I know, you think spaghetti is boring but trust me on this one!). 

Overall, for the quality of the food which was very fresh and highly flavorful (served in modest portions, which was great) was delicious. I would happily return. The only weird thing was that when we asked for bread, our waiter told us they don't actually have bread for the table but would give us the stuff that comes with another dish. Whatever! Not going to stop me from gobbling up more of their pasta! NOM!

PS we had absolutely no trouble being seated.

We enjoyed a wonderful meal at Lilia tonight, our third time there, but unfortunately tonight we noticed a definate "push" with the meal...we didn't have any linger at all between our courses and one of the servers actually picked up one of our plates that still had food on it.  We all reacted so shocked that the other server made a comment and apologized and brought us a dessert.  But they seemed to be in a huge hurry to turn the table.  We had a bottle of wine, starters, entrees and dessert...and we barely put our fork down in-between each course.  We were still processing the check when the same person came over that took the plate with food away, started picking up the napkins on the table.  While the food was amazing, bravo the the kitchen, the overall feel was not relaxed and enjoyable, but rushed and uncomfortable.  Not what I expect when I am paying what I paid for a meal!

Really not sure what all the hype is about. I am a huge foodie, own 3 restaurants, & i was SUPER EXCITED to try this place after all the hype and reviews. First of all, my parents are both Sicilian straight off the boat, and my mother cooks killer Sicilian food all of the time. So im not sure if it's my high standards, but my entire meal was NOT impressive at all. My boyfriend and I drove 40 minutes from Jersey City to Brooklyn last night for this meal, which I could not wait for. We ordered the Cacio e Pepe fritelle, roasted mushrooms, grilled clams, grilled blowfish tails, Malfaldini, & the Agnelotti. The best thing about my meal was dipping bread (which I had to ask for) into the olive oil which the grilled blowfish was in. Seriously so disappointed. The malfaldini tasted like straight pepper & ONLY pepper, as well as the Cacio e Pepe fritelle. So bland, besides the extreme amount of pepper which was all you tasted. I also paid $11 PER GLASS for each glass of Moscato, which was the tiniest wine glass I have ever seen, probably 2 sips of each was all it took to finish. I cannot believe all of the positive reviews on this place. I can cook better Italian food at my house!! 30 day wait to get a reservation?? Makes me so mad. I can get better Italian food at many other places, & wouldnt have to wait so long for a reservation either! $162 to the FACE. Never will come again.

The clams and specials were delicious. Pasta is very fresh. I enjoyed the meal. Food was on point and good ambience! My 3 is for things besides the food. 

Feedback:

- Indicate the ounces/grams of the lamb on your menu or have the server advise the guest. 

- If you serve persecco...have the correct flutes for bubbles. It does make a difference.

-Waitress could have been far more attentive to when we needed another drink,  water and the check.

Amazing casual date night spot. Service was amazing and food was remarkable.

Summer Squash - Recommend. Whole squash. Huge. Crazy tender and soft.

Cacio e Pepe Fritelle - Recommend. Its a piping hot doughnut that tastes like a bowl of pasta.

Cucumbers, Calabrian Chilies - Strong strong flavors here. The feta and fennel seeds do not yield to each other.

Radishes, Whipped Ricotta - Simple, if you like raw radishes, great. The spicy radish and the dairy really work well together.

Grilled Scallops, Walnuts - Recommend. Perfectly grilled. Tad marjoram heavy.

Blowfish Tails, Salmoriglio - Grilled to perfection. Heavy on the crushed coriander.

Agnolotti, Saffron - Sounds so good. One bite is all you need. Dried tomato and honey made it sweeter than expected.

Mafaldini, Pink Peppercorns - Recommend. Great pasta shape. Tender and toothy. Could eat a pot of this.

Spaghetti, Lemon - Recommend. So simple, so good. They really allow the housemade pasta to shine with this one. Seriously among the best bowls of pasta I've had. You're thinking, "I could make this at home, I'm not about to pay for this." You're wrong.

Black Bass, Salsa Verde - Recommend. Creamy, bright, hearty, light and heavy at the same time. 

Per our server's recommendation: Fiano de Avellino, ciropicariello. Good mineral forward choice to nurse through the gamut of dishes. 

The hype is real.

I'd been dying to come here for so long, and finally snagged a last minute reservation on Resy.

Cacio e pepe fritelle: good, but salty
Housemade Mozzarella, Toasted Garlic Bread, Lemon, Bottarga: mozzarella was excellent, and I loved the umami that the bottarga added
Grilled blowfish tails: I'd never had blowfish tails before - this was very good.  Perfectly cooked, and I loved the crushed coriander
Malfadini: meh.  For all the love this dish gets, it was underwhelming
Agnolotti: good, but didn't blow me away.  Very rich and creamy
Chocolate torta with espresso zabaglione: the cake was pretty bad.

Overall the food was good but I just wasn't wowed by anything.

Great atmosphere but food is a bit over rated! The clam dish was rubbery and not good. The Cacio e Pepe fratelle honestly was not very good either... just too heavy. The market vegetables w anchovy sauce was good but only two tiny pcs of grilled bread and a ton of sauce. Overall balance of flavor in the appetizer dishes were okay. The pastas were delicious though all on the rich side. Olive oil cake was the highlight. Sorry just being honest! Great date spot though!

Loved the food here:

Mozzarella on bread - very good
Artichoke - good
Radish with ricotta - very good
Grilled scallops - delicious
Grilled blowfish tails - very good
Malfaldini - ok
Fettuccine with sausage - ok
Mezzaluna with corn - so good we ordered this 2x
Ribeye steak - delicious 
Blueberry tart - delicious
Chocolate cake - good
Olive oil cake - good
Lemon sorbet - refreshing
I am in love with this place everything on the menu is to die for the wait is a little overrated but it's definitely worth it

I went there cuz all the hype on social media. Bad experiences about food and services. The lady who leads the table has really bad attitudes, cold and unfriendly. The food is okay like normal Italian restaurant. Overall the restaurant is so overrated. Will not come back again.

Great new Italian restaurant. I was expecting Lilia to be overrated given the social media hype it's gotten recently, but it really did blow me away with creative and seasonal takes on Italian classics. 

Lilia's reservations fill up weeks in advance, but I went with a friend as a walk in at 6:15 and were seated outside immediately. The outdoor tables were lovely and next to a public piano that was played by local musicians throughout our meal. 

We began the meal with the fresh mozzarella on garlic bread with lemon - a refreshing summer treat with tart lemon and creamy mozzarella! We then got the summer beans which were covered in spices, breadcrumbs and parmesan. And then onto the pastas... we got the mafaldini and the agnolotti. The mafaldini is what the internet has been raving about and I agree with the craze - it has beautiful waves and pink peppercorns to a bring a unique color to the dish, and the pasta was perfectly al dente. However, the agnolotti stole the show - it had a savory honey lemon saffron sauce that was memorable and the deep tastes lingered for hours.

The waitress recommended we order 1 or 2 more dishes than we did, but we were both pleased with the amount of food. 

Bottom line - go early to enjoy without needing to book far in advance or waiting hours on the corner for your table!

I thought I was going to be blown away based on the reviews but I found it to be a little underwhelming. Sure the pasta is good, but it wasn't amazing. The portion sizes seem small but I was literally stuffed sharing 3 plates with my boyfriend ( I ate most of it). There's a line before the restaurant even opens on a Wednesday night. By 6p. all the available outside seating were gone. I recommend making reservations unless you get there before 5:30 to either sit at the bar or patio. 

Cacio e Pepe Fritelle ($7)-4/5 Three decent sized balls, these were soft and delightful. They're cheesy and comes out really hot. Sort of tastes like a lighter version of a fried mac and cheese ball. 

Mafaldini ($19)- 3/5 I fell in love with mafaldini at Leuca's and thought that this would be just as good but I was disappointed. It's cooked al dente and all you could really taste was the pink peppercorns. 

Sheeps Milk Cheese Filled Agnolotti ($23)- 4.5/5 This was probably the best dish, the only bad part was that it wasn't really hot, it was just warm when it came out. It's really soft and the cheese just oozes out into your mouth. The tomatoes were delicious.The sauce was amazing, I even used it for the mafaldini.

As Simon Cowell would say, "It's a no from me, darling!"

It all started when I suggested to my boyfriend we try out Lilia to celebrate our anniversary!  So fun and sweet, right?  We figured we would head over, put our names down, and then walk around Williamsburg while we waited.

We got there and were told it'd be two and a half hours - whatever, expected.  They suggested we head back to the cafe for snacks and drinks while we wait.  We were hungry so we, too, thought that was a swell idea.  This is where it all went down hill.

The girls back there were serving the people surrounding us but it took about 15 minutes to be approached.  My boyfriend was in the bathroom so I asked if we could do the Mozzarella without the bottarga because of my dietary restrictions and was met with judgement and contempt.  They can't adjust starters.  Mind you the bottarga is merely a garnish.  YOU CAN'T LEAVE OFF THE GARNISH?  So I said nevermind and walked out front to the waiting area and texted my boyfriend to meet me.
